He further instructed them, saying, "I have heard that you two are manifestations of the Bodhisattvas Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra.

You should now go to Mount Tiantai to pay homage to the Great Master Zhiyi. They departed immediately. Later, when Yuan Ying was about to leave his post, he again visited the temple and asked, "Where are Hanshan and Shide now? Qian replied, "They have gone to Mount Tiantai. Yuan Ying sighed and said, "Alas! How could I have known that the two of them were actually the Bodhisattvas? (Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly with "Yuan Ying arrived at his post three days later... went to Guoqing and asked... This temple has [someone named] Feng...")
"Is this Master Gan Chan? And who are Han Shan and Shi De? The monk Dao Qiao replied, "The old site of Fenggan is behind the sutra repository;
it is now desolate and unoccupied. Han Shan and Shi De still reside in the monastery kitchen. When Zhiyin entered Gan’s room, he saw nothing but tiger tracks.
He asked again, "What kind of practice do they perform here? Dao Qiao said, "They do nothing but carry grain for the mortars."
He provided offerings to the Sangha. When at leisure, he would chant and recite. Entering the kitchen, he sought out Han and Shi, only to find them before the hearth warming themselves by the fire.

He clapped his hands and laughed loudly. When Dao Yin prostrated himself, the two men shouted and scolded him in unison. Taking hold of his hand, they laughed again and said, "Fenggan is so talkative!
Fenggan is so talkative! You do not even recognize Amitābha; why do you bow to us? Monks rushed in from all directions, passing along their mutual alarm.
He was astonished and asked, "For what reason does your honored office pay such courtesy to these two poor men? At that moment, the two men took each other's hands and ran out of the temple.

Dao Yin ordered them to be pursued, but they fled in haste and returned immediately to their cold rock cave. Dao Yin then questioned the monks again, saying, "Are these two willing to remain in this temple?
He then had them sought out and summoned back to the temple for their placement there. Dao Yin subsequently returned to the commandery and prepared pure robes.

The two pairs [of shoes] and the incense, medicines, and other offerings were carried there for presentation. At that time, the two men did not return to the temple; instead, the messenger went directly to the cliff to deliver them.
Seeing this, Hanshanzi shouted at the top of his voice, "Thieves! Thieves! He then entered a crevice in the rock and said, "I warn you all: each of you must exert yourselves!

The rock crevice closed of its own accord, so that they could no longer pursue him. As for Shiqi: *Note: The text provided ends abruptly with "其拾得" (As for Shiqi...), suggesting the source passage was incomplete.*

The traces [of his passing] sank away into nothingness. Later, there was a monk gathering firewood on the southern peak, two li southeast of the monastery, when he encountered a foreign monk (brahmacārin) carrying a staff who entered a cave.
The foreign monk picked up a "lock-shaped" bone (śarīra) and said, "Take this; it is a śarīra.

Thereupon, it was known that [Śibi] had entered parinirvāṇa here, and thus the cave was named "Shide" (The Gleaner). Subsequently, Daoqiao was commissioned to seek out the remaining traces; among the leaves in the forest, he found...
I obtained the verses and hymns written by Hanshan, as well as over three hundred pieces from village and rural households;
Shishi also had several dozen poems inscribed upon the stone walls of the Land Deity Hall. I have compiled these into a single scroll.
○ Tansheng visited Chan Master Weiyen.
Tansheng was the son of the Wang family of Jianchang. At birth, he had a natural amnion; it draped over his right shoulder like a monastic robe.

He left home to become a monk at a young age and studied under Huaihaim for twenty years, yet the karmic conditions were not yet harmonized. Later, he visited Weiyen. Weiyen asked, "Where have you come from?"
Baizhang arrived. Xueyan asked, "What words or phrases did Baizhang have to show to his disciples? Baizhang replied, "He usually said, 'I have one phrase that contains all a hundred flavors.
Xueyan said, "If it is salty, it has a salty flavor; if it is bland, it has a bland flavor. What about that which is neither salty nor bland?"
"This is the constant flavor. What is the phrase that possesses the hundred flavors? Cheng had no reply. Yǎn said, "What about birth and death right before one's eyes?
Cheng said, "There is no birth and death right before my eyes. Yǎn said, "How long have you been at Bǎizhàng? Cheng said, "Twenty years.
Yǎn said, "Having spent twenty years at Bǎizhàng, you still have not eliminated your worldly airs. On another day, [Cheng] was standing in attendance.
Next, Xian asked again, "What further Dharma did Baizhang preach? [Baizhang] replied, "Sometimes he would say: 'Eliminate it beyond the three phrases; realize it within the six phrases.
Xian said, 'Even from three thousand miles away, I am glad there is no connection. He asked again, 'What further Dharma did he preach?
[Baizhang] replied, 'Sometimes, when the assembly had taken their places for the lecture hall, he would drive them all away at once with his staff. Furthermore...
He summoned the assembly. As the assembly turned their heads, the Master said, "What is this? Yunyan said, "Why did you not say something sooner?
Today, because of you, I have been able to see my elder brother Hai. At these words, Wusheng attained sudden realization and prostrated himself.
○ Zongzhi visited Chan Master Weiyen.

Zongzhi was the son of the Zhang family of Haihun; he left home to become a monk and received full ordination at a young age. He attended the dharma assembly of Yaoshan and attained a secret realization of the mind-seal.
One day, Weiyen asked him, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from traveling the mountains. Weiyen said:
"Do not leave this room; bring him here quickly. [The messenger] replied, "The crows on the mountain are white as snow; the fish swimming in the ravine are never at rest.
One day, Yanyang ascended the hall and said, "I have a single phrase that I have never yet spoken to anyone.
Zhi Chu said, "It has followed me here. A monk asked Yanyang, "How do you speak this single phrase? Yanyang said, "It is not a matter of verbal expression."
Zhizhi said, "I have already finished speaking. Zhizhi left Yaoshan and went to see Puyuan. Puyuan asked, "What is your name, Layman? He replied, "Zongzhi.
Puyuan said, "Regarding the place where wisdom does not reach, what is your principle? He replied, "One must strictly avoid mentioning it.
Puyuan said, "Truly, if you mention it, then horns will grow. Three days later, Zhizhi and Tansheng were in the rear hall holding [the broom].
Zhizhou was sewing a robe. Yuanyan came forward to see him and asked, "Master Zhizhou, you said the other day: 'Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it;
if one speaks of it, horns will grow. How should one practice? Zhizhou then withdrew his body and entered the Sangha hall.
Yuanyan returned to the Abbot’s quarters. Zhizhou came back to continue sewing the robe. Yuansheng said, "Just now, why did you not answer the Master? Zhizhou replied: [The text ends here.]
"You are indeed clever," said Xuefeng Chengyuan. "I did not recommend you," he continued, then turning to Wenyuan, he asked, "Why did that Chan monk Zhidao not respond to the Master just now?
Wenyuan replied, "I do not understand; I beg the Master to instruct me. Wenyuan said, "He was, in fact, practicing among the 'beings of a different species' (heterogeneous beings)."
[Daowu] asked, "What is it like to walk among those of different species? Yuan said, "Have you not heard the Way?
Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it. If you speak of it, horns will grow. You must simply walk among those of different species. Cheng also did not understand.
Knowing that Cheng had not grasped the meaning, Yuan said, "This person's karmic conditions do not lie here. Let us return together to Yaoshan. Yan asked, "You..."
"Why have you returned so quickly? Cheng said, "It was simply because our karmic conditions did not coincide.
Yan asked, "What were those conditions? Cheng recounted the previous conversation. Yan asked, "How do you understand it? Cheng had no reply. Yan laughed loudly.
Cheng then asked, "What is 'walking among those of different species'? Yan said, "I am weary today; wait for another time to come. [Tansheng] said, "Tansheng came specifically..."
He returned for this reason. Yan said, "Go on for now. Cheng then departed. While Zhi was outside the abbot’s quarters, he heard that Cheng had not been granted an interview.
Unconsciously, he bit his finger until it bled. He went back down and asked Cheng, "Brother, you went to ask the Master about that karmic cause;
what did he say? Cheng replied, "The Master would not speak to me. Zhi then bowed his head.
The novice Gao visited Chan Master Weiyen. Gao visited Weiyen;
Weiyen asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Mount Heng. Weiyen asked, "Where are you going?"
He said, "I am going to Jiangling to receive the precepts. Yanyue said, "What is the purpose of receiving the precepts? He replied, "The purpose is to escape birth and death.
Yanyue said, "There is a person who does not receive the precepts, yet there is likewise no birth and death to escape.
Do you know this yet? Guoqing said, "If that is so, then what use are the Buddha's precepts? Yanyue said, "This novice still has them hanging from his lips and teeth. Guoqing bowed and withdrew.
Zongzhi came forward to stand in attendance. Yanyue said, "Just now there was a limping śrāmaṇera who seemed to have some measure of spiritual breath.
Zongzhi replied, "He must still be further tested before he is ready. That evening, Yanyue ascended the hall and called out, "Where is that śrāmaṇera who came earlier?
Gu went forth from the assembly and stood there. Yanyue asked, "I hear that Chang'an is very noisy; do you know this? He replied:
"My country is at peace. Yan said, "Did you obtain this from reading the scriptures, or did you obtain it by seeking instruction?

He replied, "I did not obtain it from reading the scriptures, nor did I obtain it from seeking instruction. Yan said, "There are many people who do not read the scriptures and do not seek instruction;

why is it that they do not obtain it? He replied, "I do not say that they do not obtain it; it is simply that they are unwilling to take responsibility for it. Yan looked at Zhi and said, "Do you not believe what he says?"
One day he took his leave of Xiangyan. Xiangyan asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "I am causing an obstruction for those in the assembly;

I shall go to the side of the road and pitch a thatched hut there to receive travelers with tea and soup. Xiangyan said, "The matter of birth and death is great; why do you not go to receive the precepts?
He replied, "Knowing such matters as these, I simply let them be. What else would you call 'precepts'? Xiangyan said, "Since you are like this..."
"It is so. You must not leave my side. We shall meet again from time to time. One day, he returned from outside and encountered the rain.
Xian said, "You have come? He replied, "Yes. Xian said, "How very wet you are! He replied, "I am not playing this drum or flute."
Tansheng said, "There is not even leather; what drum could one beat? Zongzhi said, "There is not even a drum; what leather could one beat?
Yanyan said, "Today there is truly a magnificent musical performance."
(Biyou) Chan Master Ruman preached the Dharma in the royal palace. Ruman resided in the capitals of Chang’an and Luoyang.
Emperor Shunzong of the Tang dynasty asked him: "From what direction does the Buddha come? Toward what direction does he go when he passes away?"
"Since it is said that you dwell eternally in the world, where is the Buddha now? Pūrṇa replied: "The Buddha comes from the unconditioned and returns to the unconditioned.
His Dharma-body is equal to empty space, eternally dwelling in the state of no-mind. Where there is thought, he returns to no-thought; where there is abiding, he returns to non-abiding.
He comes for the sake of sentient beings, and he goes for the sake of sentient beings. In the pure ocean of True Suchness, all is profoundly still."
The essence is eternally abiding; let the wise contemplate this well and no longer give rise to doubt. The Emperor asked again:
"The Buddha was born in the royal palace and passed away beneath the twin śāla trees. He dwelt in the world for forty-nine years, yet he also said that there is 'no dharma to be taught.

Mountains, rivers, and the great ocean; heaven and earth, as well as the sun and moon—all these, when their time comes, return to extinction. Who then says there is no birth and death? My doubts still remain."
Thus it is. The wise one discerns well. He replied: "The essence of the Buddha is fundamentally unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*); it is through deluded sentiments that false discrimination arises.

The Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*) is equal to empty space; it has never undergone arising or ceasing. When conditions exist, the Buddha appears in the world; when conditions are absent, the Buddha enters extinction.
He transforms sentient beings everywhere, like the moon reflected in water. It is neither permanent nor annihilated; it neither arises nor ceases. Arising...
It has never arisen, nor has it ever ceased. To perceive clearly the state of no-mind is naturally beyond verbal expression.

Upon hearing this, Emperor Dezong was greatly delighted and came to hold the Chan school in even higher esteem. A member of the Pei clan from Hedong kept a parrot that constantly recited the Buddha’s name and would not eat after noon.
Sometimes when the master tried to teach it to recite, it remained silent; other times, when told not to recite, it would immediately chant "Amituo."

Every time the dawn broke in his empty chamber, he would produce harmonious and elegant sounds, as solemn as the music of flutes and pipes. At the end of his life, he announced: "I am about to return to the West;
for you, I shall strike the *qing* stone. You must maintain mindfulness. With each strike, he recited the name of Amitābha Buddha once. After ten strikes, the ten recitations were completed.
When his breath ceased, his body was cremated, and more than ten *śarīra* relics were obtained, shining brilliantly and dazzling the eyes.
(Ciming Xugu) Chan Master Weize preached the Dharma at Foku (The Buddha’s Cave). [He was] a dharma successor of Niu-tou Zhong.
Weize was a native of Jingzhao; his secular surname was Changsun. Initially, he visited Huizhong and attained a great awakening to the profound essence of the teachings.

Later, he lived in seclusion on the western cliff of the Waterfall at Tiantai. During the Yuanhe era, his dharma assembly gradually flourished, and he first gave that cliff the name "Foku" (Buddha’s Cave).
In the cave, one day he addressed the assembly, saying: "Heaven and earth are devoid of things; I am devoid of things. Yet, it is not that there have never been things.
Thus, the sage is like a shadow, and a hundred years are like a dream. Who, then, undergoes birth and death?
The person of ultimate attainment uses this alone for illumination and is able to become the lord of the myriad things. I know this; do you all know it? One day, he suddenly announced [his passing].
A disciple said, "You should exert yourself; what more need I say? Two nights later, he sat peacefully and manifested his passing.
He was eighty years of age and had been a monk for fifty-eight years. His disciple Yunju Zhi succeeded him in the Dharma.
Once, a monk named Jizong from Huayan Monastery asked Zhi, "What is the meaning of 'seeing one's nature and becoming a Buddha'? Zhi replied, "The nature of purity is originally..."
It is profoundly still, without any movement or fluctuation. It does not belong to existence or non-existence, purity or impurity, long or short, nor to grasping or rejecting.

Its essence is inherently free and easy. To perceive clearly in this way is to clearly perceive the nature. Nature is itself Buddha; Buddha is itself nature. Therefore, it is said that "seeing one's nature is attaining Buddhahood."
Zong said, "If nature is already pure and does not belong to existence or non-existence, why is there seeing? [The other] said, "Seeing is seeing nothing.
Zong said, "Since there is nothing seen, how can there still be seeing? [The other] said, "Even the locus of seeing is non-existent. Zong said, "When seeing is thus..."
"Who is it that sees? He replied, "There is no one who can see. Zong asked, "What is the ultimate principle of this?

Zhi said, "To falsely reckon things as existing is to have subject and object; this is what is called delusion. Following such views to produce interpretations leads one straight into birth and death."
For one who sees with clarity, it is not so. Though seeing all day long, one has never seen anything; the locus where names are sought is eternally unobtainable.
When both subject and object are utterly transcended, this is called "seeing the nature. Zhong asked: "Does this nature pervade all places? He replied:

"There is not a single place it does not pervade. Zhong asked: "Do ordinary people possess it? He replied: "Since it was said above that there is nowhere it does not pervade, how could ordinary people not possess it?"
[The questioner] asked: "Why is it that the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are not constrained by birth and death, while ordinary beings alone are entangled in this suffering?
[Zhi] said: "Ordinary beings, within the nature of purity, calculate the existence of subject and object;

they thus fall into birth and death. The Buddhas, Great Beings, and Good Friends [do not do so]; within the nature of purity, they do not belong to existence or non-existence, nor to subject and object."
[The monk] did not respond. Zong said, "If it is so, then there must be people who can understand and those who cannot.

[The monk] said, "Since even 'understanding' itself cannot be found, how could there be a person who understands? Zong asked, "What is the ultimate principle? [The monk] said, "I shall now state the essential point for you."
You should immediately reflect: within the nature of purity, there are neither ordinary beings nor sages, nor are there those who have attained realization or those who have not.
Both "ordinary" and "sage" are merely names. If one generates understanding by following these names, one falls into birth and death.
If one knows that provisional names are unreal, then there is no one who corresponds to those names. Zhi further said: "This is the ultimate point of culmination. If one says, 'I am able...'"
To fail to understand this is itself a great illness. To perceive the existence of purity and defilement, or ordinary beings and sages, is also a great illness.
To form the understanding that there are neither ordinary beings nor sages likewise belongs to the denial of cause and effect and is a great illness.

To perceive a pure nature as a place where one may dwell is also a great illness; to form the understanding that there is no dwelling is also a great illness. Nevertheless, within the pure nature, although there is no movement or fluctuation...
He was fully endowed with unbreakable skillful means and applied them, while giving rise to loving-kindness and compassion. Such a state of arousal and application is the very nature of total purity;
it may be called "seeing one's nature and attaining Buddhahood. Jizong then bowed with great joy in gratitude and withdrew.

In the first year of the Yuanhe era, Chan Master Tianran was traveling to spread the Dharma in the capital. Tianran arrived in the capital and became friends with [Chan Master] Fu-niu. One day, at Huilin Temple...
Once, during a great cold, Huairan took a wooden Buddha and burned it, holding it toward the fire. The head monk of the monastery rebuked him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden Buddha?
Huairan then used a staff to stir the ashes, saying, "I am burning for its *śarīra* (relics). The head monk said, "A wooden Buddha—how could it have *śarīra*?
Huairan replied, "Since there are no *śarīra*, take two more and burn them. Thereafter, the head monk's eyebrows and beard fell out.
(Dinghai) Grand Master Dayi preached the Dharma at Linqide Palace.
Dayi resided at Mount Ehu in Xinzhou. He once offered this admonition: "Do not merely forget the body and extinguish the mind;

this is a most difficult-to-cure illness and the deepest [of afflictions]. He further said: "You must directly raise the sharp blade of a razor to slice through the meaning of the Westward Transmission."
One meaning. He also said: "With eyes wide open and eyebrows raised, look back and forth at him—who is he? He also said:
"If a person sits in stillness without applying effort, in what year will they pass the imperial examination and realize the emptiness of the mind?

In the second year of the Yuanhe era, Emperor Xianzong issued an edict to welcome him to the Linqide Hall to debate the Dharma. A Dharma Master asked, "What are the Four Noble Truths? Baizhang replied, "The Sovereign."

[The Emperor] said, "One Emperors? Where are the three Emperors? He asked again, "In the desire realm there is no dhyāna; dhyāna dwells in the form realm. Upon what does this land rely to establish dhyāna?
[The Master] replied, "The Dharma Master only knows that there is no dhyāna in the desire realm; he does not know that there is no desire in the realm of dhyāna. [The Emperor] asked, "What is dhyāna?
Master Yi pointed to the empty space with his hand. The Dharma Master had no reply. The Emperor said, "The Dharma Master lectures on the *Anantaparyāya Sūtra*."
The Master said, "As for this very point, one is still unable to cope with it. Yiyu then asked, "In walking, standing, sitting, and reclining, what ultimately constitutes the Way?
One replied, "To know is the Way. Yiyu said, "It cannot be known by wisdom, nor can it be cognized by consciousness.
How, then, can 'knowing' be the Way? Another replied, "Non-discrimination is the Way. Yiyu said, "You are quite capable of making such distinctions!"
"The characteristics of all phenomena do not move within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*). How could there be non-discrimination as the Way?
To say that the four dhyānas and eight samādhis are the Way—Master Yi said: 'The Buddha-body is unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) and does not fall into any numerical categories;

how could it reside within the four dhyānas and eight samādhis? Everyone remained speechless. Master Yi then turned back to ask Chan Master Śrī of Emperor Shunzong: 'The great earth and all sentient beings...'"

The Emperor asked, "How can one, while still alive, attain the realization of one's nature and become a Buddha? Śrī said, "Buddha-nature is like the moon in the water; it can be seen but cannot be grasped.
Yìyīn then said to the Emperor, "Buddha-nature is not something that is seen through the act of seeing. How could one grasp the moon in the water?
The Emperor then asked, "What is this Buddha-nature? Yìyīn replied, "It is not separate from what Your Majesty is currently asking."
○ Chan Master Daowu of Tiantai Temple Enters Nirvana (Dharma Heir of Shitou Xiqian):

Daowu lived in seclusion on Mount Ziling in Dangyang. Later, at Tiantai Temple to the east of the city of Jingzhou, which had been destroyed by fire, there was a monk named Lingjian who planned to restore it.
He said, "If we can secure the services of Chan Master Daowu as the master of the restoration project, it will surely succeed."

[The Master] was able to bestow blessings upon him. At that time, the Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Lord Pei, Governor of Jiangling, bowed his head and inquired about the Dharma;

he paid his respects and escorted [the Master] back to his quarters. Huiguang did not go out to welcome or see him off. Regardless of whether a guest was noble or humble, he would always have them sit and then bow to them.

Lord Pei consequently showed even greater reverence. In the fourth month of the second year of the Yuanhe era, Huiguang suffered from back pain. When the great assembly came to inquire after his illness, Huiguang abruptly summoned the steward to come forward and questioned him.
[The master] asked, "Do you understand? [The disciple] replied, "I do not. Wuzhu took up his pillow, threw it to the ground, and immediately entered nirvana.
His Dharma heirs were three generations: Hui-zhen, You-xian, and Wen-ben. Fu Zai, the Assistant Director of Music, composed the stele inscription.
(Wenzi) Chan Master Huairan Resided at Zhangjing Temple (a Dharma heir of Mazu).
Huairan was the son of the Xie family of Tong’an. He first resided at Boyuan in Dingzhou, and subsequently stayed at Mount Zhongtiao.

In the third year of the Yuanhe era, he was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Zhangjing Temple in Jingzhao. Students flocked to him. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The ultimate principle transcends words."

People of that time did not understand this; they strenuously practiced other matters, taking them to be functional achievements, yet they did not know their own nature—which is fundamentally not an object of the sensory realms—and that it is a subtle and wondrous gate of great liberation. All its discerning awareness is neither defiled nor obstructed; such is its radiance.
It has never ceased or been abandoned; from past kalpas until the present, it remains eternally unchanging. It is like the solar disc, which illuminates both near and far;
though it reaches all forms, it does not become fused with them. This spiritual lamp of wondrous clarity is not produced through artificial refinement.

Because of a lack of understanding, one grasps at objective phenomena, merely like one who presses upon the eye and falsely perceives floating flowers in the sky—exhausting oneself in vain and wandering through delusion.
Regarding the number of kalpas: if one can reflect back upon oneself, there is no second person; in every movement and action, the true mark (dharmatā) is not impaired.
When Chan Master Lingyou first established the Dharma at Mt.
Gui, the itinerant ascetic Sima went to Baizhang and said to Huaihai: "Recently, while in Hunan, I found a mountain."
It was named Daomiao. This mountain was extraordinary and sublime; it was fitting to assemble a community of Dharma companions there to establish a great site for the Way (*mahā-maṇḍala*).
At that time, Lingyou served as the steward (*karmadāna*). When Huaihai saw him, he immediately said, "This is precisely the future master of Mount Miao.

That night, Hai summoned You and instructed him, saying: "My karmic conditions for transformation lie here. Mount Miao is a magnificent realm; you should reside there, succeed to my lineage, and extensively deliver future students."
The Head Seat, Shenjue, said, "I am humbled to occupy the position of the foremost disciple; why should you, the steward, take charge of the monastery?
Baizhang replied, "If you can utter a single phrase that transcends the ordinary before the assembly, I shall grant you the abbacy. He then pointed to a pure water jar and asked:
"You must not call it a 'pure flask' (淨瓶). What would you call it? Jue said, "It cannot be called a wooden peg (木撅). Hai did not approve. He then asked Yu.
Yu kicked over the pure flask and left immediately. Hai laughed and said, "The first seat has lost to this mountain-dweller.
He then sent Yu to Mount Miao, a place so steep and precipitous that it was utterly devoid of human habitation. Five... [days passed].
After seven years, he suddenly thought to himself: "The Way lies in engaging with others to benefit living beings; dwelling alone is not right.
He then proceeded toward a mountain pass and saw tigers, leopards, jackals, and wolves crossing his path. Dàoyù said, "You need not block my way."
"If I have a karmic connection with this mountain, you may all disperse; if I have no such connection, I shall fill your bellies.
Having spoken these words, the insects and tigers dispersed in all directions. Danyou returned to his hut.

Before a full year had passed, Lan’an arrived from the place of Bai Zhang accompanied by several monks, saying, "I, An, shall serve as the steward for the Master. Once the assembly reaches five hundred, I shall resign my duties."
Thereupon, the monks gathered around him, and he ascended the hall. "The mind of a man of the Way is simple and straightforward, free from artifice.
It has no back and no face; it is free from deceitful or false thoughts. At all times, seeing and hearing are ordinary, with no further complications. Nor does one close the eyes or block the ears;
it is simply enough that the emotions do not attach themselves to external objects. The sages of old spoke only of the faults and afflictions on the side of turbidity."

If one is free from such numerous evil thoughts, emotional attachments, views, perceptions, and habitual tendencies, then—like the autumn waters, still, pure, unconditioned, limpid, and unhindered—one may be called a man of the Way, and also a man of no affairs.
A monk asked, "Does a person who has attained sudden enlightenment still have further cultivation? Dazhu said, "If one truly awakens to the source, he will know for himself when to cultivate. And:

"Not practicing" is a dualistic statement. Although one's initial resolve may, through conditions, achieve sudden enlightenment into the fundamental principle in a single thought-moment, there still remain the habitual tendencies accumulated over beginningless kalpas that have not yet been suddenly purified. One must teach them to purify and eliminate the flowing consciousnesses of present karma;

this is what "practice" means. It is not said that there is some other separate dharma, but rather that one teaches them to cultivate practice and advance toward the goal, entering the principle through hearing.

When one hears that the principle is profound and subtle, the mind becomes naturally round and luminous, no longer dwelling in the realm of delusion. Even if there are hundreds or thousands of wondrous meanings, they are all subsumed within the moment of their articulation;
this is truly like sitting down and donning one's robes, finally attaining the means to support oneself through one’s own understanding.

To state the essentials: in the ground of ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), not a single speck of dust is admitted; yet within the gateway of the myriad practices, not a single dharma is abandoned. If one proceeds with a single blade directly—
Upon entering, the sentiments of both ordinary beings and sages are exhausted; the body reveals true permanence. When principle and phenomena are non-dual, one is the Buddha of Suchness.
Dharma Master Lingyou transmitted the Dharma to Huize.
When Huize arrived at Mount Gui and visited Master Lingyou, Lingyou asked him, "Are you a novice with a master, or a novice without a master?"
Ji said, "There is a master. Yuo asked, "Where is the master? Ji walked from west to east and stood there. Yuo marveled at this.
Ji asked, "What is the dwelling place of the True Buddha? Yuo replied, "By means of the wondrous state where thought is without thought, reflect upon the infinite brilliance of spiritual awareness.
When thought is exhausted, one returns to the source; nature and characteristics abide eternally. Phenomena and principle are non-dual; the True Buddha is suchness."

They are: observation (*vipaśyanā*), awakening (*bodhi*), concentration (*samādhi*), wisdom (*prajñā*), clarity (*vidyā*), penetration (*abhijñā*), salvation (*tāraṇa*), and relinquishment (*tyāga*). Easier said than done remarked: "How sublime are these eight words!
They are truly the gradual gateway to the realization of the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).

Therefore, from observation to relinquishment, they are praised in successive order; this is called the 'Verses on the Eight Gradual Stages. (1. Observation: With the eye of the mind, one observes the external forms of the mind. From what do they arise?"
How does one lose [the mind]? By observing and further observing, one distinguishes the true from the false (the two types of awakening).

Only the true is eternally present, yet it is obscured by the false. If the true and the false are distinguished, awakening arises within them. Without departing from the false, one attains true emptiness (the third stage:

concentration). If the true does not perish, the false will not arise. The source of the six sense organs becomes as still as a pond of clear water; this is called meditative concentration (*dhyāna-samādhi*). Thus, one is liberated from birth.
Death. (4. Wisdom) To concentrate with meditative absorption (*samādhi*). Even in absorption there is still attachment; one must deliver it with wisdom (*prajñā*).

With wisdom, there is no obstruction. It is like a pearl on a platter: the platter is absorption and the pearl is wisdom. (5. Clarity) When absorption and wisdom are united, they become clear through that union.

They illuminate all things, and no object can hide its form. It is like a great round mirror: responsive yet without sentience. (6. Penetration) Only when wisdom reaches its ultimate does it become truly clear; being clear, it is never obscured.

He was a native of the Lu clan from Puba. His cranial bone was rounded and prominent, and his voice was like a bell. In his youth, he encountered the mourning for his mother;

In Daci Mountain of this province, there was a chronic lack of water. While he was contemplating moving elsewhere, he dreamed one night that a divine being stopped him.

At dawn the next day, he saw two tigers scratching the ground with their claws, and a spring gushed forth spontaneously. A monk arriving from Mount Yue said, "The Tongzi Spring has run dry; it has been moved here.

(Guiyou) Chan Master Lingyou of Mt. Gui passed away (the first patriarch of the Guiyang school, Dharma heir of Baizhang Hai).
Lingyou resided at Mt. Gui and propagated the teachings and discipline for over forty years; those who attained realization were beyond counting.

He had forty-one入室 (入室弟子) disciples. On a day in the first month of the seventh year of the Dazhong era, having washed his hands and rinsed his mouth and arranged his seat, he passed away in serene composure.

Furthermore, it is said: "At present, you must first recognize the four kinds of signless conditions (*animitta-viṣaya*), so as to avoid being tossed about and struck down by external circumstances.

A single thought of anger is burned by fire; a single thought of doubt is obstructed by earth; a single thought of joy is blown away by wind.
If one can discern in this way, one will not be turned by external conditions, but will employ them wherever they arise:

[Zhaozhou] attained a state of peace and happiness. Jishi raised his whisk and asked, "As for this very thing, how does one enter?

The monk presented this ○-sign by tracing it with his hand. Huizhi brushed it away with his sleeve. The monk again presented this ○-sign by tracing it with his hand.

After the monk had finished his greetings, he stood with his hands joined in *añjali* facing the eastern side and stared at Ji. Ji then lowered his left foot.
The monk moved over to the western side and stood with his hands joined; Ji lowered his right foot. When the monk stood with his hands joined in the middle, Ji withdrew both feet.
The monk prostrated. Zhaozhi said, "Old man," and remained seated. [Zhaozhi thought,] "I have never yet struck a single person.
He took up his staff and struck him; the monk then soared into the air and departed. On another occasion, while Zhaozhi was sitting, a monk came to pay his respects.

Zhaozhi did not look at him. The monk then asked Zhaozhi, "Do you know how to read characters? Zhaozhi replied, "I do to some extent. The monk then circled him once clockwise and asked, "What character is this?"
Ji drew a "cross" (卐) on the ground to answer him. The monk circled to the left once more and asked, "What character is this?
Ji changed the cross into a "swastika" (卍). The monk drew this circle (○) and, with both hands pressed against it, assumed the posture of an asura grasping the sun and moon;
he asked, "What character is this? Ji then drew this [a swastika inside a circle] facing it. The monk then made the gesture of *lū*.
When he reached Zhide Temple, Huiji said, "So it is, so it is. This is that which all Buddhas protect and keep in mind.

Polishing the Tranquil Mind. One should know that the matters within this gate are no ordinary affair. Thus it is said: "The wise do not seek within words;

A monk asked, "Do you not wish to become an old monk? Huineng revealed his intention. The next day, he ascended the hall; indeed, it was not like his usual manner.
Huineng clapped his hands and laughed loudly, saying, "I am glad that the old man at the head of the hall has understood the final word.
Hereafter, no one in the world will be able to do anything with him. Nevertheless, he shall live for only three years."

This is the Capable One. The ancients said: "If one places poison in milk, it can kill even when it has become clarified butter (*sarpis*).

(Biyou) Chan Master Zhiguang resided at Mount Jiuzuo. He lived in seclusion among the crags and valleys.

Suddenly, he encountered a giant python that intended to swallow him; Zhiguang’s staff flew forward first, propping open the serpent’s mouth, as he sat cross-legged and entered [samādhi].
While he was in meditative absorption (*samādhi*), a deity came to offer an apology, but Guang paid it no heed. When he emerged from his trance, the python had transformed into stone.

Huizhong, a son of the Liu family from Yangzhou, resided at Guiyang for twenty years without leaving the mountains. In the sixth year of the Xiantong era, one day he said:

The disciple said, "If sentient beings cannot attain liberation, it is because of the entanglements of their emotions. It is easy to awaken to the Way, but difficult to clarify the Way. I ask: how can one come to clarify the Way?
Zhong replied, "Simply shed your emotional attachments and biased views, and the Way will clarify itself of its own accord. Now, as for the word 'clarify' (ming), it means 'to trust.
It is like a snake-handler who trusts in the power of his incantations and the efficacy of his medicines; he thus coils and handles the snake, holding it within his breast."

There is no difficulty within one’s sleeves. Those who do not yet know the power of mantras and medicinal herbs will be struck with terror and flee; they must simply observe their own mind with clarity, for when emotional perceptions are thus seen through, they are immediately shattered.
As for those who now harbor thousands of doubts and myriad anxieties and find themselves unable to apply this method, it is because they have not yet seen their own minds.
Suddenly, he requested incense; having finished burning it, he sat upright and passed away. His posthumous title was Guiji (Return to Stillness).

Entering into principle. As for "simultaneously encompassing," it means responding in secret harmony with all conditions, yet not falling into any state of existence;

it is neither defiled nor pure, neither correct nor partial. Therefore it is said: "The vast and profound Great Way, the unattached True Teaching. The former masters of antiquity have deduced that this single station is the most wondrous and the most profound.

One must examine and discern it with care: the sovereign represents the position of correctness, while the minister represents the position of partiality. For the minister to turn toward the sovereign is...

"Correctness within partiality. When the ruler looks upon the minister, this is "partiality within correctness. The convergence of the Way between ruler and minister is spoken of as "wearing both together.
Question: "What is the Ruler? Answer: "Sublime Virtue honors the universe; lofty brilliance illuminates the great void. Question: "What is the Minister? Answer:
"The spiritual mechanism expands the sage-way; true knowledge benefits all living beings. Question: "What is the minister turning toward the ruler? Answer: "Not falling [into partiality]."
Those from various realms fix their attention and gaze upon the Sage’s countenance. [The Master] asks: "What is 'the ruler looking at the minister'? He replies:

"Though the wondrous countenance does not move, its light illuminates all without partiality. He asks: "What is 'the way of ruler and minister in perfect union'? He replies: "It is a state of total integration, without interior or exterior."
Harmonizing those above and below brings about equilibrium. It is also said: "Speaking in terms of ruler and subject, or partiality and rectitude, is intended to avoid offending the central truth;
thus, when a subject addresses a ruler, they do not dare to speak directly. This is the essential core of our Dharma. Thereupon, he composed a verse:

"A student must first recognize their own fundamental source; Do not confuse the ultimate reality with inert emptiness. The wondrously luminous essence is entirely sensitive to being offended; [Exert] strength..."

In the Xiantong era, Xuanzang returned to Min, ascended Mount Xianggu, and founded a monastery at Xuefeng, where a multitude of eminent disciples gathered.
A monk asked, "What did you gain from seeing Master Deshan that you simply left? He replied, "I went empty-handed and returned empty-handed.
He ascended the hall and said, "Venerable monks, I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion; I have already met you on Mount Wushi;
I have already met you before the Sangha Hall. He further said, "The entire great earth can be grasped..."
"Come! Like a grain of millet, I shall toss it before this lacquer bucket. "I do not understand. "Beat the drum;
let everyone come to see! (Gengyin). Chan Master Shanhui of Jiaoshan:
Shanhui was the son of the Liao family in Guangzhou. After receiving the Dharma from Chuanzi, he withdrew from the world to live in seclusion. Students gathered around him like scales of fish.
In the eleventh year of the Xiántóng era, Kāishan opened his assembly and ascended the hall.

"Since the time of the Patriarchs, people have misunderstood [the teachings] and passed this down to the present day, taking the words and phrases of the Buddhas and Patriarchs as models for teachers of men. If one acts in such a manner, it instead makes one a madman or a person devoid of wisdom.
He merely pointed out to you that the absence of dharmas is itself the Way; the Way has not a single dharma, nor does it have a Buddha."
It can be accomplished. There is no Way to be attained; there is no dharma to be grasped, and no dharma to be abandoned. Therefore, the Old Monk says:

"Before one's eyes there is no dharma, yet the meaning lies before one's eyes. This is not a dharma of the present moment. If you seek to learn from the Buddhas and patriarchs, such a person has not yet possessed the eye. Why?
Because all such things belong to that which is relied upon, and thus one does not attain autonomy. Fundamentally, this is solely for the sake of birth and death.
Vast and boundless is the nature of consciousness; it possesses no autonomy. To seek a spiritual friend across thousands of miles, one must possess the correct eye.
One must seek liberation from erroneous views and definitively examine the birth and death before one’s eyes: do they truly exist, or do they truly not exist?

If there is someone who has definitely attained the capacity of the highest faculty (agradharmika) as permitted by you—one who can clarify the Way upon hearing a single word—then why do those of middling and lower faculties, who are tossed about like waves, not decisively take hold within the midst of birth and death? Where else could they harbor doubts regarding the Buddhas and Patriarchs?
"To substitute for you in birth and death—wise people laugh at you. If you do not understand, listen to another verse:
'Toiling to uphold the laws of birth and death, you seek only from the Buddha's side; lost to the correct principle before your eyes, you strike fire to search for bubbles.

A monk asked, "Regarding the meaning of establishing the Patriarchs from of old, why did the Master say there is no such thing? He replied, "Three years without eating a meal. "Even if one has eyes..."

"There is no hungry person here. The monk asked, "Since there is no hungry person, why is it that I, so-and-so, do not awaken? Dongshan said, "Precisely because awakening has caused you, Venerable, to be deluded.
He then showed him a verse: "Clearly, there is no dharma of awakening; The dharma of awakening, instead, deludes people.
Stretch out both legs and sleep; There is neither falsehood nor truth. A monk asked, "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha? Dongshan said, "Directly..."
One must brandish the sword. If one does not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in his hut.
(Renchen) Chan Master Huiran of Sansheng was a direct successor of Linji.
Later, he took his leave to travel extensively; wherever he went among the monasteries, he was treated as a distinguished guest.
He first visited Xuefeng and later arrived at Yangshan. Yangshan asked, "What is your name? He replied, "Huiji. Yangshan said, "Huiji is my name.
[The monk] said, "My name is Huiran. Yangshan laughed heartily. One day, an official came to visit Yangshan. Yangshan asked, "What office do you hold?
He replied, "I am a *tui-guan* (Investigating Official). Yangshan held up his whisk and said, "Can you investigate this?"
"What about this? The official had no reply. The Mountain (Zhaozhou) ordered the assembly to offer their responses, but none were in accord. At that time, Yanran was ill in the Longevity Hall;
the Mountain sent an attendant to invite him to offer a response, saying, "The Master has a question for you today. [Yanran asked: "I do not know what the matter is.
[The Mountain said: "A second offense will not be tolerated. The Mountain deeply approved of this. One day, as Yanran was departing, the Mountain took up his staff.
Furong gave him the whisk. Furong said, "I already have a teacher. When I arrived at Deshan, as soon as I spread out my sitting cloth, Deshan said, 'Do not spread out your cooking cloth;
there is no leftover gruel or stale rice here. I replied, 'Even if there were, there would be nowhere to put it.
Deshan then struck me. I caught the staff and pushed it onto the meditation seat. Deshan laughed loudly. I wailed to the blue heavens and then departed to seek instruction."
In the hall, the head seat, named Tietian Tai, asked a traveling monk, "A seeker on pilgrimage must possess an official pass from his own province.
What is this 'official pass from one's own province'? The monk said, "What are you saying? Tai asked again. The monk then struck out with his sitting cloth, saying, "This lacquer bucket!
How many worthy and virtuous men have you offended before and after! Tai prepared to offer his greetings, but the monk had already passed him by.

Regarding the affairs of the two abbots: later, when San-sheng was residing there, he ascended the hall and said, "Whenever I meet a person, I come forward; once I have come forward, I do not act for the sake of others. He then descended from the seat.
When Cunen Wen heard this, he said, "Whenever I meet a person, I do not come forward; once I have come forward, I act for the sake of others."
The Biography of Chan Master Yicun Wenyan:
Wenyan was the son of the Zhang family of Jiaxing. Possessing innate wisdom from birth, he shaved his head and received full ordination. He attended upon his original teacher for several years.
Having thoroughly investigated the Vinaya-piṭaka, [Daowu] found that his own fundamental matter remained unclarified. He went to visit Daoming; as soon as Daoming saw him coming, he closed the door.
Daowu knocked on the door, and Daoming asked, "Who is it? He replied, "I am so-and-so. Daoming asked, "What are you doing here? He replied, "My own fundamental matter remains unclarified."
Yanyang requested the Master’s instruction. Ming opened the door; as soon as Yanyang saw it, he closed it.
This continued for three days in succession. On the third day, Yanyang knocked on the door. When the door was opened, Yanyang pushed his way inside.
Ming immediately seized him and said, "Speak! Speak! Startled, Yanyang had no time to answer. Ming then pushed him out and shut the door, injuring Yanyang’s right foot. Yanyang departed.
Regarding this realization: Ming then pointed toward Xuefeng. Upon arriving at the monastery, he saw a monk ask the *zhangzuo* (senior monk), "Are you going up the mountain today?
He replied, "Yes. The monk said, "I have a kōan (a causal condition) to entrust to you. Ask the Abbot about it, but you must not say these are the words of another.
When the *zhangzuo* reached the mountain and saw the Abbot ascending the hall for the assembly, as soon as the crowd had gathered, he stepped forward and grasped [the Abbot's robe].
Wanlidi said, "This old man has an iron cangue around his neck; why does he not take it off? The monk followed these instructions exactly.
Seeing the monk speak in this manner, Feng descended from his seat, grabbed him by the chest, and said, "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk had no reply.
Feng pushed him away and said, "That was not your words. The monk said, "It was my words. Feng said, "Attendant, bring the rope and the staff!"
Yangshan said, "I have come from the estate; my senior monk (zasuo) instructed me to come and tell you this:
'The assembly is going to the estate to welcome five hundred virtuous friends (śāstṛs). On the following day, Yangshan ascended the mountain. As soon as Feng saw him, he said:"
"How did you manage to reach such a state? Yan then prostrated himself. Having refined his practice through many years of diligent study, he was subsequently entrusted with the seal of the lineage.
(Jia-wu) Chan Master Cunjiang began teaching at Xinghua.
Initially, while serving as an attendant under Linji, Yuan'an came to visit Yixuan. Yixuan asked him, "Where have you come from?"
[The Master] said, "He has come from Luancheng. [The monk] asked, "May I ask you something? [The Master] said, "A newly ordained monk does not understand.

[The Master] continued, "Even if one were to shatter the Great Tang Empire, there would be no one to be found who does not understand. Go to the meditation hall. Dajian subsequently followed him and asked for instruction.
"Is this newcomer who just arrived here being 'stripped' (of his status), or not? [The Master] said: "Who am I to concern myself with whether he is stripped or not? [The Monk] said:
"The Master only knows how to pounce on a dead sparrow on the ground; you do not know how to cover it over with a turning phrase.
[The Master] said: "And what would you do? [The Monk] said: "I ask the Master to act as the newcomer. Xuán then said: "Novice Precept-holder."
"No. [Xuan] said, "Rather, it is my own fault. [The guest] said, "Your words conceal the sharp point; you are merely praising conjecture. Xuan then struck him. That evening, Xuan spoke again:
"Today when I questioned the newly arrived one, I was 'popping a dying sparrow on the ground' or 'beating it right in its nest.
But as soon as you produced a word, I shouted and raised it up to 'beat it among the blue clouds. [The guest] said, "Grass."
The bandits were utterly defeated. Xuán then struck him. Later, while serving as the head seat (shouzuo) in the assembly of Sansheng, he would often say:
"When I traveled on pilgrimage to the south, I encountered many who wielded the staff, yet I never once encountered a single person who truly understood the Buddha-dharma.
Huìrán said, "What kind of eye do you possess to speak in such a manner? Xuán gave a shout. Huìrán said, "It must be you who possesses it!"
He attained [realization]. Later, when Dajue heard this mention, he said, "How could it be that the wind blew you all the way into my gate?
Afterward, Xiang went to Dajue and served as the head of the monastery (*yuanzhu*).
One day, Dajue called out to him, "I have heard you say that during your travels in the south, you never once encountered a single person who had truly grasped the Buddha-dharma."
"By what principle do you speak in such a manner? Yang gave a shout; Jue struck him. Yang shouted again; Jue struck him again.

Yang shouted once more; Jue struck him yet again. Yang said, "I learned a 'phrase of guest and host' from my senior brother Sansheng, but I have been completely defeated by you, Senior Brother. I pray that you will grant me a Dharma-gate of peace and bliss."
He said, "This blind fellow has come here to meet with defeat. He stripped off his patched robe and gave him a severe beating.
He was enlightened beneath the words; he realized the principle of how his former master had received blows at Huangbo. While serving as abbot at Xinghua, he offered incense [in remembrance].
This single stick of incense was originally intended for my elder brother Sansheng; yet Sansheng was too distant for me.
It was originally intended for my elder brother Daqiao; yet Daqiao was too remote for me. It is better that I offer it to our late master Linji. He addressed the assembly:
"I have heard that they shout in the front corridor and they shout in the rear quarters. My sons, do not shout blindly or recklessly. Even if you were to..."
He drank himself into a stupor and fell headlong from the void; he had not a single breath left.
When he regained his composure and rose, he said to you, "It is not yet. Why? Because I have never yet scattered true pearls within the purple silk curtain.
"Xing, you all go away! Why do you shout and clamor so disorderly? One day he said to the rector Kebin, "Before long, you will become a master who leads the assembly.
Kebin replied, "I will not enter this protective community. The Master asked, "Do you enter it because you have understood, or do you enter it because you have not understood?
Kebin said, "In neither way. The Master struck him and said, "Rector Kebin, in the battle of Dharma, you have been defeated!"
"Defeated! A fine of five *guan* and one full meal of steamed rice! On the following day, Xiang himself struck the wooden gavel and said, "The rector Kebin has lost the battle of the Dharma;
he shall not eat his meal and must depart the monastery immediately. A monk asked, "What is it like when they come from the four quarters?
Xiang said, "Strike the one in the center. The monk bowed, and Xiang said, "Yesterday I attended a village vegetarian feast."
On the way, he encountered a sudden storm of wind and rain. He took refuge inside an ancient temple and managed to get through it safely.
(Yiwu) Benkong went to visit Chan Master Danying.
When Benkong first traveled to Tiantai, he used to say: "If there is someone who can seize my vital pivot (*jī*), they shall be my teacher."
He soon arrived in Jiangxi and went to visit Dao-yeng. After performing his salutations, he asked, "When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it?
Yeng said, "Cast off your karmic body and come; then I shall meet with you. [Kong] replied, "The karmic body has already been cast off. Yeng asked, "Where is the pearl? Kong was speechless.
He then surrendered himself in sincerity and entered the inner quarters. At that time, Kong was thirteen years old. [Then] Benji took up residence...
One day, a man known as the Paper-Clothed Wayfarer came to visit Caoshan. Caoshan asked, "Are you not the Paper-Clothed Wayfarer? He replied, "I dare not say so.
Caoshan asked, "What is the reality beneath the paper cloth? He replied, "Once the single robe is hung upon the body, all phenomena are entirely as they are.
Caoshan asked, "What is the function beneath the paper cloth? The Paper-Clothed Wayfarer stepped forward, stood with palms joined, and said, "Yes," and then he immediately took off his clothes.
He departed. Jìxiào said, "You only understand departing in this way; why do you not understand coming in that way?
Zhǐyī suddenly opened his eyes and asked, "When the singular, spiritual true nature does not rely upon the womb, what then? Jìxiào said, "That is not yet marvelous. Zhǐyī asked, "What is marvelous?
Jìxiào said, "Neither borrowed nor not borrowed. Zhǐyī withdrew to sit in the hall and passed away. Jìxiào presented this verse: Awakening...

The nature is perfectly luminous, a body without marks. Do not mistakenly create intimacy or distance through conceptual knowing and seeing. When thoughts differ, one becomes obscured from the profound essence; when the mind deviates, it does not dwell as a neighbor to the Way.
Through emotional attachments, the myriad dharmas sink into the realm before one; through the manifold discriminations of consciousness, the original truth is lost.
If you can fully understand these words, you will clearly see that you are the person of old, free from all concerns.
(Ciśen) Master Shibei of Xiansha opened the Dharma at Xiansha.
He was the son of the Xie family of Min County. His father made his living as a fisherman. Once, while traveling by boat at night, he fell into the water;
Shibei rowed with his oars to rescue him. Seeing the moon reflected in the water, he said, "The predecessors have said that all dharmas are like water."
"Yue, if you had lived with your father and killed him together, it would have only increased your suffering in the three miserable realms.
Now that he cannot be saved, it would be better for you to renounce worldly ties, leave the household life, and repay your father's kindness. Thereupon, Yue cut his hair and received full ordination.

Wearing straw sandals and cloth robes, he took only enough food to sustain his breath, sitting in meditation all day long. He drew near to Yicun, who, because of his ascetic practices, called him "The Head."

Dada once took his bag and set out over the mountain passes, intending to travel everywhere to seek instruction from various masters. Suddenly, upon reaching a steep and perilous place, he stubbed his toes, causing blood to flow and intense pain to arise.
He sighed and said, "This body is not something that truly exists; from where does this pain come? This body is suffering; ultimately, it is unborn.

With these words, "Enough! Enough! he ceased his travels and did not cross the mountain pass. He remained there to rely on Master Cunen for the resolution of the essential point of the mind. One day, Cunen called out to him, saying, "Bei..."
Tou-t’o said, “Why do you not go to study under all the masters? He replied, “Dharma did not come to the Eastern Land; the Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven.

Tou-t’o approved of this and praised him, saying, “Tou-t’o Pei is a man who has returned for a second birth. Later, he suddenly dreamed that his father came to thank him, saying, “Because of your leaving the household life, I have been reborn in heaven;
therefore, I have come to inform you. Tou-t’o ascended Mount Hsiang-ku, and Tou-t’o Pei entered the inner quarters. Furthermore—

Having read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he clarified the ground of the mind. From then on, his responses to those seeking instruction were swift and nimble, and they accorded with the *Sūtras* as if in a hidden resonance.
Whenever scholars from various regions encountered points they could not resolve, they would invariably seek his guidance. One day, Cunen took his leave, saying, "I take my leave of the Master;
everyone is naturally free and at ease. Daguang said, "Master Bei, go down the mountain now. Cunen asked, "Who says such a thing? [Daguang replied: "It is I."
The Preceptor said, "If you speak thus, what do you say? He replied, "I am not free and at ease. The Preceptor said, "I know. Thereupon, he built a hut for himself.

The assembly was all moved to grief. On the *renxu* day of the first month, he asked his attendant, "What date is today? The attendant replied, "The third. He said, "Thirty years."
Later, he simply said, "It is just this," and then sat upright and passed away peacefully. His posthumous title was Hongjue. Daoyuan (Daojian) was a native of Fanyang.
He shaved his head as a youth and received the full precepts (*pūrṇa-saṃvara*). He traveled extensively among monastic assemblies. Later, he visited Daoying;

after conversing with him for three consecutive days, Daoying marveled greatly at him and instructed him to apply himself with diligent austerity while serving the community. Thereupon, Daoyuan personally attended to the well and the mortar, and took charge of gathering firewood.
Cuan oversaw all temple affairs and was not hindered from discussing matters of antiquity and the present; yet none among the assembly knew this.

Praising the Way according to its true nature: Carrying the mendicant’s staff as if walking the roads of one’s native land, there is no place where his voice will not be heard.

The Precious Hall is empty within and devoid of form or appearance; it is neither high nor low, neither obstructed nor hindered. Those who study it find no likeness to its essence;
those who come can hardly capture its model. Only one with wisdom knows how to arrange it; among a thousand, there is not a single craftsman.

Although it is but a single body, it manifests as hundreds of thousands of millions of emanations. It is also said: "A single bowl for the meals of a thousand households; a solitary body wandering ten thousand miles. Green.

Tuo Kai said, "Even so, what can one do about the many monks behind him? Master Bei first resided at Meixi and later at Xuansha;
at once, the assembly from all quarters looked up to him with reverence and submission, and his students numbered a thousand.

He responded to the capacities of others and engaged with sentient beings for nearly thirty years. On the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month in the second year of the Kaiping era of the Liang dynasty, he manifested illness and passed away.
He was seventy-five years of age and forty-four years since his ordination. He was posthumously granted the title Zongyi.
(己巳) Chan Master Jujudun resided at Longya.
Having attained the essential meaning under Dongshan, he served him diligently for eight years. In the third year of the Kaiping era, he emerged into the world at the Fajie Chan Temple in Longya.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Those who investigate the mystery must first penetrate through the Buddhas and patriarchs before they can succeed. As Master Xinfeng said:"
When the teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are like an enemy born to you, only then do you have the capacity for study.
If you cannot penetrate them, you will be deceived by the Buddhas and Patriarchs. A monk asked, "Do the Buddhas and Patriarchs have a mind to deceive people?

He replied, "Tell me, does the river and the lake have a mind to obstruct people? Although the river and the lake have no mind to obstruct people, they are nonetheless obstructed by those who cross them.
It cannot be said that the rivers and lakes obstruct people; yet it cannot be said that the rivers and lakes do not obstruct people.
Although the Buddhas and Patriarchs have no intention to deceive, because people of this age cannot penetrate through them, the Buddhas and Patriarchs end up appearing to deceive them;
yet it cannot be said that the Buddhas and Patriarchs do not deceive people. If one can penetrate beyond the Buddhas and Patriarchs, such a person has surpassed the Buddhas and Patriarchs. And if...
It is thus. Only when you first realize the essence and grasp the meaning of the Buddhas and Patriarchs will you be equal to those who transcend the ordinary.

If you have not yet penetrated this, merely studying the Buddhas and Patriarchs will leave you without a time of liberation for ten thousand kalpas. [The student] asked: "How can one avoid being deceived by the Buddhas and Patriarchs?"
It is said: "As for the Way, one must awaken to it within oneself before it can be attained.
Chan Master Huileng resided at Changqing.
Later, he resided at Zhaoqing. In the third year of the Kaiping era, the King of Min, Wang Shenzhi, moved him to reside at Changqing in Fuzhou.
Master Shen knew that Lady Cui had claimed to be a *lianshi* (Daoist master). She sent a messenger with clothing and goods, saying, "The *lianshi* requests a reply from the Great Master.
[Master Shen] said, "Deliver this message to the *lianshi*: 'Please come and receive the reply yourself. A short while later, the messenger returned.

"How so? Ling remained silent for a long while. The King said, "The Great Master’s Buddha-dharma is inconceivable. Ascending the hall, he said:
"If one meets a fellow traveler on the Way and passes by with shoulders touching, the task of a lifetime of study is finished. Ascending the hall, he said:

Regarding the "Exhaustion of Dharmas" (Jinfa): Leng said, "Does it still fall back into the place of entrustment? Huiqiu was a native of Putian.

He was foremost among those who questioned and investigated within the quarters of Xuansha. He once asked, "What is the primary moon? Xuansha replied, "What would you do with that moon of yours? From this, Huiqiu attained awakening.
When Xuansha was about to pass away, the regional governor of Min, Duke Wang, sent his son to inquire after his illness and requested his final secret instructions.

When asked who would be the one to follow in his footsteps and preach the Dharma, the Master said, "Qiuzi has attained it. The King silently took note of this final instruction and then asked, "As for the Dharma seat at Drums Mountain (Gushan), who is fit to hold it?
The Master named twelve men of long-standing virtue and perfected insight from the city who were all capable of appearing in the world as teachers.
The King likewise remained silent. On the day of the formal opening of the hall, the officials and the monastic assembly gathered.
They all assembled at the Dharma assembly. The King suddenly asked the multitude, "Who is the Venerable Qiu?

Thereupon, the people pointed him out, and the King immediately invited Qiu to reside at the An-guo Chan Monastery (also known as Zhongta). Ascending the hall, [Qiu said: "This matter of porridge and rice here in my place..."

To raise the chant for you, brothers, would ultimately be impermanent. If you wish to attain what is essential and concise, I shall instead reveal it to you through the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.

Since that Way is eternal, it can also lead to ultimate realization. If you enter through the gate of Mañjuśrī, all things—unconditioned phenomena, soil, wood, tiles, and stones—will assist you in triggering the awakening of the faculty. If you enter through the gate of Avalokiteśvara, all sounds...
The echoes, the frogs, and the earthworms assist you in triggering the pivot. If you enter through the gate of Samantabhadra, you will arrive without taking a single step.
I have shown you these three gates as skillful means, like using a single broken chopstick to stir the waters of the great ocean, so that the fish and dragons may know that water is their very life.
Do you understand? If you lack the eye of wisdom to examine this with discernment, let it be as it is for them—hundreds [of times].

Yunqian was exceptionally skillful. He did not seek ultimate [enlightenment] from his former master, but went to visit Liangjie. Liangjie asked, "Where have you recently departed from? Yunqian replied, "Wulin.
Liangjie asked, "How does the Dharma-way of Wulin compare to this place? Yunqian said, "In a foreign land, bamboo shoots sprout in winter.
Liangjie said, "Cook fragrant rice in a separate steamer to offer to such a person as you. Yunqian brushed out his sleeves and departed. Liangjie said, "This fellow will run off in the future."
While Shashan Tianxia was once planting pine trees, Liu Chen’ung came to him and requested a verse. Shashan composed a verse, saying:

When Master Liu received the verse and presented it to Jia, Jia said, “Congratulations on your joy; this is the third generation.”

Dongshan was the master who resided at Qinglin and later moved to Dongshan. Whenever a newcomer arrived, he would first have them carry firewood three times before being permitted to enter the hall for formal study.
Kuangren was a native of Xingan. After leaving the household life, he went to the Eastern Capital (Luoyang) to study under masters. Before long, he suddenly said:

Ren stepped forward and asked, "What is the phrase that does not fall into sound and form?

[The master] burned [the incense]. Being near water but having no water to drink, you, Master, went to Dongshan and encountered Lingjia early in the morning.
You went out and asked: "Regarding the words 'there has not yet been,' I request the Master’s instruction. He replied: "If one does not grant assent, there is no one who will agree.

He summoned his attendant and said, "Take two hundred coins and give them to this elder. He then instructed him, saying, "In the future, there will be 'One-Eyed Dragon' (Deyan);
he will be the one who pierces through your delusions for you. Later, hearing that Deqian—who was missing one eye—had appeared in the world, he went directly to pay his respects.
Deqian asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Min Province. Deqian asked, "Have you ever been to Daopei? He replied, "I have. Deqian said, "There..."
“What phrase? Ren repeated the previous dialogue. Xuefeng Qian said, “Tongshan may truly be said to have his head straight and his tail straight;
it is simply that he did not meet a true connoisseur. Ren asked again, “If suddenly the tree falls and the vines wither, where does the phrase return?
Qian said, “It would cause Tongshan’s laughter to become even fresher. At these words, Ren attained great enlightenment and said, “Tongshan originally had a smile within his laugh.”
[He saw] Dao. From afar he gazed upon him, prostrated, and repented his transgressions. Upon arriving at Xiangyan, Yan remarked, "In the future, you will spend thirty years vomiting upside down.
While residing at Shushan, he indeed suffered from illness and vomiting for twenty-seven years before recovering. After every meal, he would pry open his mouth and say:
"Thirty years of pouring out my guts—there are still three years remaining.
(Xinwei year) Chan Master Zhìhuī resided at Chóngyún Monastery.
He was the son of Gāo of Xiánqín. Having shaved his head and received full ordination, he attained the Dharma from Běn'rén, serving him as a disciple for ten years before returning.
In Luoyang, he thatched a hut at Zhongtan and named it the Wenshi (Warm Room) Hermitage. He spent his days performing acts of charity, such as distributing water and providing medicine;
no one could fathom the depth of his realization. There was a bhikṣu suffering from leprosy who asked Huī to wash and massage him. Huī did so without any expression of difficulty.

Suddenly, there was divine light and extraordinary fragrance, and the bhikṣu vanished without a trace. In the fifth year of the Kaiping era, he returned to Guifeng and entered deep into the rocky cliffs. Looking back, he saw...
A worn *kaṣāya*, a rosary, a bronze water-pitcher, and a palm-leaf hat were hidden within a stone wall; upon being touched, they immediately crumbled.
He closed his eyes for a long while and said, "These were the ritual implements from my previous life. Consequently, he established a temple there.

Just as he began clearing the weeds, auspicious clouds emerged from between the peaks, and thus the place was named Chongyun (Clouds Upon Clouds). Tigers and leopards retreated, and furthermore, they blocked a dragon pool, causing the dragon to move elsewhere.
(壬申) Chan Master Runu resided at Daochang.
He was a native of Huzhou and received the Dharma from Wuxue. In the second month of the second year of the Qianhua era, he cleared the weeds and established a hermitage on Mount Daochang.
Riding a tiger, he traveled about, and disciples arrived from the four quarters; thus, it became a Zen monastery.
(Jiaxu) Chan Master Datong of Touzi Mountain entered nirvana. (A Dharma heir of Cuiwei Xuefa.
Datong resided at Touzi, where students gathered like clouds. On the sixth day of the fourth month in the fourth year of the Qianhua era, he manifested slight illness.
The assembly requested a physician, but he said to them all: "The movement of the four elements is a constant process of aggregation and dispersion; you need not worry, for I shall protect myself.
Having spoken these words, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away peacefully at the age of ninety-six. He was posthumously honored with the title Ciji (Compassionate Benefactor).
(Year of Yi Hai) Chan Master Shenyuan resided at Gushan.
He was the son of Li of the Great Liang dynasty. From childhood, he loathed the smell of meat and fat, and delighted in hearing the sound of bells and sutras.
At the age of twelve, several streaks of white vapor rose from the walls of the room where he lived. Shenyuan inscribed upon the wall: "O white path, change quickly from this point on."

"Zhang! Cease coming to manifest such demonic portents. You must surely eliminate your heterodox practices and return to the true vision; only then will you attain the realm of those who transcend the mundane and enter the sacred.
Having finished speaking, his breath ceased. At the age of sixteen, he dreamed that a monk from the Brahma world told him, "The time for you to leave the household life has arrived."

He then underwent the ritual of shaving his hair and receiving full ordination (*upasampadā*). Addressing his fellow students, he said, "The ancient masters have said that after the *jñapti-caturtha-karman* (the formal act consisting of one motion and three proclamations), one's entire being becomes the embodiment of precept, concentration, and wisdom.

How can this be constrained by mere rules and regulations? Thereupon, carrying his staff and alms bowl, he traveled everywhere, knocking at the gates of Chan masters to study under them and investigate the meaning of the teachings.

Xuefeng Zhenxian knew that his conditions were ripe; suddenly rising, he seized him and asked, "What is this? Yan was instantly enlightened, and he even forgot the mind that had attained realization, doing nothing but waving his hands back and forth.
Xuefeng said, "Are you applying intellectual reasoning? Yan replied, "What reasoning could there be? Xuefeng deeply approved of him.
Later, when Yan went to accept an invitation from the King of Min, Xuefeng saw him off to the gate. Upon returning to the Dharma Hall, he then—
[Zhaozhou] said, "A single holy arrow shoots straight into the nine-layered city. Fuzhao Zuo said, "He has not yet reached the mark. Zhaozhou said, "He is a man who has penetrated to the very bottom.
Fuzhao said, "If you do not believe me, wait until I go and examine him myself. He then pursued him and, meeting him midway, asked, "Where are you going, elder brother?
[Fuzhao] said, "I am going into the nine-layered city. [Zhaozhou] said, "Suppose you suddenly encounter an army of three divisions..."
[The Master] asked, "How is it when surrounded? He replied, "That house has its own path leading through the heavens.
