"I have cast aside my gourd-bag and smashed my lute; Now I no longer yearn for gold within the mercury. Since the moment I first beheld Huanglong, I have finally realized that all my prior efforts were misplaced.
Yan then instructed him to seek protection through spiritual practice. Yan’s courtesy name was Dongbin; he was a native of Jingchuan.
(Biyou) Zen Master Hyujeong Preaches the Dharma at the Royal Palace (Heir to Dongshan Jia; Second Generation of the Cao-Dong Lineage). Initially, Hyujeong studied under Ryangje.

[Hyujeong] asked, "This student has not yet seen the path of principle; I cannot avoid the functioning of emotional consciousness. [Ryangje] said, "Do you see that there is a path of principle, or not?
[Hyujeong] replied, "I see that there is no path of principle. [Ryangje] said, "From where did this emotional consciousness come?"
[The Master] said, "The student asks in earnest. [The Master] said, "In that case, you must go to a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single blade of grass.
[The student] asked, "At a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single blade of grass, is it permitted to rest in peace? [The Master] said, "You must go in this very manner.

Initially, when Jing first resided at Huayan Monastery in Fuzhou, in the third year of the Tongguang era, Emperor Zhuangzong of the Tang dynasty summoned him to the capital, where he extensively propagated the profound wind of the Dharma.
One day, the Emperor entered the temple to burn incense and asked Jing, "What deity is this? Jing replied, "It is a Dharma-protecting benevolent spirit.
The Emperor asked, "Where did you go during the period of the purge? Jing replied, "The heavens shed rain and dew; they do not flourish with the thriving nor wither with the decay.
One day, the Emperor invited him into the palace for a meal. He saw that the great masters and virtuous monks were all reading scriptures, yet only Jing and his disciples were not reading.

A monk asked, "Why do you not look at the sutras? He replied, "When the Way prevails, one does not transmit the Emperor's decrees; when times are peaceful, one refrains from singing songs of 'Great Peace'.
Another asked, "Why do your disciples also not look at the sutras? He replied, "In the den of a lion, there are no other beasts."
"The path where the Elephant King walks leaves no trace for the fox. He asked, "Great Master, Great Virtuous One, why do you read the scriptures?
He replied, "The water jelly has no eyes; to seek food, it must rely on the shrimp. He asked again, "Since you are a junior, why do you address me as 'Elder'?"
It is said: "In three years, the state will have dragon and phoenix sons; in a hundred years, Your Highness will be an old courtier.
Master Xinghua Cunjian (the second generation of Linji’s lineage, successor to Linji Xuan) entered nirvana.
While residing at Xinghua, he addressed the assembly: "If you are a veteran general, then I pray you enter with a single blade directly. Furthermore...
At a loss for what to do, Chan Master Mindé stepped forward, bowed, and upon rising, let out a shout.
Dàjiǎng also shouted. Mindé shouted again; Dàjiǎng shouted once more. Mindé then bowed and returned to the assembly.

Dàjiǎng said, "If it had been anyone else just now, they would not have escaped even a single stroke of the thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because Mindé understands this shout; he does not treat it as a mere shout."
One day, when a fellow practitioner arrived, as soon as he stepped onto the Dharma Hall, Xiang let out a shout. The monk also shouted. Xiang shouted again; the monk also shouted.
Xiang stepped forward and raised his staff. The monk shouted once more. Xiang said, "Look at this blind fellow!
He still thinks he is the master. As the monk hesitated, Xiang struck him directly. They descended from the Dharma Hall. An attendant asked, "Regarding that monk just now..."
This greatly offended the Abbot. [Zhao]jiang said, "Just now he possessed both the provisional and the real;
he possessed both illumination and function. Yet when I held my hands crosswise before his face, at that moment he could not proceed.
For a blind fellow like this, when would it be any sooner than now to strike him? The monk bowed. Jia-shen, the Later Tang Zhuangzong era.
The Emperor returned from north of the Yellow River to his temporary palace and issued an edict inviting Fán to receive honors, even requiring him to perform the rites of a disciple.

The Emperor said, "In my recovery of the Central Plains, I have obtained a treasure, yet no one has ever offered a price for it. Fán replied, "May I briefly borrow your Majesty’s treasure to examine it?"
The Emperor extended the legs of his *fuhou* (official headgear) with both hands. Xiang said, "This is the treasure of a sovereign; who would dare to set its price?

The Emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed upon him purple robes and a monastic title, but Xiang declined them both. Thereupon, the Emperor granted him a state horse. The horse suddenly bolted, and Xiang fell, injuring his foot.
On the day of Yiyou, Xiang one day called for the head of the monastery and said, "Make me a wooden crutch. The head made it.
Having finished his business, he received [the monks] with favor and walked around the monastery. He asked the monks, "Do you recognize this old monk?
They replied, "How could we not recognize the Master? He said, "The Dharma Master Liǎojiào can speak, but he cannot practice. Then he went to the Dharma Hall.
He ordered the *vinaya-dhara* to strike the bell to assemble the community, saying, "Do you still recognize this old monk?
When the assembly remained silent, Huai-jang threw down his crutch and passed away with a composed expression. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Guangji.
The Biography of Chan Master Huìyǒng’s Transmission of the Dharma to Yánzhǎo:

Yánzhǎo relied upon Yìcún for five years. On one occasion, he requested further instruction regarding Linji’s statement that when the two head monks of the hall both shouted at once, Linji said, "Guest and host are clearly distinguished.
Yìcún remarked, "In the past, I went with Yántóu and Qīnshān to visit Linji, at which time..."
He had already entered nirvana. If one wishes to understand his dialogue regarding host and guest, one must consult the venerable masters of his lineage.
Zhaoyan then took his leave and went to see Master Yan. Yan used to call out to himself, "Master of the House. Zhaoyan said, "What difficulty is there in picking up and playing with it yourself?
He then traveled to Yuezhou to visit Daofu. Daofu asked, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "Zhedong. Daofu said, "Have you passed through Xiao..."
"Is there no river? he asked. [The Master] said, "A great vessel drifts alone through the void. "Is there no small river to cross? he asked.

[The Master] said, "Mirror-like waters and the Qian Mountains—birds cannot fly across them. "Do not speak of hearsay," [the Master] said. "The vast blue sea still fears the power of the *meng-lun* warship;
yet with sails flying toward the Milky Way, one crosses the Five Lakes. Yunfeng stood up, brandished his whisk, and said, "What can be done about this? "What is this? [the Master] asked.
[The Master] said, "Indeed, I do not recognize you. [Yunmen] said, "Appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unrolling; these are used in the same way as by the Master.

[The Master] said, "Divining with a ladle and listening to empty sounds; sleeping soundly and speaking much in dreams. [Yunmen] said, "A vast marsh conceals mountains; its principle can subdue even a leopard.

[The Master] said, "Abandoning transgressions and releasing faults—you must depart at once. [Yunmen] said, "To depart is to lose [the opportunity]. He then went out to the Dharma Hall and said, "As for a traveler on foot... (He continued to speak).

Since the conditions for exhausting his good roots were not yet met, [the Master] could not simply let him depart. He turned back and said, "I have just now rashly presented my petty ignorance and presumed to trouble your venerable countenance.
I humbly thank you for your compassion in not imposing punishment upon me. [The Master] asked, "Did you just say that you came from the East?"
"Is this not from Cuiyan? He replied, "Xuedou personally dwells to the east of Bao’ai. He said, "Not chasing after lost sheep, his frantic interpretations have ceased;
he has come here instead to recite verses. He said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present one's sword;
if you are no poet, do not offer your verse. He said, "The poem is quickly hidden away; let me borrow your sword for a moment. He replied, "A person with a broken head carries a sword."
[The Master] departs. [The student] says: "It is not only that he touched upon the transformation of customs; it also reveals his own bluntness. [The Master] says:

"If he did not touch upon the transformation of customs, how could one know the mind of the ancient Buddhas? [The student] asks: "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? [The Master] says: "To grant permission again and again.

[The student] asks: "What do you have now, Master? [The Master] says: "The patch-robed monks coming from the East cannot distinguish beans from wheat; they only hear 'never ceasing,' but how can they suppress themselves with 'merely ceasing'?"
He said, "A great wave surges a thousand fathoms; the clear ripples do not depart from the water. He said, "One phrase cuts off the current;

ten thousand functions are stilled and eliminated. Zhaomo then prostrated himself. Xingfu said, "This patch-robed monk is truly outstanding! He served as the *karmadāna* at Huayan Monastery. It happened that Attendant Shoukuo came from Nanuan;
Zhaomo marveled at him in his heart and formed a friendship with him, whereby he silently realized the essential principles of the Three Mysteries (*sanxuan*).
He sighed and said, "Is Linji’s application of the Dharma like this? He sent Huikuo to see Huiyong; Zhaowang then went to attend upon him.
Upon entering the gate, he did not prostrate. Huiyong said, "Upon entering the gate, one must discern the master. Zhaowang said, "I ask the Master to distinguish it for me definitively.
Huiyong snapped his fingers once on his left knee; Zhaowang then shouted. Huiyong snapped his fingers again on his right knee; Zhaowang shouted once more. Huiyong said, "The left..."
"Setting aside for a moment that single blow on the left side, what about that single blow on the right side? Yunyan said, "Blind. Yantong then raised his staff.
Zhaorui said, "Do not wield blind shackles and blind blows; do not seize and strike the Master. Do not say I did not warn you.

Yantong threw down the staff and said, "Today I have been thoroughly outwitted by this yellow-faced barbarian from Zhejiang. Zhaorui said, "The Master is much like one who, unable to obtain alms, falsely claims [to have received them]."
[The Master] was not hungry. [Yunmen] asked, "Have you ever been to this place before? [Yunmen] said, "What kind of talk is that? [Yunmen] said, "I am simply asking you a question in good faith.
[Yunmen] said, "You cannot let this pass either. [Yunmen] said, "Sit for a moment and have some tea. The next day, [Yunmen] asked, "Where were you this summer?
[Yunmen] said, "I was at Huayan in Xiangzhou, spending the summer retreat with Attendant Kuang. [Yunmen] said, "So it is."
He came to see the Master in person. The Master asked, "What did he say to you? He replied, "From beginning to end, he only instructed me to always act as the master.
Yung then struck him and pushed him out of the abbot’s quarters, saying, "What use is there for a fellow like this who brings such disgrace upon himself?
From that time on, Zhao took his words to heart and served as the gardener under the assembly. One day, Yung went to the garden.
A question was asked: "Regarding 'one blow from the south,' how do you deliberate upon it? He replied, "I deliberate upon it as something extraordinary.
Zhaoyan then asked, "How do you deliberate upon it here, Master? Yungong then picked up his staff and said, "Under the blow is the patience of non-arising;
when the moment arrives, one does not defer to the teacher. At this, Zhaoyan attained a sudden and great enlightenment. One day, [Yungong] said to Zhaoyan, "You have mounted..."
"It was not by mere chance that you came to shoulder the Great Dharma through the power of your vows. Have you heard the words Linji spoke when he was about to pass away?
He replied, 'I have heard them. [The Master continued,] 'Linji said: "Who would have known that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would perish with this blind donkey?"'"
"His life was like that of a lion: upon seeing him, he would kill. Now that he is about to die, for what reason does he kneel and tuck his tail in such a manner?

He replied, "He is secretly entrusting [the lineage] as he approaches his end; once the master is completely extinguished, [the transmission will cease]. He asked again, "Why did the Three Sages likewise remain silent?"
[The Master] said, "You are a true successor who has personally received the transmission into the inner chamber; you are not like a traveler outside the gate. [The monk] nodded his head in assent.

The Master asked again, "Regarding the four kinds of critical examination (*liaojian*) in your teaching, what dharma do they examine? He replied, "If ordinary speech does not linger in ordinary sentiment, it immediately falls into the conceptual understanding of the sages.
This is a great malady among students. The former sages took pity on them and provided skillful means (*upāya*), like using one wedge to drive out another. [The Master] said, "It is like this..."
"What is 'seizing the person but not seizing the environment'? He said: "A golden bullet fresh from the red furnace; it pierces through the Chan master’s iron face-skin.
"How is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? He said: "The straw has just been parted, yet the head is already split open;
the chaotic clouds have just begun to unfold, yet the shadow still remains. "How is 'seizing both person and environment'? He said: "Stepping forward with your feet, you must act with urgency."
Urgent! Hurry! The whip is upon the collar; the grass is slow. How can it be that neither the person nor the environment is taken away? He said:
"I always remember the third month in Jiangnan, where the *shàgū* cries and the hundred flowers are fragrant. He asked again: "Linji has three statements.
On that day, someone asked: 'What is the first statement? Linji said: 'The seal of the three essentials opens; the vermilion dot is narrow; there is no room for hesitation.'"

The Master proposed dividing the roles of host and guest. Zhaozhou shouted as soon as he heard the words. "What is the second phrase? Linji said, "How could a wondrous understanding allow for non-attachment?
Zhaozhou asked, "When the *upāya* contends, who loses the mechanism of cutting off the flow? Zhaozhou said, "It was already wrong before you even asked.
"What is the third phrase? Linji said, "Just look at the puppeteer on the stage; all the pulling and tugging depends entirely on the person inside."
Zhao said, "If one attempts to break through with clarity, it will not suffice. Thereupon, Yuanying considered that [Zhao] could sustain the Dharma-way of Linji.

A Defense Commissioner asked Yuanying, "Great Good Knowledge, do you still possess seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing? Yuanying slapped him. The Commissioner did not approve. He then asked Zhao the same question as before.
Zhao said, "Thorny brambles and wild cudgels have been discarded for a long time. [The Commissioner] said, "This is wondrous function."
"How is it? Zhaomo asked. The Prince, wearing his sword, was full of noble bearing; the poor man, having been overthrown, spoke with a faltering voice. Master Shen deeply approved of this.

He then raised [the matter of] Yung, who followed the question by striking him with his palm. Zhaomo said, "This is for your own benefit. Only then did Master Shen understand the matter in its entirety.

When the Master arrived at Xinghua, Shoukuo was serving as his attendant. Remembering what had been said at that time, [Shoukuo] said, "Please cite it for me.
Shoukuo then cited the exchange: Xinghua asked the Master, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Wutai.
Xinghua said, "Have you seen Mañjuśrī? The Master then gave a shout. Xinghua said, "I am asking you: have you seen Mañjuśrī?"
"What? Why did you act so aggressively? The Master shouted again. Xinghua was speechless. The Master bowed to him.
On the following day, Xinghua instructed Shoukuo to call for the Master; however, the Master had already departed. Xinghua ascended the hall and said, "Look at this monk!
Carrying a broken string and a rope, he has gone off toward the south. In the future, people will say they saw Xinghua."
Huazhai came forward. "The public case of today is exactly like that of such a time. [Huazhai] asked, "Why was it that Xinghua had no words at that moment?
[Lumen] replied, "Because he saw that the Master did not understand the 'Guest and Host' phrase, he remained silent.

When he wished to call upon the Master to engage in debate, the Master had already departed. On the following day, Lumen specifically prepared tea and addressed the assembly in the evening session, saying: "Now,"...

Students who are like dragons and elephants must carefully enter the room for decisive discernment; they must not easily grasp a single phrase and consider it the ultimate, then claim, "I am quick-witted. It is just as when I first saw Xinghua. My words at that time were: [he said], "If you can speak a word, I will give you thirty blows; if you cannot speak a word, I will also give you thirty blows. When I heard this, I immediately went forward and gave him a slap. He struck me with his staff and said, "This fellow has some spirit! At that moment, I attained a realization.

I have been saying this for forty years, yet no one has ever been able to explain it. You should know that the Way is not something to be grasped through intellectual understanding. If you wish to see the true person, you must first cast away all your habitual patterns of thought. Only then will you be able to see the original face. This is what is meant by "the sword of the patriarchs. It is not something you can obtain by mere study; it requires you to personally encounter a true teacher and undergo a transformation. Do not let your mind be led astray by external appearances. If you can be thus, you will naturally accord with the Way. This is the essential point of our school. Do not be negligent. Go and practice accordingly.
One has attained something that can be moved and turned. When people see one uttering a shout or two shouts and then stop speaking, they take it to be the Buddha-dharma.
Today, having been seen through by those with clear eyes, it becomes nothing but a source of ridicule. What is the point of this?

It is simply because of pride and ignorance (*māna-avidyā*) that one cannot turn back to draw near to those of superior caliber. Fortunately, there are enlightened practitioners who do not spare themselves.
Life. To testify before the assembly: this kindness is difficult to repay. Why? Xinghua said:

"Even if you were to shout yourself up to the thirty-third heaven and then crash back down until you had not a single breath left, and you were to slowly regain consciousness and say to me, 'It is not yet,' why would it be so?

The pearl is with you; why do you drink so recklessly? These are words of medicinal admonition, yet the followers of the Way find them difficult to believe.
Now you must discern this clearly; will you not then rejoice that your lifelong study of the Way is finally complete?
The Dharma Transmission of Chan Master Guichen to Wenyi:
Wenyi was the son of the Lu family of Yuhang. From birth he was exceptionally gifted; at the age of seven, he shaved his head and received the precepts.

In his youth, he received full ordination, thoroughly studied the Vinaya, and explored the Confucian classics. Taking up his staff, he traveled south and arrived in Fuzhou, where he visited Huileng. However, he did not achieve great enlightenment. Later—
The three men, including Tongshao, Fashu, and Jin, traveled from Zhangzhou to the outskirts of Lake [Huguang].

Encountering rain and snow, with mountain streams and waterfalls surging in flood, they unpacked their belongings and took refuge in an ancient temple at the corner of a city wall. Upon entering the hall, they found an elderly monk huddled by a brazier.

As the three men sat by the fire, the old monk asked Yì, "Where are you going on this journey? Yì replied, "I am traveling as a wandering monk (*yǒngjié*). The monk asked, "What is it? [Yì remained silent.]

Regarding the matter of traveling on pilgrimage, Yuan Yi said, "I do not know. The Master said, "Not knowing is most intimate. Again, while the three of them were discussing the *Zhao Lun*, they reached the passage:
"Heaven and earth share the same root as I. The old monk asked, "Are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth the same as you, venerable masters, or are they different?
Yuan Yi said, "Different. The old monk held up two fingers. Yuan Yi said, "The same. The old monk again held up two fingers.
He rose and departed, greatly surprised. As he walked along the corridors, he read the inscription on the lintel which said, "Stone Mountain Kṣitigarbha," and thus realized it was Master Guichen.

When the snow cleared, Xueji took his leave. As Guichen saw him off at the gate, he asked, "Upādhyāya, you usually say that the three realms are mind-only and all phenomena are consciousness-only. Now, look at this stone in the courtyard—tell me, what is it?"
"Is it within the mind? Is it outside the mind? Huizhi said, "It is within the mind. Daolin Xianchen laughed and said, "For a wandering monk, what need is there for such origins?
Why place a flat stone upon your head? Huizhi was cornered and had no reply.

He then took leave of Xiu and Jin, immediately unpacking his bundle and sitting beneath the seats to seek decisive instruction. For nearly a month, he presented his insights and expounded on principles. Daolin spoke:
Chen said, "The Buddha-dharma is not like that. Yì said, "I am at the end of my words and the limit of my reasoning.
Chen said, "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, everything is already fully accomplished. At these words, Yì attained great enlightenment. Shàoxiū initially studied together with Wényì under Guìchén.
Each believed they had reached the ultimate attainment. Later, when they were traveling together toward Jiānyáng, Yì suddenly asked him on the road:
"Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. Does this negate the myriad phenomena? Or does it not negate them?
[Daoyi] said, "It does not negate them. Yizhi said, "What are you talking about—negating or not negating? Xiu was utterly bewildered. He returned to Dizang and asked, "You left not long ago;
why have you come back? [Dizang] said, "There was a matter I could not resolve; how could I have feared the toil of traversing mountains and rivers? [Xiu] said, "You have traveled so much..."
"Mountains and rivers—this is not bad either. Xiu, not yet having understood the meaning, asked: "Regarding the statement, 'Among the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed'—what is its intent?
Chen said, "Do you say that the ancients rejected the myriad phenomena, or did they not reject them? Xiu said, "They did not reject them. Chen said, "Then there are two [positions].
Xiu was startled and fell into deep reflection. He then asked Chen again, "I wonder, did the ancients reject the myriad phenomena or not?"
Xiang said, "What do you call the myriad phenomena? At this, Xiu Fang attained awakening.
When Hongjin was serving as the First Seat under Dizang, one day when Cheng ascended the hall, two monks came forward to prostrate. Cheng said, "Both are wrong. The two monks were speechless.
After the session, they requested instruction from Xiu. Xiu said, "You yourselves are majestic and dignified; yet you prostrate and intend to ask [for an answer]."
"Others—how could that not be an error? Jìn refused to accept it. Nǐuxiū then asked, "And what about you, Upādhyāya?
Jìn said, "You are yourself lost in delusion and darkness; how can you act as a teacher for others? Nǐuxiū was filled with indignation and went to the Abbot’s quarters to seek further instruction.
Dàchén pointed toward the corridor and said, "The head cook has gone to the storehouse. At this, Nǐuxiū attained realization. A day later, Jìn asked Nǐuxiū, "You clearly know that birth..."
"This is the principle of non-arising. Why then is one carried away by birth and death? Xiu said, "A bamboo shoot will ultimately become a bamboo stalk.
Can you now take it and use it as a strip of bamboo? Jin said, "You will realize this for yourself in the future.
Xiu said, "My own understanding is only like this. What is your intention, Venerable Sir? Jin then pointed and said, "This!"
"This is the Karmadāna’s quarters. Which one is the Head Cook’s quarters? Xiu then bowed in thanks.
(Dinghai year) Chan Master Huanzhang of Ruelong entered nirvana.
Huanzhang had resided at Ruelong; in the fourth month of the second year of the Tiānchéng era, he requested a burial site from the Senior Uncle Qian Wang. The Senior Uncle...

He smiled and said, "Is that how it is for you, Master? He then sent men to select a site in the western gate to build a stupa. Once the stupa was completed, he went to take leave of King Qian, entrusting him with the protection of the Dharma and the care of the people.
Upon his return, he sat in meditation and passed away. His lifespan was eighty-seven years, and he had spent seventy summer retreats in seated meditation.
(Wuzi) Chan Master Changjue resided at Pujing Changjue.
Initially, he visited Guizong Zhang, whereupon hearing the Dharma, he attained awakening. Thereafter, while traveling to the capital, he was outside the Lijing Gate.

He lived in solitude for two years. During this time, there was a neighbor named Zhang who invited Huizhao to receive offerings. Having attained realization, Zhang set up a mat and invited him to stay overnight.
At night, he and his wife peeked through a crack and saw that Huizhao’s body completely filled the single mat. Their admiration increased all the more, and they said:
The disciple’s couple were advanced in years; they now wished to cede the front hall to supplement the master’s chamber.
Huizhao joyfully accepted it, and by the third year of the Tiānchéng era, it had become a large monastery, granted the name Pǔjìng.

Fearing that the times were shallow and ignorant, making it difficult to uphold the ultimate teachings, Huizhao said, "I would rather not strive to propagate the Dharma. Consequently, on the eighth, thirteenth, and eighteenth days of every month, he provided baths for the monks.
He spoke in ten thousand ways. He often said to his disciples, "If only the gate of wisdom remains unobstructed, how could blessings ever be hindered?
From Zhan resided at Baofu, where his students numbered no fewer than seven hundred. On the third day of the third month in the third year of the Tiancheng era, he manifested slight illness.
When a monk entered his quarters to inquire after him, Zhan said, "I have known you for many years; what arts or methods do you possess?"
They came to his rescue, saying, "The Master possesses great skill in the arts of longevity. We have heard that you, O Monk, do not observe dietary taboos.

He then said to the assembly, "In these past ten days, my strength has been exhausted and weakened; there is nothing else—it is simply that my time has come. A monk asked, "Since your time has already arrived—"
The Master said, "Going is it; staying is called the Way, the Way. [A disciple] asked, "If that is so, I dare not act rashly.
He replied, "Losing money and suffering punishment. Having finished speaking, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away.
Xingchong succeeded to the Dharma of Congzhan. While residing at Gushan Ba’en, he said to his disciples: "Although I am no longer here, I have never ceased to act for the sake of you brothers. If...

To fully comprehend how to repay this debt of gratitude is the constant dwelling place of those who act for others. I grant you that you have emerged from conceptual thoughts and intellectual understanding regarding the field of the five aggregates.
If you do not thoroughly understand this, I guarantee that you have not yet emerged from conceptual thoughts and intellectual understanding.

Therefore, the ancients called this "the livelihood of ghosts" or being "a guest beneath the frog’s robe. If you wish to attain swift resonance with reality, then right now, standing where you are, realize it immediately.
Examine and discern what faults there are in grasping at perception. It is not that the faculties and thoughts are sluggish; rather, investigate this over days and nights.
Suddenly, one day you may catch sight of it—do not consider a small measure sufficient, but continue to probe until the ultimate limit.
Whether in brothels or taverns, whether defiled or pure, whether good or evil, take the things you see as your object of inquiry.
Examine the teachings: they are entirely this very realm. Entering it is like entering the Vinaya.

If you perceive even a single dharma, however slight as a hair or a speck of dust, and do not see this matter, I call that the obscuration of ignorance. You must reach the point where you do not see any dharma as a separate entity;
only then will you attain perfect completeness. Reaching this stage, you can further turn and cast yourself about, opening and closing with total freedom, leaving no seams or traces behind.
It is like water entering water, fire entering fire, wind entering wind, and space entering space.

If one can act in this way, directly drawing a single sword and severing the net of doubt of all people under heaven in a single stroke, without creating anything resembling [the truth], then one is as the ancients said:
"When great functions arise in profusion, every movement is entirely true. If there is such a person who reaches such a state...
The realm. Who would dare to step forward and say what is right or wrong? Why is this? This person is a man of true substance;
he transcends all measures and limits, and has penetrated beyond cause and effect in every respect. No one can restrain such a person. If one can act in this manner, then it is acceptable.
If you have not yet attained this, you must simply observe carefully. Do not speak or breathe recklessly; do not cause yourself to sink and fall for immeasurable kalpas.
Do not let it come to such a time that you say, "I have repaid my debt of gratitude," or "I have not repaid... [The text ends here]. Guichen resided at Luohan Temple, or at Dizang Shishan.
In the third year of the Tianning era of the Later Tang dynasty, a monk came to inform him that Baofu had passed away.
Baoshou had already passed away. Baofu said, "When Baofu passes away, Dizang shall enter the stupa. That autumn, he returned once more to his former residence in the city of Min.

He traveled extensively through all the monasteries near the city before returning home. Shortly thereafter, he manifested a slight illness. A monk asked, "How is the Master’s health compared to before?
Baolin leaned on his staff against the ground and said, "Tell me, does this still hurt? The monk replied, "The Master..."
He asked, "Who is it? [Xuanzhen] replied, "I am asking you. He asked again, "Is your pain still there? Xuanzhen said, "It turns out you have been engaging in intellectual reasoning with me all along.

Thereupon, he bathed, sat upright, and passed away. His remains were cremated, his *śarīra* were collected, and a stupa was erected. He was posthumously titled "True Response" (Zhenying). Later, Xiankoubing (Xuanzhao) resided at Lingyao Temple.
In the third year of the Tiancheng era, the King of Min invited him into his inner chambers to inquire about the Dharma. During a tea break, Xian took up [the whisk].
Qizhaozi said, "Does the Great King understand? He replied, "I do not. Qizhaozi said, "The King of Men and the Dharma King each have their own realization.
He remained for ten days, after which he declined on account of illness. On the second day of the twelfth month, he bathed, ascended the hall, addressed the assembly, and passed away.
The cremation was accompanied by auspicious radiance that filled the mountains, and five-colored *śarīra* relics were obtained;
he was posthumously titled "Compassionate Savior" (*Cíjì*). (Gengyin) Chan Master Wenyuan resided at Lingshu.

Having personally transmitted the seal of the school, he traveled extensively to visit various quarters, vigorously expounding upon the Great Matter. Upon reaching Jiuyang, he met the Imperial Censor Chen Cao.

The Minister requested an audience for a vegetarian feast. As soon as he saw him, [Dongshan] asked: "I shall not ask about the Confucian classics; you have your own masters for the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
What, then, is the matter of a monk’s traveling on pilgrimage? The Minister replied: "How many people has Your Reverence questioned thus far?"
[The Master] said, "I am asking the Elder right now. [The Elder] said, "Let that be for a moment. What is the meaning of the Teachings?
[The Master] said, "Yellow scrolls and red axes. [The Elder] said, "This is merely speech and written words. What is the meaning of the Teachings?

[The Master] said, "The mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail; the mind wishes to contemplate, yet thoughts vanish. [The Elder] said, "The mouth wishing to speak while words fail—this is in response to the existence of speech."
The mind desires to take it as an object of contemplation, yet its deliberations vanish. This is done to counteract deluded thoughts. "What is the intent of the teaching? Cáo remained silent.
Yǎn said, "I have heard that you, Minister, study the Lotus Sūtra; is this true? "It is," [Cáo] replied. Yǎn said, "The sūtra states:
'All livelihoods and productive activities are not at variance with the true mark (dharmatā). Now tell me, how many people are there in the Heaven of Neither Thought nor Non-Thought?"
He stepped down from his seat. Cao remained speechless. Yan said, "Minister, do not be so hasty. You have cast aside the Three Canons and Five Treatises to enter the monastic groves specifically;
yet after ten or twenty years, you still cannot manage it. How could you, Minister, possibly understand? Cao bowed and said, "I am at fault.
In the first year of the Changxing era, he went to Caoqi to pay respects at the Patriarch’s stupa. Ling...

Shumen was invited to serve as the First Seat (Śrāmaṇera). Previously, when Shumen did not accept the invitation for the First Seat, those who urged him would simply say, "My First Seat has already left the household life.
After some time, he was invited again, and he replied, "My First Seat has already gone on pilgrimage and realized the Way.
After another long period, he was invited once more, and he said, "My First Seat has already crossed the mountain pass. Suddenly one day, he ordered the bell to be struck to receive the First Seat.
The assembly all went out to welcome him. Xian arrived as expected. Min greeted him with a smile and said, "I have waited for you for a very long time;

why have you come so late? He then immediately appointed him. Xian did not decline and accepted the post. Shortly thereafter, the ruler of Guang, Prince Liu, was about to raise an army and went to Min to decide whether it should be undertaken.

Min, having foreseen this beforehand, sealed a small casket with his own hand and told his attendant, "When the Prince comes, bring this out and show it to him. Thereupon, he proceeded [to his death].

He passed away while sitting. When the King arrived, he heard that Daimin had already attained parinirvāṇa and was greatly astonished. He asked, "When did the Master fall ill? [Daimin] replied, "The Master never fell ill.
Just now, he sealed a small casket and instructed me to wait for the King's arrival. The King opened the casket and found a note inside.
He was called "The Eye and Mirror of the Human and Heavenly Eyes. The Head Seat (shouzuo) of the hall was Wang; he subsequently invited Xian to succeed him on the Dharma seat.
(Xinmao year) Chan Master Yanzhao resided at Fengxue.
Having relied upon Nan yuan for six years, he took his leave. In the second year of Changxing, he arrived at Ruzhou and saw a thatched cottage.
A few rafters leaned against the mountain like the dwelling of fugitives. When a farmer was asked what place this was, he replied, "It is the ancient Fengxue Temple.
During a year of famine, the community abandoned it and departed; nothing remains but Buddha images, bells, and drums. Baizhao said, "May I dwell here?"
He replied, "It may be so. Thus, Baozhao remained there. During the day he begged for food in the villages; at night he burned pine resin.
He lived as a solitary practitioner for seven years (*Renchen*). In the second year of Changqing, Chan Master Huileng entered nirvana (*Xuefeng Cun* was his Dharma heir).
Huileng established the Dharma in two locations with fifteen hundred disciples. His transformative influence spread through Min and Yue for twenty-seven years.
On the fifth day of the fifth month in the third year of the Changxing era, he passed away at the age of seventy-nine.
Dao-kuang of Zhaoqing in Quanzhou had served as the head of the work-crew under Changqing; while he was frequently conversing with the assembly of monks, one day Changqing saw him and said:
"What are you doing with such incessant chatter every day? [Qing asked]. "Three days without work, three days without food," [the monk] replied.

"If that is so, then you are sharpening your bow and polishing your arrows," [Qing said]. "I am waiting specifically for Weichi to arrive," [the monk] replied. "What happens after Weichi arrives? [Qing asked].

"I will make his sinews and bones lie spread upon the ground, and his eyes bulge out," [the monk] replied. Qing then desisted. After taking up residence at the monastery, he once led the community in manual labor (*pǔqǐng*).

While carrying mud, Huangbo stood in the middle of the path, leaning on his staff, and asked a monk, "Is the cave above full of mud, or is the cave below full of mud? The monk replied, "The cave above is full of mud.
Huangbo struck him with a blow of his staff. He then asked another monk, who replied, "The cave below is full of mud. Huangbo likewise struck him with a blow of his staff.
He asked Deqian again. Qian set down his mud-brick carrying pole and, with palms joined, said, "I ask the Master to examine me. Kuang then ceased.
(Gui-si year) The Chan master Qiruan of Dazhang Mountain in Fuzhou entered nirvana (he was a dharma heir of Xuansha Shibei).

Qiruan had studied under Master Bei and realized the essential meaning. He lived in seclusion on Xiaojie Mountain, where he hollowed out a large, rotten pine tree to serve as a small hermitage; he was capable of nothing more than this.
Rongshen. One day, Qinghuo was visiting Chongzhao. As they were approaching, Huiri was gathering millet.
Huo asked, "Where is Master Ruru? Ruru replied, "From where have you come? Huo said, "From down in the valley.
Ruru asked, "How did you manage to get here? Huo said, "What place is this? Ruru then bowed and said, "Come, let us go drink tea down there."
The two men then realized this was the case. They proceeded to the hermitage and were deeply moved by his lofty discourse; they did not notice that night had fallen.

Suddenly, they saw jackals and tigers rushing to the front of the hut, circling it naturally and submissively. A poem appeared, saying: "Your journey is no ordinary journey; Who knows the sentiments of your coming and going?
A single meal remains unsated, Yet ten thousand households find no peace in life. Without the Way, it is difficult to be subdued; An empty fist [cannot hold anything]."
"Do not contend with him. At the place where the dragon roared and clouds arose, he let out two or three leisurely cries.
The two men sought out Daechang to establish a hermitage and invited him to reside there. Sitting alone in both locations, he passed away after fifty-two years.
(Jia-ma) Chan Master Wenyan opened the Dharma at Yunmen.
Residing at Lingshu, he soon moved to Guangtai Temple at Yunmen. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Do not say that I am merely deceiving you all today.
Rather, being driven by necessity, I shall create a scene of total disorder before you. Now, let me ask you all:"
People, from the beginning there has been nothing at all; what is lacking? I tell you all: directly beneath you there is nothing.

Even this [statement] is already a burying of you. Yet you still wish to step forward, seeking understanding by chasing after words and phrases, creating a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions, and setting up broad challenges and difficulties—only to win a reputation for glibness, moving further and further away from the Way. There is...
When is there rest? If this matter were contained within words, then how could the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings not be comprised of words?

Why, then, do you speak of a "separate transmission outside the teachings"? If it were obtained through scholarly understanding or intellectual ingenuity, then even the sages of the Ten Stages, who preach the Dharma like clouds and rain, are still rebuked for their realization of nature as being "like looking through a fine gauze."
By this one may know that all who possess a mind differ as vastly from heaven and earth.
Nevertheless, for one who has attained the realization, how could the fire of the Way ever burn their mouth? Though they speak of matters all day long, it never touches their lips or teeth;
they have never uttered a single word. Though they wear clothes and eat meals all day long, they have never touched a single grain of rice or a single thread.
"Silk. Although this is so, it is still merely talk from the gate. You must truly attain suchness before you can succeed.

If one speaks according to the school of Nanshan, presenting one's own function within the phrase, it is all in vain to stand and contemplate. Even if one were to take responsibility under a single phrase, one is still but a drowsy fellow.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "On level ground there are countless dead people; only those who pass through the thorns [are alive]."

Linji was a master of the hand. He further said: "Even if you reach the point where heaven and earth, the great earth, are free from even a hair’s breadth of affliction, this is still a 'turning phrase.
Only when you do not see a single color is it half-raised. Even if you attain such a state, you must further know there is a time for the 'total raising.
To the assembly he said: "When light does not penetrate through, there are two kinds of illness: being unenlightened in all places, and having something before one's face."

The object is one. Furthermore, even if you have penetrated the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*) such that there is a vague sense of something persisting, this too is because your light has not yet fully permeated.
Moreover, the Dharmakāya also has two kinds of illnesses: first, having attained the Dharmakāya, one fails to forget the attachment to phenomena (*dharmagrāha*), and one's own views still remain;
thus, one sits within the precincts of the Dharmakāya. Second, even if you manage to penetrate the Dharmakāya, [you must let go].
To let it pass is not permissible. Examine it closely: what essence is there? This too is a sickness.
A monk asked, "How can one ensure that the twelve periods of the day do not pass in vain? Yuanwu said, "Where would you place this question? The monk said, "I do not understand.

I beg the Master to provide an illustration. Yuanwu composed a verse: "If you look up and fail to respond, you are already mistaken. If you attempt to deliberate with thought, when will you ever awaken?"
Yan was lame in his feet and used to carry a staff. Once, while walking along, he saw the assembly engaged in communal labor. Raising his staff, he said: "Look, look!
The people of Uttarakuru see how difficult it is for you to carry firewood; they are wrestling in the courtyard to offer you their support."
He further recalled for you the *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, which says: "The wisdom of all-knowledge is pure; it is non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
He stood surrounded by the assembly for a long time without dispersing, and then said: "You people have come here for no reason; what are you looking for?
This old monk does nothing but eat his meals and defecate. What else could he possibly do? You all—
"I am currently traveling on foot, studying Chan and inquiring after the Way. Let me ask you: what is it that you have realized by visiting various teachers?
Try to state it. Thereupon, having no choice, he recited the verse of Sanping: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing.
He then turned to look at the monk and asked, "What do you call 'seeing and hearing'? He added, "There is no further sound or form to present to you."
He said to the monk, "What is there in these verbal sounds and forms? He further said, "If one understands this point, there is nothing at all.
He said to the monk, "What matter is there? He further said, "As for essence and function, what does it matter whether they are divided or not? Then he said, "Speech is the essence."
"Essence is function. Holding up his staff, he said, "The staff is essence; the lantern is function. Are these distinct or not?
Have you not heard it said that 'the wisdom of all wisdoms is pure'? He went into the Sangha hall, where the monks rose to greet him.
Yanguan stood over them and said, "Shitou spoke of reciprocity and non-reciprocity. A monk then asked, "What is non-reciprocity? Yanguan—
He pointed with his finger and said, "This is the head of the board. He asked again, "What is mutual interpenetration?

[Yunmen] replied, "What do you call this 'the head of the board'? A lecturer-monk came for an audience; after some time had passed, he remarked, "Before I reached Yunmen, it was like the newly risen moon;
once I arrived there, it became all crooked and bent. Yanben heard of this and asked, "Was that what you said?"
Yangshan said, "It is so. He said, "Very good. I ask you: what is the newly risen moon? The monk then cut off his own head and made the gesture of gazing at the moon.
Yangshan said, "If you continue like this, you will lose your eyesight in the future. Ten days later, the monk returned.
Yan again asked, "Have you understood yet? He replied, "I have not. Yan said, "Then ask me. The monk then asked, "What is the meaning of the newly risen moon?
Yan replied, "It is curved and crooked. The monk was at a loss. Later, as it turned out, he lost his sight. A monk asked Lingshu, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Lingshu remained silent and passed away. Later, his disciples established a formal biography of his conduct.
A stele inscription was intended to include these words. [Yunmen] asked Xuedou, "How should you inscribe upon the stele the place where our former teacher remained silent?
Xuedou replied, "The Master asked, 'If one kills one's father and mother, one repents before the Buddha; but if one kills the Buddha and the Patriarchs, where does one repent?'"
Yangshan said, "Lù. Yangshan asked, "I have heard it said in antiquity: 'If one has realized it, karmic obstacles are originally empty; if one has not realized it, one must repay past debts.
I wonder, was the Second Patriarch realized or not? Yangshan said, "Què. Yangshan asked, "One lifetime accumulates evil without knowing good;
one lifetime accumulates good without knowing evil. What is the meaning of this? Yangshan said, "Zhú. Yanyang asked the steward, "Where have you been?"

[Daowei] said, "Come, cut some sacrificial grass. [Yanshou] said, "How many patriarchs have you cut down? [Daowei] said, "Three hundred. [Yanshou] said, "Three thousand blows in the morning, eight hundred blows in the evening.
The handle of the ladle at the eastern house is long; the handle of the ladle at the western house is short. What about that? Sui remained silent. Yanshou then struck him.
[Yanshou] asked, "Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon reflected in water? [Daowei] said, "In the clear waves, there is no path through. [Yanshou] said, "..."
"From where did the Master obtain this? [Yanguan] said, "If you ask again, from where would it come? [The monk asked], "At such a time as this, how is it?
[Yanguan] said, "Layer upon layer, mountain passes and roads. [The monk asked], "When there is nothing above to grasp at and nothing below for one's own self, how is it?
[Yanguan] said, "Regarding the phrase 'concealing the body,' how do you speak? The monk then bowed. Yanguan said, "I let you off one move; now bring me another question."
The monk remained silent. Xian said, "This dead shrimp was offered as an offering to an Arhat.
He asked another monk, "Tonight we are making offerings to the Arhats; do you say they will come back or not? The monk had no reply.

Xian said, "Then ask me. The monk then asked. Xian said, "Change the water and add incense. [The monk said,] "If that is so, then they will come. [Xian said,] "What kind of steamed buns would satisfy their hunger?"
"Disciple, come down quickly. [The Master asked: "What is the pure Dharma-body? [He] said: "A flower-and-medicine railing. [The Master asked: "When one goes in this very way, what then?
[He] said: "A golden-maned lion. [The Master asked: "What is the teaching of a single lifetime? [He] said: "Speaking in response to one. [The Master asked:
"When it is neither the mechanism before one's eyes nor the matter before one's eyes, what then? [He] said: "Speaking upside-down. [The Master asked: "Question—"
"What is the samādhi of every dust mote? He replied, "Rice in the bowl; water in the bucket. "Question: What is the Dharma-body? He replied, "Not contained within the six [senses]. "Question:
What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? He replied, "A sesame cake. "Question: What is the Buddha?
He replied, "A dried piece of excrement. "Question: Where do all Buddhas emerge from? He replied, "The eastern mountain flows over the water."

[The Master] was walking. A monk asked, "If not a single thought arises, is there still any fault? [The Master] said, "Mount Sumeru. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body?
[The Master] said, "Hiding one's body within the Big Dipper. He ascended the hall and said: "The eyelashes span across the ten directions;

Master Jing initially studied under Master Bei. Upon encountering Bei’s address to the assembly, which said, "All of you, if you can for a lifetime act as if you have lost your parents, I guarantee that you will reach thorough penetration," Jing took up these words and asked: "As it says in the teachings, one must not use what is already known..."
He attempted to fathom the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed knowledge and vision. [Zhao] Bei asked, "Furthermore, how so? You say you have thoroughly investigated the mind that knows to its very bottom;
can you still fathom it? From this, Jing gained faith and entered the Way. Later, he resided at Tiantai for more than thirty years without descending from the mountain.
He extensively mastered the three studies, his conduct was solitary and upright, and in the intervals between his meditative stillness, he constantly read...
The Dragon Canon (Longzang) is revered from near and far. At that time, there was a senior monk (Upādhyāya) named Dajing. Once, someone asked him:
"Whenever I sit in meditation at night, my thoughts fly about in confusion. I do not yet understand the method for subduing them; I pray you will deign to grant me instruction. He replied:
"If, while sitting peacefully at night, your thoughts fly about in confusion, take that very mind which is flying about and investigate the place where it flies about."

When one investigates until no place remains, where can the fluttering thoughts exist? When one turns back to investigate the investigating mind itself, where is that very mind capable of investigation?
Furthermore, the wisdom that is able to illuminate is fundamentally empty, and the objects it perceives are likewise quiescent—yet they are not merely quiescent.
This is because there is no person who can achieve stillness. That which illuminates yet is not illumination is because there is no objective realm to be illuminated.
When both realm and wisdom are stilled, the mind and its concerns are at peace. One does not seek out branches externally, nor does one dwell in meditative concentration internally.

Both paths are extinguished, and the single nature is serene. This is the essential path for returning to the source. One day, upon encountering the meaning of "illusion" within the teachings, he then—
He recited a verse and asked the various schools of practitioners: "If all dharmas are like illusory existences, then committing various transgressions and evils should entail no fault.
Why, then, do the karmic actions one performs not perish, such that one must rely on the Buddha's compassion to provide guidance and conversion?

At that time, there was an Elder named Xiao Jing who replied: "An illusory person creates illusory Mount Cakravāḍa; illusory karma can summon illusory objects of treatment. [This is because] one does not understand..."
Just as illusions arise from illusions, when one awakens to the fact that illusions are unconditioned (asaṃskṛta), they vanish.
(Year of Yiwei) Chan Master Wenyi resided at Chongshou Temple.
After receiving the mind-seal (citta-mudrā), he traveled to Fuzhou. The Governor of the prefecture invited him to reside at Chongshou Monastery. At that time, there was Zifang.
From the time of Changqing onward, [Dongshan] asked Yì, "You have long been close to Changqing; why did you instead succeed Dizang?
Yì replied, "Because I could not understand how, amidst the myriad phenomena, one's own body alone is revealed. Just as [Dongshan] raised his whisk to show him, Yì said:
"Does one negate the myriad phenomena, or does one not negate them? [The Master] said: "One does not negate them. [The student] asked: "Then is it the 'unveiled body'?

[The Master] said: "It is negation. [The student] asked: "What about within the myriad phenomena? At this, he suddenly realized the essential meaning and sighed, saying: "I have nearly spent this life in vain. There was also a man named Zizhao.

In his usual practice, [Zhao] would discuss matters of antiquity and the present with Yì. Upon hearing that [Yì] had succeeded Dìzàng, he was filled with indignation and resentment; he immediately led his assembly to come and reprimand him.
When Yì learned of this, he led the entire community out to welcome him, treating him with special courtesy and assigning them their respective seats as host and guest, each hanging a whisk.
During the tea service, Zhao suddenly changed countenance and raised his voice, asking: "Whom do you, Elder, succeed in opening the hall? Yì replied: "Dì."
Zang said, "I have greatly failed my late teacher Changqing. [Changqing] said, "I do not understand one turning word of Changqing.
[Changqing] asked, "Why do you not ask? [Zang] said, "What is the meaning of 'the body alone is revealed amidst the myriad phenomena'? Zhao held up his whisk.
Yi said, "This is what you learned from Changqing. As for the Head Seat’s own portion, how is it? Zhao was speechless.
Yi said, "As for the saying, 'Among the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed'—does this negate the myriad phenomena or not? Zhao replied, "It does not negate them.
Yi asked, "What about the two attendants? Both said they do negate them. Yi then said, "So, among the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed, eh? Zhao remained silent.

The assembly all withdrew with expressions of shame. Yì called out, "Wait! Wait! Though one who has killed his father and mother may still repent through the general confession, it is truly difficult to repent for slandering the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
From that time on, Zhāo returned to study under Yì, where he clarified his own realization.
(Dingyou year) Chan Master Yanzhao opened the Dharma at Fengxue.
Yanzhao resided at Fengxue for seven years as a solitary practitioner. Lay donors renovated the site, and it subsequently became a monastic community (*saṃghārāma*).

In the second year of the Tianfu era, the Prefectural Governor, having heard of his reputation, requested that he open the Dharma and succeed Nan’uan; he then ascended the seat. The former master said: "If you wish to obtain..."
"Kindly do not bring your questions here. Do you understand? The question lies within the answer; the answer lies within the question.
