Yuan asked, "Where is the fire? The monk replied, "Can't you see it? Yuan said, "I don't see it. The monk said, "Blind man! At that moment, the entire assembly declared, "This is Master Yuan!"

This was a failure. Only Master Kuān heard of it and remarked, "It must have been my elder brother Yuǎn who did this. Later, he returned to Shǔ, where the assembly requested that he reside at Dǎojiāng.
A monk asked, "Why does the exquisite flavor of *amṛta* turn into poison? Yuǎn said, "At Dǎojiāng, paper is as precious as gold.
[He also said,] "When one son leaves home to become a monk, the nine generations of his clan are liberated; why then did Maudgalyāyana’s mother fall into hell?"

He was called Que. Later, he resided at Xianglin in Qingcheng. Addressing the assembly, he said: "In general, when traveling on pilgrimage to seek out spiritual teachers, you must go with your eyes open;
you must distinguish between the black and the white, and discern the shallow and the deep, before you can succeed. In this matter, one must first establish a firm resolve.
When the Elder Śākyamuni was on the causal ground, every single word and every single thought were acts of establishing resolve. A monk asked: "What is..."
"Regarding the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West," [he] said, "Sitting for too long leads to fatigue.

"Regarding what it is like when one immediately turns back," [he] said, "One falls into a deep pit. He asked, "What is the single lamp within the room? [He] said, "Three people testify that a tortoise is a turtle.
He asked, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? [He] said, "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains."
(Guimao) Zhifeng met Chan Master Deshao. Zhifeng was a native of Yuhang. From birth, he loathed meat and blood;
his skin and body were fragrant and pure. He left the household life and received full ordination, becoming thoroughly versed in the Three Studies.
He once dreamed of ascending Mount Sumeru, where he beheld three Buddhas seated in a row: first Śākyamuni, then Maitreya; he prostrated before them both.
As for his feet, he could not recognize the third honored one, but merely gazed upward at him. Śākyamuni Buddha said, "This is the Lion-Moon Buddha (Siṃhacandra), the teacher of Maitreya;
pay homage whenever you encounter him. After waking, he consulted the Tripitaka and found it accorded with his dream.
During the Tianfu era of the Jin dynasty, he met Deshao and attained awakening. One day, while sitting in meditative absorption within the Samantabhadra Hall, suddenly—
A divine being knelt before him. When he asked who it was, the being replied, "I am a deity who protects the precepts.
He asked, "I have a long-standing transgression that I have not yet extinguished; do you know of it? The being replied, "What sin does the Master have? It is merely a minor oversight.
Whenever you discard the water from your bowl, it is the property of a donor. To pour it away every time is improper. Having spoken, the being vanished. Upon this, [Daofeng] himself...
He drank all of this water used for washing his alms bowl. After a long time, it caused him to contract a spleen ailment, which was only cured after ten years.
Wenyi resided at Qingliang. The Ruler of Tang invited him into the palace to view the peonies and requested that he compose a poem on the spot. Wenyi replied immediately:

*Clad in coarse wool, facing a fragrant thicket;* *From the start, our inclinations have been different.* *My hair has turned white from this day forward;* *These flowers are the same red as last year’s.* *How lush and radiant they are!*
Following the morning dew, its fragrance pursues the evening breeze. What need is there to wait for it to wither? Thus, from the very beginning, one knows it is empty.
(Yisi) Chan Master Shenyuan of Gushan entered nirvana. (He was a Dharma heir of Xuefeng Cun.
Shenyuan resided at Gushan for over thirty years, and disciples gathered like clouds. He passed away in the Yisi year of the Tianfu era.
(Dingwei) Chan Master Mingzhao Deqian entered nirvana. (A successor of Luoshan Xian. Deqian resided at Mingzhao and composed a verse.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "The single melody of Mingzhao is rarely matched by others; this is the sublime essence of the True School.
In a flash of sparks from flint, where has it gone? A child born this morning ought to know. He passed away shortly thereafter.
Huayan. He ascended the hall and said: "In a hundred years, look only to this very day. As for the matter of this day, how is it?
I have lived on this mountain for forty years, using nothing but a single sword to revive the eyes of men. He then took up his headcloth and said, "Is there a Cunda here now?
He held it out toward the various quarters, spreading it as if to cast it away. A monk asked, "Cunda offered his final alms; what was his ultimate sincerity?"
When asked, "How should one be diligent at such a time? Xuefeng Qian replied, "Do not let us be mutually disappointed. When asked, "Where have you gone since the Master passed away?
Qian raised one foot and said, "Look beneath this foot. When asked, "What serves as the ultimate after a hundred years? Qian took his headcloth, threw it down, and departed.
In the middle of the night, he asked his attendant, "On the occasion of the Vulture Peak assembly in the past, Śākyamuni Tathāgata..."
He extended his two feet, emitting the radiance of a hundred jewels. He then extended his feet and said, "How much shall I emit now?
The attendant replied, "The World-Honored One of old; tonight it is the Master. [Baizhang] modestly brushed his eyebrows with his hand and said, "Do not let us down!
He then spoke this verse: "Displaying full majesty amidst a thicket of blades, May you all maintain this well. An iron ox in the midst of fire."
A calf was born. At the parting of ways, who could have fathomed my mechanism? Having finished the verse, he sat upright and passed away (in the year Wushen).
Zen Master Wenyuan preached the Dharma at the royal palace.
While residing at Yunmen, his Dharma path flourished greatly. The Lord of Guangzhou repeatedly invited him into the inner palace to inquire about the Dharma, treating him as a teacher.
At the ritual, the King asked, "What is Chan? The monk replied, "I am answering because Your Majesty has asked.

One day, during a vegetarian feast, the assembly of monks took turns questioning Xiyuan, asking, "Are the fruits on Lingshu mature yet? He replied, "In what year did you come to believe that they grow?"
[Daowu] said, "It is 'ripe'. [Daowu] said, "Be most careful not to forget it. The King was greatly pleased and bestowed upon him the title Chan Master Kuangzhen.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month of the first year of the Qianguo era, the King welcomed Daoyan into the palace to inquire about the Way. In the ninth month, he returned to the mountain and addressed the assembly, saying, "I have been away from the mountain for sixty-seven days.
Now, tell me: what is the state of affairs regarding these sixty-seven days? The assembly was at a loss.
Nengdui. Yan Da said, "Why do you not say that the Master eats much noodles in the capital? Shouchu was the son of the Chen family from Fengxiang.
As a child, whenever he heard the sound of bells and drums, he would immediately stop eating and sit upright for the entire day. His mother tested him many times.
He was neither fed nor sought after. At the age of sixteen, he shaved his head, received full ordination, and traveled to visit Wenyuan.

Wenyuan asked, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "Chadu. Wenyuan asked, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? He replied, "Baoci in Hunan. Wenyuan asked, "When did you leave there?
He replied, "The twenty-fifth of the eighth month. Wenyuan said, "I grant you three blows of the staff. Initially, [Xuedou] was bewildered; by the following day, however—
The Master asked after his health and said, "Yesterday you were granted three blows of the staff by the Venerable Master. I do not know where my fault lay. Dongshan replied, "The rice-sack;
Jiangxi and Hunan—just go like that! At these words, [Dongshan] attained great enlightenment. He then said, "In the future, I shall go to places where there is no human habitation.
Without storing a single grain of rice or planting a single stalk of vegetable, I will receive and attend to those from the ten directions who come to me."

"Come," [the Master said]. "I shall pull out every nail and extract every wedge for you. I will strip away your greasy cap and cast off your stinking hemp robe, so that you may become a free and easy person, a monk of no affairs. Would this not be a joy for you?
The man replied, "Your body is as small as a coconut, yet you have opened such a wide mouth. He then prostrated himself at once and took his leave that very day. Traveling north, he reached Xianghan.
In the first year of the Qiangu (Gian-yu) era, while residing at Dongshan, he addressed the assembly: "Speech within speech is called a 'dead word.
Speech within which there is no speech is called a 'living word. What is the living word? At this point, it is truly difficult to find someone who can grasp it.
It is simply because they have not reached its source that they fall into the eighth realm of demons. One must recognize that which is neither named nor an object, and is without 'is' or 'is-not.'"
There is nothing that is not so. In every instance, in every thing, there is nothing that is not fully complete. I have attained the field of peace and bliss; I seek nothing further.

Whenever there is a challenge or a strike, I immediately beat the meditation seat and raise the whisk. Furthermore, without begrudging anything, I bestow it, I establish it, I put it into practice, and I employ it.

Within the pit of foul water, I play with a tailless monkey. On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, even the drum— (Note: The final phrase "鼓也" (gǔ yě) likely functions as a concluding marker or indicates the end of a rhythmic or performative section.)
It is shattered. The monkey has run off again; hands flustered and feet in turmoil, nothing at all is accomplished. What regret can avail now?
If one were a true monk, it would be better to freeze to death or starve to death than ever to put on that "falcon-smelling robe.
It is also said: "Words do not unfold the matter; speech does not hit the mark. Those who ride upon words perish; those who linger in phrases are lost. Regarding these four—

Within these words and phrases, you must see clearly and attain a state of liberation. This matter of the patch-robed monk’s rafters and tiles, his rice and gruel, is fit to serve as a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) for gods and humans.
If you do not understand this, you will ultimately remain muddled and confused. It is further said:
To proclaim the vehicle of the school and expound the Great Teaching, one must possess a refined and brilliant Dharma-eye to be able to discern and discriminate.
When the monastic and the lay are intimately connected, and truth and falsehood arise from a single source—like water and milk in the same vessel—it becomes difficult to distinguish them.

Dongshan, in his daily practice, used the eye within his mind to observe the forms outside his body; observing again and again, he was thus able to differentiate the genuine from the counterfeit. If it were not so, how could it be called [the Dharma-eye]?
"Good spiritual friends! As for a good spiritual friend, they drive away the oxen of the plowman and snatch the food from the hungry man;

only then can one be called a 'good spiritual friend. Who, then, in the world today is a true good spiritual friend? How many such spiritual friends have you venerable ones encountered through practice? This is no trivial matter;

you must practice until you penetrate to the very bottom and see through it, so as to transcend the thousand sages. Do not stop there. You must investigate until you see through it, so as to transcend the thousand sages. Do not...

Only through such proof can one truly manifest the character of a great man. Have you not seen how the Elder Śākyamuni, at the moment the morning star appeared, attained sudden and great enlightenment and simultaneously became a Buddha together with all sentient beings of the great earth? There is no distinction between before and after; is this not a source of profound joy?
Even so, if one encounters a clear-eyed monk, it is well to strike him across the spine with a staff.
A monk asked, “When Vimalakīrti held up the four worlds in his palm, where did Vimalakīrti’s own body reside? [The Master] said, “It is behind you, O scholar.
The monk asked, “Why is it behind me? [The Master] said, “Give me back the head of your phrase. [Another] asked, “What is the Buddha? [The Master] said—
Three *jin* of Hemp. ○ Xuánzé first visited Qīngfēng and asked, "What is the student’s own self?
Fēng replied, "The child of the fire element comes seeking fire. Later, while at Fǎyǎn’s assembly, he merely followed along with the crowd and never requested an audience for private instruction.
One day, Wényì asked, "Why does Supervisor Xuánzé not come for private instruction? He replied, "Master..."
"Shang, do you not know that Master Qingfeng had a point of entry for you?
He said, 'Try to bring it up for me. You replied, 'I asked Qingfeng, "What is the Buddha? and he said, "The child Bingding comes to seek fire.
Yiyi said, 'Those are fine words, but I fear you have misunderstood them. Try explaining them further. You said, 'Bingding belongs to the element of fire; [he seeks] with fire..."
He went to seek out Huo. "If such-and-such a person is the Buddha," [Touzi] said, "I shall go further to seek the Buddha. Daoyi remarked, "The Prior has indeed misunderstood.
Touzi, feeling indignant, rose immediately and crossed the river alone. Daoyi said, "If this man returns, he may still be saved; if he does not return, he cannot be saved.
When Touzi reached the middle of the road, he reflected to himself, "He is a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) to five hundred people."
"How could he possibly have deceived me? He then returned to consult him again. Xuefeng Yi said, "Just ask me anything, and I will answer for you.

The monk immediately asked, "What is the Buddha? Yi replied, "The boy Bingding comes seeking fire. At these words, the monk attained great enlightenment. He later resided at Ba'en Monastery in Jinling.
On the day of his opening the hall, Prince Li and Xuefeng Yi were both present in the assembly. A monk asked, "The Dragon..."
Mist rose as he recited; a tiger roared and the wind arose. The student knew these were matters pertaining to the transcendental realm, yet when it came to this point, why did he not understand?
Yanze said, "Try to understand it well. The monk raised his head to look, then looked again. Yanze then withdrew from him and entered the assembly.
When Fayi and King Li were present, they both turned pale with shock. Fayi returned to his quarters and ordered an attendant to summon the monk for an inquiry.
When the monk arrived, Fayi said, "The question you asked just now—you claimed to possess the eye [of wisdom]. Why did you fail to prostrate before the assembly of devas and humans?
You have merely covered it over! Fayi then struck him once with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*). Three days later, the monk passed away emitting light. —Hao.
Jian was known among the assembly as "Jian the Talkative. He was constantly sewing his sitting mat.
When he first arrived at Yunmen during his travels, Yunmen said, "The Master of Yunfeng said, 'When the door is opened, Bodhidharma enters. I ask you: what do you say?
Jian replied, "I strike the Master's nostrils. Yunmen said, "The Earth Deity loses his temper and, seizing Mount Sumeru, gives him a blow that sends him leaping up to the Brahma Heaven."
"O Heavenly One! You have smashed Śakra’s nostrils. Why do you hide yourself inside those nostrils?
He said, "Master, please do not deceive people. [The Master] said, "You have struck my old nose; what then? Jian had no reply. The Gatekeeper said:
[The Master] knew that [the monk] was merely one who parrots words. He spoke on his behalf, saying: "Luo luo li. Thereafter, upon hearing these words, [the monk] attained great enlightenment.
He entered the world and resided at the Xin-kai-yuan (Newly Opened Court) in Ba-ling, yet he never again acted as a formal Dharma heir. He simply sent three turning phrases to the Master’s gate.
A monk asked: "What is the Way? He replied: "A person with clear eyes falls into a well. [Another monk] asked: "What is the blowing? [He replied: "..."
Maojian replied, "Shan-shan; every branch supports the moon. [The Master] asked, "What is the school of Deva?
He replied, "Snow served in a silver bowl. The Master said, "In the future, on the anniversary of this old monk’s death, it will suffice to cite these three turning words."
The debt of gratitude is repaid. From this day forward, on the anniversary of his passing, let us simply raise these three turning words.
(Jiyou Year) Zen Master Yunmen Wenyan entered nirvana (Xuefeng Cun was his Dharma heir; he was the first generation of the Yunmen lineage).
Wenyan resided at Yunmen for thirty years, preaching the Dharma like clouds and rain, such that no one could fathom him. He once composed:
The Verse on the Essential Principles says: Kang’s round form stagnates in lack of clarity; The demon’s depth is empty, lost amidst the striking of ice-cold water.

When the phoenix’s feathers unfold, it soars beyond the azure sky; To what can the eightfold sharpness of Jin’s spear be compared? (1) This mechanism is a response; yet responding to the mechanism leads to delusion.

Clearing away the dust of the mundane world, one stays far from defilement. Dwelling at twilight, day after day—who possesses this? Hanging upon the very basis, what matter is it that separates one from the dust and delusion?
(2) Wasting the light of time, the forest of vines falls into ruin; in vain do people’s minds linger, their bodies weary and frail. (3) “Duo duo duo! Li kou xi! (Exert yourself! Strive!
The Chan practitioner is startled; his eyebrows hang down between them. (4) Above, he sees not heaven; below, he sees not earth. His throat and gullet are completely blocked.
"From where does this breath emerge? Those who laugh at me are many; those who smile at me are few. (5) Whenever Yuanruo looked back at a monk, he would say, "Jian" (Mirror).
When the monk wished to respond, he would say, "Ei" (Aha!). The *Records of the Disciples* state: "Gu, Jian, and Ei.

Deshan Yuanmi deleted the character "Gu," retaining only the two characters "Jian" and "Ei" as a verse; this is called the "Extraction of 'Gu' Verse. [Recorded during] the Ganyou era of the Han dynasty.
On the tenth day of the fourth month of the second year, he sat upright and manifested his passing. He was posthumously titled Great Master Kuangzhen Hongming of the Daciyun Monastery.
As for the Venerable Lang, from his youth he studied at lecture halls. There, he heard a monk ask Yunmen, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya?
Yunmen replied, "Hiding one's body within the Big Dipper. Lang could not fathom the subtle meaning, so he went to visit Yunmen. As soon as Yunmen saw him, he...
The Master seized him and said, "Speak! Speak! Lang hesitated. Yunmen pushed him away and presented this verse:
"Yunmen towers high, the white clouds hang low; The waters are swift, the fish dare not dwell. Entering the gate, his understanding was already known;

Why labor to tread again upon the mud? Lang thereupon attained great enlightenment. Later, when Shikuan was studying under Yunmen, one day he heard the mallet struck for the assembly and [the Master] said: "Please..."
The Master appointed Kuan as the steward (dianzuo). Kuan performed a somersault and stepped out from among the assembly, saying, "The Zen of Yunmen belongs to me!
On another day, [the Master] asked Kuan, "How many sesame cakes did you eat today? He replied, "Five. [The Master] said, "How many did the pillar eat?
He replied, "I ask the Master to come to the tea hall and drink tea. One day, Kuan visited Baimiao. Baimiao said, "This old monk..."

There was a verse on the wooden fish (*mokugyo*). [The Master] said, "Please recite it. [The monk] said: "I humbly observe that this is but a piece of rotten wood; Buddhas and sentient beings are no different.
If one strikes it with a staff, the paths of the holy and the ordinary are instantly severed.
Kuan said, "Does this verse have merit or not? He replied, "It has no merit. Kuan said, "If Buddhas and sentient beings are no different, why [strike it]? The attendant monk rescued him.
Yangshan said, "There is a robe to be bestowed. Guankui said, "It must be that the paths of the sage and the ordinary man have been cut off.

At that moment, the entire assembly at Baimiao turned pale with shock. Yuanmi received the mind-seal of Yunmen. Later, he resided at Deshan in Dingzhou as its ninth patriarch and was titled Grand Master Yuanming.
In the Dharma Hall, he said: "Deshan has three phrases of speech to show you all. One phrase covers heaven and earth."
*Kūn*. One phrase cuts off the flow of all streams; one phrase follows the waves and drifts with the current. How do you distinguish between them?
If you can distinguish them, you have the capacity for study and practice. If you cannot distinguish them, you will simply roll along the streets of Chang’an.

It is also said: "Only study the living word; do not study the dead word. If you can realize it beneath the living word, you will remain forever unobstructed for eons. Every speck of dust is a Buddha-land."
"A single leaf is one Śākyamuni" is a dead word. "Raising an eyebrow, blinking an eye; pointing a finger, holding up a fly-whisk" is a dead word.
"Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—there is no further confusion" is a dead word. At that time, a monk asked, "What is a living word?
He replied, "A Persian looks up. Baizhang Zixiang received the Dharma from Yunmen. After he took up residence [at Baizhang], he once asked a monk:
"Without destroying conventional designations, one speaks of the true reality. How do you understand this?
The monk pointed to a chair and said, "This is a chair. Xiang struck the chair with his hand and said, "Bring me my shoe bag.
The monk had no reply. Xiang rebuked him, saying, "This hollow-headed fellow! When Men heard of this, he remarked, "It must have been my brother Xiang who did it."
(Gengxu) On the second day of the eleventh month in the third year of Qianguyu (952), Chan Master Chang’er Xingxiu passed away.
He was a dharma heir of Xuefeng Yicun and an incarnation of the Buddha Dingguang. On this day, the King of Wuyue, Qian Hongchu, offered a vegetarian feast for the monks on his birthday.
There was a Chan Master named Yongming, who was likewise an extraordinary man. When King Wu asked Ming, "Is there currently any true monk appearing?

he replied, "The 'Long-Eared Bhikṣu' is the emanation-body of Dīpaṃkara Buddha. The King hurriedly prepared his carriage to go pay his respects. Upon arrival, he addressed him as "Dīpaṃkara Appearing in the World.
The Master remained silent, saying only, "Yongming is too talkative. A short while later, he sat in the lotus posture and passed away; such was his manner.

As he lived on, his skin became increasingly supple and moist, and his nails and hair grew back. He maintained the three-month purification ritual every month, and at times, *śarīra* (relics) were found [in his remains].
Later, when he encountered Jin troops invading the borders, they wounded him with blades; the blood flowed white, and the soldiers retreated in fear.

From then on, the texture of his flesh lost its luster, so he had his skeletal body coated with lacquer. His posthumous title was Great Master Zonghui. [End of entry for] Hui-ming. Next is [the entry for] Chan Master Yuanzhao.

The Dharma-eye and the Mind-seal. At the initial hut at Damei, when a Chan practitioner came to inquire about the clarity [of his realization], [Zhaozhou] asked him, "Where have you recently departed from?

He replied, "Chengdu. [Zhaozhou] said, "If you, the Senior Monk, have left Chengdu to come to this mountain, then Chengdu is deficient of the Senior Monk, and this place has a surplus of the Senior Monk.
If there is a surplus, then there are dharmas external to the mind; if there is a deficiency, then the mind-dharmas are incomplete. This is speaking in terms of principle.
He remained there for a while; when they did not reach a mutual understanding, he departed. The assembly had no response. He later moved to Tiantai.

There was a senior monk named Mingyan, who prided himself on his sharp discernment. He came to visit Ming. Ming asked him, "Among all the sages of antiquity and the former worthies, were there any who did not attain enlightenment?
Mingyan replied, "How could there be any among the sages and former worthies who did not attain enlightenment? Ming said, "When one person awakens and returns to the source..."
He declared, "The ten directions, situated in emptiness, shall all utterly perish. Raising his hand, he pointed and said, "Right now, Mount Tiantai stands majestic;
how can it be made to perish? Yan opened his eyes wide and stared fixedly at him before fleeing. Later, he moved to Ba’en Temple in Hangzhou.
In the third year of the Qianguo era, the King of Wuyue invited him into his palace and questioned him on the Dharma, attaining a profound and secret resonance with the Way.
(Xin Hai) Chan Master Daoyan Preaching the Dharma at the Imperial Palace.
Daoyan was the son of the Wang family in Hezhong. Initially, he went to visit Wenyi, who asked him, "Apart from your formal inquiries and requests for instruction, what sutra are you studying?
Daoyan replied, "The Avataṃsaka Sūtra. Wenyi asked, "As for the six aspects—totality, particularity, sameness, difference, formation, and disintegration—to which category do they belong?"
[Cheng] said, "The text is found within the 'Ten Stages' (Daśabhūmika) chapter. According to principle, all phenomena—both mundane and supramundane—possess the six characteristics.
[Qian] asked, "Does emptiness (*śūnyatā*) also possess the six characteristics? [Cheng] remained silent, offering no response.

[Qian] said, "You asked me, yet Qian instead asks whether emptiness possesses the six characteristics. [Cheng] said, "Emptiness. Thereupon, Qian attained awakening and prostrated in gratitude. [Cheng] said, "You..."

"How do you understand this? [Fayan] said, "Empty. Fayi agreed with him. On another day, as men and women entered the monastery, Fayi asked Xuanqian, "The Vinaya states that if one hears the sound of hairpins and bracelets from across the wall, it is called breaking the precepts.
Seeing gold and silver intermingled, and seeing people dressed in red and purple crowding together—is this breaking the precepts or not?
[Xuanqian] replied, "What an excellent way of entry! Fayi said, "In the future, you will have [disciples]."

A group of five hundred practitioners of the *kṣauma* (woolen robe) school were held in high esteem by kings and nobles. [The Master] secretly took his leave and traveled to an ancient temple in Quzhou, where he read the Tripitaka.

While once sitting in meditative absorption (*dhyāna*), he beheld Mañjuśrī manifesting his form. Later, when he went to Hangzhou to pay homage at the Aśoka Stūpa, he knelt and placed it upon his head;
tears fell like rain. Suddenly, he saw a *śarīra* relic appear outside the hanging bell. Grief and joy welled up within him simultaneously. Furthermore, he once...
After practicing the *Samantabhadra Repentance* for twenty-one days, he suddenly saw the elephant of Samantabhadra beneath the triple gate of the temple.

The elephant’s trunk extended directly toward the place where he was performing the repentance. On the *xinhai* day, the King of Wuyue invited him into his palace and conferred upon him the Bodhisattva Precepts.
Yanzhao avoided the rebels at Yingzhou; once the rebellion was quelled, a man surnamed Song and titled Grand Master (Taishi) of Ruzhou donated his residence to establish a Buddhist monastery.
He was invited to reside at Zhao. In the first year of the Guangshun era, the temple was granted the name Guanghui;
its Dharma seat became preeminent throughout the land. (Renzi) Chan Master Huiyong of Nanyuan passed away (he was the Dharma heir of Xinghua Jiang and the third generation of Linji).

Huiyong resided at Nanyuan and entered nirvana in the Renzi year. Initially, when Huiyong ascended the hall, those from all quarters were fully prepared for the "simultaneity of the chick pecking and the hen breaking the shell."
At that time, Master Yan did not possess the function of "the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching. A monk asked, "What is the simultaneous act of pecking and hatching?
Yan said, "A master does not peck or hatch; pecking and hatching are both lost at once. The monk said, "This is still not where I was asking.
Yan asked, "Where were you asking? The monk said, "Lost. Yan then struck him. The monk did not accept this, and later, while at Yunmen’s assembly...
Hearing these two monks recount this story, one monk said, "At that time, why did Nan-yuan’s staff break?
That monk suddenly attained awakening and immediately returned to pay his respects. By then, Yongyong had already passed away, so he went to see Yanzhao.

Yanzhao asked, "Are you the one who at that time questioned the former master about the 'simultaneity of the pecking and the hatching'? He replied, "I am. Yanzhao asked, "How did you understand it then? He replied:
"I was like someone inside the shadow of a lamp at that time," [Zhao] said. "You understand!
Yanshou, having received the prediction of enlightenment from Deshao, reflected upon his two former vows; unable to decide whether to advance or retreat, he subsequently ascended the Rock of Zhiyi.
He prepared two slips of paper as lots: one read "Single-minded Meditative Concentration" (*citta-ekāgra-dhyāna*), and the other read "All Good Deeds Return to the Pure Land.
Drawing them at random, he did so seven times and each time obtained the lot for "All Good Deeds Return to the Pure Land. From then on, he devoted himself single-mindedly to pure practices.
In the second year of the Zhuguang era, he entered the world to reside at Xuedou, where students gathered like the spokes of a wheel.
(Jia-yin) Chan Master Daohan resided at Yongming during the first year of the Mingde era.
In the first year of the Mingde era, Qian Hongchu, the King of Wuyue, was commissioned by imperial decree to construct a great monastery within the Southern Palace,
named Huiji Yongming (which is the present-day Jingci Monastery), and invited Daohan to preside over it as its first abbot.
(Bingchen year) Chan Master Zhìhuī of Chóngyún entered nirvana (the fourth generation of the Caodong school, successor of Băishuǐ Rén).
Zhìhuī resided at Chóngyún for over forty years. During his humble days, the Military Commissioner Wáng Yànchāo had once followed Zhìhuī.
Yu wished to become a śramaṇa. Senghui gazed at him intently and said, "Your worldly karmic ties are deep; you shall serve as the boundary wall for my family.

Later, Chao indeed governed Yongxing and performed the rites of a disciple toward Senghui. In the summer of the third year of the Xiande era, Senghui went to Yongxing to part from Chao and entrusted him with the protection of the Dharma.
Chao wept and said, "Master, can you truly bear to abandon your disciple? Senghui smiled and said, "I borrow..."
"A thousand years is but another parting. On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, he wrote a verse, saying:

"I have a small cottage, built for me by my parents. For eighty years I have come and gone within it; Lately, I have noticed it is falling into decay. I had intended to move elsewhere long ago, But such matters involve likes and dislikes.
I shall wait until it collapses of its own accord, So that neither side shall be hindered. Thereupon, he sat in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
He passed away at the age of eighty-four, having spent sixty-four summer retreats.
(Wu-wu year) Chan Master Wen-yi of Qingliang entered nirvana (the first generation of the Fayan lineage, successor to Dizang Chen).
While Wen-yi resided at Qingliang, those from distant regions who admired his Dharma traveled great distances to reach him. This was in the fifth year of Xian-de.

In the seventh month of that year, he manifested a slight illness. On the fifth day of the intercalary month, he bathed, took leave of the assembly, and passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture.

His remains were kept in the stupa for twenty-one days; his countenance remained as if alive. He was seventy-four years old and had completed fifty-four summer retreats. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at Danyang.

Imperially posthumously titled Dàfǎyǎn (Great Dharma Eye). Tàiqīn initially resided at Shuanglín in Hóngzhōu. After Wényì passed away, the Li ruler invited Tàiqīn to succeed him. He ascended the hall and said:
"This mountain monk originally intended to dwell in the mountains to hide his ineptitude and spend his time nursing his illness.
However, because my late master has a case that remains unresolved, I have come forth to settle it for him. If anyone asks..."
He then spoke as if to him. At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "What is the unresolved case of the former master?
Qin struck him and said, "The patriarch has not settled it; the calamity reaches his descendants. The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie?
He replied, "The fault lies with me; the calamity reaches you. Lord Li asked calmly, "What unresolved case did the former master have?"

He said, "I am manifesting analysis. The Master was startled by this. Lingyin Qingsong went to study under Wenyi. Wenyi pointed to the falling rain and said, "Every drop falls right into the eyes of the Venerable.
At first, Song did not understand the meaning. Later, while reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he attained awakening and received Wenyi’s seal of approval.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the ten directions are always before you; do you see them? If you say..."
Seeing. Is it seeing with the mind? Is it seeing with the eyes? Therefore it is said: "All dharmas are neither born nor extinguished.
If one can understand in this way, the Buddhas are ever present before one. ○ Baizhang Daoheng studied under Wenyi.

Once, while seeking instruction, he recounted the story of the non-Buddhist (tīrthika) who asked the Buddha: "I do not ask about words; I do not ask about wordlessness. Before he had finished speaking, Wenyi said: "Stop!"
"Abiding. You intend to go toward the World-Honored One; will you remain for a long time at the assembly? Always enter awakening from this. Abiding at Baizhang, he ascended the hall.
An ancient said: 'The ten directions gather together; each and every one studies non-action. This is the field for selecting Buddhas;
when the mind is empty, one passes the examination—how does one return? What is the empty mind? It is not that place of sitting coldly with eyes closed. This is the mind."

"Emptiness. This is precisely the conceptual understanding of the mental consciousness (*manovijñāna*). One must realize that the mind is empty; simply by recognizing the mind itself, one sees that the mind is empty.
Therefore it is said: "The past has already passed; do not calculate the future. Sit upright and without concern—when has anyone ever called you?
Even if someone were to call out to you, "Venerable Sir," whether you respond to them or not, if you respond with "Yes," [you have missed the point].
"Who is calling for the Elder? If you do not respond, it is not that you suffer from deafness; rather, the substance of the three periods of time is empty.

Furthermore, I am no mere block of wood. Therefore it is said: 'When the mind is empty, one can see the Dharma King. Do you see the Dharma King? It is simply this old, sick monk. On another occasion, he ascended the hall.
As soon as the assembly had gathered, he said, "Go drink tea. At other times, when the assembly had gathered, he would simply say, "Adieu."
"Chóng! Sometimes, when the assembly had gathered, he would simply say, "Rest. Later, there was a verse that said: "Bai Zhang has three secrets:
'Drink tea,' 'Be careful,' 'Rest. Receive this directly; I dare guarantee you have not yet reached the end. Yunju Qingxi succeeded to the Dharma of Fayen.
The messenger Liao entered the hall and saw the offering of a *fayan* (Dharma-eye) fruit. He asked, "What kind of fruit is that before you, Zhen?
He replied, "It is a false fruit. Liao said, "Since it is a false fruit, why do you use it to make an offering to Zhen?
He replied, "I simply want the messenger to recognize what is false."
(Gengshen) Chan Master Wuyin of Heishan in Jizhou entered nirvana. (A dharma successor of Jiufeng Qian. Wuyin resided at Heishan.
In the Gengshen year of the Jianlong era, he manifested a slight illness and ordered his attendant to open the abbot’s quarters.
Assembling the great assembly, he said, "Those who come later as students do not yet know Heishan; recognize him right now! Thereupon, he passed away with serene composure.
The posthumous title for his character was Miaoxiang (Wondrous Appearance). Regarding Fayuan: he resided at Xuedou, and the number of monastics and laypeople who took refuge in him was immense.
In the first year of the Jianlong era, when the King of Wuyue saw that Lingyin Temple was in ruin, he invited Fayuan to restore it.
(Xin-you) Chan Master Daoyan of Yongming entered nirvana. (The Dharma heir of Fayan Yi; the second generation of the Fayan lineage. Daoyan resided at Yongming.

On the [blank] day of the ninth month in the second year of Jianlong, he passed away. At the time of his enshrinement in the coffin, a white light radiated during the day, witnessed by the entire assembly.
During his cremation, the śarīra relics were beyond counting. There was a butcher who, reflecting upon his own evil karma, [was moved].
He moved about and, approaching the fire pit, wept and begged for [the seeds]. In a short while, he obtained seven grains.
○ Chan Master Yanshou resided at Yongming;
as the seat at Yongming was vacant, the King of Wuyue invited Yanshou to serve as abbot. The assembly reached two thousand people, and he was then titled "Maitreya."
Descending from the hall, he ascended the seat. A monk asked, "What is the wondrous purport of Yongming? He replied, "Add more incense. The monk said, "Thank you for the instruction.
He replied, "Be glad that there is no connection. The monk bowed. Shou said, "Listen to this verse:
'If you wish to know the purport of Yongming, / Before the gate is a lake of water. / When the sun shines, radiance arises; / When the wind comes, waves stir. He then addressed the assembly.

Those who study today mostly prefer to seek intellectual understanding and reconciliation. How could this be ultimate understanding? It serves merely to dispel emotional attachments. Such discourse exists only to shatter attachments.

Once emotions have dissolved and attachments are exhausted, where would the discourse and its understanding remain? The true nature is vividly clear; it is quiescent, with nothing to be preserved or extinguished.
Therefore, to speak of "identity" or "non-identity" is to fall into the duality of right and wrong; to momentarily hang onto "existence" or "non-existence" is not [the truth].
Right Mindfulness. Thus the Great Master, the Third Patriarch, said: "As soon as there is right and wrong, one becomes distracted and loses the mind.

At that time, a monk asked: "If one engages with existence and non-existence, both become deviant thoughts; if one involves the subject and object, one falls entirely into existence and non-existence.
What is right mindfulness and knowing? He replied: "The auspicious grass grows in a fortunate season; the lotus blooms in early spring. Two monks came to visit Shou.
The Master asked the head attendant, "Have you ever been here before? He replied, "I have. He asked again, "Has the second senior monk been here?

He replied, "He has not. Shou said, "One has gained; the other has lost. A short while later, an attendant monk asked, "I do not know which of those two monks from just now was the one who gained and which was the one who lost.
Shou said, "Have you ever known these two monks? He replied, "I have never known them. Shou said, "Then you yourself have both gained and lost."
He said, "Those in the same pit share no different soil. He once said to a monk, "This mind is neither horizontal nor vertical;
it is neither other nor self. How do we know this? If one says it contains all phenomena, that is horizontal. If one says it gives birth to all phenomena, that is vertical.
If one says it arises from itself, how could the mind further give birth to a mind? If one says it arises from another, that is not possible."

As for the phrase "how much more so" (*ji shen*): could there be anything else? If you say they arise through co-arising, then since self and other do not even exist [independently], with what could there be co-arising?
If you say they arise without cause, one should consider that even when a cause exists, we do not permit the claim of arising; how much less so can it be said they arise without cause?

Furthermore, it is said: the Buddhas, according to conditions and distinctions, respond to the various capacities of sentient beings, giving rise to the good and destroying the evil, causing them to enter [the Way].
The ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*) is a conventional expression of the four kinds of *siddhānta*. It is like using an empty fist to show something to a small child;
how could there be any real dharma therein? The monk asked, "In that case, are all dharmas the mind? He replied, "If it were so, then duality would be established.
The monk asked, "In that case, is nothing established, being neither [existent nor non-existent]? He replied, "To say 'neither' also establishes duality. Have you not heard?"
Śūraṅgama said: "I am truly Mañjuśrī, yet there is no such Mañjuśrī. If there were such a one, there would be two Mañjuśrīs. However, today I am not without Mañjuśrī;
within this, there are truly neither the marks of 'is' nor 'is not. [The interlocutor] asked: "Since there are no dual marks, is it permissible to speak of 'one'? He replied:

"To speak of 'is' and 'is not' already deviates from the Great Principle; to speak of 'one' and 'two' likewise turns one's back on the Perfect Teaching. [The interlocutor] asked: "As for [the state of] suchness..."
“What kind of mental application is required to accord with this principle? “Answer: When both object and wisdom are forgotten. “How can one speak of ‘accordance’ [if they are forgotten]? “Answer:

In such a state, the path of speech and thought is severed, and the way of mind and intellect is cut off. “Answer: This too is but forced speech; it merely turns according to the intentions of others. Though one wishes to conceal one’s form, the traces have not yet been forgotten.
“How can one attain the forgetting of both form and trace? “Answer: Fundamentally there are no traces. How could there be [any forgetting]? How could there be [any attainment]?”
[The Master] spoke of forgetting. [The disciple] said, "I understand it now. It must be like a person drinking water; they know for themselves whether it is cold or warm.

At the moment of great awakening, one must spiritualize and clarify it. [The Master] said, "In this gate of mine, there is neither the principle of delusion nor awakening, nor clarity or lack of clarity.
'Letting go of your hands, you have not a single thing. To labor in vain and speak in a thousand ways—this matter is not for those of inferior capacity."

"A person of great capacity. No one was able to shoulder the burden of the former masters. It is said: "If one were to search throughout the entire ten-direction universe for a single person to serve as a companion, none would be found.
It is also said: "There is only this one person who inherits and succeeds to the ancestral seat; ultimately, there is no second person.

If you have not yet personally arrived at this realization, you will merely exhaust your mental faculties in vain. Even to speak of it as "the profound within the profound" or "the wondrous within the wondrous" is merely a gate of expedient means.

In the midst [of this], there are peripheral words that assist one in entering [the path]. When one personally contemplates from within one's own state, looking back upon them, they are all seen as demonic teachings—vain and floating minds, full of clever insights that cannot bring about the realization of Perfect Enlightenment (*pariniṣpanna-bodhi*). They merely take the forms of words and traces;

when such literary elegance arises, it is entirely clinging to the gates of expedient means (*upāya-mukha*) while being deluded regarding the true path. One must, like the hundred... [as before]... [continue].
"Only when you let go of yourself at the tip of the one-footed pole can you proceed. [The student] said, "I pray that you grant me your final word.
[The Master] said, "A conjured person asks a phantom man about the sound of a valley echo; the answer is the sound of a spring. To convey my fundamental purport: a clay ox walks upon the water."

Jiǎzǐ (Beginning from the second year of Qiándé of Emperor Taizǔ of the Song dynasty) Wùchén (Renamed Kāibǎo) Bǐngzǐ (The first year of Tàipíngxíguó of Emperor Tàizōng) Jiǎshēn (Renamed Yōng)
Xih (Wuzi—reign name changed to Duangong); Gengyin—reign name changed to Chunhua; Yiwei—reign name changed to Zhidao; Wuxu (the first year of Emperor Zhenzong’s Xianping era);
