Renwu (the 7th year of Taiping Xingguo). In the seventh year of the Taiping Xingguo era, Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty issued an edict to establish the Translation Court in Dongjing, following the precedents of the Tang dynasty, and appointed high-ranking ministers as Commissioners for the Translation and Polishing of Scriptures.
(甲子) Chan Master Guangzuo resided at Zhimen. He was a native of Zhejiang.
Having entered Sichuan to study under Xianglin Chengyuan, he received the seal of the mind. Upon returning, he took up residence at Zhimen in Suizhou.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I remember, while still in my mother’s womb, there was a saying; today I shall bring it forth for you. Great!
"O assembly, you must not engage in rational deliberation. Is there anyone who can deliberate upon this?
If it cannot be deliberated upon, do not err when citing it thirty years hence. [The Master] Xi Ji, whose courtesy name was Changzhao, was the son of the Hu family of Yongjia.
When his mother first became pregnant, she had no desire for pungent foods or blood. Upon his birth, there was an object covering his head, resembling a purple cap.

He left the household life and received full ordination, studying *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā* at Qingsong. He once lamented that the scriptural texts of the Tiantai teachings had frequently been destroyed by war and fire, leaving those who transmitted them without a reliable basis.
He then earnestly petitioned Master Daoshao, saying, "The teachings of the Great Master Zhiyi have passed through many years and are now mostly scattered and lost.
Only in the kingdom of Silla are the original texts complete. Were it not for the compassionate power of the Venerable Master, who could possibly bring them here? When Daoshao heard this, he...
Regarding King Wu Yue: one day, while the King was reading the *Yǒngjia jí*, he came across the passage stating, "Those who simultaneously eliminate the four abodes are equal to this [state];
if they merely suppress ignorance, their realization is inferior. He questioned Shao about it, and Shao replied, "This is a matter of doctrinal interpretation."
"You may ask Xi Ji. The King summoned Ji and questioned him. Ji replied, "This appears in the *Miaoxuan* (Wondrous Profundity) section of the works of Zhiyi.
It was said that at the end of the Tang dynasty, the Buddhist scriptures were dispersed abroad and no longer exist here.

In the second year of the Qiande era of the Song dynasty, Your Majesty dispatched an envoy, carrying the letter from Shao, to the kingdom of Goryeo to transcribe them; they have now been returned complete. The King then built [a monastery] for Ji.
At Sijiaoxi, he was granted the title Jingguang. There was a master named Ming of Xingjiao who, though only in his early twenties, often expressed doubt while attending the sutra assemblies, saying:
"Kāśyapa held Śākyamuni’s robe, which was only six feet tall, yet it covered the body of Maitreya, which was a hundred feet high."
"It should fit its measure exactly. Is it the robe that is long, or is it the body that is short? He then went to Yunju to ask Shao.
Shao said, "Dharma Master, you have already understood this yourself. Ming shook his sleeves and withdrew. Shao said, "This young fellow—if I were to answer you, it would not be right;
there must be cause and effect. If you are not [right], I shall see to it. Ming returned to Luoxi. His mouth—[remained silent].
He immediately spat up blood. Jingjue was startled and said, "This newly ordained monk has come to offend a Bodhisattva. Ming recounted the previous conversation.
Jingjue said, "You have not understood the National Teacher’s meaning. Go quickly and repent! Ming then approached him with full decorum and, weeping bitterly, said:
"I pray that the Upādhyāya will, out of compassion, grant me permission to repent. Yaoshan said, "It is like a person who falls to the ground and rises from the ground;
I have never taught you how to rise from a fall. Dayue Ming said, "If you grant me permission to repent, I shall serve you for the rest of my life.
Yaoshan then composed a verse: "The Way of all Buddhas is equal, yet appears as high or low; Śākyamuni and Maitreya are like seals pressing into clay. From this point on, Ming served him.
He recovered from his illness and returned to thank Jì, saying, "Had it not been for the Master’s instruction, I would have nearly lost this life.

When the Hermitage Master Xiáng of Lotus Peak on Mount Lú received the essential meaning from Fèngxiān Shēn, he addressed the assembly while residing at the hermitage, saying: "If it concerns this matter, it is most urgent;
one must clearly realize it before it can be attained. If you can realize it within the midst of daily life, you will avoid being bound by constraints."
One attains ease wherever one is; furthermore, there is no need to suppress the mind with effort. One must naturally accord with the ancient tracks before one can succeed.
As soon as you reach the stage of formal training, you must immediately manifest this principle so that the Buddha-dharma may find rest in its proper place.
Elder, please take this to heart. Furthermore, whenever I bring up [this matter]...
Holding up his staff, he said, "When the ancients reached this point, why were they unwilling to stay? For twenty years before and after, not a single person could answer.
As he was about to pass away, he provided the answer on their behalf, saying: 'Because they cannot find strength on the road. He then asked again, 'Ultimately, how is it?
Once more, crossing the staff over his shoulder, he provided the answer on their behalf: 'Carrying the knotted staff across my shoulder, I do not look back at anyone.'"
"Go straight into the thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. Having finished speaking, he passed away (Bingyin year).
Chan Master Weishan resided at Fuchang.

Having attained enlightenment through his studies under Master Kuan, he took up residence at Fuchang Temple in Jingnan. He was revered and dignified, and he cherished the Dharma with great secrecy and gravity.
When Dao first resided there, there were only some ten or so rooms and a few remaining monks. Yet, he was diligent in offering incense at dawn and lighting lamps at dusk;

when he ascended the seat to preach the Dharma, it was as if he were facing a thousand-fold assembly. It took more than ten years before his disciples finally gathered, and those from all quarters came to revere and submit to him.
(Wucheng) Master Zhifeng resided at Pumen.
Having attained realization under Deshao, he was appointed by the King of Wuyue, Qian Hongchu, to reside at Gongcheng Mountain and was granted the title Pujue.
At the beginning of the Kaibao era, the King further established the Pumen Jingsha and invited him to expound the essentials of the school. [Yitong], whose courtesy name was...

Wei Yuan, surnamed Yin, was of noble lineage from the kingdom of Goryeo. His physical features were extraordinary: he possessed a *uṣṇīṣa* upon his crown, and his eyebrows measured five or six inches in length.

When he reached China at the age of twenty-something, he studied under De Shao and attained awakening. Subsequently, upon visiting Xi Ji, he suddenly clarified the principles of the "one mind and three contemplations.
After some time, he suddenly took leave of his fellow students, packed his belongings, and set out for the East. On his way, he made a detour through Siming.
As he was about to board a sea vessel, the Prefect Qian Weizhi earnestly detained him and stopped his departure.

In the first year of the Kaibao era (968), the Canal Commissioner Gu Chenghui converted his residence into a Chanjiao Monastery and invited Tong to reside there. He further bestowed the monastic name "Baoyun" upon it.
( gengwu) Biography of Chan Master Yanzhao. Xingnian was the son of the Di family of Lai Prefecture.
He was a man of simple gravity and refined discernment, who specialized in the practice of dhūta austerities.

As soon as he had received full ordination, he traveled extensively among monastic assemblies. He constantly recited the Lotus Sūtra in secret, and because of this, the community came to call him "Nian Fahua" (Lotus-Chanting Nian). Upon reaching...

While staying at Yanzhao’s assembly, he followed the crowd in their activities and did not engage in any private inquiry. Nevertheless, he always harbored doubts that there was a distinct transmission outside the teachings.
Yanzhao often reflected on the prophecy concerning Dayang, which stated that the Linji school would come to an end with Feng; he feared that he might be the one destined by it.
He gazed intently at those seated below and thought, "None among them is fit to carry on the Way of the Dharma like Nanian.
One day, as Nanian was standing in attendance, Zhaoming shed tears and said, "Alas, the Way of Linji has reached me and is about to fall to the ground.

Nanian replied, "Looking at this assembly, is there truly no one? Zhaoming said, "Those who are clever and quick-witted are many, but those who have realized their own nature are few. Nanian said, "If that is so..."
"What about such-and-such? Zhaoming said, "Although I have long looked forward to you, I still fear that you may be so attached to this scripture that you are unable to let it go.
[The student] thought, "This is indeed a matter of concern; I wish to hear its essential point. Zhaoming then ascended the hall and said:
"When the World-Honored One looked upon the great assembly with his blue-lotus eyes—at that very moment, tell me, what did he say? If you say 'nothing'..."
He spoke and spoke. Furthermore, he was burying the former sages. Before his words were finished, Nian suddenly descended from the seat.

Returning to the abbot’s quarters, Master Zhao asked the attendant, "Why did Nian not respond to the Abbot? The attendant replied, "He understood. The next day, Nian and Zen Yuan-tou went together to pay their respects.
As they were inquiring after the Master's health, Zhao asked Zen, "What is it that the World-Honored One did not speak?"
Zhao said, "The magpie cries at the top of the tree. Zhen asked, "Why do you perform so much 'foolish merit'?
Why do you not investigate the meaning of these words? He then asked Nanian, "How about you? Nanian replied, "Moving the countenance reveals the ancient path;
one does not fall into the trap of a sharp, abrupt mechanism. Zhao said to Zhen, "Why do you not look at Nanian’s phrasing from the *Lotus Sūtra*? On another day...
When Huizhao ascended the seat, he looked over the assembly and then descended immediately. Huizhao returned to his quarters.

After receiving Huizhao’s seal of approval, Huinian vanished his traces and concealed his brilliance; no one knew his whereabouts. One day, when Chuzhi of Baizhao arrived at Xuanhua in Ruizhou, Huizhao ordered Huinian to go and deliver a message.
As soon as they met, Huinian held up his sitting cloth and asked: "Is it this unfolding? or "Is it not?"?
Zhengyan said, "This very thing is it. Chushi said, "Look for yourself. As soon as he spoke, Zhengyan gave a shout.
Chushi said, "I have personally attended upon spiritual teachers; I would never dare to act so recklessly. Zhengyan said, "The grass-robbers are utterly defeated.
Chushi said, "If I see Master Fengxue tomorrow, I shall report this to him in detail. Zhengyan said, "Do as you wish, but do not forget."
Nian first returned and reported this to Zhao. Zhao said, "Today you have again captured another bandit. Nian replied, "A skilled hand does not advertise its name.
The next day, Chu arrived and met with him; as soon as he was seen, he recounted the previous conversation. Zhao said:
It is not only that he was caught for his embezzlement yesterday or today; rather, it is because his name has been renowned throughout all quarters.

(When Linji took his leave of Guishan, Yangshan was attending at his side. Guishan asked Yangshan, "What will become of this man's Dharma path in the future? Yangshan replied, "This man's Dharma path will spread widely in the future. In the regions of Wu and Yue, he will stop wherever he encounters wind. Guishan asked again, "Who will be his successor?

Yangshan said, "There will indeed be one, but as the time will be long and distant, I do not wish to mention him to you, Master. Guishan pressed him, saying, "I also wish to know. Yangshan replied, "Does the Sutra not say: 'With this profound mind, serve the dust-motes and lands; this is what is called...'"?)* *Note: The passage ends mid-quote from the *Avatamsaka Sūtra*, verse 28.10, which continues: "...this is what is called making offerings to all Buddhas.'"*
He repaid the Buddha’s kindness. Thus it is known that Xingsheng was the later incarnation of Yangshan.
(Xinwei year) National Teacher Deshao passed away (the Dharma heir of Fayan Yi; the second generation of the Fayan lineage).
Deshao resided at Tiantai, where his Dharma path flourished greatly. In the fourth year of the Kaibao era, the western peak of Huading suddenly collapsed, and a sound [resounded].
The entire region was shaken. In the sixth month, a star fell upon the summit of the peak, and all the trees turned white.

On the twenty-eighth day, Shao suddenly gathered the assembly, took his leave, and passed away. He was eighty-two years old; he had spent sixty-five summer retreats [in the monastic community]. Hongshou first studied under Deshao.
One day, while serving as a laborer alongside Deshao, he attained awakening upon hearing the sound of a piece of firewood falling. He composed a verse, saying: "The falling strike is not..."
"Other things—whether horizontal or vertical—are not dust. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth: all fully reveal the body of the Dharma King. Shao gave his seal of approval.
Later, while residing at Xingjiao Temple in Hangzhou, Prime Minister Wang Sui, serving as Censor-in-Chief, was dispatched to govern Qiantang.
One day he went to visit [Zhao]shou; having reached the lakeside, he dismissed his attendants and walked alone up to the master’s quarters. At that moment, Shou was just carrying...

It was warm. [Hanshan] sat as usual, wrapped in his coarse woolen robe. Suddenly seeing him, the official asked, "What is your surname, sir? He replied, "I follow my surname. The official immediately prostrated himself.
Hanshan pushed aside his rush mat and sat on the ground with him. They conversed and laughed for the entire day before the official departed.

A disciple protested, saying, "That was a king's minister who came; why did you not offer him a formal greeting? This is a matter that concerns the entire community and is no small affair. On another day, Suixing...

He came again. The monks of the temple struck the great bell crosswise, and Wanxiu went out to welcome him with his ten thousand fingers. However, Huishou had already stepped forward and was standing beneath a pine tree.
Seeing him from afar, Wanxiu hurriedly descended from his carriage and took hold of his hand, saying, "Why do you not meet me as you did on the previous day?
Why have you suddenly adopted such formalities? Huishou looked to his left and right, and as he walked, he said, "The Minister may well do so; it is only that the monastery officials..."
As for Chenhe Suoyi, he was a man of Henan whose courtesy name was Zizheng. He lived his life admiring the character of Pei Xiu.

Having studied under Chan Master Shengnian, he attained the meaning beyond words. As he observed Hongshou’s own practice, his own realization grew ever deeper until he ultimately clarified the Great Dharma.
At the time of his death, he wrote this verse: "The lamp in the painted hall has already been extinguished; Pointing my finger, to whom shall I speak? Going and staying are fundamentally [empty]..."
**Changchun (常春)**: "The spring breeze sweeps away the lingering snow. **Yuan'an (遇安)**: He served Master Deshao as his teacher. While reading the *Śūraṃgama Sūtra*, he came to the passage:
"When knowledge and vision establish knowledge, this is the root of ignorance; when knowledge and vision are without seeing, this is nirvāṇa. Yuan'an then read it by breaking the phrasing:
"Knowledge and vision establish / Knowledge, this is the root of ignorance / Knowledge and vision are without / Seeing, this is nirvāṇa."
At this, he had an awakening. Someone said to Hui’an, “The verse has been broken. Hui’an replied, “This is the place where I attained realization;
I shall not change it for the rest of my life. This was called "An’s *Śūraṅgama*. Later, he resided at the Upper Hall of Rui鹿 Temple in Wenzhou.
(Ren-shen) Chan Master Daoquan resided at Jiufeng.
Daoquan was the son of the Liu family from Anfu. Having shaved his head, received the precepts, and heard of the reputation of Changsha Huilun, he longed to see him.
At that time, the Ma clan had usurped control of Jingzhou and Chu; Daoquan, being over twenty years of age, formed a friendship with a companion and ventured there despite the dangers.
When the Ma family exterminated Wang Kui, they took over his duties. Upon seeing Sengquan and his companions, Kui suspected them of being spies;

he bound them and intended to throw them into the river. Sengquan remained composed and showed no fear. Kui was struck by this and asked Daolun, "This practitioner looks upon death as if he were merely looking at the tip of his nose.
What kind of person can be so? Daolun replied, "He is one who has cast aside his own body for the sake of the Dharma."
The man heard of the old monk’s reputation for being a hollow name and came specifically to resolve his doubts. Daokui explained the matter to him, but Huizhuan departed with an air of arrogance.
He stayed with Shuilun at Yanshou Monastery for ten years; after Shuilun passed away, Huizhuan returned to Mount Lu. In the fifth year of the Kaibao era, he resided at Jiufeng.
A monk asked, "I have heard that you, Master, personally saw Yanshou—was this true? He replied, "Has the wheat ripened in front of the mountain yet? The monk asked again.
"Is there still Buddha-dharma within the mountains of Jiufeng? He replied, "There is. [The Master] asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma within the mountains of Jiufeng?
He replied, "The large stones are large; the small stones are small."
(Guiyou) Chan Master Yanzhao of Fengxue passed away (the Dharma heir of Nanyuan Yong and the fourth generation of Linji).
Yanzhao resided at Fengxue and loudly proclaimed the Way of Linji; at that time, there was no one who could match his spiritual acuity.
On the first day of the eighth month in the sixth year of the Kaibao era, he ascended the seat and spoke this verse: "The Way lies in seizing the opportune moment to save all beings. Far...

Those who have recently come to admire him are already overflowing with devotion. In years to come, there will be elders whose sentiments resemble his: incense smoke rising day after day and lamps burning night after night.
On the fifteenth day, he passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. On the preceding day, he had written a letter of parting for his lay patrons. He was seventy-eight years old.
Xia Wu (590): Zhen Yuantou. Initially, he studied under Yanzhao. Yanzhao once asked him, "When the Huichang persecution of the Dharma occurred, where did the Dharma-protecting benevolent spirits go?
Zhen replied, "They are always in the midst of the marketplace; yet, for all that, no one sees them.
Yanzhao said, "You have reached thorough penetration. Later, he resided at Guanghui.
(Jiaxu) Chan Master Yongan Enters Nirvana (The Third Generation of Fayan, Dharma Heir of Tiantai Shao).
Yongan received the Dharma from Deshao. He resided at Ba’en Monastery in Hangzhou. In the seventh year of the Kaibao era, he addressed the assembly to take his leave. At that time, a monk asked:
"In the past, the Tathāgata’s True Dharma Eye was personally transmitted to Kāśyapa; I wonder about the Master’s profound style."
"How will you understand this after a hundred years? [The monk] said, "Where do you see Kāśyapa coming from? [The Master] said, "If that is so, then you shall believe, accept, and practice it;
you must not forget this principle. [The Master] said, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of such [intellectual] principles.
Having spoken, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away. At his cremation, his tongue remained unburnt, supple, and like a red lotus flower.

Master Shōnen of Shushan: Having received the Great Dharma from Fengxue, Master Shōnen of Shushan opened the Dharma at Shushan in Ruzhou; scholars bowed before his reputation like grass bending to the wind.
He was the first patriarch. Upon entering the hall for the formal lecture, he said: "The Buddha-dharma has been entrusted to kings, ministers, and powerful patrons so that it may not be severed.
From lamp to lamp, it has continued down to this day. Tell me, assembly, what is it that continues?
After a long silence, he said: "It must be my elder brother, Kāśyapa. A monk asked: "What is the Buddha? He replied: [He remained silent].

"The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it. [A monk asked: "I do not know in what phrase this saying is contained. [The Master said: "It cannot be contained within the Three Mysteries;

how could the Four Phrases encompass it? [The monk asked: "What is the meaning of this? [The Master said: "Heaven is long and earth is enduring; the sun and moon shine together. Furthermore, a monk asked:
"What is the underlying intent of 'the daughter-in-law rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it'? [The Master said: "An old man of a hundred years."
Nanquan lost his father. [The monk] asked, "A hundred-year-old man—how could he have a father? Nanquan said, "You understand.
He added, "This is solitary sitting, where there is neither high nor low; from the beginning, not a single dharma has been given to anyone.
One night, a monk entered the room. Nanquan asked, "Who is it? The monk did not answer. Nanquan said, "I recognize you. The monk laughed. Nanquan said, "Could this not be someone else?"
He then composed a verse, saying: Treading lightly on the ground for fear others might know; Your speech and laughter are clear—do not doubt them further.
O wise one, extract it with vigor this very moment; Do not wait until dawn when you lose the rooster.
(Yi Hai) Chan Master Yongming Yanshou Manifested Birth in the Pure Land (Dharma Heir of Tiantai Shaokang; Third Generation of Fayen).
Yanshou resided at Yongming for fifteen years. He had one thousand seven hundred disciples.

He once conferred the Bodhisattva precepts upon the assembly, provided food for ghosts and spirits, released various living creatures, scattered flowers during the six periods of the day, and daily recited one hundred and eight items of practice.
When scholars came to inquire of him, he stood like a wall ten thousand fathoms high. He took the pointing to the mind as his school and awakening as his standard.

By evening, he would go to a separate peak to practice the Way and recite the Buddha’s name, never ceasing regardless of cold or heat; he considered this too difficult for others to sustain and did not wish to force them to do so.

Nevertheless, those who followed him in secret often numbered in the hundreds. On clear nights under a bright moon, the sounds of conch shells, celestial music, and [divine voices] were occasionally heard from the sky.
As for the sound [of his passing], the King sighed every time, saying: "Since ancient times, there has never been one from the West whose earnestness and sincerity have reached such a degree.

He specially constructed the Xiangyan Hall to fulfill the Master's aspiration. On the twenty-sixth day of the second month in the eighth year of Kaibao, he rose at dawn, burned incense, addressed the assembly, sat in the lotus posture, and passed away. He was seventy-two years old and had forty-two years of ordination. His remains were cremated.

Lìshòu’s entire body was covered in scales. Because the three schools—Xiánshǒu, Cí'ēn, and Tiāntái—were as incompatible as ice and charcoal and had not attained a comprehensive understanding of the Great Canon, Lìshòu housed those among their disciples who were refined in the principles of the Dharma within two pavilions. There they extensively read various texts and engaged in mutual debate;
Lìshòu then took the Mind-essence school as his standard to weigh and harmonize them. Furthermore, he compiled sixty sections of Mahāyāna sūtras and śāstras.

He compiled three hundred works by sages and worthies from India and this land to substantiate the principle that all is but mind, totaling one hundred fascicles titled the *Zongjing lu* (Record of the Mirror of the Source).
He also authored the *Wanshan tonggui ji* (Collection on the Convergence of Myriad Good Deeds) and other works, all of which circulate in the world.
(Dingchou year) Master Jingqin entered nirvana. (The second generation successor of Yunmen Wenyan. Jingqin resided at Shuangfeng.
In the third month of the second year of the Taiping Xingguo era, he said to his disciples, "You may build a 'egg-shaped' pagoda.
On the twenty-third day of the fifth month, the work was completed. Jingqin said, "Tomorrow, at the hour of the rat, I shall depart."

When the appointed time arrived, the attendant reported that it was the third watch. Yunqin then requested incense to be burned; with palms joined, he passed away. Yuan De resided at Yuan Tong on Mount Lu.
During the Song dynasty, an imperial envoy was sent to demand his submission. Hu Ze, the Governor of Jiujiang in Jiangnan, held the city and refused to surrender.
When the troops of General Cao Han crossed the river and entered the monastery, the practitioners fled in terror, but Yuan De sat in meditation as before.
On an ordinary day, Zhang Han arrived while [Zhao]de was not rising from his seat. Enraged, he scolded him, saying, "Elder, have you not heard of the General who kills without batting an eye?
De gazed intently at him and said, "How do you know there is no monk who does not fear birth and death? At this, Han was struck with alarm and trepidation.
He sighed in admiration and asked, "For what reason did the meditators disperse? De replied, "They gathered when the drum was beaten.
Han sent out an auxiliary general to beat it again, yet none of the meditators arrived. Han asked, "Why did they not come? De replied, "You have a murderous intent; that is why they did so."
He himself struck the drum, and the practitioners of meditation gathered. HAN bowed twice and asked for a strategy to ensure victory.

Zhide replied, "This is not something known by those who practice meditation. On the day of Dingchou in the tenth month, Zhide ascended the seat and said, "Today is the day I shall sever all worldly ties.
I leave behind my patched robe and the wooden sandals I wear, entrusting them to the mountains, and have my disciples pile up green stones [to mark the site]."

A stupa was erected for him. He said, "In the future, when this stupa turns red in color, I shall return. Thereupon, he passed away peacefully at the age of eighty, having spent sixty-three years as a monk. His posthumous title was Daoji.
(Wuyi) Chan Master Daoqi resided at Yunju.
He was the son of the Jin family of Nanchang. Whether walking in meditation or sitting in contemplation, he was concerned that he had not yet clarified his own fundamental matter.

Carrying a single alms bowl, he traveled extensively through the monastic communities. At that time, Fatai Qin was residing at Shanglan; Daoqi went there to rely upon him. Qin appointed him to oversee the Sūtra Library.
One day, [Tian]yi said to [Feng]qi: "Suppose someone asks me the meaning of the Westward Journey; I would answer him, 'Neither east nor west.
Master Zang, how do you understand this? Qi replied, "Neither east nor west. Yi said, "If you understand it in this way, how can it be right?
Qi said, "I say that Qi is simply like this. I wonder, however, what your own venerable intention is, Master? Yi said, "He has his own descendants. — Qi.

Thereupon, he suddenly clarified its essential meaning. He spoke in verse: "In surpassing excellence beyond meeting beings and benefiting life; throughout my life I have been unworthy compared to others.
My own descendants shall be used in the future; when the time is right, one shall emerge from the world as a Great Fool. Later, he moved to Yunju.
He said to his disciples: "Dharma said that among the scriptures of this land, only the *Laṅkāvatāra* can serve as a seal for the mind.

When I read the verses of this sutra, they say: 'All phenomena have no intrinsic nature; it is taught that they are nothing but mind. Failing to see one's own mind, one gives rise to conceptual discrimination.
This may be called the most profound discourse on reality by the Great Compassionate Father. It is simply that we ourselves fail to receive it."
One bears a debt of gratitude as vast as the sands of the Ganges. Someone may ask: "In that case, does seeing one's own mind immediately sever conceptual discrimination?
He replied: "It is not so. It is like training a horse; when the horse sees its own reflection, it is not startled. Why?
Because it knows that the reflection has emerged from its own body. By this I know that one must sever conceptual discrimination, and furthermore, one must relinquish it."
This is the characteristic of the mind. Observe it right now, as it truly is, before you. You will not see even a hair’s breadth of the Patriarchs. The Master said:
"If you see the present, you should also see the past and future. If you do not see the past, you should likewise not see the future or the present.
These words are clear; yet people remain deluded and ignorant. Zhi Li (Zhilie), courtesy name Yueyan, of the Jin clan of Siming.
My son, at first, when my parents had no heir, they prayed to the Buddha. In a dream, a divine monk appeared carrying a young boy and presented him to them, saying, "This is the Buddha’s son, Rāhula.
Thereupon she became pregnant. She left the household life, received full ordination, and studied under Baoyun, attaining realization through the Tiantai teachings.
(辛未) From the time Venerable Sajam resided at Hwangseoksan, he was the son of the Zheng family of Tongam.
He traveled to visit Yunhwa, where he remained for five years and secretly received the teachings of the mind-dharma.

His speech was eloquent and expansive. When he crossed the Huairen River, there was a *jiao* (water monster) that harmed travelers; when Yan recited a verse to admonish it, the *jiao* immediately departed.

Passing through Huangyang Gorge, he became thirsty and wished to drink, but the stream had run dry; Yan plucked at it with his staff, and water appeared. At Wuping, Huangshi Rock was infested with snakes and tigers;
when Yan arrived, he could command the snakes and tigers to obey him. He once ordered the monks of a neighboring temple to die, yet Yan himself did not [die].

Knowing the Dharma, he informed the authorities and then set himself on fire. The officials pursued him; when they caught him, he sat in the courtyard while his case was being investigated. He did not answer, but instead took paper and composed a verse:
"The wild monk outside the clouds has died; The wild monk outside the clouds has been burned. These two dharmas are without distinction; The path to Bodhi is not far.
His calligraphy was bold and forceful, like large seal script carved in deep grooves. The officials were greatly enraged, considering him a madman, and he departed.
The *saṃghāṭī* was left out in the midday sun. Once it was released from its folds, he used it to cover his head and dressed himself in white robes.
(Guiwei year) [This concludes] the biography of Chan Master Shenian.

Shanzhao, whose Dharma lineage was transmitted by [Shenian], was the son of the Yu family of Taiyuan. His capacity and insight were profound and far-reaching; regarding all forms of written literature, he did not rely on the instruction of teachers.

He naturally attained profound understanding. At the age of fourteen, he shaved his head and received full ordination. Carrying his staff, he traveled to various regions, staying briefly wherever he went.
He took no pleasure in sightseeing; some criticized him for lacking aesthetic refinement. Daoshao sighed and said, "How vulgar are such words!

Since the ancients first practiced *fangjia* (wandering on foot), it was precisely because their sacred minds had not yet attained full realization that they hurried about to seek discernment. It was not for the sake of mountains and rivers. Thus he journeyed on.

I studied under seventy-one old masters, all of whom I mastered their respective lineages. Yet, until the end, I harbored doubts that the descendants of Linji possessed some other extraordinary quality.
Finally, I studied under Xingnian. One day, as Xingnian ascended the seat, Zhao stepped forward and asked, "What is the meaning of Baizhang rolling up his mat?
He replied, "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the entire body is revealed. Zhao asked, "What about your own intention, Master? He replied:
Where the Elephant King walks, the tracks of foxes vanish. Upon these words, he attained great enlightenment. He bowed and rose, saying:

"The moon in the empty expanse over the ten-thousand-year-old azure pool—only after searching and grasping again and again does one finally come to know it. Someone asked, "What principle did you perceive that you were so immediately convinced?
He replied, "This is precisely where I surrendered my body and life. Congxian received the mind-seal from Fayen and resided at [the monastery].

At Guanyin Monastery on the [blank] day of the ninth month in the year Guiwei, the Elder addressed his patron, Yuan the Court Historian, saying, "In two or three days, this old monk shall return to my hometown.
Yuan asked, "The Master is advanced in years; why do you still long for your hometown? He replied, "I am returning to my hometown to seek out fine salt to eat.
Yuan could not fathom these words. The following day, he passed away while sitting upright, free from ailment.
(Biyou) Master Zhifeng Entered Nirvana (The Third Generation of Fayan, Dharma Heir of Tiantai Shao).
Zhifeng resided at Huayan Monastery on Wuyun Mountain. Whenever he went out, he would carry a large fan to beg for money, which he used to buy meat to feed tigers.
A tiger would always meet him and carry him back to the mountain. In the second year of the Renshou era (985), he passed away in peace.

*Record of Master Shengnian’s Transmission of the Dharma to Yuanlian:* Yuanlian was a native of the Chen family in Quanzhou. Initially, he relied upon Zhengjue, where he daily attended to the cooking fires. At intervals, he would recite the sutras. Zhiguo...
A question was asked: "What sutra are you reciting? He replied, "The Vimalakīrti Sūtra. Jue said, "The sutra is right here; where is Vimalakīrti?
Liau was completely at a loss for an answer. He wept and said, "When a great man is questioned by another, to have no words to offer—is this not shameful?
Thereupon, he visited over fifty venerable masters in succession, but found no accord with them. He then went to Shoushan to seek instruction.
Chongnian asked, "From where have you recently come? Lian replied, "From Hanchang. Chongnian raised his fist and said, "Is there such a thing as this in Hanchang?
Lian said, "What kind of bowl is this that makes a ringing sound? Chongnian said, "Blind! Lian said, "Exactly! and with a single clap, he departed.
On another day, Chongnian asked again, "When a student reaches the Jewel Mountain in person but returns empty-handed, what then?"
[Zhaozhou] said, "A torch held before every door. At these words, Liai attained great enlightenment and said, "I no longer doubt the tongues of the old monks throughout the world.
[Zhaozhou] asked, "How is it that you have understood? Tell me and let me see. Liai said:
"It is simply water-calcite from the earth. [The Master] said, "Do you understand? Liai then prostrated himself. ○ Daoquan resided at Jiufeng.
In the ninth year of the Taiping Xingguo era, he moved to reside at Guizong. On a day in the eleventh month of the second year of the Yongxi era.
At midnight, he sat in the full lotus posture and passed away amidst the assembly.
(Bingxu) The Biography of Chan Master Shengnian: Having received the transmission of the Dharma, he returned to his home province.
He was the son of the Jia family from Jizhou; he left the household life, received full ordination, and traveled to visit various masters until he met Shengnian. One day, Shengnian raised [a koan]...

[Master] Zhuhui held up a bamboo stick and asked, "If you call it a bamboo stick, that is 'contact' (touching). If you do not call it a bamboo stick, that is 'aversion' (turning away). What shall you call it?
Xingche seized the stick, threw it to the ground, and said, "What is this? Nanquan said, "Blind! At these words, Xingche attained great enlightenment.

Wu'en, whose courtesy name was Xiujǐ, was a native of the Lu family from Chángshū. He left home to become a monk in his youth and maintained the practice of eating only once a day throughout his life. He did not... [text ends].
He remained apart from his robes and bowl and did not accumulate wealth or treasures. When lying down, he always lay on his right side; when sitting, he always sat in the full lotus posture.
During every *poṣadha*, his tears flowed incessantly. He universally instructed others in the pure practices of the Western Paradise and the perfect meaning of the One Vehicle (*ekayāna*).

To those who harbored doubts or whose capacities were not yet ready, he replied: "I am merely providing them with the conditions for the 'poison drum'. On the first day of the eighth month of the year Yiyou, at night, he beheld a white light emanating from...
Jingchu said to his disciples, "I am about to depart. He then ceased eating grain and refrained from speech, single-mindedly reciting the Buddha’s name.
In a dream, he saw a śramaṇa holding a golden incense burner and burning incense, who circumambulated his room three times and declared, "I come to welcome you for the consecration (abhiṣeka).

Upon waking from the dream, his disciples arrived; they still smelled a wondrous fragrance. On the twenty-fifth day, he expounded upon the essential points of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā*, as well as the contemplation of the mind.
Having finished his discourse on the meaning [of the teachings], he sat upright and passed away. People heard the sounds of pipes, strings, bells, and chimes resonating clearly in the air;

they gradually faded and receded, departing toward the west. Upon cremation, the *śarīra* relics were beyond counting. Initially, the lineage of Jingxi was transmitted through five generations to Qingsong.
Song transmitted it to Xiji and Zhiyin. Thereafter, it split into two schools. Ji transmitted it to Yitong, and Tong transmitted it to Zhixian.

Lizunshi received the transmission from Zhijin; En received it from Zun; Hong received it from En; Min received it from Yuan; Qing received it from Qing; Zhiyuan received it from Qing; Qingshao received it from Zhiyuan;
and Jiqi received it from Qingshao. Each followed their respective teachings, and Zhili established them as the "School Outside the Mountains" (Shanwai zong).
(Dinghai year) Chan Master Chengyuan of Xianglin Monastery entered nirvana (the second generation successor of Yunmen Wenyan).
Chengyuan had resided at Xianglin in Qingcheng for forty years. In the second month of the fourth year of the Yongxi era, as he was about to pass away:
At the age of eighty, Yuan went to take leave of the Prefect, Song Dang, saying, "I, an old monk, am going on pilgrimage. The Vice Governor said, "This monk is mad;
at eighty years old, where do you intend to go on pilgrimage? Dang replied, "A great spiritual teacher has the freedom to come and go as he pleases.
Upon returning, Yuan addressed the assembly: "It took me forty years to finally achieve integration. Having spoken these words, he passed away.
Yunmen received countless disciples; among those who practiced the Way in his generation, only the lineage of Xianglin was most flourishing.
When Yanzhu resided at Nan'an Shan, he regretted that those who heard his teachings were divided between doubt and faith, and consequently remained silent for six years.
Yanshi was required to deliver cloth [as tax]. The commoners paid this in his stead year after year. Yanshen could not bear it; he placed the cloth inside a bundle and prayed for exemption.
The officials Zhang Ye and Ouyang Cheng looked at one another in great anger. They pursued him and questioned him about the circumstances, but he did not answer.

Thinking it was a supernatural fire, they noted that the hat he wore was bright and fresh. Yanshen took paper and composed a verse, saying: "The power of universal compassion and patience is all mine..."
Born from the mind, he was constrained by the suffering of officials and kings, and the Buddha-dharma did not circulate.

From this time on, he also spoke to ○ Xiji at Yanfalou Creek, where the Tiantai school flourished greatly. On the [blank] day of the eleventh month in the fourth year of the Yongxi era, he fell ill and passed away.
He left an injunction forbidding weeping or the offering of memorial sacrifices. Having spoken these words, he immediately closed his eyes. ○ Xingjing and Xingshao were both natives of Qiantang.
He entered the monastic order together with Tongyi Yanshou and resided at Shibi. At that time, the Dharma path of Deshao was flourishing greatly; Jingshao followed him there.
Deshao, observing that he was a vessel for the Dharma, sent him to study the Three Contemplations at Luoxi. Before long, his studies were complete, and he returned to Shibi.
For fifty years, from beginning to end, he never once traveled among the villages and towns. [This concludes the biography of] Jingshao. Next is Qian Tang.
Ren (Renxiao). Initially, he transmitted the Way of Xi Ji, refining his study of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā*.
Later, he studied under De Shao, through whom he realized the profound mysteries. (Wuzi year) Dharma Master Yitong of Baoyun Monastery manifested birth in the Pure Land.
(A successor of Xi Ji in the Tiantai school) Yitong resided at Baoyun and propagated the teachings and contemplations for nearly twenty years. He once addressed people as "countrymen," saying:
"I regard the Pure Land as my native home; all of you shall surely be reborn there, for you are all people of my homeland.

Those who ascended the hall and received his teachings were beyond counting. On the eighteenth day of the first month of the first year of the Duan-gong era, he passed away reclining on his right side.

His body was cremated, and the resulting śarīra relics filled the bone stupa located in the northwest corner of Ayuwang Temple. Later, when the stupa collapsed, the bones were moved [to another location]. Its...
The bone crystals were brilliant and luminous; the śarīra relics were five-colored and grew upon the bones. Some obtained enough to fill their cupped hands.
○ Zunshe’s courtesy name was Zhibai. He was the son of the Ye family of Ninghai. His mother dreamed of swallowing a bright pearl before giving birth to him.
After he left home to receive full ordination, he went to study under Yitong. On the way, he dreamed of an elderly monk who said, "I am Master Mañjuśrī. Upon waking...
His vision was clear, as vivid as a dream. Before long, he attained realization through the Tiantai teachings. Tongru entered *parinirvāṇa*.

Shi returned to Tiantai, where he fell ill due to his arduous studies. He employed dhāraṇī-mantras for subjugation and made a vow, saying: "If the propagation of the Four Teachings is to be my responsibility, may this illness be cured;
otherwise, I shall end my life here. When the seven weeks were complete, a voice from the air said: "The Buddhas of the ten directions..."
The Buddha said, "May your merit and lifespan increase. That evening, he saw a giant holding a vajra, which he pointed at his mouth.
Guanyin extended her hand into his mouth and drew out several worms; she then poured down nectar, and his chronic illness was instantly cured.
(Year Jichou) The Biography of Chan Master Shengnian’s Transmission of the Dharma to Zhisong.
Zhisong was a native of Fanyang. While traveling to seek instruction, he visited Shengnian and asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?"
It is said: "On the outskirts of the city of King Chu, the River Ru flows eastward; there is a provincial inspection post at Mount Song. He then composed the *Three Mysterious Verses*, saying:
"If you must use it, you must use it directly; let not the mind and intellect waver or stir. When the three-year-old lion roars, the fox species vanish from the ten directions.
I possess the nature of True Suchness (Tathatā), as if hidden behind a curtain. Break through the gates of the six sense-doors, and the seal of Vairocana is revealed. The True Bone.
"The Vajra-body may be praised; with a single sweep of the six sense-objects, they are forever unobstructed. The vast and empty world takes emptiness as its essence;
within that essence, non-action is truly arriving home. Nianwen then invited him for tea. He asked, "Are these three verses composed by you? He replied, "Yes.
[Nianwen] said, "Suppose someone were to instruct you: when the thirty-two marks of a Buddha are manifested, what then? He replied, "I, this person, do not..."
"This is a wild fox spirit," [Nanquan] said. [Shoushan] said, "I would rather spare my eyebrows. [Nanquan] asked, "How many have you lost?
He then struck Shoushan on the head with his bamboo staff and said, "This fellow will cause trouble hereafter. Shoushan took his leave of Nanquan.

"It is in my hands," [Huangbo] said. "Do not involve me in this entanglement. Desheng struck his meditation mat once and said, "As expected, you have involved me.
