The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all wisdom? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all wisdom. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all liberation? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all liberation. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all knowledge and vision of liberation? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all knowledge and vision of liberation. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all bodhisattvas? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all bodhisattvas. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all sravakas and pratyekabuddhas? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all sravakas and pratyekabuddhas. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all worldly dharmas? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all worldly dharmas. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all supramundane dharmas? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all supramundane dharmas. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all dharmas of the past, present, and future? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all dharmas of the past, present, and future. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all dharmas of the beginningless and endless? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all dharmas of the beginningless and endless. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all dharmas of the conditioned and unconditioned? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all dharmas of the conditioned and unconditioned. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all dharmas of existence and non-existence? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all dharmas of existence and non-existence. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student transcends all dharmas of being and non-being? He replied, "The Great Image transcends all dharmas of being and non-being. The monk
The Master replied: "An iron ox was drenched with water at Shanfu. He asked: "What is the point of intimacy for a student? He replied: "A lion is played with in Xihe. Zhao said:
"If one understands these three phrases, one has already mastered the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan). There are further words of the Three Essentials (Sanyao) remaining;
it is vital that you realize them. This is no ordinary matter. He then offered a verse for the assembly: "The matters of the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials..."
Difficult to distinguish. When one attains the meaning and forgets the words, the Way is easy to approach. A single phrase clearly encompasses the myriad phenomena;
on the Double Ninth, the chrysanthemums are fresh. Do you understand? If you understand in such a way, it is not a matter of impulsive temperament.
How should a patch-robed monk understand this? Again, he raised the words of the Three Mysteries, saying: "Do you understand the timing of the Three Mysteries? You must truly grasp them."
Only after grasping the intent of the ancients will your own mind become clear; furthermore, you will attain mastery in adaptive transformation and enjoy inexhaustible benefit.
This is called the Buddha of Self-Enjoyment Body. Without relying on the teachings of others, one recognizes it and secures one’s own livelihood.
Thus Nanquan said, "When I was eighteen, I already knew how to manage my livelihood. A monk then asked, "The ancients at eighteen..."
The Master said, "I understand how to make a living, but I do not know what kind of living it is. He replied, "Two water-buffaloes with no halter for their double horns.
He further said, "If you wish to attain clarity regarding this, you must first grasp the essential purport of the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan).
Only then will you be able to enjoy it without hindrance, celebrating within yourself and fulfilling your life's purpose. You who are great men—"
The teaching causes one to blame oneself; when encountering matters, one lacks penetration. Since it provides no benefit or salvation, I present for you all these verses:
The First Mystery: The Dharma-realm is vast and boundless; the myriad phenomena and all things are entirely complete within the mirror. The Second Mystery: The World-Honored One asked Ānanda;
with extensive learning, he answered according to the circumstances, his capacity matching the measure of the vessel’s circumference. The Third Mystery: Directly emerging from antiquity.
"Your Majesty: Beyond the four propositions and the hundred negations, Master Lü asked Fenggan. Zhao then said: 'This is a verse on the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan).
What is the essential meaning of these Three Mysteries? You must resolve this with absolute clarity.
Do not merely look into the empty air and falsely interpret it by saying, "I have personally attended the Master; he explained it to me," while offering nothing but empty words.'"
"If you deceive others with your words, there will come a day when you must swallow iron rods; do not say I did not warn you. Furthermore, while picking chrysanthemums, he said to the assembly:
"Golden flowers carpet the earth; jade stamens support the heavens. The bright sun hangs in the sky, making heaven and earth radiant. Clouds rise to bring rain; dew condenses to become frost.
Without violating the principle of things, I shall utter a phrase. Come, can anyone speak it? Is there anyone who has attained it?"
If you cannot say it, there is a speck of dust in your eye; you must simply remove it before you can attain it. Therefore, Fengxue said:

"If you establish even a single atom of dust, the state will flourish and the country will prosper, yet the village elder will frown. If you do not establish even a single atom of dust, the state will perish and the country will fall, yet the village elder will be at peace.
If you understand this clearly, it has no part in you, O *śrāmaṇera*; it is entirely the old monk. If you do not understand this clearly, the old [monk...]
The monk is the *ācārya*. The *ācārya* and this old monk can both enlighten the people of the world, and they can both blind the people of the world.
Do you wish to know the old monk and the *ācārya*? [He] pats his knee and says: "This here is the *ācārya*; this here is the old monk.
Now, ask you all, venerable seniors: Are the old monk and the *ācārya* the same, or are they different?
If you say they go together, then the senior monk is the senior monk and this old monk is the old monk. If you say they go separately, yet you also say that this old monk is the *ācārya*.
If you can clarify this point, then within a single phrase there are the three mysteries and the three essentials;
guest and host will be clearly distinguished, your lifelong task will be accomplished, and your studies as a seeker will be complete. Therefore, Yongjia said:
"To grind one's bones to powder would not suffice to repay a single phrase; it is clearly transcendent beyond billions [of worlds]. He also said:
"One day, the two head monks of Linji’s two halls met face-to-face and both let out a shout. A monk asked, "Does Linji still have guest and host?
He replied, "Guest and host are perfectly distinct. Zhao composed a verse on this: "The head monks of the two halls are both masters; the principle therein..."
The *yǒufēn* (share of the dharma) is distinct between guest and host, as clear as a mirror; the Master merely points out the flowers in one’s eyes.
(Year Yiwu) Zen Master Yu’ān of Shàngfāng entered nirvana (the third generation of Fǎyǎn, successor of Tiāntái Sháo).
Yu’ān resided at Ruìlù in Wēnzhōu. In the spring of the first year of Zhìdào, he was about to pass away. His disciple Yùnrén attended him.
An stood up and spoke a verse to instruct him, saying: "This is not something carried from the mountain peak; how could it have been transmitted from Mount Kukkuṭapāda?
Since ancient times, all sages and worthies have been like this; it is not I who am fashioning it for you today.

Having finished his instructions, he bathed himself, changed his robes, and sat upright, ordering the coffin to be carried to the chamber. After a long while, he entered the coffin himself. Three days later, his disciples opened the coffin.
Seeing that Dao’an was lying on his right side, the fourfold assembly wailed in grief. Dao’an rose again, ascended the hall to preach the Dharma, and rebuked them with solemn admonitions:
"Those who open my coffin a second time are not my disciples. Having finished speaking, he entered the coffin once more and passed away forever.
Daoben was the son of the Zheng family of Yongjia. From childhood, he was unwilling to remain in the secular world. At the age of twenty-five, he left home to receive the precepts.

He visited Master Deshao, who guided him with the dialogue concerning the wind and the banner; he attained enlightenment upon hearing these words. He served him diligently for ten years. In the year Yiwu (1035), he resided at Rui鹿 (Ruilu) in Wenzhou.
His feet never stepped into cities or towns, his hands never handled wealth or silk, he did not provide bedding, and he did not wear silk garments.

He ate only at the hour of the Rabbit (the morning meal), remaining in seated meditation throughout the day. From evening until dawn, he instructed and exhorted his disciples. This continued for over thirty years. His...
His resolve became even more intense. He said to the assembly, "When I first saw [Zhili] at Tiantai, I attained realization upon his words.

Yet for a thousand days, throughout the four modes of deportment, it was as if something were obstructing my chest, like living with an enemy. One day, I suddenly had a profound awakening, as if washing my face and touching my own nose.
I composed a verse, saying: 'It is not the wind or the banner that moves; it is your own mind that moves. From of old..."
The transmission has continued down to the present day. Hereafter, those who wander like water and clouds should understand that the Patriarch was truly a connoisseur of the sound.
He also said: "If one sees the mind upon seeing form, it will be difficult to answer when someone comes to question you.

If you seek to explain it through various principles, you will betray the three matters of your lifelong patched robe. He further said: "From vast kalpas past, it has always been thus; it remains thus."
Heaven is the same as earth. When heaven and earth are one, what form can there be?
What form is it that is not so? (Bingshen) Minister Zheng visited Chan Master Shanzhao.
Shanzhao was residing at Fenyang. When Minister Zheng arrived, they engaged in a conversation over tea. Minister Zheng presented this verse: "Let the yellow paper no longer obscure [the truth]."
"The eye: the blue clouds naturally possess their own shade. Do not bury the heart of the Patriarch with the intellectual interpretations of idle scholars.

He further said, "Use this very verse to test the elders throughout the land. [The student] said, "In that case, even Fenyang is included within it. He replied, "Carrying the cangue, you pass the indictment. [The student] said, "There is no need for further examination.

He replied, "A double layer of legal case. [The student] said, "If one knows, then one attains it. Zheng [Yuanzuo] remained silent for a long time. Zhao [Chongyin] [said]: *Note on terminology: "Cangue" (擔枷) refers to a wooden neck-shackle used as punishment; "passing the indictment" (過狀) implies being found guilty. "Double layer of legal case" (兩重公案) suggests a complex, unresolved matter.*
He let out a sigh. Zheng said, "Wenbao, Wenbao. [The Master] asked, "Where is he? [Zheng] replied, "How could he bear it when I could not even get my breath out?
He said, 'The Elder has been detained here. [The Master] asked, "What words are those? [Zheng] replied, "They are true.

[The Master] said, "You must not let him go. [Zheng] requested, "Please grant me a verse, Master. [The Master] said, "I am not familiar with paper and ink," and then composed and showed him this verse: "Abandoned..."
Seeking secluded paths amidst the grass, the pines on the crags spread their shadows far and wide. How many seekers of the profound mystery have lost their original mind! Zhizong resided in Bingfen.
When Director of Works Zheng arrived, Zheng said, "The Chan Master Shanzhao of Fenyang loves to read books.

He then left behind this verse: "Do not let yellow paper blind your eyes; The blue clouds already cast their shadow over your gaze. Do not mistake worldly learning for wisdom; [Otherwise, you will fail to see the Way.]”
[Zhaozhou] buried the patriarch’s mind. [Dongshan] said, "The Minister of Works is accustomed to finding his advantage. [Zhaozhou] said, "This thief! [Dongshan] said, "No further interrogation.
Zheng asked, "When one is atop a hundred-foot pole playing alone with a ball, or when one's waist is bound by a silken cord at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom precipice—what then?
[Dongshan] said, "Planting your feet in Youzhou; wrestling in Guangnan. Zheng was speechless. Song said, "I have thoroughly exposed this barbarian. [Zhaozhou] said, "Two."
For ten years within the realm of Jiangnan, this time we finally see the Chan Master say, "A blind old woman blowing on fire.
(Dingyou year) Chan Master Yunju Daoqi entered nirvana. (He was a Dharma heir of Faden Qin; the third generation of the Fayen lineage.
Daoqi resided at Yunju for twenty years. In the ninth month of the third year of Zhidao, he manifested illness. On the eighth day, at the hour of Shen.
He ordered the drum to be beaten to assemble the multitude. When the assembly had gathered, he smiled and recounted the origins and details of his renunciation.
He then bowed in thanks to those present at the gathering and said: "This old monk, being pressed by the elements of wind and fire, has come specifically to meet you all.
But where do you see me? Do you see me in the four great elements and five aggregates? Or do you see me in the six sense bases and twelve sense fields? It is in these seeds..."
The place of their planting cannot be seen; who, then, is it that questions me now? If you can truly see this, it may be said that future students will have something to rely upon.
After a long silence, he said: "After my passing, you should entrust the affairs of the monastery to Qihuan.
He then passed away. ○ Chengzhi was a native of Jianning. He succeeded Baidang Daoheng and resided at Qixian. A monk asked: "The immortal Vimokṣa held onto goodness..."
Cai Shou said, "I see all the various Buddhas as fine motes of dust. [The Master asked,] "When you had not yet grasped my hand, what did you see?
Zhi said, "What do you see now? Zhi was by nature lofty and simple; he disciplined himself with rigorous strictness, and his actions never contravened the laws and measures [of propriety].
In his later years, he recited the Tripitaka three times. He considered reading while seated to be a lack of reverence, so he would stand while reciting and walk while perusing the texts.
(Gengzi) Chan Master Jingxuan resided at Dayang.

He was the first son of the Zhang family of Jiangxia; he left home to become a monk in his youth. While listening to the *Nirvana Sutra on Perfect Enlightenment*, he asked the lecturer, "What is meant by 'Perfect Enlightenment'?
The lecturer replied, "'Perfect' takes the harmonious integration of the tainted as its meaning; 'Enlightenment' takes the exhaustion of all things without remainder as its meaning. Jingxuan laughed.
He said, "To empty all existence and non-existence—what is this called but Perfect Enlightenment? The lecturer sighed and said, "This child is young in years, yet his insight is so preeminent.
What I possess is not enough to benefit him; it would be just like placing foul food into a precious vessel—is that appropriate?"
While traveling, Xuán visited Liángshān Yuànguān and asked, "What is the formless site of enlightenment?
Yuànguān pointed to an image of Avalokiteśvara on the wall and said, "This was painted by the scholar Wu. As Xuán was about to offer a response, Yuànguān hurriedly asked, "This one has form;
which one is formless? Xuán then attained realization and prostrated himself. Yuànguān said, "Why do you not..."
Daoqu said a single phrase: "To speak of the Way is not to decline; I fear it would only stain the paper and ink. Guanzhen laughed and said, "These words shall be inscribed upon a stele.
Xuanyan offered this verse: "In my former days as a beginner, I studied the Way in confusion. I sought out knowledge across ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains.

Though I could discern the present and debate the past, in the end I could not comprehend. When told directly that there is 'no-mind,' my doubts only increased further. Now, having received the Master’s pointing-out, [the barrier of] Qin..."
At that time, Jingzhao saw his parents before they were born; as he now awakens to this, what is there to be gained? At night, he released a black chicken that flew away amidst the snow.
Guanzhi considered this sufficient to revitalize the school of Dongshan. After Guanzhi passed away, he took leave of the stupa and left the mountain.

Upon arriving at Dayang, Master Jian joyfully yielded the Dharma seat to him. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The ancient worthy said: 'Tie up the ox and lead it toward the east bank of the stream.'"
One cannot avoid paying taxes and corvée labor to the government; one must lead the ox toward the west bank of the stream.
One cannot avoid paying taxes and corvée labor to the government; it is better to pay a little according to one's means. This will not hinder anything and will prevent unnecessary trouble.

What is the principle of "paying a little according to one's means"? Simply cut off both extremes—the existence and non-existence of all phenomena—and let the conceptualizations of ordinary people and sages be exhausted.
The essence is revealed as true permanence; phenomena and principle are non-dual. This is precisely the Buddha of Suchness (*tathatā*). If one can be thus, then every dharma is without dependence;
it is the Great Path of equality where the myriad existents are unattached, rolling freely wherever one goes.

What further matter could there be? In the third year of the Xianping era, Yunchong visited Jingxuan. Jingxuan asked, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Xiangzhou. Jingxuan asked, "What [have you been doing]?"
"What is the phrase that is not separated [from the truth]? [The Master] said, "It is not easy for an abbot to preside over a monastery.
[The monk] said, "Please sit and drink tea. The attendant asked, "Why did the Abbot, upon the newcomer’s response just now, immediately tell him to sit and drink tea?
[The Master] said, "I offered him a Korean aconite; he repaid me with a shipload of anise from abroad. Go ask him yourself; he has words for you."
The attendant invited Cong to drink tea and asked, "Just now, when you replied to the Abbot that 'the position of a monastic head is not easy,' what was your meaning?
He said, "Brass does not equal gold."
(Xin-chou) Chan Master Yuncong resided at Guyin.
While residing at Guyin, he ascended the hall and said: "Before the fifteenth day, all Buddhas are born; after the fifteenth day, all Buddhas pass away.
Before the fifteenth day, all Buddhas are born—you must not depart from here. If you depart..."
"Here with me. I have a hook to hook you. After the fifteenth day, all Buddhas will pass away; you shall not remain here with me.
If you do remain here with me, I have a锥 (chui) to pierce you. Now tell me: what is it exactly on the fifteenth day?"
"Using the hook is it; using the awl is it. There is a verse that says: "On the very fifteenth day, The hook and the awl cease at once.
If you intend to ask further how it is, Turning your head, the sun has already risen. When Cóng resided at Shìmén, the Prefect, acting on personal whims, flogged and humiliated him.
Upon his return, the assembly of monks welcomed him on the left side of the road. The Head Seat said, "The Prefect was without fault; he was merely yielding to [the circumstances]."
He addressed the Master, saying, "Cōng points to the ground with his finger and says, 'A pile of bones rises from level ground. As he pointed, a mound of earth surged up.
When Shǒu heard this, he ordered it to be scraped away, but it surged back up as before. Later, Shǒu’s entire family perished in Xiāngzhōu.
(Year of the Water Tiger) Dharma Master Zuǎnshì returned to Tiantai.

Having resided at Siming for twelve years, in the year of the Water Tiger, he returned to Tiantai and constructed a vihāra in the western corner, leading the assembly to practice the *Nianfo Sanmei* (Samādhi of Buddha-Recitation).
Zhu Yan served as a judicial secretary (*panguan*) and had long studied the *Haiyan* (Ocean Eye), yet he remained unaware of its full meaning.
Upon entering [the assembly], one day he asked the lecturer-monk Yijiang, "After this body dies, where does this mind go? Jiang replied, "Before this body has died, where is this mind?
Yuanyan attained realization of the essential meaning and composed a verse, saying: "The four elements need not be realized sequentially;
The six sense faculties are empty when they function. It is difficult to present speech or silence to the Master; It lies only in the midst of ordinary words."
While they were silent, Jiang said, "You must still spit it out.
(Jiachen year) Chan Master Yuanlian resided at Guanghui.
Having received the Dharma from Shoushan, he entered the world to reside at Guanghui in Ruzhou. He addressed the assembly: "I was in my late teacher’s assembly..."
In the middle [of the story], he saw [the Master] raise his bamboo whisk and asked, "Does the donkey understand? Xing was enlightened from this point on.
I say that although he was indeed enlightened, he had not yet fully grasped the intent of the former master. These words must reach such a state before one can truly comprehend them;
how could those who have not yet forgotten their emotional views avoid doubt and slander? Furthermore, I see in the *Zhimen Gāngzōng Gē* (The Song of the Essential Principles of Zhimen): "Hu..."
A bee does not pine for its old nest; a fierce warrior will never die at home. [The Master] said: "Brother Zuo, why exhaust yourself with so much effort?
When I usually speak of Chan, it is like a fan in my hand: when raised, there is wind; when not raised, there is not even a single breath.
Since you call yourself a master of the school, why instead give people the actual dharma? It would be better to take a torch and shine light upon them."
"Look! To open one's mouth like this—how thick is that skin? Yantou said, "If one were to give the true Dharma to others, even earth could not contain it.
He further said, "The Buddha-dharma is fundamentally without affairs; all the sages of antiquity were merely feigning strangeness."
The "Strong Birth" program suppresses the worthy and reduces them to the lowly, burying their descendants.
Furthermore, Yunmen, Zhaozhou, Deshan, and Linji died without awakening; throughout their lives, they suffered indignities. Here, this old monk is not like that.
Even if Śākyamuni Buddha himself were to appear, I would exile him to another world to ensure his tracks are severed. Why is this so?
"Relieve your anxieties and cease grieving for your descendants. An old monk speaks thus: if you all can understand it here, will you not be joyful?
It shall enable you to cast off your fur robes and become a free and easy patch-robed monk.
But if you do not understand, there will be new branches next year; the spring wind will continue to trouble you without end. — Yang Yi (style name).

Dadian was a native of Jianning. As a youth, he was designated a "Divine Child" (shéntóng); by his maturity, he bore a reputation for talent and learning, yet he was unaware of the existence of the Buddha.

One day, while passing by a colleague, he saw him reading the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. He laughed and censured him, saying, "How can this possibly surpass the teachings of Confucius and Mencus?

Why is it so excessively sycophantic? His colleague continued reading as if nothing were amiss. Dadian grew suspicious and thought, "Could this perhaps come from beyond the right [of Confucianism]? He then read several leaves himself; only then did he become bewildered and begin to feel a slight sense of awe.

He paid his respects with faith. Later, when he was serving as a Hanlin Academician, Li Weimian ordered him to visit [the master] for consultation. Subsequently, while serving as Director of the Imperial Library, he was sent out to govern Ruzhou;
there, he first went to pay his respects to Yuanlian. He asked, "A cloth drum is being beaten at the front of the hall—who is the one who knows it?

Yuanlian replied, "The wind that comes is deeply discerning. He said, "If that is so, then when Zen guests meet, they simply snap their fingers. Yuanlian said, "A gentleman may be worth eight hundred million in response."
"Yes, yes. Lián said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated. During their conversation at night, Lián asked, "Master Secretariat, with whom have you been discussing matters lately?
[The Master] replied, "I recently asked Chan Master Liang of Yunmen: 'When two tigers bite each other, what then?'"
Liang said, "The 'single unified form' (yī hé xiàng). Mozi said, "I simply keep watching;
I wonder if speaking in such a way is permissible? Liang replied, "It is not so here. Mozi said, "Please, Master, offer another turn of phrase.

Liang made a gesture with his hand as if pulling up a nose-ring and said, "This beast will leap about even more! At these words, Yi was suddenly liberated from doubt. Furthermore, half— [text fragment].
Cai attained a great awakening and composed a verse, saying: "The eight-cornered millstone runs through the void; The golden-maned lion transforms into a dog.
If you wish to hide your body within the Northern Dipper, You must join your palms before the Southern Star. He once asked Lia:
"I recall the Master’s words that all sinful karma arises from wealth and treasure, and you have exhorted people to distance themselves from profit. Furthermore..."
"The sentient beings of Jambudvīpa take wealth as their life; states gather people through wealth. Within the teachings, there are two kinds of giving:
that of material wealth and that of the Dharma. How can you urge people to distance themselves from wealth? [The Master] said: "The iron cage at the tip of the banner pole. He said:
"The stallion at the sea altar is as large as a donkey. He said: "The chicken of Chu is not the phoenix of Mount Dan. He said: "Two thousand years have passed since the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa."
The bhikṣu, possessing little sense of shame, later entrusted a letter to Li Wei, in which he recounted the origins and details of his spiritual lineage, stating:

"This sick man, from his youth, was dull-witted and obtuse, yet I was fortunate enough to receive your favor and patronage. I have long heard the essential teachings of the Southern School and have for a long time accompanied you on your travels through the capital."

Through consultation during movement and stillness, and through guidance and inspiration in every turn, you have enabled those whose hearts were hollow to reach a profound realization, and those who were as blank as a wall to be free of shame;
you truly stand where disciples occupy the space between the mats and beneath the seats.

Furthermore, the Great Master An-gong constantly bestowed his guidance, and we were also graced by the visit of the Great Being Yunmen Liang-gong to this humble retreat. Liang’s essential teaching was precisely the same as that of Master An-gong.
Che and [the other] both came from Nengren Temple on Mount Lu, Guizong, and Yunju; all were descendants of the lineage of Fayan.
Last year, while serving as the acting governor of this prefecture, I happened to meet Guanghui Chan Master, who was the true successor of Shoushan Nian.
Nian succeeded Fengxue; Fengxue succeeded Nan yuan; Nan yuan succeeded Xinghua; Xinghua succeeded Linji; Linji succeeded Huangbo; and Huangbo...
He succeeded Baizhang Hai. Hai succeeded Mazu. Mazu succeeded Master Rang, who was the direct heir of Caoxi.
In the monastic hall, affairs were few; after meals, he had much leisure. Sometimes [the Master] would sit and invite him to come, or at other times he would order his carriage to follow him.

He questioned him in manifold ways, and all his obscurities and blockages were resolved. After half a year, he was vast and free from doubt; it was as if he had forgotten and then suddenly remembered. As if...
Suddenly awakening from sleep, that which had long been a thorn in my breast fell away with a resounding crash; matters unclarified for kalpas on end were suddenly revealed in their vastness.
Thus, there was a thorough and decisive discernment, and no further obstruction in responding to circumstances. Reflecting deeply upon the former masters, I am moved.
Generally, there were many who sought out masters through extensive searching. For example, Xuefeng went up to Dongshan nine times and to Touzi three times before finally succeeding Deshan;
Linji received the Dharma from Dayu but ultimately inherited Huangbo; Yunyan was guided and instructed by Daowu and thus became a son of Yaoshan;
Danxia received the seal of approval from Mazu yet became a descendant of Shitou. Such cases were numerous in antiquity.

This is so; there is no cause for objection in principle. As for the present circumstances of this infirm man’s succession to the lineage, they truly depend upon Guanghui, yet the source of his inspiration and encouragement has properly emerged from Mount Ao.

How joyful, how fortunate! The monk Daoyuan of Wu compiled the records of the patriarchs and Buddhas of India as well as the spiritual encounters of the masters of this land [China] into thirty fascicles titled the *Jingde Chuandeng Lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp of the Jingde Era), which he then presented [to the throne].

It was presented. When the True Emperor (Zhēnzōng) read it, he praised it highly. He issued an imperial decree for Yang Yi and others, Academicians of the Hanlin Academy, to edit and correct the text and compose a preface.
It was then included in the Great Canon (Dàzàng) and circulated throughout the realm.
(Ciming Wuma) Qingpou studied under Chan Master Jingxuan.
Having received the Dharma from Jingxuan, he served as the head gardener at Dayang. One day, while planting melons, Jingxuan asked, "When will the sweet melons be ripe?
He replied, "They are already overripe right now. Jingxuan said, "Pick out the sweet ones and bring them here. He replied, "I give [them all]."
"Who eats it? he asked. "One who does not enter the garden," [Xuan] replied. The monk asked, "I wonder, does one who does not enter the garden eat it or not?
"Do you recognize him? Xuan asked. "Although I do not recognize him, I cannot help but give it to him," the monk said.

Xuan smiled and departed. A monk asked Baofu, "When Sāgara emerges from the sea, heaven and earth tremble; when face-to-face presentation occurs, what is the matter like? Baofu replied, "The Golden-Winged Bird."
The Bird-King presides over the universe. Among these, who is the one who emerges? [He] said: "If you suddenly encounter the moment of emergence, what then?
[He] said: "It is like a hawk seizing a pigeon. If you do not believe me, you shall know it as true only when you verify it before your own skull.
[He] said: "In that case, I shall place my hands at my chest and retreat three paces. [He] said: "That turtle beneath the seat of Mount Sumeru—do not wait!"
Having suffered a second humiliation, he returned to Mount Luofu to see Xianru. At first he visited Xuanyue. Xuanyue asked, "Where are you from? He replied, "Yizhou.
Xuanyue asked, "How many li is it from here? He replied, "Five thousand li. Xuanyue said, "Coming as you have done, have you ever set foot upon this ground?
He replied, "I have not set foot upon it. Xuanyue asked, "Are you able to fly through the air? He replied, "I am not able to fly through the air. Xuanyue said:
"How did you reach this point? "Step by step, I was not lost in direction; throughout my entire being, there was no place for discrimination.
"Have you attained the Samādhi that transcends the quarters? "The Sage’s mind cannot be grasped; how could Samādhi manifest a name? "So it is, so it is."
"You should believe this; thus the fundamental substance is fully manifest. Principle and phenomena are non-dual. Guard and maintain this well.
(Wu-xin) Master Benxian entered nirvana (the third generation of the Fayan lineage, successor to Tiantai Shao).
Benxian resided at Ruiluo, where disciples gathered like spokes in a wheel. In the second month of the first year of the Dazhong Xiangfu era, he addressed his disciples:
The Master said to Dayou, "You may construct a stone niche for me. On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, the Mid-Autumn Festival, I shall pass away.
Dayou received these instructions and completed the work by the fifteenth day of the eighth month. Monastics and laypeople from near and far rushed to pay their respects.

On that day, the Master conducted his formal inquiries as usual. At noon, he sat upright in the abbot’s quarters, formed the *ratnamudrā* (jewel seal) with his hands, and said to Dayou, "An ancient said:"
"Riding the tiger's head, grabbing the tiger's tail—what about the matter in the middle? Zhaozhou replied, "It is also just like Zhaozhou.
Xian said, "You ask me. Zhaozhou then asked, "Riding the tiger's head, grabbing the tiger's tail—what about the matter in the middle?"
The Master first said, "I cannot manage it either. Having finished speaking, he suddenly opened one eye, looked slightly, and then passed away.
(Jiyou year) Chan Master Xiaocong resided at Dongshan.

He was the son of the Du family of Qujiang. He left home to become a monk in his youth; his skull was remarkably prominent, and he wore a single robe through both winter and summer. He traveled throughout... [text fragment ends]
He traveled through the regions of Jing and Chu, where he lived among the local communities, rising and resting with the common folk until no one recognized him.
While at Yunju, he served as the head of the lamp-keepers (*dēngtóu*). There, he heard a monk say that the Monk Sengqie of Sizhou had recently appeared in Yangzhou.
A Zen practitioner then posed a question: "If he is indeed the Monk Sengqie of Sizhou, why has he instead appeared in Yangzhou? Congpo [responded].
Sō came from the side, and the assembly playfully set him up as an opponent. Cōng said, "A gentleman loves wealth, but he acquires it through the proper way.
The assembly looked at him and laughed. Later, a monk reported this to Master Xiáng of Lotus Peak. Xiáng was greatly surprised and exclaimed, "The descendants of Yúnmén still exist!
In the middle of the night, he spread out his sitting mat and bowed toward Mount Yúnjí. Thereupon, Cōng became renowned throughout the monastic community. He eventually arrived at Dòng...
Shan Yi followed Dao Quan. In the year Jǐyǒu, Quan moved to Xiqian Monastery and appointed Cōng to succeed him on the seat. Guo succeeded Wenshu Ying and took up residence at Tianshen.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The entire Tripitaka is the character 'left' (之). The Patriarch’s coming from the West is the character 'right' (右).
What is the correct meaning? After a long silence, he said: "When the weather is fine, cover the roof; while there is leisure, thresh the grain. Pay the tax."

The King granted him land. He would drum upon his belly and sing aloud. Whenever Congfan saw a monk approaching with something to ask, he would glare at him with angry eyes and say, "I am a master of the art of striking tigers;
you do not understand it, so leave! Hongyin lived in seclusion on Mount Heng for twenty years.
A wealthy and nobleman from Xiangyin came to visit Fuyan Monastery; seeing that Yin’s countenance was serene and tranquil, and that he carried only a single bowl...

He hung his belongings on the wall; he possessed nothing else of value. [Wuzhuo] was deeply moved by this and, bowing and kneeling, requested, "Master, would you rather remain a long-term guest to others, or would you also wish to dwell in the mountains?
Shending is my family’s place for planting blessings; it has long lacked a patriarchal master.
I pray that you will go there with me. Wenyi smiled and said, "Agreed. He then loaded Wenyi onto his own horse and returned home. Upon arriving at Shending, Wenyi prepared fish...
The drum was beaten for rice gruel as in other regions; in one year a monastic community was formed, and after ten years there were thirty members.

[He] returned to visit his parents and stayed at Ye County. Ascending the hall, he said: "Now, for those who travel on foot as Chan practitioners, you must possess the eye of study when investigating the Way.

You must attain the phrase of realization in your view of the ground; only then will you have the affinity for mutual intimacy. Thus, you will not be deluded by various circumstances, nor will you fall [into error]."
Regarding the evil realms, how can one thoroughly comprehend them? At times, the words reach [the mind] but the meaning does not;

one falsely conditions upon the objects before one and discriminates among reflected phenomena. At times, the meaning reaches [the mind] but the words do not; it is like the blind men feeling an elephant, each asserting a different perspective.
At times, both meaning and words reach [the mind], shattering the realm of empty space so that light illuminates the ten directions. At times, both meaning and words...
"Not yet. A man without eyes wanders back and forth; suddenly, without realizing it, he falls into a deep pit. A monk requested instruction on the "Pine Tree" kōan.
[Baizhang] said, "I am not unwilling to explain it to you, but will you believe me? The monk replied, "Since the Master speaks with such gravity, how could I dare not believe?
[Baizhang] asked, "Do you hear the sound of water dripping from the eaves? At these words, the monk was suddenly enlightened and involuntarily let out a cry.
Xuefeng said, "Ye. Xuefeng asked, "What principle have you seen? The monk then replied with a verse: "The water droplets from the eaves, Clear and distinct;
The universe is shattered, And in this very moment, the mind is stilled. Xuefeng was pleased. Xuefeng’s tenure as abbot was stern, austere, and frugal.
When Fayuan Yihuai went to visit him, it was in the midst of cold snow. Xuefeng scolded and drove him away. Upon his arrival—
He splashed them with water. The other monks were all enraged and departed; only Huiyuan remained, sitting calmly with his robes soaked.
Daoxingsheng said, "If you do not leave, I shall beat you. Huiyuan replied, "The two of us have come from thousands of miles away to visit the Master;

how could we leave because of a single ladle of water? Even if you were to kill me, I would not go. Daoxingsheng then ordered him to be enrolled as a resident monk and subsequently entrusted him with the succession.

Yuan was appointed as the steward (*karmadāna*). The assembly suffered from a lack of provisions and lived in austere conditions. Yuan took advantage of an official inspection tour to secretly procure oil and flour to prepare five-flavored congee for the monks.
When the inspector discovered the value of what had been taken, he fined Yuan and compelled him to return the estimated worth of his robes and alms bowl. After this, Yuan was driven out.

Because Yuan was staying in a corridor room, the inspector saw him there and again demanded rent money. Yuan went to the market with his alms bowl to beg for money to repay it. Thereupon, the inspector...
[The Master] said, "Yuanzhen has the intention to study Chan. He then called him back to the monastery. Yuanzhen was the son of the Lin family in Suzhou.
His mother dreamed of swallowing a great pearl before becoming pregnant; many extraordinary omens attended his birth. His appearance was grand and striking, and his mouth could hold two fists.

At the age of seven, he would often submerge himself in a deep pool without his clothes becoming wet. At thirty, he shaved his head, received the full precepts, and went to visit Yanguan Qiu to seek instruction. His realization... [was awakened].

He clarified the Mind-Seal (Mind-Print). He returned to reside at Mingjue Monastery, where he devoted himself solely to drinking wine. When intoxicated, he would sing songs to admonish the world and guide the common people;
consequently, he was called the "Wine Immortal. His song said: "Following the waters, the red peach blossoms Wander through the streets before and behind.
More than a hundred times, Zhang San knows me, Li Si also knows me. If you do not know me, Between these two fists, which one is larger? Two.
Among these, one is great; once he took a single stroke and split open the void. He rubbed it until it returned to its original state, then picked up Mount Sumeru as a pillow and lay down.
At the head of the Yangtze River, the waves are deepest; when travelers reach this point, they all hesitate.
If at some future time you reach a place where there are no waves, you must still apply your mind as you did when the waves were present. Again, we hear the golden goblet being filled.
Mount Yu returns with its report of collapse; do not let the night-watchmen hasten the passing of time. Seize the moonlight to return home. "One-six, two-six"—the matter is already complete.

"One-nine, two-nine"—I simply wish to drink wine. Stretching out my two legs, I sleep one awakening. Upon rising, heaven and earth remain as they were before. Before the gate, the green trees hold no singing birds;

beneath the courtyard, the gray moss has fallen flowers. For now— *Note: This passage is a poetic rendering of the traditional Chinese children’s rhyming game known as "The Twelve Months" (Shíèr Yīyuè), which uses the cyclical numbers of the twelve months to create rhythmic verses.*
Discussing this matter with the east wind: to whom does the fullness of spring’s colors belong? It is like paying a high price to paint the moon with cinnabar;

when calculated, it is a labor spent in vain. To lie drunk beneath the shade of green willows and, upon waking, insist on speaking of *tathatā* (Suchness)—it is like a clay figure repeatedly admonishing others not to lose the pearl within their robes.
When autumn arrives, the mountains grow cold and the waters chill; when spring comes, the willows turn green and the peach blossoms bloom.
Red. A single point moves in accordance with ten thousand transformations. The river village is shrouded in misty rain. Is it empty? Is it not empty?
With a strainer, one scoops up the northwest wind. Born into this Jambudvīpa world, human sentiments abound with likes and dislikes;
one simply wishes to drink a little wine, which is why one lies prostrate in the streets and by the roads. After death, one is reborn in this Sahā world, having no desire for transcendence.

Pure Land. Why is this? In the Western Pure Land, there are no wine shops. On the first day of the Yuanxuan Festival in the second year of the Xiangfu era, early in the morning, after he had finished bathing, he went to his chamber, clenched his fists, raised his right hand over his left, opened his mouth, and passed away.
(Gengxu) Layman Xu Shi, a former Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice, was serving as the Governor of Nanchang when he passed by Lotus Peak.
There he heard from Master Xiang that the Chan practitioner Cong was in Jiangxi and that he should go seek him out, for this monk was a "human and celestial eye. He then went to visit Cong and spoke.

He attained enlightenment. At that time, Huicong used to plant pine trees himself while reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* without ceasing. Huishi presented him with a poem, which said: "His speech is entirely unimpeded;
He treads high upon the tracks of the Patriarchs. Sitting through the night upon the cloud-connected rocks, In spring he plants rain-soaked pines."

The mirror divides the golden hall’s candlelight; the mountain answers the moonlit tower’s bell. When asked about the meaning of the Westward Journey, he faces the distant peaks from within the empty hall.
One day, while Shi and Lektan Cheng were sitting with Shanglan Pu, Cheng said, "I have heard the Langzhong say:
'Sitting through the night on the Cloud-Linked Stone, planting spring pines amidst the rain. What was his response to Dongshan at that time? Shi replied, "Today I let it go."
Yuanwu asked early in the morning, "I have heard that the Great Sage of Sizhou appeared in Yangzhou—is this true or not?
Cheng said, "Have some different tea brought here. Yuanwu said, "His reputation is not in vain. Cheng said, "When will you, Master, return to the mountain?
Yuanwu said, "Today you were seen through by Shanglan. Cheng then gave a shout. Yuanwu said, "It must be you who can do it. Shi said, "What can one do with the boat? Break it apart!"

Hudou entered the Sangha Hall of Shanglan one day and asked the Head Seat, "How many years of age are you? He replied, "Sixty-eight. Hudou asked, "How many years of *śrāmaṇera* ordination have you completed?
He replied, "Forty-seven summer retreats. Hudou asked, "As for the Holy Monk, how many years of ordination has he received? He replied, "He received the precepts simultaneously with empty space.
Hudou struck the head of the wooden clappers and said, "The official eats rice; he does not eat as much salt as the Head Seat. (From the *Chushi*).
Chuan was the son of the Lee clan of Chonju. In his youth he was a Confucian scholar; at the age of twenty-two, he received the tonsure.
His mother, who possessed virtuous conduct, sent him away to travel and study under various masters. Chuan had joined eyebrows and handsome eyes, and was tall and robust.

However, he was somewhat unrestrained, and wherever he went, he was rebuked by senior masters for being too young for the monastic community. Chuan sat cross-legged on a cliff and laughed, saying: "When dragons and elephants trample, they do not heed the measuring line."
He was not one whom a donkey could carry; he once used a bamboo staff to shoulder a chest of bones as he traveled between the regions of Xiang and Mian.
Together with Shouzhi, he formed a companion and entered Luoyang. Hearing that Chanzhao’s reputation for the Way was preeminent in the world, he resolved to attend upon him personally.
At that time, the imperial court was inquiring into the offenses of Hedong, and heavy troops were stationed throughout Luzhou and Zezhou; many urged him not to go.
Yuan did not look back; he changed his clothes to resemble those of a servant and joined the ranks of the fire brigade, sleeping in the open and lodging in the grass until he finally reached Fenyang.

As for Zhaozhuang’s [disciple] Zhizhi: he was the son of the Wang family of Taiyuan; having abandoned his home at a young age, he received ordination after successfully passing the examination on the *Lotus Sūtra*.
He lectured on the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, and his fame filled the Three Rivers. At that time, Zen Master Shanzhao appeared in the world at Fenshui;
Dongzhao went there to study, surrendered himself to enter the inner chamber, and was specially granted the seal of approval. Guquan was a man from the south.

From youth, he was intelligent and quick-witted, yet by nature he was tolerant of filth and spoke with great, insolent words. As a śramaṇa, he cast aside the precepts and acted according to his own whims, looking down upon other monastics wherever he went.

The monastic community repeatedly deleted [the text], yet Quan did not take this to heart. He went to attend upon Zhaoyan, who marveled at him and secretly bestowed upon him the transmission of the Dharma.
(Xin Hai year) Tanying attended upon Chan Master Yuncong.
Tanying was the son of the Qiu family of Qiantang; he became a full monk at the age of thirteen. Regarding books, there was nothing he had not read. Ten...

In his eighties and nineties, [Zhao] Ying traveled to the capital. He first visited Jingxuan and asked, "The Dongshan school uniquely establishes the categories of 'partial and correct' and 'ruler and minister.
What does this intend to clarify? Jingxuan replied, "The state of affairs before one's parents were born. Ying asked, "How does one realize and embody this?

Jingxuan said, "At midnight it is perfectly bright; at dawn, nothing is revealed. Ying left in bewilderment and went to visit Yuncong. Regarding the words of Dayang, he said, "The Master’s meaning is like..."

Yang asked, "What do you say? [Dongshan] replied, "The Great Sun is not wrong; it is simply that his mouth is too narrow. Even if he spoke with his whole mouth, he could not finish. [Dongshan] said, "I am not like this.
Yang asked, "What is the matter before one's parents were born? [Dongshan] replied, "A brick from the latrine.

Yang asked, "What is the state when midnight is truly bright, yet nothing is revealed at dawn? [Dongshan] replied, "A cat sleeping beneath a cluster of peonies. Yingyu was struck with doubt and alarm.
He questioned him daily, yet in the end he gained no benefit. He resolved with vigor, saying, "I shall investigate this even unto death;
if I do not understand, I will never leave the mountain. One day, while Yìng was engaged in communal labor (*pǔqǐng*), Cōng saw him and asked, "Are you carrying firewood today?

He replied, "Yes. Cōng said, "Yúnmén once asked: 'When a person carries firewood, does the firewood carry the person? How do you understand this? Yìng was unable to respond. Thereupon, Cōng leaned his staff against a rock.
Jiashan sat down and said with a smile, "This matter is like a person learning calligraphy: those who can imitate the dots and strokes are skilled; those who cannot are clumsy. Why is this so?

It is simply because they have not yet forgotten the 'dharma. If there is attachment to the dharma, one will naturally produce interruptions. Only when the brush forgets the hand, and the hand forgets the mind, can it be done.
At this, Xingyin suddenly attained a silent realization of his meaning. After a long while, he said, "Shitou said: 'Attachment to phenomena...'"
"Originally it was delusion; even 'conforming to principle' is not awakening. Since you say it is 'conforming to principle,' why do you call it 'not awakening'?
He replied, "Do you take this phrase to be a medicinal word or a diseased word? He said, "It is a medicinal word. Cong scolded him, saying, "You are taking the disease for the medicine!"

"Furthermore, how excellent! It is said that 'the matter is like a box finding its lid; the principle is like an arrow with a straight shaft and a sharp point—how could there be anything more marvelous?

Yet you still consider this a defect; this I truly do not understand. He replied: "Even if one borrows that 'marvelous' state, it merely clarifies the relationship between phenomena (shi) and principle (li).
The intent of the Patriarchs is beyond the reach of intellectual consciousness; how much less can phenomena and principle exhaust it? Therefore, the World-Honored One [said...]"

Xing said, "Principles obstruct right knowledge and vision; phenomena obstruct the continuity of birth and death. Ying was startled as if awakening from a dream and asked, "How then should one utilize them?
Xing replied, "If speech does not leave the old nest, how can one escape the entanglements? Ying sighed and said, "As soon as it touches the lips, it falls into the realm of conceptual thought;
these are all gates of death and are ultimately not the path of life. That very day, he took his leave. Xiaoshun.

He was the son of the Hu family of Yichun. In his youth, he was coarse and fierce, but suddenly awakened to the nature of floating illusions and abandoned worldly life to become a monk under Master Xiaocong of Dongshan.
At that time, Xiaocong sent him to Wuchang to beg for alms. His first visit was to the home of Layman Liu, a man of noble conduct who was revered by his contemporaries;
whatever he intended to give or take away, none failed to comply with him. Because Shun was young, they did not know whether he had eaten enough.

"Enter! he said. The scholar found this quite easy. The scholar said, "I have a question for you, old man. If your words accord with mine, I shall open my commentary; if they do not, I ask that you return to Xinfeng.
He asked, "How was it before the ancient mirror had been polished? [Dongshan] said, "Black as lacquer. He asked, "And after it has been polished?
[Dongshan] said, "It shines upon heaven and reflects upon earth. The scholar laughed and said, "Has the man of the Way not come from Dongshan himself?"
Wu Shun shook out his sleeves and entered the residence. Yuanchong silently felt ashamed and hurried home. He recounted the incident to Chong, who composed verses on his behalf.
When asked, "What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? he replied, "The journey to Hanyang is not far. When asked, "What is it like after it has been polished?
he replied, "The Yellow Crane Tower and Parrot Isle. At these words, Wu Shun attained great enlightenment. Li Zunxu, the Commandery Marshal, visited Yun Chong and asked:
Regarding the matter of leaving the household life: Cong raised the case of Lord Cui Zhao asking Jingshan Qian, "May I, your disciple, leave the household life?
Qian replied, "Leaving the household life is the business of a great man; it is not something that generals or ministers can accomplish. He answered with this kōan.
Under these words, Xù attained great enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "To study the Way, one must be an iron man; when the hand touches the heart, judgment is immediate.
He then spontaneously added a refrain: "To study the Way, one must be an iron man; when the hand touches the heart, judgment is immediate.
One should head straight for supreme Bodhi, and pay no heed to any right or wrong. One day, while seeing off the Elder Jiān, Xù asked: "Recently..."
Departing from Shangdang, he was able to reach the Central Capital. Just as they were about to engage in a discourse like that of a scholar’s whisk, he suddenly turned back his tiger-patterned staff.
Pointing toward the verdant peaks of Yunping, he sought the clear streams of Xueling. "I do not know how matters stand in this place compared to that one," [the other] asked.

Jian replied, "The sharp sword sweeps away all, and heaven and earth are silent; the frosty blade is just raised, and the Ox and Cow constellations grow cold. Xu said, "It happens to coincide with the present..."
Jiashan was deaf-mute. Xuanzhe said, "One arrow brings down two pheasants. Xuanjue said, "Why is it that the Senior Monk sleeps in straw sandals?
Jiashan gave him a flick with his sleeve. Xuanjue bowed his head and said, "Today I may truly be said to have been subdued. Jiashan said: [The text ends here.]
Puhua emerged from the Sangha hall. Xu Shi was traveling westward from Chuzhou to Sichuan; on his way through Ruyang, he went to pay his respects to Yuanlian.
Yuanlian happened to be receiving him before the Buddha statue. Shi said, "Which shall I bow to first: the Buddha or the Elder? Yuanlian replied, "A toad swallowing a tiger."
[Changsha] said, "If that is so, then you will not bow at all. [Yunju] said, "The Commissioner has fallen into a trap. [Changsha] said, "Elder Xu possesses the 'one eye'.
Lian then brushed away [the incense burner] with his sleeve and said, "Today I have seen through it," and then he prostrated. ○ Chu-yuan.
Dōgen attended Zen Master Shōkō for two years, yet he was not permitted to enter the inner quarters. Dōgen went to see Shōkō;

Shōkō, discerning his resolve, would invariably respond with insults toward his attendants, or disparage the various schools of Zen. Furthermore, whenever he offered instruction, it was always of a mundane and vulgar nature. One night, Dōgen lamented:
"I have been at this Dharma seat for two summers already, yet I have received no direct guidance. My thoughts increase only worldly toil as the years pass."

"The moon has drifted away; my own matter remains unclear, and I have lost the benefit of leaving the household life. Before he had finished speaking, Zhaorun stared intently at him and scolded, "You are a wicked teacher!
How dare you deceive me for profit? In a rage, he raised his staff to chase him away. Yuanwu reached out as if to intervene, but Zhaorun covered his mouth.
Yuanwu attained great enlightenment and said, "Now I know that Linji’s Way transcends ordinary sentiment."
(Guichou) Master Jie of the Fifth Patriarch’s Monastery examined Master Jie of Qiye.
He resided at Mount Wuzu and delighted in testing and verifying the progress of his disciples. At that time, Qiye Chongxian was renowned as one who had thoroughly completed his training.

Furthermore, there was a man of keen discernment. The two men traveled together to the Huai River region, and upon reaching the foot of Mount Dong, Xian did not wish to proceed further and ordered Yue to go on ahead.
Yue wrapped his robe around his waist and entered the abbot’s quarters directly. At that time, Jie returned from outside and saw him;
he called out, "What is your name, monk? Yue replied, "Qi Yue. Jie said, "How does he compare to Mount Tai? Yue was speechless. Jie immediately struck him and drove him out.
The next day, he went to pay his respects again. Baizhang asked, "What are you doing? Huairang turned his head and drew a circle with his hand to show him.
Baizhang asked, "What is this? Huairang said, "Old and decrepit as I am, you do not even recognize a plain sesame cake.
Baizhang said, "While the hearth is still hot, let me add another one on top. As Huairang hesitated, Baizhang dragged his staff and drove him out the door. A few days later...
Yue went to see Jie again. Jie then lifted up his sitting mat and said, "When spread out, it encompasses the great trichiliocosm; when not spread out, not even a hair's breadth remains.

He asked, "Is it this spreading that is it, or is it this not-spreading? Jie stepped down from his meditation seat, seized Yue, and held him fast, saying, "Since you are an old acquaintance, why must you act like this? Yue was again speechless, and Jie struck him out.
○ Chongxian visited Chan Master Guangzuo.

Chongxian was the son of the Li family from Suining Prefecture. He shaved his head and received full ordination. Later, he left Sichuan and lived a life of wandering between the regions of Jingzhou and Zhuzhou.

He held the sutras across his lap at the lecture hall, investigating principles and exhausting the profound mysteries. His interrogations were as swift as whirling blades, and his quick-witted eloquence was peerless.
For many years, he served as the guest prefect at Dayang Temple. Once, while discussing the fundamental tenets of Zhaozhou with a visiting monk, the guest asked:

"When Chan Master Fayan encountered Jue Tiezui at Jinling in the past, he asked him whether he remembered the karmic conditions regarding Zhaozhou’s 'cypress tree' case. Did you remember it? Jue replied, "My late master..."
"There were no such words. Do not slander our former master. Fayan clapped his hands and said, "Truly, he has come from the lion’s den.
Jue said, "There were no such words," yet Fayan approved him. Wherein lies the meaning? Xian said, "In the Gate of the Patriarchs, there is both suppression and exaltation."

Is there a fixed method for this? At that time, there was an ascetic named Han Dabo, whose appearance was austere. As he lay sleeping by [Xian’s] side, [Han] would often depart with a hidden smile. Once the guests had retired, Xian rebuked him, saying, "I was just conversing with the guests; why did you smile? Han replied, "I smiled because I knew your 'eye of wisdom' was not yet upright and your discernment of the Dharma was not clear. Xian asked, "Is there a reason for this? Han answered him with a verse: The guest's eye of wisdom is not yet upright; In choosing the Dharma, he lacks clarity. If one does not understand the meaning of the words, How can one speak of the Way? If one does not know the source of the principle, How can one attain the fruit of the Path? If one does not see the root of the tree, How can one grasp its branches? If one does not know the origin of the water, How can one reach its current? If one does not know the beginning of the Way, How can one attain its end? If one does not know the mind of the Buddha, How can one preach the Dharma? If one does not know the nature of reality, How can one attain liberation? If one does not know the self, How can one know others? If one does not know the ultimate truth, How can one speak of the provisional? If one does not know the One, How can one speak of the many? If one does not know the root, How can one speak of the branches? If one does not know the source, How can one speak of the flow? If one does not know the beginning, How can one speak of the end? If one does not know the mind, How can one speak of the teachings? If one does not know the essence, How can one speak of the form? If one does not know the absolute, How can one speak of the relative? If one does not know the true, How can one speak of the false? If one does not know the internal, How can one speak of the external? If one does not know the within, How can one speak of the without? If one does not know the fundamental, How can one speak of the derivative? If one does not know the primary, How can one speak of the secondary? If one does not know the master, How can one speak of the servant? If one does not know the leader, How can one speak of the follower? If one does not know the sovereign, How can one speak of the subject? If one does not know the ruler, How can one speak of the ruled? If one does not know the father, How can one speak of the son? Yuan said, "Tangming asked Shoushan, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Shou replied, 'At the foot of King Chu’s city, the Ru River flows east.
Yi asked, "What is the intent of these words? Yuan said, "A lantern hanging over the water. Yi [laughed].
Yi said, "If that is so, then I have failed the ancients. Yuan said, "If you harbor doubts, Inner Secretary, then seek another teacher.

Yi said, "A three-legged frog leaps up into the sky. Yuan said, "Leap as much as you wish. Yi then laughed heartily. He was lodged in the meditation hall, where he questioned Zhi-zheng morning and evening regarding his doubts.
Upon hearing the words and deeds of former masters, he regretted that he had met him so late. [Later, Yi] saw him in the imperial court.
The Prince of the Household (Fu-ma-du-wei) Li Zunxū said, "I have recently encountered a man of the Way who is truly a 'Lion of the West River.
I replied, 'I am constrained by official regulations and cannot go to pay my respects; what can be done? When Yì returned home, he told Yuán: 'Lord Li is one among those who follow the Buddha-dharma.
Having heard that the wind of your Way has reached afar, he has a desire to see you, yet for the sake of the law, he is not permitted to pass through with his attendants.'"
At dawn, Yuan went to pay his respects to Xun. As Xun was reviewing the visitor’s card, he sent a boy to inquire, saying, "If you can speak the Way, then you may meet with the Senior Monk.
Yuan said, "I have come specifically today to pay my respects. Again, Xun ordered the boy to say, "The inscription on the stele is carved in white characters;
one plants green pines along the path. Yuan said, "Were it not for this auspicious day, such an occasion would surely be difficult to encounter on any other day. The boy—
The Master (Zi) came out again and said, "The Commandant says: 'If that is so, then you have met the Senior Monk (Shangzuo). Yuan said, 'From head to toe.
Xue then came out, sat down, and asked, 'I have heard that there is a golden-haired lion in West River; is this true?'"
Yuan said, "Where did you get this news? Xue immediately gave a shout. Yuan said, "A wild jackal howls. Xue shouted again. Yuan said, "Exactly so. Xue laughed loudly.
After Yuan had taken his leave, Xue asked, "What is that one phrase of yours, Venerable, as you depart?
Yuan said, "Good news. Xue said, "How is this any different from other places? Yuan said, "As for you, Marshal, what do you say?"
Xù said, "I shall give the Senior Monk twenty blows. Yuán said, "Solely for the sake of its circulation. Xù shouted again. Yuán said, "Blind!
Xù said, "Go well. Yuán said, "Yes, yes. From then on, he went back and forth between the gates of Yang and Li, taking the Dharma as his friend.
(Wu-wu) Chan Master Hongyin preached on the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*.
Hongyin resided at Shendeng. He was incomparably content with austerity and plainness. He had a single dilapidated wooden bed;

at night, Hongyin would sit upon it while thirty followers sat in a circle to listen to his instructions. Hongyin recited a verse by Dongshan: "Greed, anger, and ignorance are utterly devoid of knowledge."
"Thanks to me, this morning I have come to know him. When he walks, he strikes; when he sits, he beats. Entrust this to the Mind-King and examine it carefully.
For immeasurable kalpas, he has not been liberated. I ask you three: do you know? The ancients spoke thus, but Shending does not agree.
Greed, anger, and ignorance are truly without knowledge; throughout the twelve hours of the day, let him be as he is. When he walks, he simply goes."
As soon as he sat down, [the master] followed along. He entrusted him with the sovereign mind; there was nothing further to be done.

For immeasurable kalpas, it has been fundamentally liberated. Why must one further inquire whether one knows or not? A monk asked: "The attendant of Niaoke wished to travel to various regions to study the Buddha-dharma.
When Niaoke merely blew on some cloth-hair, he immediately attained awakening. How is this? Yin said: "This matter is known. This person had long accumulated [merit]."
Pure karma requires eons of cultivation before one can truly understand it. [The Master] then picked up a tuft of cloth, held it up, blew upon it, and said, "Do you understand?
Do not fail this old monk. After a long silence, he said, "When I was at Shoushan, I was with my elder brother, Master Fenyang."
It was once said thus. Fenyang composed a verse, saying: "The attendant, with a beginner's mind, yearned for superior conditions;
He took leave of his master, intending to go and study Chan. Niaoke knew that his faculties were ripe; Blowing on his hair, he attained peace of mind at that very moment.
Observe how he spoke—truly a master. The śramaṇa Benyan of Zhidu Temple visited Yuanwen; they conversed through the night, and [Benyan] later told it to the regional commander.
It is said: Master Yin was what is called a "venerable elder of the true lineage. It was regrettable that he remained submerged in obscurity within the mountains.

When the Prefect invited him with formal rites to open a Dharma assembly, Yin could not decline; he then ascended the seat to preach the Dharma. Monastics and laypeople cheered and cried out in joy, experiencing something they had never known before.
Thus, Yin’s reputation became widely renowned. When Qisong was young, he traveled to Shen Ding Temple, where Yin sat upon the hall platform and received his ceremonial scarf (zhǎn).
Two small jars stood beneath the courtyard eaves. [The master] said, "Your arrival is precisely the right time; this temple shall have sauce for its meals starting this year.

The next day, as porridge was being served, one of the laborers took a basket and cast its contents into the monks' alms bowls. Huìsōng looked up and down at them; some were already chewing, while others left the food as it was.
Huìsōng drew out his sleeve to examine them, finding they were all broken pieces of cakes and biscuits. He questioned the elders.

The Old One said, "In this monastery, we have never cooked porridge since time immemorial. However, if there is a donor who invites us for a formal meal, the Abbot assigns the monks in order to attend.
He instructs them to take back any dry leftovers to the storehouse, where they are broken down, toasted, and ground into a fine powder to be distributed as a substitute for flour.
The Abbot said, "It so happens that you arrived at just such a time; it is indeed fitting. Sōng was greatly astonished. (Chu)
Yuán became a companion in the joy of the Dharma with Yang Yì and Li Zūnxū. After a long time, he took his leave to return to Hedong.
Yì said, "I have a phrase to entrust to Tang Ming. Yuán said, "The bright moon shines upon the traveler at night. Yì said, "But that does not quite fit."
Yuan said, "The deepening of night is still tolerable; the afternoon is what truly makes one sorrowful. Yi asked, "Why has the Vajra statue in front of Kai Bao Temple been sweating lately?
Yuan said, "I know. Yi asked, "As you are about to depart, Master, do you have no word for us?
Yuan said, "Layer upon layer, the mountain passes and roads. Yi said, "If that is so, then I shall follow you, Master. Yuan sighed.
Upon hearing a single sound, Zhenyi said, "A true lion cub; a great lion's roar. Yuanwu said, "Let it go, and then bring it back.
Zhenyi said, "Just now I tripped and fell, and then my servant helped me up. Yuanwu said, "When will there ever be an end to this? Zhenyi laughed heartily.
When Yuanwu returned to Tangming, Xuanzun and Fawu sent two monks to inquire after him; Yuanwu drew a pair of feet at the end of his reply.
He wrote down the names of the monks and sent them along with it. Xue composed a verse, saying: "The black brush tip has traveled more than a thousand li;
The golden coffin reveals the pair of feet. Humans and devas can hardly fathom it; Take care, O red-bearded barbarian! Yuan returned south because his mother was elderly. Upon reaching Junzhou, he...

He went to visit Xue Xiaocong. Xiaocong ordered him to lead the assembly. Previously, Zhishan Shanzhao had said to Yuanzhao, "I have traveled everywhere visiting the descendants of Yunmen, yet I have specifically harbored regret for not having seen Xiaocong.
Therefore, Yuanzhao remained in attendance at his side for three years. Zunsui resided at Tiantzhu.
Prime Minister Wang Qinruo governed Hangzhou and, having heard of Shishao’s reputation for his practice, reported it to the court. He was granted the title Ciyun.
(Jiwei year) Chan Master Chongxian took up residence at Cuifeng.

Having attained the gate of the Dharma from Zhi, he then went on to study extensively under various masters. When Dongshan Xiaocong was newly arrived and came for an audience, [Chongxian] immediately...
Question: "What is the meaning of 'Mugon’s Water Buffalo' at Mount Huangbo? Most who answered failed to accord with the profound intent. When Xian arrived, he was asked the same question as before.
Xian said, "This is merely for later generations to use as a banner. Cong was about to speak when Xian struck him once with his sitting cloth.
He set out to leave. Cōng called out, “Wait a moment, Upādhyāya! Xiǎn replied, “I have not yet entered the hall. Later, when Xiǎn served as the guest prefect at Dàlóng, one day [Cōng] asked him:
“The one who speaks is not it; the one who remains silent is not it. That which is neither speech nor silence is even more so. To be all of these together is entirely not it.”
"Setting aside the manifestation of great function, people of this age know it exists; but I wonder how the Great Dragon [responds]?
Yunyan said, "You possess such a view and understanding. Xiangyan said, "This old fellow is like crumbling walls and melting ice. The Dragon said, "I grant you thirty blows!"
Xian manifested his prostrations and returned to the assembly. Long called back the monk who had just been questioning him; Xian came out immediately.
Long said, "Why did my old self crumble like ice melting away? Xian replied, "It only becomes more evident that there is a flaw. Long’s expression darkened and he said, "I cannot stand it!
I cannot stand it! Xian then withdrew. Later, he related this to Nanyue Ya. Ya said, "Great Dragon, why do you not grant him his original [nature]?"
While the fodder was being distributed, Xian said, "The Master must still travel on foot. He then asked Lohan Lin, "Since the Dharma is thus and not otherwise, how can you provide guidance?
Lin replied, "Precisely because the Dharma is thus and not otherwise. Xian said, "The assembly, take note of this man's 'head-word,'" and he shook out his robe and returned to the ranks.
After Lin descended from the hall, he had an attendant invite Xian to the abbot’s quarters and questioned him further.
Zuo said, "Just now you were unwilling to acknowledge this old monk. Xian said, "The Master is the contemporary patriarch; how would I dare be unwilling?
Lin said, "Why did you shake out your robes and return to the assembly? Xian said, "Do you permit me to speak of the Way?"
Lin said, "Tell me what you have to say. Xian gave him a single slap. The novice Zenghui was on close terms with Xian;
while they were together on the banks of the Huai River, Zenghui asked where Xian was going. Xian replied, "I am about to travel to Qiantang, pass Xixing, and ascend Mount Tiantai and Yandang.
Zenghui said, "Lingyin is a most excellent place in all the world. Master Shan is an old friend of mine; I shall write a letter of recommendation for you."
Xian arrived at Lingyin and remained submerged among the multitude for three years. Suddenly, an envoy was dispatched to western Zhejiang to seek out Xian at Lingyin;

yet no one recognized him. At that time, there were over a thousand monks in the hall. The envoy’s officials searched through the bedding registers and sought him by physical description until they finally found him.

Fahui asked about the letter he had previously sent. Xian took it into his sleeve and said, "Your honor’s intent is diligent; however, as a wandering monk, I have no worldly pursuits—how could I dare hope for such a recommendation?
Fahui laughed heartily. Shan was amazed by this. When the seat at Cui Peak on Wujiang was vacant, he was appointed to succeed there.
He burned incense as a dharma heir of Beita (that is, Zhimen). On the day he began teaching the Dharma, he looked out at the assembly and said: "If..."
In discussing the fundamental aspects of views, it is not necessary to ascend this high seat.
Instead, he pointed with his finger and said, "Everyone, follow my hand and look; immeasurable Buddha-lands appear all at once. Each of you must observe them closely.
If you do not know their boundaries, you will inevitably be mired in the mud and water. Thereupon, he ascended the seat and looked around the assembly, saying, "People..."

The heavens gather universally. What matter do you seek to clarify by joining together? How can you engage in a mere exchange of guest and host, racing back and forth in question and answer, and presume this to be the vehicle of the Patriarchal School?
This vast and expansive tradition of the Gate possesses sovereign majesty and virtue; its brilliance transcends past and present. It holds fast heaven and earth.

The thousand sages have said it can only be known by oneself; even the five vehicles cannot establish it. Therefore, though one may realize the essential meaning before a sound is uttered, one remains lost upon turning back to look.

At the point of discernment, one knows where to return upon hearing a single word; yet you still remain obscured by the realm of conscious intellect. If you all wish to recognize the true mark, how so?

Simply let there be no grasping or looking upward above, and cut off all selfhood below. Then, the natural radiance will manifest before you, and each person will stand like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
Can you discern this clearly or not? If you have not discerned it, discern it! If you have not clarified it, clarify it! Since you have already discerned it...
Once clarity is attained, one is able to cut off the stream of birth and death and occupy the seat of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

At this very moment, when wondrous and perfect transcendental realization occurs, one is capable of repaying the unrepayable debt of gratitude and assisting in the transformation of non-action. Xian once studied under Dalong.
Dalong’s junior disciple asked, "Why do you not offer incense to your former master? Xian replied, "In the past, a monk asked my former master, 'What is...'"
Regarding the "Solid Dharma-body," my former teacher said: "The mountain flowers bloom like brocade; the stream water is as deep blue as indigo.
I have now offered this verse on this causal connection to repay his kindness. Furthermore, I once studied under Dayu Shouzhi, with whom I traveled for the longest time among all my teachers.
Yue knew that Xian had not inherited Zhi’s lineage, so he specifically went to examine him. One day, while walking through the mountains with Xian, Yue suddenly said:
"Entering a wild field, one does not pick; one takes whatever grass comes to hand. It is never absent from what meets the eye—why do you not speak when the moment arises?

Xian picked up a stalk of grain and showed it to him. Yue did not approve, saying, "Even in a dream, I have never seen such a thing. Xian said, "If you do not approve," [he continued], "then you yourself must see it."
This was Huaiyi of Xiu. He was the son of the Chen family of Leqing, Yongjia, whose family had for generations made their living as fishermen.

His mother dreamed that a star fell upon her house, and she subsequently conceived. Upon his birth, there were many auspicious omens. When he was a child sitting at the stern of a boat, his father caught a fish and handed it to Huaiyi to string.
Huaiyi could not bear to do it, so he secretly threw it into the river. His father became angry and whipped Huaiyi, yet Huaiyi remained as calm as before.
He traveled extensively in the capital and received the tonsure. A strange monk spoke of the *Lotus Sūtra* while patting Huai’s chest and saying, “Yunmen and Linji have departed.
Huai subsequently visited Shan of Jinkuan and Xing of Yue County, but neither was in accord with him. Traveling east, he arrived at Cuifeng and visited Chongxian.
Chongxian asked, “What is your name? He replied, “Yihuai. Chongxian said, “Why do you not call yourself Huayi (‘Embracing Righteousness’) instead?”
Huishai said, "I attained it at that very moment. Xian said, "Who gave you that name? Huishai replied, "It has been ten years since I received the precepts.
Xian said, "How many pairs of straw sandals have you worn out on your travels? Huishai said, "Master, do not deceive people.
Xian said, "I have no measure of transgression; you also have no measure of transgression. What do you say to this? Huishai was speechless. Xian struck him.

Xuan said, "You empty-headed liar, get out! Next, during the period of entering the room, Xuan said, "It cannot be thus; it cannot be not thus; it cannot be both thus and not thus. While Huai was about to deliberate upon this, Xuan struck him again.

This occurred several times. Subsequently, Huai served as the water-bearer. While drawing water, his carrying pole broke, and he suddenly attained great enlightenment. He then composed a verse of realization: The water is drawn up, the pole is broken;
