"Taking the *dhātu* as the primary principle. [Xuanze] asked, "What is the primary principle of the *dharmadhātu*? [Huishou] replied, "Taking the mind as the primary principle. [Xuanze] asked, "What is the primary principle of the mind? Huishou was unable to respond.
Huai said, "A difference of a hair's breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth. You must observe for yourself; you will surely achieve an awakening.
Huishou was then struck with awe and submitted with reverence, wishing to remain and receive the Dharma. Later, he heard a monk mention Baizhao’s visit to Xuanze.
Baoci asked, "When feeling has not yet arisen, how is it? Baoci replied, "Separated. At this, [the questioner] attained great enlightenment.

Daolung, in his youth, served Shimen Che as his teacher and personally received the essential instructions of Dongshan. Later, he visited Yuanlian. At that time, Yuanlian was in the process of shaving his hair;
he had Daolung bring a stool over. Yuanlian said, "Monk, I have a poem about the stool; listen to it. The poem said: "Put it down."

He was then at peace. Long attained great enlightenment upon hearing these words and subsequently succeeded Liai as his dharma heir. He traveled to the capital and stayed as a guest at Jingde Monastery.
Every day he would wander through the city markets, returning home at the second watch. One night, he was unable to enter and lay down beneath the monastery gate.

Emperor Renzong dreamed that he arrived at the monastery gate and saw a dragon coiled upon the ground; startled awake, he dispatched an imperial messenger in the middle of the night to search for him and found Long there.

He was greatly delighted by the monk’s demeanor while lying down at night. Consequently, he summoned him for an audience and inquired about his fundamental tenets; the Emperor was exceedingly pleased.

He was lodged at Daixiangguo Temple, where they exchanged verses and rhymes that flowed incessantly along the roads. At times, he was invited to stay overnight within the imperial palace, receiving exceptionally generous treatment.
(Ji-chou) Chan Master Weizheng Entered Nirvana (a successor of Jingsu and the fourth generation of the Fayan lineage).
Weizheng was the son of the Huang family of Huating. In his youth, he followed Qian-tang Benru to pursue his monastic studies. When the local people wished to open the treasury [to support him],...

He offered the ordination certificate to Zheng, who sighed and said, "In antiquity, the conferring of ordination was based on the clarity of one's spiritual capacity and the profundity of their understanding; now it is the opposite. We have strayed far from the ways of the ancients.

Since I have fallen into the ranks of the Triple Gem, the time for such a thing must surely come. He then knelt in thanks and refused to accept it. When asked the reason for this, he replied: [The text continues with the Master’s response regarding the decline of the Dharma and the necessity of his own ordination.]
I reply: That person was not one who truly knew me; he merely took my words and bestowed hundreds of thousands [of coins] upon a single youth, providing for him for the rest of his life.
He was able to give material goods, yet did he demand a reward? The Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, possesses great vows to deliver sentient beings and thus provides compassionate shelter;
this is precisely what the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* is. You should humble yourself to recite and uphold it; let all your gratitude be directed toward this one source. In this regard—
Yiwei was content with his lot and regarded it as extraordinary. At the age of eighteen, he became a *bhikṣu*.

Clad alone in a tattered woolen robe, he further made a vow to provide for the annual expenses and maintain the affairs of the monastery. Zheng declined his offer, saying, "I have heard that one should rely on the alms bowl to beg for food."

I have never heard of one enjoying [the Dharma] while sitting idly; I have heard that one must visit all the patriarchs in succession. I have never heard of one neglecting study to rely solely on oneself. Moreover, my years are young and my vigor intact;
this is precisely the time for physical strength to perform ritual homage, not the season for retiring to a hermitage. Thereupon, he set out to travel.
Sŏngju received the mind-dharma from Uisou at Songgung-san Jeongto-yeon. He assisted Sŏngju for a long time and subsequently inherited his seat.
Ye Cheongchin, the Internal Secretary (Naehan), sought out Sŏngju to discuss the Way. One day, Ye said to Sŏngju, "There will be guests gathered tomorrow;
I hope you, Master, will come to sprinkle them with the nectar of the Dharma. Sŏngju granted his consent. The next day, when Ye sent someone to invite him, Sŏngju bestowed upon him a verse.
He said: "Yesterday I already set the date for today; as I stepped out the door leaning on my staff, I reflected further: 'To be a monk, one ought to dwell among the crags and valleys;

it is most unsuitable to be amidst the banquets of a kingdom. In the end, he did not go. He used to ride a yellow calf when going out or coming in, with his *kamaṇḍalu*, headcloth, and alms bowl all hung upon its horns;
thus, the common people called him the 'Yellow Ox of Rectitude' (*Zhenghuáng Niú*). When Vice-Minister Jiang Tang was sent out to serve as regional governor...

In Hangzhou, he maintained a relationship of "external friendship" with Zheng. Whenever Zheng went to visit him, he would unyoke his oxen beneath the courtyard of the prefectural office and remain there for the entire day, engaging in conversation and laughter before departing.

Zheng disciplined himself with rigorous austerity; in winter he did not use a brazier, instead making a ball of reed flowers and tucking his feet inside it. When guests arrived, he shared this with them.
During the summer and autumn, he delighted in gazing at the moon, chanting and laughing until dawn, which he took as his regular practice. Someone once asked him about this.
The Master was renowned by the title "Chan Master," yet why did he not speak of Chan? He replied, "It would merely waste words. I am too weary to resort to such circuitous explanations;
I simply trouble the myriad phenomena day and night to expound it for you. Words have their limits, but this Dharma is inexhaustible—what is called the 'Inexhaustible Treasury of Creation.
On the first month of spring in the first year of the Huangyou era, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Now, as for..."
Movement is contrasted with stillness; from the beginning, there has been no limit to this. I have moved for sixty-four years, and now I am still.

Yet, fundamentally, what is there to be either moving or still? Thereupon, he passed away in profound tranquility. As for the city of Bianjing, temples had already been destroyed since the Zhou dynasty.
During the Jianlong era of Emperor Taizu of the Song dynasty, the two monastic streets (Liangjie) were restored, yet they remained merely schools for doctrinal study (*yixue*).

Scholars and officials of exceptional intelligence and talent all grew weary of hearing about the names and characteristics (*mingxiang*) of phenomena; thus, the school of Bodhidharma had not yet spread widely.
Yang Yi and Chao Hui of the Hanlin Academy were the first to clarify and promote it. In the first year of the Huangyou era, the eunuch Li Yunning petitioned to donate the Bian... [temple].
He established a Zen seat at a newly constructed estate. The Emperor bestowed upon it the plaque name "Shifang Jingyin Chan Monastery.

Ju-ne, whose courtesy name was Zhong-min, was the son of the Jian family from Zizhou. From birth he was exceptionally gifted; when he read books, he could recite them from memory after a single glance.

Having received the tonsure and the full precepts, he later became preeminent in doctrinal studies throughout the two circuits of Sichuan. At that time, there was a Zen practitioner returning from the south who extolled the Way of the Patriarchs.
He was renowned throughout the world. Master Mada was a native of Shifang. He was the one prophesied by Prajñātāra.

Among the eminent and talented men of Shu who were famous for their mastery of the sūtras and śāstras, there was Master Liang; yet Liang abandoned his disciples and hid in the Western Mountains. There was also Master Jian;
Jian burned his commentaries and sub-commentaries, declaring that "a drop of water cannot rival the vast ocean. Nan spoke with a sigh for a long while and said, "Do you understand what he meant?"
Nan said, "I am unable to know it. If you wish to know it, why begrudge making one journey? Thereupon, Nan departed from Shu and wandered through Jing and Chu.
He spent many years, passing through repeated cycles of cold and heat, yet until then he had gained nothing. Later, he studied under Yanqing Rong and finally attained realization.
Rong was a successor of Zhimen Zuo and belonged to the Yunmen school. Having received the Dharma, Nan entered the world at Lu Shan Gui Zong and subsequently moved to Yuan.
Tong. When Emperor Renzong heard of his reputation, at the beginning of the Huangyou era, he issued an imperial decree for him to reside at the Jiyin Chan Monastery of the Ten Directions.

Zhen’e claimed that due to eye ailments, he was unable to comply with the decree. An edict was issued ordering him to recommend a successor; Zhen’e recommended Huailian to take charge of the monastery.

Huailian’s courtesy name was Qizhi; he was the son of the Chen family of Zhangzhou. On the night of his birth, a dream occurred in which Śākyamuni descended into the room, and thus he was given the childhood name Sizhou.

He remained a śramaṇa for a long time, dedicating himself earnestly to the study of dhyāna without neglecting his practice even while sleeping or eating. One day, while washing his face, he splashed some water onto the ground; this triggered a slight awakening.

He immediately sought out a teacher to inquire further and went to visit Huai Cheng of Shimen. Having found the karmic affinity for realization, he received Cheng’s seal of approval and stayed there for over ten years.
Once, while sitting in meditation in his chamber, he saw a golden snake emerge from the earth, which vanished in an instant. Yuanyou—
Tongne was appointed to serve as the *zhangji* (recorder). Xia Song, courtesy name Ziqiao, was a native of De’an.
During the Huángyù era, he served as a Participant in State Affairs (*cānzhī zhèngshì*). Since retiring from office to live in seclusion at Qìjī Valley, he had daily associated with elderly monks.
Once, when Lǔ of Shànglán arrived, Song asked, "When the hundred limbs fall apart and scatter, which one is the Elder’s own true self? Lǔ replied, "I left Qíyáng on the twentieth day of last month."
Fengxue Songxiu departed. Chengzhou Puqie asked, "When the hundred limbs fall apart and scatter, which one is you, sir?
Songxiu immediately shouted. Puqie said, "That shout was not without purpose, but ultimately, which one is you, sir?
Songxiu replied with a verse: "Do not mistake the foremost pivot before the wind; In the great void, where can thought be lodged? If this mountain monk..."
"One must communicate the news: when the moon rises over ten thousand miles of cloudless sky," Pu said, "this too is merely playing with one's spirit.
Chan Master Fanghai of Yangqi entered nirvana (he was a dharma successor of Shishuang Yuan and the eighth generation of Linji).
In the first year of the Huangyou era, Fanghai demonstrated his passing; he was interred at Yungai, and the direct lineage of Linji was entrusted to Shouduan.
Ren Yong was the son of the Zhu family of Siming. From childhood he became a monk and mastered the Tiantai teachings. Later, changing his robes, he went to pay his respects to Chongxian.
Chongxian, sensing that Ren Yong was capable of upholding the Great Dharma, teased him, saying, "Principal of the Yangxiang Monastery. Enraged by this insult, Ren Yong descended the mountain.

Gazing toward Xuedou, he prostrated himself and vowed, "In this life I shall travel as a wandering monk to study Chan; if my realization does not surpass Xuedou, I swear never to return to my hometown."

He immediately went to Letan, but for more than ten years his doubts remained unresolved. Hearing that Fange had moved to Yunge and was able to serve as a guiding key for students, he went straight to his quarters.

Before a single word had been exchanged, he suddenly realized the Mind-Seal. After Fange passed away, he studied under his fellow practitioner Shouduan, investigating the most profound mysteries to their ultimate limit.
Later, he appeared in the world and presided over Baoning twice.
(Year of the Water Tiger) Chan Master Huailian began his teaching at Jingyin Monastery.

Upon arriving in the capital, Emperor Renzong summoned him to the Huacheng Hall for an audience and questioned him on the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma. His responses were in accord with the Emperor’s wishes.

He was granted the title "Great Enlightenment" (Dàjué). Upon the conclusion of the vegetarian feast, an imperial edict was proclaimed that he should follow the ritual protocols of the Chan monasteries of the South. He then ascended the hall to expound the Dharma.
Zanyuan had attended Chuyuan at Shishuang for a long time; after Chuyuan passed away, Yuan planted trees on the site where his remains were interred, and he tended them for eight years.
Chushi resided at Jiangshan. At that time, Prime Minister Wang Anshi was observing the mourning period for his mother and was reciting sutras in the mountains.
He regarded Yuanwu as a brother and inquired about the essential meaning of the Patriarchs. Yuanwu did not answer.
As Wang pressed him further, Yuanwu said, "You have three obstacles to Prajñā and one endowment for the Way. After one or two more lifetimes, you may attain full maturity."
Shi said, "I wish to hear your explanation. Yuan said, "Your Excellency has received a nature of great vigor and strength, and your worldly affinities are deep.

Possessing such vigorous and strong nature while encountering such deep worldly affinities, you will surely take upon yourself the heavy burden of the world and harbor the ambition to transform the state.
Whether employed or not, your mind cannot remain at peace; with a mind that is not yet at peace, how can you ever fulfill your ambition to govern the world? When will it ever be unified?"
"Alas for ten thousand years! You are prone to anger and your studies still cling to mere principles; regarding the Way, you remain ignorant despite your knowledge—this is the third fault.
To regard fame and profit as if shedding your hair [in ordination], and to find sweetness in the simple and austere like a dhūta practitioner—this is to draw near to the Way.
For now, you should cause the teachings of the vehicle to flourish through them. Shi bowed twice and received the instruction. ○ Liaoyuan, courtesy name Juelao.
He was the son of the Lin family of Rāozhou. At birth, auspicious light illuminated the heavens. By the age of two, he could recite the *Analects* and the poems of various masters;

by five, he had memorized three thousand verses. The villagers hailed him as a "Divine Child. Later, while reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he came to cherish it so much that he abandoned his previous studies entirely.
He petitioned his parents to leave the household life, subsequently shaved his head, received full ordination, and traveled to Mount Lu to visit Shanxian.
Xian Da praised him highly. He also visited Juen, who was astonished by his calligraphy and ink-stroke, saying, "His skeletal structure already resembles Xuedou;
he is a talent of the future. Juen then appointed him to serve as the recorder (*jishi*). Changzong was the son of the Shi family in Jianzhou.
His mother dreamed of a tall man with a complexion like gold, who held three stalks of white lotus flowers and bestowed them upon her; she received only one stalk, while the others were left behind.

Dì conceived while awake and later gave birth to three sons; the eldest and middle brothers both died in infancy, and it was the youngest whom she ordained and conferred the full precepts (*upasampadā*) upon.
Initially he relied on Zhicái, but having heard of Huínán’s reputation, he took leave of Cáizhī and went to Guīzōng, where he devoted himself to his service.
○ Dàolóng recommended Huáilián to take his place, wishing to return to Lúshān to recuperate from illness; although he submitted a memorial for this, it was not permitted.
The Imperial Decree: To the north of Huguo Temple, a vihāra was constructed for him to reside in, named Huayan Chan Monastery.
(In the year of Xinmao), Chan Master Hainan attained the Samādhi of Līlā-vihāra.

While Hainan was residing at Guizong Temple, it was consumed by fire overnight, leaving nothing but ashes. The great assembly was thrown into a tumult that echoed through the mountains and valleys. Nan sat upright and composed.

As was his custom, Monk Hongzhun wished to support Nan from behind and flee. Nan rebuked him, saying, "Even if you, Master, were to loathe this world, what would the Dharma-lineage of Ciming rely upon?
Thereupon, he slowly adjusted his robes and rose; by then, the fire had already reached his sitting platform.

He was cast into prison. The local officials, incited by his private resentment, subjected him to a hundred forms of torture and flogging, yet he remained silent and spoke not a word, doing nothing but refusing to eat.
After two months, he was released; his hair and beard were unshorn, and only skin and bone remained. Zhenke met him on the road.
Seeing him, he wept and said, "Elder brother, how could you come to this? Nan-chi shouted, "You vulgar fellow! You truly did not realize that I was prostrating. Later, he said to his disciples:
"While I was in prison, I realized the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of Playful Mastery (*līlā-vikrīḍita*) as described in the *Lotus Sūtra*. The Sūtra says:
'The Bodhisattva plays with supernatural powers (*abhijñā*), purifies Buddha-lands, and does not take pleasure in [worldly] things; he censures those who are small-minded.'"
This is because they are unable to bring sentient beings to maturity. The disciple requested to hear his explanation. Nan said:
"Generally, when a prison official governs those who have committed crimes, he examines their true and false circumstances and invariably inflicts severe flogging.

Once the reality of their deception is fully exposed, they are released of their own accord. Even if there were cruel punishments, they could not be applied; even if the crime reached the point of death, it would still be accepted with equanimity."
The mind is that which reaches the point where intellect and emotion are exhausted. Now, those who study Chan suffer from the madness of frantic seeking and the disease of deception;

if these are not tempered by the wisdom of insight and knowledge, by what means can they be liberated? Therefore, throughout his life, he used only three kinds of speech to test the monks of the world.
Hongzhun was a native of Guilin; he followed Huinanyou for many years, possessing a natural aptitude.

He was pure and sincere, never having offended anyone. Upon hearing of another's virtue, he would speak of it as if it were his own; a radiant joy would well up from within him, manifesting between his brows.
When he heard of another's evil, he would invariably join his palms and strike the air as if in repentance.

In his later years, he did not take charge of the monastery affairs, but dwelt at Hanxi. His lifespan exceeded eighty years. At the time of his death, all his disciples had gathered for the funeral offerings; only...
A single servant remained. Daozhun took up his *qing* stone and sat before the altar of the Earth God (*tudi*). After reciting the *Ratnaketu-dhāraṇī Sūtra* once, he sat peacefully and passed away.
For three days his body did not incline; onlookers stood as thick as a wall. Suddenly, Daozhun opened his eyes and smiled, then had [the servant] sit upon the ground.

After a short while, a disciple returned. Daozhun called him to stand at his right side. For a long time they remained silent; when he looked, the disciple had already departed, his countenance unchanged.
Monastics and laypeople sculpted an image of him and enshrined it in a niche. Daozhen, style name Boxiang, was the son of the Dai family of Fuzhou.
His father dreamed that a majestic figure wearing a yellow crown and robes arrived at their home with a retinue of attendants; his mother subsequently became pregnant.

He further dreamed that a monk with bushy eyebrows and blue eyes arrived, and immediately thereafter, Zhen was born. From childhood, he abstained from meat. At the age of fourteen, he left the household life, and at nineteen, he received full ordination as a *bhikṣu*.
Having read through the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna sūtras and śāstras, he set them aside, saying, "These are merely expedient teachings. Thereupon, he took up a single alms bowl and departed.
Having traveled extensively throughout Jianghuai, he received the essential instructions from Fayuan. While traveling through Danyang, he stayed at Yinzhen.

One day, as he walked along the riverbank, he looked back at his boat and thought silently to himself, "I shall go wherever it leads; let me follow my karmic conditions. He asked the boatman, "May I ride on the stern of your boat?
The boatman laughed and said, "Where do you wish to go? My boat is bound for Bianzhou. Zhen replied:
I wished to travel to the capital, so I took him along northward to pay my respects to Huailian. Huailian ordered him to take his place among the assembly below the seat.
Benru, whose style name was Shenzhao, was a native of Siming. He initially relied upon Zhili to request instruction on the meaning of the *Sūtra-king*.
Ritual Master Li said, "Serve as my attendant for three years, and then I shall speak to you. After the service was completed, he requested him again.
Ritual Master Li let out a thunderous shout and then called out, "Benru! At this, Benru attained sudden enlightenment and presented a verse, saying: "Everywhere I encounter the path home;
At every turn, I return to my native land. This matter is originally manifest; Why wait for deliberation? Ritual Master Li said, "Toward..."
If I were to tell you now, how could there be a "today"? Later, while residing at Chengtian Temple on Mount Dongshan, he once saw a tiger sleeping in the southwest corner of the temple grounds.
He struck it with his staff and said, "This is not your place to sleep. The tiger lowered its head and departed.

He subsequently built a hermitage upon the spot where the tiger had lain, established a society for the recitation of the Buddha's name, and eventually it became a great monastery. Emperor Renzong bestowed a name upon it.
Bailian. On the fifth day of the fifth month in the third year of the Huangyou era, he ascended the seat to preach the Dharma and took his final leave of the assembly.
That evening, the rafters and beams of the Dharma Hall, the storage pavilion, and the abbot’s quarters all broke. When the bells and drums were struck, they produced no sound.
Fishermen on the river saw a monk in the clouds heading westward. At dawn the following day, he passed away peacefully in the right-side reclining posture. ○ Yiyu traveled...
At Xishan, he gazed upon the profound seclusion of the Twin Peaks and resided there for three years before finally responding to the invitation from Fachang.
Fachang was located north of Fenning; amidst thousands of peaks and myriad valleys stood but a few old rooms.

Upon arriving, Yuanwu found himself practicing "sword-plowing and fire-seeding" (slash-and-burn agriculture), which, though exceptionally peaceful and joyful, proved too austere for most monks. Unable to endure such deprivation, many abandoned him, leaving him a solitary practitioner.
Chan Master Shouduan opened the Dharma at Chengtian Temple in Jiangzhou.
While residing at Guizong, he lived in simplicity; when he was appointed to dwell at Chengtian Temple in Jiangzhou, his reputation became exceedingly great.
○ Chan Master Xuedou Chongxian Enters Nirvana (The fifth generation successor of Yunmen in the lineage of Zhimen Zu).
Chongxian resided at Xuedou in Mingzhou, where his school of Zen flourished greatly.

On the [blank] day of the sixth month in the fourth year of the Huangyou era, while wandering the mountains and surveying the surroundings, he said to his attendant, "When shall we return here again? The attendant sorrowfully requested a final verse of farewell.

Fahien said, "Throughout my life, I have only been troubled by the excess of words. On the following day, he took up his staff, distributed his shoes, robes, and alms bowl to his disciples, and said, "On the seventh day of the seventh month, we shall meet again.
When that time arrived, he washed himself, adjusted his robes, and passed away with his head pointing north. He was posthumously granted the title Mingjue (Bright Enlightenment).
Fahien once lamented that students seek the branches while losing the source, and thus composed the "Verses on the Daily Diminution of the Way."
It is said: "Two-thirds of one's life have already passed; the single point of the numinous altar remains unpolished. Wallowing in trivial pursuits, one greedily hastens toward the end of life;
when called back, one cannot turn—what can be done? Also known as the Verse on the Non-Correspondence of Name and Reality:

"The words of Buddhas and Patriarchs revolve like jade and roll like pearls; even mastery of them still defiles the field of the mind. Old Lu only knows how to husk rice; how could he attain the wind [of liberation]?"

This has flowed through the ages and been passed down. Furthermore, regarding the verse on the contrast between delusion and awakening, it says: "Drizzling plum rains sprinkle the high tiers; In the fifth month, the mountain chamber is cold as ice.
Do not say that heaven and earth have violated their great trust; It is simply that you have not yet realized the mind-ground is in a state of scorching heat.
Furthermore, regarding the verse on the nobility of being like a fool, it says: "The rain has passed, and the cold clouds part at dawn; Several peaks, like paintings, rise up in azure majesty."
"Śūnyatā-born (Subhūti) did not understand sitting in the crag; he provoked heavenly flowers to fall and the earth to tremble. Furthermore, the verse on "Great Merit Without a Master" says:
"At the peak of Oxhead Mountain, heavy clouds lock the sky; Sitting alone in vast stillness, this body is entrusted here.

A hundred birds do not come as spring passes by; I know not who is the person who reaches the hermitage. Furthermore, the verse on "Concealing One's Traces and Delighting Oneself" says: "The painting of those years..."
I love Dongting Lake; seventy-two peaks rise green from its heart. Now, reclining in ease, I recall those former times; Lu Gong has come to join me, leaning against the stone screen.
Furthermore, as he was rarely in accord with the world, he offered this verse: "The Gate of the Layman is high; I have not yet had the chance to visit.
For now, it is fitting to rest idly by these rocky crags. Of the thirty-six thousand acres of Taihu Lake, the moon speaks from its heart—to whom can it tell? And again:
The Verses on the Two Gates of Changing the Track: 1. The kalpa-fire once blazed forth; the wooden man’s tears fell first.
How pitiable is Master Fu, who everywhere loses his pavilions. 2. De-yun idly strikes the ancient mallet; how many times has he struck the peak of Miaofeng?
He calls out to that "deluded sage," making him carry snow together to fill the well. Before the Patriarchs and Buddhas were born, he had already beaten the poison-drum. Now...
Who would delight in hearing this? Please try to unravel the entanglements; three layers of winding, then winding again. True gold need not undergo a hundred refinements.
Vaisālī has been lost; no one knows how to look at the arrow. (4) ○ Yunfeng Yuan-yi, the Head Seat, attained the Dharma under Xuedou.
Li Linzong asked Yuan-yi: "I desire to transcend the mundane world, yet I have not yet done so. I request the Master to resolve this for me today."
Yiqing said, "What is it that transcends the mundane? Zong was bewildered. Yiqing asked, "Do you understand yet? At that moment, Zong suddenly attained realization and composed a verse, which says:
"The mirror of the mind has always been lucid; The great river is fundamentally deep. It was only after the Master’s question That I finally understood."
Sand and stones turned into gold. Zhiyi said, "You are heading straight for hell. Zong said, "I and you are without form;
why would there be hell? Zhiyi said, "Where are you now? Zong said, "I am here before you, answering you. Zhiyi said, "This very place is the golden land."
(Guisi) Chan Master Shouduan resided at Yuan tong.

Having already appointed Shouduan to head Chengtian Monastery, he further yielded the position of Yuan tong to him, taking up residence himself in the East Hall. At that time, Shouduan was twenty-eight years old;

because his predecessor had yielded the leadership of the monastic community to him, he felt a profound sense of personal responsibility and thus approached his duties with great reverence and solemnity.
The assembly, by setting aside their private interests for the public good, caused the ancestral style of the school to flourish greatly.
Guo Xiangzheng, whose courtesy name was Gongfu and alternative style name Jingkong, was born when his mother dreamed of Li Bai.

In the fourth year of the Huangyou era, when Foyan Qianqiu was residing at the Yuantong Shutang, Xiangzheng—then serving as the Magistrate of Xingzi County—went there to inquire about the heart-dharma. Later, when Qianqiu moved from Chengtian Temple to Yuantong Temple, Xiangzheng [continued his studies].
Furthermore, he was comforted by the influence of virtuous transformation; his comings and goings were especially frequent. Zongben, the son of Guan of Wuxi, was nineteen years old.

He served as a disciple under Chengtian Dao-sheng of Suzhou. Wearing tattered clothes and with a soiled face, he personally attended to the well and the mortar. At night, he would enter the room to pay his respects.
Dao-sheng said, "As a *dhūta* who bears the burdens of the assembly, you must be suffering greatly; are you not weary? Zongben replied, "If one were to abandon even a single dharma..."
He was named Mǎnzú Pútí (Fulfillment of Bodhi). Truly desiring to realize this very body through bodily witness (*kāyena sākṣātkṛ-*), how could he dare speak of weariness?
Shēng marveled at him. Ten years later, he shaved his head and received full ordination. After another three years, he took leave of Shēng to travel and study under various masters.

He visited Yìhuái of Chīzhōu. Huái raised the following question: "When Maitreya descended from the Inner Palace, Asaṅga asked: 'Four hundred years in the human realm correspond to one day and night in that heaven...'"

This constitutes one day and night. During that single period, Maitreya brought five hundred *koṭi* of devaputras to accomplishment, causing them to realize the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
It was not yet known what dharma he had preached. Tianqin said, "He preached only this very dharma. Thereupon, he questioned Ben.
"What is this Dharma? Furthermore, Huiyang had previously practiced the Pure Land method. He gave this instruction from within his room:
"If one says to abandon the defiled and take up the pure, or to loathe this and rejoice in that, this is the sentiment of grasping and rejecting—the deluded thought of sentient beings.
If one says there is no Pure Land, one again contradicts the words of the Buddha. For those who practice the Pure Land, how should they practice? He then answered himself: "When born..."

He was destined for birth [in the noble family]. When he departed, it was truly as if he had not gone. After long periods of initial inquiry, he finally attained enlightenment, yet none among the assembly were aware of it.
He once served as an attendant; he enjoyed sleeping, and his snoring was loud. Someone reported this to Huai, who said, "This youth is the banner of diligence for my house.
You all shall rely upon him in the future; do not speak of this much. Only then did the assembly realize the truth.
(Jia-mu) Chan Master Huinan resided at Jicui. Huinan resided at Huangbo;
he built a hermitage by the stream and named it Jicui. ○ Faryuan initially resided at Taiping Xingguo in Shuzhou, then resided at Tianping in Gusu.
In the first year of the Zhihe era, he resided at Fushan. One day, together with...
When the Academician Wang Zhi was discussing the Way, Xuanyuan drew a circle and asked him, "First, one must not have a single horse and a lone spear;
second, one must not return home wearing brocade. The magpie must not be joyful, and the crow must not suffer misfortune.
Speak quickly! Wang Zhi was at a loss. Xuanyuan said, "I have seen you through. Shouduan resided at Yuan Tong and upheld the Linji school’s style of teaching. Before long—

Ji Ju-ne was weary of worldly affairs and sought solitude. When the Prefect arrived, he expressed his status as a guest. The Prefect felt compassion and looked intently at Ji. Ji simply smiled and responded with a "yes" and "yes.
The next day, Ji ascended the seat and said: "Chan Master Fayan’s verse says: 'Difficult, difficult, difficult—it is difficult to dispel emotions.
When emotions are exhausted, the perfect luminosity is a single cold pearl. Even using skillful means to dispel emotions is still not it; one must further eliminate them.'"
"This is truly groundless. The assembly was asked, "How shall you deal with this emotion? He let out a shout, descended from his seat, and departed with his bundle over his shoulder.

The entire assembly was greatly startled; they tried to detain him, but could not, so he eventually crossed the river. He spent the summer retreat in an empty room at Wuzu Monastery and later at a small temple in Shuzhou called Fahua.
The Governor of Shu, having heard of Duan’s lofty reputation, sent an official letter inviting him to reside there. (Xingwei was a man of great stature.)

He was named Yu Shizi. At nineteen, he traveled to the capital to visit the Mahayana master Fangyi. For thirteen years, he served as a laborer, performing tasks such as clearing away debris, splitting firewood, and assisting with the cooking.
Only then did he shave his head, receive full ordination, and take leave of Fangyi to travel elsewhere.

He went to Luoyang to receive the teachings of the Xianshou school from the Great Tripitaka Master, where he achieved renown and succeeded him on the teaching seat; at times, there were always a thousand followers. Not long after, he traveled south and met [his] fellow...
Xue Falang dressed his skirts high and wrapped his two calves with cloth. He called out to those walking with him, who gathered to watch and sighed in admiration.
Falang merely smiled and exchanged greetings of courtesy. Daowei asked, "You now call yourself a practitioner of Chan; tell me the profound meaning of the Chan school.
Falang replied, "Wait until after I have died, and I shall explain it for you. Daowei said, "Are you mad? Falang replied, "I am already dead."
"Xixi, you are currently burning with great intensity. He then hurried away. Daowei asked his followers, "Liang’s learning and insight are profound and extensive;

his knowledge of the Dharma and understanding of its meaning exceed my own. Now that he has willingly joined this Chan school, there must surely be something superior about it. Thereupon, he went alone to visit Huinán.
(Biyu) Chan Master Shouduan established the Dharma at Baiyun.
While he was at Fahua, there were so many monastic disciples arriving that there was no room for them. The scholar-officials admired him, and he moved his residence to Haihui at Baiyun.
He addressed the assembly: "Clearly and brightly you know it—this is simply this very thing. Why do you fail to penetrate it? It is only because..."
When seeing someone open their mouth, one immediately calls it "speech"; when seeing someone close their mouth, one immediately calls it "a long silence.
Furthermore, it is said: "Every movement, every action, every word spoken, and every breath exhaled—throughout the entirety of the ten directions of the world, there is nothing that is not oneself.
Thus, people fall into the mire of conceptualization, lingering in their hearts with the resentments of former days. Have you not heard of Yunmen?
The Way is heard through sound; the mind is clarified by seeing form. He then raised his hand and said, "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, bring the money to buy some sesame cakes.
Lowering his hand, he said, "It turns out it was actually steamed buns. Furthermore, do you not recall when I was at Fahua, where I once addressed the assembly, saying:
"Master Wuye said that even a single hair’s breadth of thoughts regarding the holy or the ordinary—"

"Not yet exhausted. You have not yet escaped being reborn in the wombs of donkeys or horses. Great assembly, even if you were to suddenly exhaust all thoughts and sentiments regarding sagehood and ordinariness to the point of a single hair’s breadth, you would still not escape being reborn in the wombs of donkeys or horses.
You blind fellows, simply look at it like this! *Chan* (Investigate). He further addressed the assembly: “If you can truly bring forth a sweat once, then even upon a single blade of grass,”

He then manifested jade towers and crystal palaces. If you have not yet truly managed to break into a sweat once, then even if you possess jade towers and crystal palaces, they will be covered over by a single blade of grass. Now tell me, how can one break into a sweat? After a long silence, he said:
"I have a pair of hands that are utterly destitute; I have never easily performed the 'Three Platforms' dance. A monk asked, "When wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it.

What is it like when one speaks? The Master said, "Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun. The monk said, "In that case, there is nowhere left to stand. The Master said, "Pounded by the pestle and ground by the millstone.
The monk said, "The official will not tolerate even a needle; yet in private, carts and horses pass through. The Master said, "Indeed."
"Is it noble? Is it base? The monk snapped his fingers once. Fenduan said, "Exactly so. The monk stuck out his tongue.

Fenduan said, "Poverty at home is still tolerable; poverty on the road is what kills one with sorrow. The monk laughed heartily. Fenduan said, "I let you off by one move. Huailian resided at Jingyin Monastery.
He exchanged verses and eulogies with Emperor Renzong, and they sang and responded to one another in turn. This continued until the second year of the Zhihe era.
In the third month, he requested to retire to live in the mountains, but the Emperor did not grant his request. He dispatched an envoy to proclaim:
"The mountain is the very essence of suchness (tathatā). Where would you go? When the Emperor first read the *Recorded Sayings* of Touzi, a monk asked: "What is the white ox on the open ground?"
Touzi said, "Heh heh! From this point on, there shall be a mutual accord. He then composed fourteen verses on the Buddhist scriptures. Now, he presented one to Liaan, saying:
"If you ask about the Host, True stillness merges with the vast sky. Three heads and six arms— In the twelfth month, it is truly spring wind.
Liaan replied in verse: "If you ask about the Host, Its clarity resembles the azure void. Thunder and clouds stir from time to time."
The earth and heavens were filled with a harmonious breeze. The Emperor was delighted and bestowed upon him a bowl made of *nāgakesara* (dragon-brain) sandalwood.

After Hui-lian had finished expressing his gratitude, he said, "In the Buddha-dharma, one wears dyed robes and eats from an earthenware bowl. This bowl is not in accordance with the Dharma. He then burned it.

When the imperial messenger returned and reported this, the Emperor sighed in deep amazement. Hongying was the son of the Chen family of Shaowu. From childhood, he was alert and quick-witted; when reading, he could take in five lines at once.
Both parents descended [to meet him] and cherished him deeply. They intended for him to become a scholar, but Ying vowed not to eat until he could leave the household life.
Upon receiving full ordination, he immediately set out to seek the Way. Initially, he relied upon Cao Shan Ya; after a long time, he took his leave and ascended to Yunju Quan.
The cliffs and valleys were of supreme beauty, so he eventually shut his room and ceased socializing with others. Looking down upon the four seas, there was no one whose views accorded with his own.
He intended to grow old on this mountain; by chance, one night while reading the *Huayan Shiming lun* (Treatise on the Ten Clarifications of the Avataṃsaka), he reached the passage:
"Because true wisdom has no essential nature, it cannot know of itself that it lacks nature; thus it is the nature of the absence of nature. It cannot know of itself that it lacks nature."
Therefore, it is called ignorance (*avidyā*). The sixth stage of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* states: "Because one does not comprehend the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), it is designated as ignorance.
This indicates that since true wisdom is fundamentally without intrinsic nature, it cannot understand itself; yet, if it encounters conditions for comprehension, it does so.
Then ignorance will be extinguished. This is called the essential gate to attaining Buddhahood. I vow that by means of this Dharma, I shall perpetuate the lineage of the Buddhas.

Yet, in all directions today, with whom can one discuss this? After a long time spent walking in meditation at night, he heard two monks cite the karmic cause and condition regarding Hui-nan’s "Buddha-hand and donkey-foot.
Finding this extraordinary, he went to inquire where Master Nan was currently residing. They replied, "He is at Huangbo. At dawn, he set out directly.
He went to visit Huangbo. He conversed with him until dawn, saying, "The responsibility for carrying the Great Dharma rests entirely upon your person;
take great care of yourself. Pan Xingsi, style name Yanzhi, was a native of Nanchang. Initially, he was appointed as County Magistrate of Dehua. He was from the same prefecture as Xu Jian.

When he was first appointed as the Magistrate of Jiangzhou, he went to visit [Wu]ji. Ji did not offer him formal courtesy, so he returned home with his visiting card and ultimately did not take up his post.
He sought the Way from Huineng and received his seal of approval. He once said, "I am a reclusive scholar of a clear age," and thus styled himself the Layman Qingyi (Pure Recluse).
He lived in seclusion on the eastern shore of Donghu Lake in Yuzhang, delighting himself with the lute and books. One day, his fellow practitioners...
Qingyuan came to visit. Seeing him brushing his zither, Qingyuan said, "Even at such an advanced age, you are still fiddling with this string.
Sishi replied, "I want to play it so that it sounds right. Qingyuan said, "It is not few. Sishi said, "How many people can truly understand?
Qingyuan was the son of the Deng family of Yuzhang; his courtesy name was Qian’an. He was also a successor of Nanquan.
(Propyl Year, 7th Month) The Biography of Chan Master Huineng’s Dharma Heir, Xingwei.
Xingwei went to visit Huineng and remained in his service for two years. Every time he entered the master’s quarters, Huineng would invariably close his eyes; only after a long while would he speak.
Weiyi said, "When the Master sees Xingwei, why does he necessarily close his eyes? He replied, "When Magu saw Liangsu coming, he was carrying a hoe and weeding grass;
Liangsu attained realization there. When I see you coming, I simply close my eyes idly; though you may not attain realization."
However, there was still a doubt that remained. Wei Zizhi did not understand it. At that time, Ledan Yue was sitting in summer retreat with Nan at Jicui.

Yue was renowned for his mastery of the sutras and śāstras; Wei would often sit beside him to listen to their discussions. Consequently, while reading the *Biographies of the Lesser Śākyamuni*, he came across this passage:
"The Minister Wei asked Master Yangshan Ji, 'How do you usually receive and guide people, O Chan Master?'"
Ji said, "When a monk comes, you must ask him why he has come. The monk replied, "I have come to pay my respects.
Ji asked again, "Do you see me? The monk replied, "I see you. Ji then asked, "What does the old monk resemble? The monk had no reply. Wei said, "If he says he sees you..."
"But what about the donkey? If you say you do not see it, then whom are you currently paying homage to? Because of this, it was difficult to answer.
Jì said, "There is no one like the Minister in his analytical discernment. Yuèchēn praised him, and Wěi also agreed with this.

Nándú said, "That the lineage of the Míu-yǎng school has not reached the present day is due to this very fault. Wěi pondered this day and night, yet he did not understand its meaning. He was about to—
He traveled westward and established a hut beneath Mount Song and Mount Shao to serve as a rice-and-gruel monk. One night, he was sitting in attendance with another monk.
The monk asked, "The *Lotus Sūtra* speaks of attaining the *dhāraṇī* that understands the languages of all sentient beings.
What kind of speech is this *dhāraṇī*? He looked south toward the incense burner; the monk immediately reached out his hand to check for fire, but there was no fire. Again—
He then added incense sticks and stood in his place as before. Nanxian said, "It is this *dhāraṇī*. Daowei was struck with great surprise and asked, "How do you interpret it?
Nanxian told the monk to leave for now. As the monk pulled back the curtain and hurried out, Nanxian said, "If you did not understand, how could you have been like that?
Only then did Daowei attain realization. Nanxian resided at Huangbo, where students flocked to him from all directions. Although...

When those who had long been deeply immersed in study and had repeatedly sought instruction arrived, they would become despondent and lose their composure, and thus submit to the ranks of his disciples.
Pan Xingsi once asked him the reason for this. Nan said, "If a father is strict, his son will be filial. Today’s instruction shall serve as tomorrow’s model. It is like the earth:
that which is high it lowers, and that which is hollow it levels. He will eventually ascend to the heights of a thousand fathoms; as for me—"
I am also with it when it is exhausted and reaches the depths of the Nine Abysses; I am also with it then.
When its capacities are spent, delusions are exhausted and it is naturally released. It is further said: "To nurture and cherish is how spring and summer bring forth life;
to frost and snow is how autumn and winter bring things to maturity. How could I wish to remain without words? Furthermore:
In the southern hall, he once asked the monks: "Every person has their own karmic conditions of birth (*jìngyuán*). Where do you, Venerable Sirs, have your conditions of birth?
How is my hand like the Buddha’s hand? How is my foot like a donkey’s foot? For over thirty years, he presented these three questions.

The scholars could not fathom this. When someone ventured to respond, Nan said, "I do not know whether it is permissible or not. He sat with his eyes closed and his body poised. Xingsi asked him again for the reason.

Nan said, "Those who have already passed through the barrier walk straight ahead with their arms swinging; how would they know there is a barrier official? How could they ask the barrier official whether it is permissible or not?
This is one who has not yet penetrated the barrier. He then recited his own verse: "The circumstances of my birth, those who speak of them all recognize; The water jelly..."
When have you ever been able to leave the shrimp? You see only the sun rising in the east; who can further drink Zhaozhou’s tea?
My hand and the Buddha’s hand are raised together—Zen practitioners, realize this directly! Without moving a weapon, the Way is expressed; right where you are, you transcend Buddhas and Patriarchs.
My feet and the donkey’s feet walk side by side; at every step, one treads upon the Unborn. Wait until the clouds part and the sun appears.
Manifesting, one finally knows that this Way extends both lengthwise and crosswise. General Verse: Where the conditions for birth are severed, the donkey’s hoof is extended;
when the donkey’s hoof is extended, the Buddha’s hand opens wide. To report to the seekers of the Five Lakes: pass through each of the three barriers one by one. (Huiyuan)
He succeeded Xuedou and later relied upon Shanjian Xian. When the seat at Dongshan became vacant, Xian recommended him to accept the invitation from the people of Yunzhou.
At that time, Nan was residing at Huangbo; he traveled out of the city to meet him. Nan remained silent without saying a word, merely burning incense and sitting upright facing him.
From the hour of Shen until the third watch, Yuan rose and said, "It is late at night; it would hinder the Master’s rest."
He hurried out. The next day, they each returned to the mountain. Nan asked the head seat Yong, "While you were at Mount Lu, did you know this old man Dongshan?

Did you recognize him? Yong replied, "I did not recognize him; I have only heard his name. After a long silence, Yong stepped forward and said, "Master, when you saw him this time, what kind of person was he?
Nan said, "An extraordinary man. Yong withdrew and asked the attendant, "Did you accompany the Master when he saw Dongshan? What did you two talk about at night?"
When asked what had happened, the attendant told him the truth. Yong said, "I fear you have killed all the people in the world.

During the Jiayou era, the man Chen Qing was executed for spreading heretical rumors. Guyuan was sentenced to flogging because he had once stayed at Qing’s hut; he was then consigned to the labor camp in Chenzhou.

In the height of summer, while carrying earth along a main road, he set down his burden and sat down. Onlookers gathered like a wall around him as he recited this verse: [Verse omitted per instructions]
This morning, on the sixth day of the sixth month, Guquan’s retribution was fulfilled. He was neither ascending to heaven nor entering hell.

Having spoken thus, he smiled and passed away with a serene stillness like a cicada shedding its shell. A wondrous fragrance pervaded the air. When his body was cremated, the *śarīra* relics were beyond counting.
The people of Ch’en erected a stupa for them, which remains enshrined as a shrine to this day.
(Dingyou year) Hongying visited Chan Master Zhenke.
Just as he was entering the room for instruction, Zhen asked, "What is the meaning of a woman emerging from meditative absorption? Hongying reached out his hand, pinched Zhen’s knee, and departed.
Zhen laughed and said, "The customer who wants to buy spoons and chopsticks has not yet arrived. Zhen recognized that Hongying had transcended all constraints.

He broke free from conventional molds, and [the Master] praised him highly. ○ Fashou appeared in the world at Mount Sishimen in Huai. Aside from his staff and alms bowl, he carried nothing but his monastic robes.
Disciples flocked to follow him; Fashou, lamenting that the ancestral Way was not flourishing, took it upon himself to uphold it.
(Jihai) Qingxian visited Chan Master Huineng.
Qingxian was the son of the Zhuo family of Fuzhou. His mother dreamed that a foreign monk gave her a bright pearl, after which she conceived.
Upon his birth, a white light illuminated the room. From childhood, he would not approach wine or meat. He left home to travel afar; wherever he stayed, he rarely engaged with others.
There was one who approached him; with a single movement of his hand, [Changqing] sent him away. [The monk] served Huineng as a father. Neng held him in high esteem.
When the seat at Chengtian Temple in Jiangzhou became vacant, Juren selected Liaoyuan for the position. Upon seeing him, the regional commander looked down on him slightly, but Juren said:
Yuan’s physical appearance was youthful, yet his virtue was mature; even ten thousand aged monks could not have refuted him. Consequently, Yuan resided at Chengtian Temple.
Regarding the Dharma Flower [Sutra], no one knew its origin. He first encountered it at Jingde Temple and remained there for a long time in the lecture halls.
One day, while reading the *Record of Yunmen*, he suddenly attained awakening. Before long, his knowledge of past lives became fully realized. Thus it is traditionally said.

He recited the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, and thus this became his name. At times he would speak and laugh to himself; he frequently wandered through the market streets, sometimes raising his hand to trace patterns in the air or standing motionless for a long time.
He associated with butchers and wine-sellers, eating and drinking without discrimination. Both monastics and laypeople alike regarded him as a madman.
A monk asked, "Is the Master an ordinary person or a sage? The Master raised his hand and said, "I do not dwell here.

One day, Prime Minister Lü Yijian prepared an invitation for a *dhāraṇī* recitation feast (*fǎhuá zhāi*) and sent word in advance. The next day, [Fahai] arrived as expected and took his seat in the hall.

When Lü Yijian prostrated himself and asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, [the Master] replied: "Originally there is not a single thing; in one flavor, all is true. He was asked again.

When he arrived, he inquired whether [the prediction] was true or false. He asked for a brush and wrote the two characters "Bozhou" (Maozhou) in large script. Later, when he was dismissed from the相位 (prime ministership), he took charge of Bozhou and first realized the previous prophecy.
He gathered the assembly of immortals and kings and questioned them: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? [The Master] said:

"In the shadows of the green mountains, a surge of blue rises; the precious pagoda chants aloud, shaking the morning breeze. [The King] said: "Please have Fahu burn incense. [The Master] said: "Not yet."
He sought [the Way] through fasting and purification, rather than seeking it from the Buddha. His assistant, Xu Yue, asked about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West.

[Zongmi] said: "The one at the eastern end of the street. Yue said: "I do not understand. He replied: "Three kinds of people do not understand. When Emperor Renzong’s succession had not yet been established, he burned incense and prayed in silence at night.
On the following day, he prepared a vegetarian feast and reverently invited the Dharma Master Fahua. At dawn, the Emperor’s robes were damp with dew.
He stood waiting. After a short while, an attendant galloped in to report that Fahua was heading straight for the inner palace; though the imperial guards tried to stop him, they could not.
The Emperor laughed and said, "I invited him to come. A moment later he arrived and, without hesitation, ascended the imperial couch and sat cross-legged.

Having finished receiving the offerings, he was about to depart. The Emperor questioned him regarding the succession to the throne. [The Master] took up his brush and wrote the numbers "thirteen" three times in a vertical column;
then, casting down his brush, he left. When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, he was indeed the thirteenth son of Prince Puzhou An-yi.
On the day of his passing on the eleventh month of the *wuzi* year of the Qingli era, he said to those around him: "Since immeasurable kalpas past, I have brought this to fulfillment."

"In the land of Śrāvastī, I manifested my divided body to propagate the transformation [of sentient beings]. Now I return south. Having finished speaking, he passed away while lying on his right side.
(Gengzi year) Chan Master Daguan Tanying entered nirvana (the seventh generation of Linji, successor of Cuiyin Cong). Tanying resided at Jinshan.
On the eve of the New Year in the fourth year of the Jiayou era, he dispatched an attendant to send a letter bidding farewell to Diao [Yuan] of Yangzhou.

Jingchun said, "I shall depart at dawn; there will be no time for us to meet again. Take good care of yourself. When Jingchun opened the letter, he was greatly startled and cried out, "What shall we do?
He wrote back a final parting message and nothing more. In the middle of the night, he sent word to Yangzhou to dispatch a messenger by horse.

As the boat neared the shore, Huiming joyfully ordered the drums to be beaten and ascended the seat. There, he recounted the origins of his renunciation of the world and expressed his gratitude to those who had assisted the monastic community.
"Practice diligently and do not be indolent. A junior monk said, "After my passing, you should succeed me as the Head Monk (Xián Jiànsì).

Having finished reading the letter from Jǐngchún, the assembly crowded around him as he walked toward the Abbot’s quarters. Yǐng sat in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) and motioned for them all to stand at a distance. After a long while, he passed away.
Hóngyīng was traveling through the Western Hills when he stayed overnight with Pán Xīngsì at Shuānglǐng. Xīngsì said, "I have seen [the dragon pool] at Lóngtán..."
During the reign of Emperor [Wu] Ti, [the monk Seng]ying happened to encounter Confucius. Startled, he asked for the reason, saying: "Confucius said:
'My disciples, do you think that I am concealing anything from you? I have nothing hidden from you. There is no action of mine that I do not share with you; such is the person I am, Qiu.
What do you, Master, think of this? Ying laughed and said: "The people of Chu mistake the mountain pheasant for a phoenix; it is so handed down through the ages."
[The Master] laughed and said, "I did not expect that your words, Layman, would be so similar to mine. When you brought me tea, I received it from you;
when you brought me soup, I accepted it from you; when you came to greet me, I raised my hand. If you say this is 'speaking,' what exactly is being spoken?"

If one were to say that nothing was spoken, how could Longtan have attained enlightenment so easily? This is what is meant by "there being no dharma that can be spoken"—this is called preaching the Dharma.
Even with the eloquence of the World-Honored One, he could not add more than these two phrases. Students need only seek to understand and realize this.
It is like using five-colored paints to depict the void. In Bird Nest (Niaoke), there was no Buddha-dharma to transmit; he could not simply sit in silence.
He idly picked up a piece of cloth and blew upon it, whereupon the attendant attained enlightenment. Scholars have said, "Picking up the cloth and blowing upon it, his entire being was revealed.
Such an understanding has not yet emerged from the scriptural teachings (*śāsana*); how can such a person be called a guest in the gate of the Patriarchs?
When Jiufeng was asked, "Is there still Buddha-dharma in the deep mountains? he could not help but say, "There is.
When pressed further until he had nothing more to say, he replied, "The large stones are large; the small stones are small. Scholars speculate on this, saying:

"The lands preach, sentient beings preach, and throughout the three periods of time, preaching blazes forth. If this were truly so, the teachings themselves would be sufficient; why then [seek further]?
"Do you wish to further inquire about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? You must seek to attain clarity in your very being.
It is like a person with cataracts seeking medical treatment: the physician can only remove the film over the eye; he cannot bestow light upon them.

Thereupon, [Zhaozhou] pushed his chair forward and said in alarm, "I was worried that the Dharma-way of Jicui might have no successor. Now I know it rests entirely with you, my son; you are truly great."
Self-Love. Shun asked the Master in the Hermitage at Shuangling, "Good question for a student. [The Master] said, "Close your throat and lips and utter a single phrase.
The Head Seat had once spoken it; did you do so? Yinggan laughed. Later, he spoke a verse: "The mother-in-law tastes the vinegar with a three-foot beak;
The daughter-in-law washes her face and touches her own nose. Daowu’s answer to the question gained him a waist-cloth; Xuan..."
The letter opened to find it was on white paper. It was submitted with humility, thinking that beneath his name there was no empty title.
(Xin-chou year) Chan Master Qisong presented the *Record of the Orthodox Lineage of the Transmission of the Dharma*.
Qisong’s courtesy name was Zhongling; he styled himself Qianzi. He was born in Tengzhou into the Li clan of Tanjin. At thirteen, he received the tonsure.

At fourteen he received full ordination, and at nineteen he began his travels. At that time, in Ningfeng Village, there was an extraordinary woman named Yao Daogu, over a hundred years of age yet with the countenance of a young maiden.
She lived in strict austerity on a mountain, and Sengsong went to visit her. Daogu invited him to stay for two nights.
In the middle of the night, they heard a sound from within a pond like the clashing of copper vessels. Sengsong asked Daogu about it, and she said, "Ah, this is the dragon’s cry."
Those who heard this regarded it as an auspicious omen, saying, "In the future, you shall attain great renown in the world; proceed without delay.

Thereupon, he descended to the regions of the Yangtze and Xiang rivers and ascended Mount Chongyue to pay his respects to Shen Dingyin, but they did not reach a spiritual accord. He then went to Yuanjun, where he received the transmission of the dharma from Xiao Cong.
While traveling to Kuangshan, the abbot of Kaixian appointed him as secretary. Hui-sung laughed and said, "Would I do this for the sake of a single cup of ginger-and-apricot broth? He then departed.
He resided at West Lake in Hangzhou for thirty years, keeping his door closed and not engaging in idle social intercourse.

At night, he would carry an image of Avalokiteśvara upon his head and recite her name; he would only go to sleep after completing tens of thousands of recitations. From that time on, he was beyond the concerns of the mundane world.

Without having studied the chapters and sentences of the scriptures, he was able to compose them. He wrote over ten treatises on the origins of the teachings (*Yuanjiao lun*) to oppose the doctrines of Zongmi and Han Yu that sought to exclude Buddhism.

He compiled the *Record of the Orthodox Lineage of the Transmission of the Dharma* (*Chuanfa Zhengzong ji*) and the *Chart of the Patriarchs* (*Dingzutú*), establishing Mahākāśyapa as the first patriarch for uniquely inheriting the treasury of the great Dharma-eye, and tracing the lineage back through him to Bodhidharma as the twenty-eighth patriarch, who secretly transmitted the entrustment.

He established a system of written characters, calling it the "Separate Transmission Outside the Teachings. Once the work was completed, he carried it to the capital and presented it to Emperor Renzong along with a ten-thousand-word memorial, the gist of which stated:

There was no one who surpassed this man among the path-farers. When he arrived at Ruiwang Monastery on the day of the opening of the hall, the assembly gathered and struck the drum;

the drum spun upon the ground, revolving and resounding with a great roar. The crowd was startled and retreated, whereupon a monk stepped forward and said, "This is an auspicious sign that the Dharma-thunder of this Venerable One shall shake the earth.
As soon as he had finished speaking, the monk vanished. Zhenke resided at Mount Shan. He often inquired of the monk Luzu, who frequently saw monks...
He came to take his seat. Why did he immediately turn his back to the wall? No one had yet grasped his essential point (*ki*). He himself composed a verse, saying:

There was a scholar named Huang Guobo who asked Baizhang Hua: "Since you are Baizhang, why [did he do that]?"

He requested that Zhao speak on his behalf. Zhao said, "Just ask what will come next. Huang asked again. Zhao said, "Holding hands and walking together on the southern side of Mount Sumeru.

Huang stood there reflecting. He asked, "What is the meaning of this? Zhao said, "A mosquito biting an iron ox. Huang reflected once more and said, "I do not understand. Please, Master, [explain it to me]."
[The Master] said, "I shall speak for the sake of so-and-so. [The disciple] said, "Come away from your wife and children, and the old monk will speak for you.

He then rose and sat in the full lotus posture, called for his attendant, had incense lit, and entered nirvana.
(Year of the Earth-Snake) Biography of Chan Master Shouduan.

Fayan, whose secular surname was Deng and who hailed from Mianzhou, was thirty-five years old when he shaved his head and received full ordination at his home monastery. There, he recited the Lotus Sūtra, prostrating to each character as he went.

One night, while encountering the character "shǐ" (shit), just as he was about to chant the name of the character and prostrate, a sudden doubt arose. He immediately reported this to the elder masters, saying: [text continues]

"How can the character for 'excrement' (shi) also be called the Dharma Jewel? An elder said, "Based on what you have asked, you possess precisely the capacity of a vessel within the School of the Lineage (Zongmen).
On another day, he went to Chengdu to study the *Śata-dharma-vijñapti-mātratā-śāstra*.

There, he heard that when a Bodhisattva enters the Path of Vision (darśana-mārga), wisdom merges with principle and the object merges with the spirit; the means of realization and the object realized are not distinguished. [This occurred] in the Western Regions.
Daosheng once challenged a bhikṣu, saying, "Since you do not distinguish between the capacity to realize and that which is realized, by what means then do you realize? No one was able to respond.

The non-Buddhists (tīrthikas) disparaged him, ordering that he be forbidden from sounding the bells and drums and forced to wear the *kāṣāya* robe in reverse. When Xuanchi arrived there, he rescued this doctrine, saying:

"This can be understood. What is this matter of self-knowing? He then questioned his primary lecturer (Benjiang).
The lecturer said, "If you wish to clarify this, you should go to the South and seek out one who transmits the Buddha-mind school. Yan subsequently traveled south, arriving at Xingyuan.

After staying there for some time, he went with a monk from his quarters to attend a formal invitation. When his primary teacher heard of this, he sent a letter to Yan. Upon opening the seal, Yan saw only:
Two lines of verse say: "You have already emerged from the vinegar jar, yet you remain submerged in the soy sauce vat.
Yan then went to Zhexi to study under Zongben. He mastered all the kōans of past and present, yet there was one he could not penetrate.
A monk asked Xinghua, "When they come from the four quarters and the eight directions, what then? Xinghua said, "Strike the one in the center. The monk bowed; Xinghua said, "Yesterday..."
One day he went to a certain village. On the way to the midday meal, he encountered a sudden storm of wind and rain and took refuge in an old temple, where he was able to pass through it safely.
He requested instruction from Linji Yixuan (Linji Ben). Yixuan said, "This is a matter concerning the lineage of Linji;
you must ask his descendants before you can understand it. Thereupon, Huayan went to see Fayuan and asked about the previous conversation. Fayuan said, "I have a parable for you..."

It was just like a firewood-seller from a village of three households standing at a crossroads with a flat load on his shoulder, asking people, "What matters are you discussing in the Hall of Imperial Scribes today? Yanmo said to him, "If that is the case, it is not yet sufficient.
Yuanzhi said, "Yan’s capacity is extraordinary. One day he said to him, "I am old; I fear you will let this opportunity pass in vain."
"Guangyin, you may go and rely on Baiyun. Although this old man was born later than I, I have not yet met him in person;
however, having seen his verse on the story of Linji’s three blows of the staff, I know he possesses a capacity that transcends ordinary men and will surely enable you to realize the Great Matter.
Yanqian bowed and took his leave. Upon arriving at Baiyun, Shouduan said, "Laiju, have you come? He then raised the case of a monk asking Nanquan about the ox-headed man.
Regarding the story of Nizhu: he asked a question, and Duan rebuked him; Duan showed him again, citing the circumstances of the World-Honored One’s secret words and Kāśyapa’s lack of concealment.
After a long time, he had not yet attained realization. One day, as he was hurrying up the hall from the corridor, his state of doubt suddenly vanished.
He offered this spontaneous verse: "A plot of vacant land before the mountain; With palms joined, I earnestly question my forefather:
How many times have I sold it only to buy it back? Out of love for the pines and bamboos that draw in the pure breeze.
Duan Te granted him formal approval, saying: "The Zen of the thorny jujube fruit belongs to you. Having received the seal of the mind, Zuxin went again to visit Zhenke. Zhenke spoke with him.
He marveled at this greatly. After staying with him for two years, Zhen passed away, whereupon he returned to Huangbo. The Southern Envoy [Changsha] shared the seat with him and received him.

Qiji said, "I have seen Master Wei; he has found a place of peace and happiness. Yong said, "Try explaining it to me. Qiji then recounted what he had attained.
Yong said, "You are Wei, but you are not yet [the true] Wei. Qiji returned home unable to fathom this and told Wei about it.
Wei laughed heartily and said, "You are not Yong, yet you are not not-Yong. Qiji went to Jingcui and questioned Nanquan about it; Nanquan also laughed heartily. Yong [heard of this].
Upon hearing this, he composed a verse, saying: "Light and darkness intermingle; the pivot of killing and enlivening— This is the realm of the Great Man, known by Samantabhadra.
Born from the same root, yet dying on different branches— It makes one laugh to death that old, ancient master in the hermitage."
