Again, he addressed the assembly: "Heaven and earth share the same root as I; the myriad things are of one body with me.
From head to foot, they extend horizontally and vertically. If a fire were to break out in the continent of Uttarakuru, it would burn the eyebrows of Śakra."

Mao, the Dragon King of the Eastern Sea, could not restrain his pain and let out a single clap of thunder that caused the oceans to overflow and the mountains to collapse, darkening the vast sky with clouds.

At this moment, Old Zhao of the Ten-Crossroads Street woke up from his drunken stupor, clapped his hands, and laughed heartily, saying, "In the city of Yunchang, there have been few thieves lately. He then took up his staff and said, "Thieves! Thieves!"
○ Chan Master Mingjiao Qisong Enters Nirvana (The fifth generation of Yunmen, successor to Dongshan Cong).
After Qisong returned from the capital, he increasingly devoted himself to writing. The Academician Cai Xiang invited him to reside at Furi Temple.
After several years, he retired to the Yong’an Hermitage north of Lingyin. Every clear morning, he would recite the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
He ceased [his activities]. After his midday meal, he read books. When guests arrived, they engaged in pure conversation that did not touch upon worldly affairs.
On a day in the sixth month of the fifth year of the Xīníng era, he rose at dawn and wrote a gāthā: "The moon is bright in the late night; I now walk alone.

I do not emulate the old man of Dàméi, Who was greedy to hear the cries of the flying squirrel. At midnight, he passed away. During the cremation, five things remained indestructible: his crown, ears, tongue, [teeth], and [flesh].

He remained in the state of pure innocence (*kumārabhūta*). His prayer beads, which he always carried with him, and his cranial bone both produced *śarīra* relics, red and white, crystalline and pure, shaped like large beans.
He lived to the age of sixty-six, having spent fifty-three years in the rainy-season retreats (*varṣā*). Over one hundred volumes of his collected writings were circulated in the world.
(Guichou) Dharma Master Haoyue Huibian entered nirvana. Huibian, styled Nuweng, was the son of the Fu family of Huating.
He resided at the lecture hall of Tiantong Temple in Hangzhou. Su Shi, who was then serving as the Prefectural Governor, frequently visited him for spiritual excursions beyond the secular world.
For twenty-five years he lectured and taught, with a following of over a thousand people coming and going. There were none...
Why did he retire to the thatched hall? On the morning of a winter day in the sixth year of the Xīníng era, he rose, washed his face and hands, took leave of the assembly, and passed away.
Yìqīng was the son of the Lí family from Qīngshè. Having left home to receive the full precepts, his teacher sent him to study the *Śataśāstra* (Treatise on the Hundred Dharmas).

Before long, he sighed and said: "The path of three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* is far; what benefit is there in exhausting myself? Thereupon, he went to Luò and listened to the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra* for five years. He then turned his gaze inward.
"Texts," he said. "They are all like meat on a skewer; everywhere their meaning and flavor are the same.

Once, while lecturing upon the verses of the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, he suddenly had a sharp realization and exclaimed, "The Dharma transcends words; how can it be lectured? He immediately abandoned his studies to travel abroad.
Upon reaching Fushan, he found that at that time Fayuan was living in seclusion at Huishengyan. There, Fayuan dreamed that he obtained a fine hawk and raised it.

When he awoke, Qing had arrived. [Hui]yuan quickly took this as an auspicious omen and received him with formal courtesy, instructing him to contemplate the kōan concerning the externalist’s question to the Buddha regarding whether to ask about speech or non-speech. After three years, Yuan asked, "Do you remember the pivot of the dialogue?
Try to bring it forth. As Qing was about to respond, Yuan covered his mouth with his hand; Qing attained clear and thorough awakening, whereupon he prostrated himself.
Baizhang bowed. Yuan said, "Have you attained a subtle realization of the profound mechanism? He replied, "Even if there were one, it must be spat out.
At that time, Attendant Zizhi was standing nearby and said, "Qing Huayan has today been like a sick man who has broken a sweat. Qing turned his head and looked back, saying, "Shut that dog's mouth!"
From this point on, another three years passed. Yuan went out to the foot of the cave and revealed the fundamental tenets to him. Qing fully and wondrously harmonized with them;
he subsequently entrusted him with his *dàyáng* (Great Yang) robe and sandals, saying: "Succeed me in continuing the tradition of the Dòngshàng school; protect and uphold it well.

Du Yan and Zhang Fangping both retired from official service and resided in Suíyáng. Du Yan often laughed at Fangping’s devotion to Buddhism; whenever he was in the company of guests, he would invariably mock him.
Fengping merely smiled. There was a man named Zhu Chengshi who traveled between the two elders' gates for the sake of medical science.
He said to Fengping, "Master Du is a great man in the world; it is a pity he does not yet know of this matter. Why do you not encourage him to awaken to it?
Fengping replied, "Your karmic connection with this elder is more mature than mine; I can only assist him. One day, Zhiyuan summoned Zhu.
He felt his pulse with great urgency. Zhu said to the messenger, "Go first and inform the Gentleman [Zhang Shangying], but simply say that you have not yet finished reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.
The messenger galloped off to report this. Zhiyan remained silent for a long while before finally arriving. Zhiyan said, "I considered you a man of broad learning and capable understanding;
I did not expect that recently you too would fall into the ranks of the mediocre and dull. As for this so-called *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, what kind of talk is it that you are so obsessed with?"
"Indeed. The subtle words of the sages do not exceed those of Confucius and Mencius. To abandon these and adopt others is a great delusion.
Zhu said, "Since you, Excellency, have not yet read this scripture, how can you know that it does not equal Confucius and Mencius? From my perspective, it seems to surpass them."
From within his sleeve, he produced the first scroll and said, "Your Excellency, please examine this. Yan took it and read it silently; before he knew it, he had finished the entire roll.
Suddenly, he rose in great alarm and exclaimed, "How could such a book exist in this world? He dispatched a messenger to bring all the remaining scrolls.
He read it through entirely. Taking Zhu’s hand, he said, "You are truly my spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).
An Dao knew this; why did you not tell me? He immediately ordered his carriage to visit Hui Ping. Ping said, "It is like a person who has lost an object and suddenly finds it again.

One should simply rejoice in the recovery; there is no need to regret the lateness. It was not that I did not wish to inform you, but rather because of the karmic affinity between you and Master Zhu."

He simply sent him away after he had matured [his understanding]. Even when Buddhas and patriarchs transform people, they must necessarily rely on "commonality of purpose" (*samānārthatā*). Yuan was greatly delighted.
Yuan’s courtesy name was Shichang; during the Qingli era, he was titled the Prime Minister of Integrity and Purity and enfeoffed as the Duke of Qi.
(Yimao) Chan Master Jingduan resided at Westyu in Huzhou.
He was the son of the Qiu family of Wuxing. Having left home and received full ordination, he studied the Tiantai teachings and listened to the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.

Upon reaching the section on the "Seven Investigations and Eight Returns," he knelt and spoke this verse: "The seven places investigated the mind, yet the investigation did not succeed; Ānanda remained bewildered."
Do not glance at it; simply cause him to investigate until he realizes the state of no-mind. This too is merely pouring earth into the mud.
The teaching of the "Eight Returns" has been transmitted for a long time; since antiquity, the ancestral styles have each been analyzed and divided.

Even if one reaches the point where there is nothing further to return to, it is still like a shrimp that cannot leap out of its basket. He then composed a verse. An alternative version of the commentary says: "Winding and twisting like a door hook, one—"
"Each turn of the whisk brings forth a new wave of sorrow. It would be better to become a Zen monk; when you reach the state of no-mind, simply rest there.

Chanqi Yue, having attained silent realization within the master's room, immediately stepped out onto the courtyard floor, turned his body around, and threw himself down. Yue certified his attainment.
Later, upon seeing a person playing with a lion, he was further awakened to a sense of urgency. He then fashioned a lion skin out of colored cloth and donned it;
consequently, he was known as Duan Shizi (Lion Duan). He resided in Xiyu, which was close to Huzhou. On snowy mornings, he would wear his colored robes and enter the city;
children would clamor and chase after him, and he would beg for money from them, giving it immediately to the poor. He frequently recited the Dharma.
He was fond of chanting the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* and also enjoyed singing the lyrics of the "Fisherman. There was a mad monk named Tóuhuítóu who deluded the masses with heterodox ways.
While he was eating meat with Lü Gong, the Governor of Rùn, Duan walked straight up to him, pointed at him, and asked: "At this very moment, what is the Buddha?
Tóuhuítóu was so flustered that he had no reply. Duan struck him on the head, pushed him over, and departed. There was also a sorcerer...
Fahao Butuo excavated the ground outside the city walls of Xiu Prefecture and discovered a Buddhist statue. He erected a stupa upon it, and the entire city came to revere and believe in it.
One day, while Fahao was gazing intently at the statue, Duan seized him, asking, "What is the Buddha? As Butuo hesitated, Duan kicked him away and departed.
Zhang Bo’end, style name Pingshu, was a native of Tiantai. He once traveled to Chengdu, where he met a Realized Man (zhenren) who bestowed upon him the elixir of the Golden Elixir (jindan).

He received the secret instructions on the firing of the elixir. In the second year of the Yimao cycle, he composed the *Wuzhen pian*. Furthermore, by extensively studying under Chan masters, he attained realization;

upon reading the *Zuying ji*, he suddenly clarified the ground of his mind. He then said: "The Elixir is the supreme treasure of the physical body; once refined, its transformations are inexhaustible."
Furthermore, he was able to awaken to the True Principle within his own nature and decisively realize the wondrous function of non-arising. Later, he passed away while sitting in the lotus posture.
Upon cremation, a thousand or ten hundred grains of *śarīra* were obtained. Subsequently, there were those who saw him once again.
(Dingsi Year) Chan Master Sengyin entered nirvana (the Dharma heir Jian of Chengtian). Sengyin resided at Ruian.
In the ninth month of the tenth year of the Xining era, he bathed, changed his robes, and left behind this verse: "The numinous sword leaning against the void floats with cold radiance;
Buddhas, patriarchs, and demonic armies are gathered by a single stroke. Carrying the moon and roaring with the wind, it returns to the precious scabbard. Iron [sword].
The oxen were startled and scattered across the head of Qujiang. Having finished speaking, he sat in *padmāsana* and passed away. Upon cremation, five-colored *śarīra* relics were obtained.
(Wu-wu year) The layman Wu Xun visited Master Zuxin. Wu Xun’s courtesy name was Defu.
In the first year of the Yuanfeng era, he served as the legal magistrate (*faco*) of Yuzhang. At that time, the regional commander Wang Shao invited him...
When Zu Xin entered the city, Xun went there to pay his respects. Zu Xin said, "I shall not ask about your lifelong studies, your intellectual understanding, or your extensive learning.

Instead, bring me a single phrase for the time before your parents were yet born. Xun was at a loss for an answer. Consequently, he spent day and night contemplating these words until he suddenly realized their meaning for himself.
Before he could manifest this realization, he happened to read the biography of Deng Yinpeng and saw that he had passed away while standing upside down.
When he removed his robe, it likewise conformed to his body without slipping off. He suddenly wondered, "That transformation was extraordinary and thus unfathomable;
yet why does the robe also conform to it? He questioned his own mind. The mind said, "As you stand in attendance now, is this conformity or is it opposition?

He replied, "It is conformity. [The mind] asked, "Do you still have doubts? He replied, "I have no doubts. [The mind] said, "Since you yourself have no doubts, why do you doubt that other? Be certain of these words."
He then offered an explanation, presenting three verses that said: "No gateways within, no flanks on four sides; Students toil in vain, frantic to grasp shadows. Take heed:
the moon of the ancient garden Has remained as it was all night, never hidden. "I, a former disciple of Layman Lufeng, Have painted the Master’s true likeness with perfect fidelity.
Gathering the entire earth to form a single eye, It turns and surges forth in a manner quite extraordinary."
Generally new. Ha! This fellow of much worldly knowledge has gnawed through all the public cases of the past and present.
Suddenly, from amidst a heap of filth, he picks up a dung-ball of a dung beetle—obviously not worth a single coin, and not to be exchanged for ten thousand taels of gold.
He casually picks it up and shows it to others, simply because a spinning plate is difficult to watch. Hei! In his heart, he also offers two verses, saying: "In the water..."
Attaining the Fire-World is rare even in this age; looking at it makes one’s doubts all the more peculiar. From of old, there existed neither teacher nor disciple;
now, however, the Old Barbarian is permitted to know. At the Sea Gate, the mountains are perilous and tracks are cut off; having trodden the sturdy barrier, the Way is truly passed through.
"The foundation for an era of Great Peace already exists; it does not matter whether one is from the south, north, west, or east. Wuxin was the son of the Huang family of Qujiang.

At birth, he had a purple fleshy covering on his left shoulder that exposed the right, resembling the shape of a *saṃghāṭī* robe. He was tall and imposing with a dark face like that of a monk from India.
Upon reaching maturity, he shaved his head and surpassed all others in his integrity and resolve. He was fond of confronting people directly with his criticisms. Initially, he went to visit Fashou.
Xiu asked, "Where are you from, Senior? He replied, "Guangnan Shaoshan. Xiu asked, "Have you ever been to Yunmen? He replied, "I have.
Xiu asked, "Have you ever been to Lingshu? He replied, "I have. Xiu asked, "What are the branches and twigs of Lingshu?

He replied, "The long ones are naturally long; the short ones are naturally short. Xiu said, "The barbarians of Guangnan must not be allowed to rule in disorder. He replied, "To the north, donkeys are just like this."
Ma shook his sleeves and departed. He then went to Huanglong to pay his respects to Zu Xin. Xin held up his fist and asked, "To call it a 'fist' is to encounter resistance;
not to call it a 'fist' is to turn one's back. What do you call it? Ma was at a loss for an answer.
It took two years before he finally attained realization; yet, his eloquence remained unimpeded. Zu Xin was concerned by this, and while conversing with him, they reached this point...
Ruì said, "Hurry up! Stop, stop! Talking about food—how could that ever satisfy a person? Xīnwù was at a loss for a reply and spoke calmly, saying, "Wùxīn has reached this point;
my bow is broken and my arrows are spent. I pray that the Master will, out of compassion, point out a place of peace and happiness.
Ruì said, "A single speck of dust flies and obscures the heavens; a single mustard seed falls and covers the earth. As for a place of peace and happiness, I fear you, Reverend, are already there."
There are many antiquities; one must simply die the thieving mind that has persisted for immeasurable kalpas before it can be resolved. Xintu went out.
One day, while sitting in silence on the lower platform, he heard the administrative officer beating a novice. Suddenly, like a bolt of lightning, he experienced a great awakening.
He hurried to see [Huayan] Xinxin. Forgetting to put on his shoes, he praised himself, saying, "Everyone under heaven has merely 'studied' the Way;
only I have 'awakened' to it. Xinxin laughed and said, "To be ranked first in the examination for selecting Buddhas—how could you possibly match that?
He was thus nicknamed "Old Man Sishin" (Dead Heart). His dwelling was titled "The Chamber of Dead Heart. Fashou initially resided at Sifan in Huaixi, and later moved to Qixian.
The worthy Changlu of Mount Jiangshan: During the Yuanfeng era, the Grand Councilor Jiang Yingshu was a spiritual friend to Xiu.
He composed thirty chapters of a commentary on the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, for which he held considerable confidence in his own insight.

While serving as the Transport Commissioner on the Huai River, he visited Xiu at Changlu and inscribed upon the wall of the abbot’s quarters: "I have spent three days composing this commentary on the *Avataṃsaka*. Regarding the Buddha-dharma, I—"
"There is a great causal connection. On another day, this land shall be compared to the eastern outskirts of Vārāṇasī;

only those who possess the Buddha-eye shall know it. Xiu said, "Why do you speak so lightly? As for the *Avataṃsaka*, it is the Perfect and Sudden Supreme Vehicle, realized through direct perception (*pratyakṣa*).
To now say it is comparable to the eastern outskirts of Vārāṇasī is to employ inference (*anumāna*); it is not the Perfect and Sudden school."

It is said: "On another day, the one true dharma-realm has neither past nor present; therefore it is said that throughout the ten ages of past and present, beginning and end do not shift from the present moment.
If one speaks of "another day," how could "this day" not be it? Furthermore, it is said: "Only those who possess the Buddha-eye can know this. As the Sūtra says:
"In the equal and true dharma-realm, there are no Buddhas and no sentient beings; when the sentiments of ordinary and sage are exhausted..."

When both self and other are forgotten, how could there be any distinction between the foolish and the wise? If one must wait for the Buddha-eye, then would the celestial eye and the human eye not be unable to know [this]?
Shu repented and apologized. Zanyuan resided at Jiangshan. At the beginning of the Xining era, Wang Anshi was appointed as Chancellor;
his prestige shook the world, and there were no months that passed without news of him. Yet Yuan never once spoke of it. Anshi’s younger brother, Anshang, asked about the Buddha-dharma.
The general meaning is as follows: Yuan said, "Buddhas and patriarchs are no different from ordinary people. That which makes them different is simply their ability to guard their own thoughts.
A tree atop a high peak must have a root; its root lies in the tiniest sprout. Water that floods the heavens must have a source; its source lies in a mere trickle.
If one stirs a thought within the pure and tranquil mind without cause, how perilous and precarious it is—worse even than a tree on a high peak. Vast...

Yet, their arrogance and license exceed even the "overflowing to the heavens" [of the flood]. How could they be moved? The Buddhas and Patriarchs transmitted the Dharma to one another, invariably exhorting them with these words:
"Guard and uphold it well for yourself. When asked, "Is the Buddha-Dharma merely this? they replied: "The most beautiful is not ornate; the ultimate word is not prolix."
Now, vanity and worldly entanglement are extremely far removed from the Way. Yet, in the customs of the age, these are used to express public discourse on the methods of governing the world;
it is still said that those who bring order to the state do not rely on many words, but rather on how they practice their efforts. How much more so, then, regarding the supramundane Dharma?
In the first year of the Yuanfeng era, Shi retired from the government. When his boat reached Shitou, the carriages and horses of the scholar-officials filled the mountains.
When Gu entered the monastery, it was already past the second watch. Yuan came out to welcome him; after a single bow, he withdrew.
Shi sat on the eastern side, while his officials and guests filled the seats. Shi looked around and asked where Yuan was. An attendant replied, "He has been asleep for a long time."
(Jihwei) In the fourth month of the second year of the Yuanfeng era, Chan Master Chenghao opened the Dharma at Dayang.
Zhang Shangying, while serving as an envoy to the Jingxi Nanlu circuit, heard the name of Guinyin’s head seat, Chenghao, and went to see him.
He asked, "Whose Dharma heir are you, Master? He replied, "Beitapa of Fuzhou."
[The Master] asked, "What words or phrases did Beita have? [Fengxue] replied, "It was simply because he refused to explain it through to others.

Ying praised this as excellent and subsequently invited Daoyuan Hao to reside at Dayangshan. Zhao Bian retired from office and returned to Quzhou, where he built a residence named Gaozhai (High Studio).
He composed a verse which said: "Girded with gold, I have already retired and hidden away; The message within this is but ordinary. People of the time..."
"One must know that the old man of Gaozhai is simply Zhao Sili of Ke Village. He spoke again, saying, "Be careful not to mistake him.
Furthermore, he recorded on his tomb mound: "My official duties have been fulfilled; I am seventy-two years of age. After a hundred years, I shall return to this mountain land."
That true *dharmakāya* is neither identical to nor separate from [the world]; it fills the great trichiliocosm and universally manifests compassion and wisdom.
It cannot be hidden away, nor can it be set aside. Such is the meaning of the discourse on the "graveyard. Thus it was, in the eighth month of autumn in the seventh year of Yuánfēng.
One day, he suddenly took leave of all his relatives and friends. His son Jí asked about his final affairs, whereupon Bì rebuked him with a stern voice. After a short while—
He spoke as he normally did and passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. His age was seventy-seven; he was posthumously titled Qingxian (Pure Contributor).

Yuanjing resided at Upper Tianzhu, where the Tiantai teachings flourished greatly. At that time, there was a madman in Xiuzhou known as "Turning Back" who deluded the masses with heterodox ways, proclaiming that a stūpa should be built as a field of merit for the people of Wu.
Donors gathered like clouds, yet they were intimidated by Yuanjing and did not dare [to proceed].
Upon entering the borders of Hangzhou, he first sent one hundred thousand coins to the Upper Tianzhu Temple to provide a meal for the monks, dispatching a messenger with this message:
"I have now provided a certain amount of funds for construction; I wish to offer them for the maintenance of one hall. Jing replied in a letter:

"I acknowledge that you intend to use these pure offerings (*śuddha-dāna*) for the purpose of feeding the monks. I have heard that the scriptures contain explicit instructions prohibiting the interchanging of such funds. Since the Holy One has left us [this teaching]..."
Minghui said, "I do not know what words to use when addressing the Buddha; I await your instructions to compose the memorial text.
When he turned his head, he was greatly startled and felt ashamed before his disciples. However, Jing’s own disciples urged him to pay his respects for now.

Jing spoke with a stern voice, saying, "One who has left the household life must possess the true eye to succeed. If he were truly a sage, how would I dare not show him respect? But if he is merely a charlatan—"

[The Master] said, "This is delusion. To know [the Buddha] and yet equate him with such [delusions] is to lose right mindfulness. I have heard that the Holy One possesses the supernormal power of knowing the minds of others.
This evening, we shall earnestly entreat him. Tomorrow, we shall come to this mountain to observe the fast together with the Buddhas of the ten directions.

He then knelt according to the ritual, recited the text of the petition, and burned it. The next day, he led the assembly out to welcome him, but as they turned their heads, he had not arrived at all.
(Gengshen) Chan Master Chenghao resided at Yùquán.
Having stayed at Dàyáng for several months, he moved to take up residence at the Jìngdé Chan Monastery at Yùquán. Hao’s spiritual acumen was solitary and sharp.

The students were unable to reach a consensus. At that time, the position of Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera) was vacant. The Rector (Karmadāna) said, "Such-and-such a person and such-and-such a person have previously established a monastic community at such-and-such a place;

they are the ones to whom the Zen assembly turns for guidance. It would be appropriate to follow the custom of other regions and invite one of them to fill the post. Huihao rebuked him, saying, "Dullard! Dullard!"
It is also said: "Meng Babang, Meng Babang! One day, Huihao passed by the kitchen and saw them preparing evening noodles. He asked, "Are there guests coming?
They replied, "The assembly of monks is preparing their midday meal (*yao-shi*). Huihao called for the administrative official (*zhishi*) and addressed him, saying:
"In the past, when I practiced Chan, I drew water and pounded rice for others. Now, with rice and flour already prepared, you simply steam and cook them to provide this meal. Thus he spoke.
The Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Arhats are no different [from this state]. Having eaten their fill, they pay no heed to study or cultivation.

Amidst a hundred kinds of discursive thoughts and the fragrant scents of the five flavors, they falsely fashion the entrails of donkeys into meals and stewed bones of live sheep and turtles to feed the eighty thousand parasites within the corpse.
"With eyes open, you follow and are bound by sensory objects; with eyes closed, you follow and revolve within dreams.

You do not know that the Lord of Fate, the Judge of Merit, and the Great King Who Seizes Excesses will follow you to compile a record and erase your ledger of provisions. The day will surely come when they cause you to suffer.

Thereupon, the assembly, unable to endure their desolation, slandered the county magistrate, saying: "The Elder cannot settle the community; he only looks down upon those above and looks up to those below."

He departed. [The official] inspected the minor items. The County Magistrate summoned Huìhào and reprimanded him, saying, "Great *kalyāṇamitra*, you should not be wandering back and forth between the two corridors and the mountain gate instead of sitting upright within the abbot’s quarters.
Huìhào replied, "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten *kalpas*, yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him;
he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood. Your Excellency, you take sitting to be the Buddha."
"Indeed! You have committed the crime of killing the Buddha by sitting here. The official was bewildered and, with even greater reverence, paid him homage.

Zuxin resided at Huanglong for twelve years. Five times he requested to leave. In the third year of the Yuanfeng era, he retired from his duties and lived at Xiyuan, naming his hall "Hui" (Obscurity).
He said, "What I have resigned from are worldly affairs; now I wish to devote myself exclusively to the practice of the Buddha-dharma. Thereupon—
A notice was posted at his door, saying: "To all students of Chan: if you wish to exhaustively realize this Way, you must examine it for yourself; no one can take your place.

During your practice, if you should happen to penetrate the causal conditions, you will naturally find a point of joyful entry. Only then should you come to the inner chamber to disclose your realization."
Wait for me to evaluate the right and wrong, the deep and shallow; as long as it has not yet been revealed, simply rest. The Way will manifest of itself.
To toil and strive in pursuit of it only increases confusion and distress. This is the Way that transcends words; its essence lies in self-acceptance, not in awakening through another.
Only when it is revealed in this way will you clearly understand and penetrate the root of birth and death throughout immeasurable kalpas. If you see...
To attain the Way that transcends words is to see that all sounds, forms, speech, right, and wrong are nothing other than this; there is no separate dharma.
If one does not perceive the Way that transcends words, one will instead take the various causes and conditions encountered before one's eyes and use them as the realization attained.
I only fear that you will mistakenly recognize the gateway; failing to realize the light and shadow before your eyes, you will instead produce superfluous teachings.

In the end, this is nothing but self-deception and a waste of mental effort. It is therefore fitting that you should, day and night, discipline yourself with sincerity, observing while walking and standing.
Contemplate with subtle scrutiny; do not apply your mind to anything else. After a long time, there will naturally be a way of entry.

This is not a matter of achieving mastery through study over days or mornings. If you are unable to investigate and examine in this manner, it would be better to read the sutras and recite your prayers to pass these remaining years of life;
this would still be superior to living in confusion and slandering the Dharma. When the time comes to spend your final years, I dare guarantee that you will become a person of no [delusion].
As for serving people, I have no other burdens. As for the rest of those who enter my room, I shall visit them only twice—on the first and fifteenth days of the month; please come to see me then.
When Xie Jingwen was governing Tanzhou, he sent for Guishan Xin to lead the Great Miao Monastery, but Xin declined three times and would not go.
Jingwen asked him the reason, and Xin said: "Before Mazu and Baizhang, there were no affairs of 'abbot' (zhuchi). Practitioners sought one another in empty and secluded places."

"It was merely a matter of dwelling by the shores of solitude. Although there were abbots thereafter who were honored and venerated by kings and ministers as teachers of gods and men, the situation today is not so.
They merely hang their names upon government offices like subjects registered in the census, and are simply dispatched to be summoned by the *wubo* (police runners).
How could such a thing be done again? Therefore, Jingwen did not dare to trouble him with matters of the monastery, but wished instead for a single audience."
Huishin traveled to Changsha. Jingwen wished to receive his dharma instruction, and Huishin accepted him as a disciple. His fundamental principle was stated as follows:

"The Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teaching are like describing food to someone else. Since the flavor of the food depends on the description of another, the essence of the food must be personally tasted by oneself.
Once one has personally tasted it, one can fully know its flavor—whether it is sweet, pungent, salty, or bitter."
Fading away. When Bodhidharma came from the West, he pointed directly at the human mind to see one's nature and attain Buddhahood; it was likewise thus.

Since the true nature is manifested through words and letters, the essential point lies in seeing it for oneself personally. If one can see it personally, one will be able to fully understand what is currently true and what is delusory, and what constitutes birth and death.
Once one can fully understand the distinction between the true and the delusory, as well as birth and death, one turns back to contemplate this one [mind].
All spoken words and written characters are merely conventional expressions; they possess no ultimate reality. If you do not understand this now, where does the illness lie?

The illness lies in seeing, hearing, cognizing, and perceiving. Because you do not know the true limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) as it truly is, you mistake these acts of seeing, hearing, cognizing, and perceiving for what you have personally seen.
You fail to realize that these acts of seeing, hearing, cognizing, and perceiving all arise dependent upon external objects.

Yet there is still discrimination. If there were no external objects before one, then this very seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing would be like the hair of a tortoise or the horns of a hare—having no point of reference at all.
Jingwen heard what he had never heard before. ○ Changzong first visited Huineng at Guizong;
having gained nothing, he departed. When Guizong was destroyed by fire, Huineng moved to Shimen Nanta, and later moved to Huangbo Ji.

Cui. He later moved to Huanglong; he resided at all these places in total. Over a period of twenty years, he traveled back and forth seven times, receiving the essential instructions of the Dharma in secret and resolving his will to greatly support the Linji school.
He left the secular world to reside at Letan. In the third year of the Yuanfeng era, an imperial decree transformed the monastic quarters of Donglin from a Vinaya center into a Chan seat.
When the Academician Wang Shao was appointed as the Governor of Nanchang, he wished to invite Zen Master Zu to preside over it.

Hui-zhi took charge of the community, assuming full responsibility on Hui-yuan’s behalf. When it was known that Hui-yuan had fled under the cover of night, Liu Yao issued proclamations to all districts, ordering them to search for him everywhere.
He was found in a remote valley at Xintu and subsequently accepted his summons. Monastics from all over the world gathered there, drawn by his reputation;

they spoke among themselves, saying, "Master Huiyuan possessed a prophetic record stating that seven hundred years after our extinction, there would appear a Great Being in human form who would reform our Way."
This place now accords with his words. ○ Xingwei resided at Mount Yangshan. During a summer night while sitting in a deep forest, he bared his torso to feed the mosquitoes and gadflies.
Subsequently, his intestines became poisoned; it did not heal for ten days. He severed them with a knife for about a foot, yet the flow of blood would not stop.
The disciples wept and said, "Master, why alone do you not endure [this] for even a little longer? He replied, "Because it obstructs my practice of the Way.

Prostrate upon this bed, I shall be of no benefit to anything; is death not better than life? On the [blank] day of the eleventh month in the third year of the Yuanfeng era, he spoke a *gāthā* and passed away.
Upon cremation, five-colored *śarīra* were obtained, with his bones and stones linked together by cords. A stupa was erected.

At the eastern [section] of the monastery, there was one from the Peng family of Pingxiang who had traveled extensively throughout various regions. In his later years, he arrived at Letan to study under Changzong.

After a long time, he had not yet received formal certification. Changzong showed him the karmic conditions concerning the bird’s nest and the blowing of cloth hair, but he did not understand them at all.
One day, he suddenly attained enlightenment to the essential meaning and composed a verse, saying: "In disheveled neglect of artifice lies the Bird's Nest; West Lake..."
On the lake, he controlled the smoke-net; when the cloth-hair was pulled out, there were not many seeds remaining. Even those with iron eyes and copper pupils could do nothing about it.

Zongyin certified this, and from then on, he was promoted as the head of the assembly. In the third year of the Yuanfeng era, Zong took up residence at Donglin, and subsequently used Qian to succeed him on the Dharma seat.
Kai-xian Guangjian Xingying was the son of the Mao family in Gui Prefecture. Initially, he visited Qingxian. After some time...

He realized the profound essence of the teachings. Next, he studied under Changzong, where his doubts were suddenly extinguished. He served as the world-transcending founder for nearly twenty years. Initially, he suffered from chronic phlegm and abdominal ailments;

though he repeatedly requested to leave, he was not permitted to do so. He lay ill in the monastic quarters for three years, after which he rose one day and resolved to renovate the Buddhist monastery from its foundations.
It took nine years to complete. Su Che (style name Ziyou), whose sobriquet was Yingbin, was the younger brother of [Su Shi]. Together with his elder brother...
Su Shi was of equal renown [to the masters of Chan]. He once offered a verse to Liaoyuan, saying: "Coarse sand is offered to the Buddha, and the Buddha joyfully accepts it;
A strange stone is offered to the monk, and the monk does not disdain it. I have come from afar empty-handed—do you still require anything?

There is nothing else that can be added. Liaoyuan said: "Held in empty hands, it is difficult to let go; The Three Sages and Ten Holy Ones gather their heads to gaze upon it. This kind of offering can..."
He partook of the offerings; even the wooden horse and the clay ox were delighted. In the third year of the Yuanfeng era, Zhe was exiled to Gaoyang.
He met Huangbo Quan, who looked at him intently and said, "You are serene and wise. If you devote yourself to the school of our lineage, why should you fear not accomplishing this Way?"
Zhe had thus participated in the entirety [of the teaching], yet there was no realization. It happened that Chong came to reside at Shousheng;
Zhe went there to inquire about this matter. Chong did not answer. Zhe pressed him further, and Chong said, "Yuanzhao never spoke of the Way to others;
I now have nothing with which to speak to you. Thereupon, Zhe attained the meaning beyond words. He subsequently studied under Shun of Hongzhou, who showed him the method of "pinching" (chù).

Regarding the "rhinoceros horn" (the nose) as the causal condition, Zhe attained great enlightenment upon hearing the words. He presented a verse, saying: "In middle age I heard the Way and realized my former errors;
By chance we met, the old Master Shun. Pinching the nose, I directly entered the true countenance; Shaking my head, I would not accept any other hammer or tongs.
Withered cane and tattered robes—what business have you, sir? White wine and green salt—who am I? I am ashamed before the waning moon over the eastern eaves."
A cup of ambrosia, as smooth as molasses.
(Xin-you) Chan Master Qingxian entered nirvana (the ninth generation of Linji, dharma successor of Huanglong Nan). Qingxian resided at Longqing Xitang.
On the seventh day of the third month in the fourth year of the Yuanfeng era, he informed the assembly that he was about to enter extinction.
He spoke in verse: "Exposed and manifest in this floating world, Suddenly entering extinction. Fifty-three years [of life], In the sixth, seventh, and eighth months.
On the Southern Peak and Tiantai, Pine winds and mountain stream snow. Take care, O connoisseur! A red furnace and an *utpala* flower.

Having finished the verse, he entered the bath. Upon emerging from the bath, he sat naked; only then did he place a cloth over his knees and pass away, his countenance and expression remaining unchanged. As they were dressing him, his hand—

His feet were supple and soft. After his hair had been shaved, it grew back again. When a painter approached to copy his true likeness, his head suddenly raised itself; the next day, it returned to its normal position.
When the Prefect came to view him, he wished to keep his entire body [as a relic], but the monk Liyan said, "His final instructions command that he be cremated."
When the fuel was exhausted, the fire was extinguished; yet his legs remained crossed in the lotus position without dispersing.
They doused the remaining wood with oil, and only after adding more did it finally burn away. On that day, clouds rose and winds blew, flying roof-tiles and breaking trees.

Wherever the smoke reached—forty *li* in every direction, east, west, south, and north—all among the grasses, trees, sand, and pebbles yielded *śarīra* relics, golden in color. The total amount obtained was nearly several *hu*. (Su Che)
I wished to compose a commemorative inscription for him, yet I harbored doubts regarding his affairs. At that time, I was lying ill with a fever. In a dream, someone rebuked me, saying:

"Master Xian’s deeds—why do you doubt them? Doubt leads to illness. Within the dream, I composed an inscription, which said: "I bow my head to the Honored One of the Three Realms; Master Xian’s achievements did not stop at this.
Out of pity for the narrow-minded and inferior of the world, he merely displayed a small portion of his greatness. ○ Shaoxian was a native of Quanzhou. He attained...
Fazhi Xian resided at Xinghua. He possessed great discernment and managed a community of a thousand followers as if they were merely one, two, three, or four.

At first, Changsha was unaware of the benefits of providing meals for the Sangha and making offerings to the Buddha; however, Xian organized a great assembly known as the "Karmic Connection Feast" (jueyuan zhai).
Subsequently, those who emulated him held such feasts every month. Among the people of Jing and Hu, there was none who did not admire them, and the practice even spread to the Man tribes.
At that time, Chancellor Zhang Dun was on a mission to the Jinghu region to open up the Meishan area. He traveled there together with Huixian.
When the local Miao elders heard Huixian’s name, they all joined their palms in reverence and submitted to his regulations. Huixian played a significant role in the pacification of Meishan.
In the eight prefectures of Xiangnan, several hundred monks were ordained each year; during the height of Huineng’s flourishing influence, monastics from Jinghu flocked to Jiangnan.
For over a hundred *li*, there was no place to lodge, and the area was frequently plagued by bandits and robbers.

When Xiàn was fifty years old, he established a guest house and invited the *Sengzhu* (Abbot) to preside over it, so that travelers might be received, provided with lodging and food, and allowed to depart. Later, he contracted a paralytic ailment, and his left hand became insensate;

nevertheless, he continued to oversee the affairs of the monastery’s administration. Every day, he joined the assembly of monks for the morning gruel and meal. Xiàn took diligent practice as his primary Buddhist service. [The] high officials...
He was revered as an ancient Buddha. On the [blank] day of the ninth month in the fourth year of the Yuanfeng era, he passed into *nirvāṇa*.
When his body was cremated and the *śarīra* were collected, his two eyeballs remained uncorrupted, and his two intestines likewise remained uncorrupted.

As more oil was added and the fire intensified, they burned like iron bands, curving and twisting with a brilliant color. Consequently, they were enshrined together in a stupa. ○ Yiqing moved from Baiyun Haihui to reside at Touzi.

At Mount [Name], the disciples advanced even further; those who attained secret penetration and hidden realization were exceedingly numerous. This truly fulfilled the prophecy that "the strange sprouts would flourish anew.
Initially, when Master Daotong first opened the mountain, he had left a record saying: "If my stupa turns red, it shall be my second coming.
Later, the local people happened to repair his stupa, and it took on the color of agate. Not long after, Qingling took charge of the monastery affairs. ○ Muzhe heard this at Linchuan.
As for the master’s disciple, Zhen: when he was traveling abroad, Zhé was able to recognize his potential. Zhen was naturally bold and expansive, possessing a stature that surpassed others;
he was nicknamed "Zhen the Chest-Tapper. Zhé associated with him for twenty years without ever witnessing a lapse in propriety.

Zhen said to others, "Thirty years from now, Zhé will perform great Buddhist works. After Zhen passed away, Zhé enshrined him in a stupa on West Mountain and observed a period of mourning for three years before departing.

While traveling through the region of Xiang, he moved with his single alms-bowl as clouds drift and birds fly; his coming and going weighed the prestige of the monastic communities. When Xie Jingwen was serving as the governor of Tanzhou, he invited him to reside at Yuelu.
Shortly thereafter, he was transferred to Daguang Miao, where his assembly numbered two thousand. He imposed no formal constraints upon them, yet everyone regulated themselves.
Only after the morning gruel did he receive his disciples to inquire about the Way, which was termed "entering the room. In other quarters, this occurred but once a month.

Furthermore, Master Zhe lectured on it without a single day of omission. After the evening session ended, Zhe would personally engage in manual labor, treating his attendants as if they were strangers passing by.
Morning incense and evening lamps continued for fourteen years. At night he performed prostrations, holding a broom to check the lamps in the halls and corridors;
when weary, he would cover his head with his cassock and take a brief nap in the Hall of the Three Sages. During his time as a commoner, the scholar Xu Xi—
Yi encountered [Hui]yu and recognized him as exceptional from the very beginning. On the day before Yu was to pass away, he composed a verse to bid farewell to Xi, saying:

"This year I am seventy-seven; when setting out, one must choose an auspicious day. Last night I consulted the tortoise-master, who reported that tomorrow morning will be auspicious. Xi was greatly astonished.
He called for Hu Weiqing to go with him. Upon meeting Fang, who was sitting in his quarters, he entrusted the affairs of the monastery to the *jian-si* (superintendent), saying:
"I have resided on this mountain for thirty years, and because I wished to protect and cherish the permanent property (*changzhu*), I have personally supervised it every day.
Now I am departing; you all must be diligent. Having finished speaking, he raised his staff and said: "Tell me, to whom does this belong? Xī and Qing were both [startled].
He held his breath. He then cast himself to the ground, lay upon his bed with his arm as a pillow, and passed away.
(Renxu year) Chan Master Zongben resided at Qionglung Fozhen Zongben. He presided over Ruiwang.
The Governor of Hangzhou earnestly requested him to reside at Jingci. He remained there for nine years. In the fifth year of the Yuanfeng era.
Zeng Xiaoxu, the Academician, escorted him back to console the people of Suzhou who were longing for him. He resided at Mount Qionglung.
While he was staying at Jingci Monastery, a woman of the Zhang family had died; her mother dreamed that her daughter’s karmic retribution had turned her into a snake.

Upon waking, she found the snake beneath the coffin and brought it to Ben, who preached the Dharma for her and instructed her to place the snake back in its original spot. Suddenly, a black cicada flew over the coffin and the snake vanished. The mother—
The Master said, "If my daughter truly enters my cage, I shall take you further to Jingci Temple. She did indeed enter. The Master then preached the Dharma for her.
The woman said in a dream, "I am fortunate that I have been liberated from the two retributions. Puzi was the son of the Xie family of Jianyang.

In his youth, he studied Confucian classics and gained renown as a candidate for the jinshi examination. Later, upon reading Buddhist scriptures, he came to recognize the source of his own mind; his innate spiritual faculties were awakened.

He subsequently left the household life and received ordination. Having received full precepts, he traveled to various regions and visited Fushan Fayuan, where he entered the master’s room to seek instruction;

his mind merged with the truth and his spirit attained realization. The people of Shu invited him to reside at the two monasteries of Ganlu and Taiping, where his reputation for the Way spread widely.
Later, Zizhi retired to Jingyin. In the fifth year of the Yuanfeng era, the people of the capital requested that he reside at Huayan Temple in Dongjing. [Huaizhi of Jinhua.]
The son of the Wu family entered the monastic order and joined the lecture halls for twelve years.

He once desired to synthesize the divergent doctrines of the various schools, composing a work to be transmitted to posterity in order to clarify the fundamental intent of the temporal teachings throughout the generations. A Chan practitioner said to him:
"Du Shun was the patriarch of the Xianshou school; yet when he spoke of the Dharmakāya, he said: 'In Huai Prefecture, an ox eats grain; in Yizhou, a horse’s belly [swells]. "
Zhang [asked], "To which principle of Tiantai does this verse ultimately refer? Zhi was unable to answer. He then traveled to Dongshan to consult Kewen.
He asked, "Regarding the ancients' 'one shout,' it was not used as a single shout; what was its underlying meaning? Kewen scolded him. Zhi stepped out.
Kewen laughed and said, "A monk from Zhejiang enjoys mountain wandering after his midday meal. Zhi attained realization. After some time, he took his leave.

The inscription read: "Although your Zen is of an extraordinary caliber, it is a pity that your karmic conditions are not sufficient. Zhi understood its meaning; he bowed in gratitude for the gift and departed.
He dwelt in a hermitage on Mount Heng for over twenty years. When scholars and officials visited his dwelling, he did not pay them much heed or respond.

When people asked him the reason, he said: "Those men of wealth and rank are eloquent, erudite, and widely learned. I am but a monk who eats his rice; my speech is dull and slow, and I have nothing [of value] to offer."
He spoke thus, naturally departing in a state of simple-mindedness. A verse says: All myriad affairs are brought to rest, entrusted to the simple and the foolish;

Its traces at times allow the wild deer to join in. Not removing the hempen robe, he makes his fist a pillow; For many lifetimes, his dreams have remained in the Green Silk Hermitage. [The questioner] asked about the Master’s dwelling in the mountains.

"What is the underlying intent? Zhi said: "Dwelling in the mountains, I alone shut my thatched gate with no other pursuit. Three pieces of firewood, arranged in the shape of the Chinese character 'pin' (品), are roasted;
there is no need to wield a brush for literary brilliance to be revealed. Daokai was the son of the Cui family from Yizhou. From his youth, he abstained from grains to study the Way.
Later, he traveled to the capital, where he received ordination and the full precepts. He visited Yiqing at Haihui Temple and asked about the Buddha.
"The ancestral words and phrases are like the everyday tea and rice of a household. Apart from these, are there any other words for instructing others?
Qing said, "You say that when the Son of Heaven issues an edict within the realm, does he still need the aid of Yu, Tang, Yao, or Shun?
Kai attempted to offer a reply, but Qing struck him with his whisk and said, "From the moment you first conceived the thought [to speak], you have already received twenty blows. Thereupon—
Kai suddenly realized the meaning of the teaching; he bowed twice and immediately departed. Qing called out, "Come back! but Kai did not look back.

Qing said, "Have you reached the stage of non-doubt? Kai covered his ears with his hands. Later, when Kai was in charge of the communal meals, Qing asked, "The kitchen duties must be quite exhausting.
Kai replied, "I dare not say so. Qing asked, "Do you cook the rice yourself? Do you boil the porridge? Kai replied, "I have hired laborers to husk the rice and prepare it."
At Huo, while the practitioner was boiling gruel and cooking rice, [Qingyuan] asked, "What are you doing?
He replied, "Out of compassion, Master, you have let me be at ease. Later, they went to visit Qingyuan. Qingyuan gave him a staff and said, "It is only right that it should be so.

He replied, "Carrying the Master's shoes and holding his staff is no extra burden for me. Qingyuan said, "There is another companion here. He replied, "That one person does not accept instruction. Qingyuan [nodded].
He then left. When evening came, Qing said, "The conversation from earlier was not yet finished. [Fayan] said, "Please ask him to continue.
Qing said, "Born in the hour of the Rabbit (Mao), born in the month of the Dog (Wu). Fayan immediately had a lamp lit and brought it over. Qing said, "Coming up and going down—none of it is in vain."
[The Master] said, "It is fitting for those who serve at one's side to act in this manner. [The attendant] said, "Every household has its servants and maids.

[The Master] said, "As for a monk of advanced years, it is impossible to do without them. [The attendant] said, "With such earnest devotion, you will surely have the opportunity to repay his kindness.
In the fifth year of the Yuanfeng era, he emerged from seclusion at Xian Dong in Yizhou. He subsequently presided over Zhaoti, Longmen, Dayang in Yingzhou, and Dahong in Suizhou.
On the *guihai* day [the 18th day of the fifth month], Chan Master Yiqing of Touzi entered nirvana (a dharma heir of Dayang Xuan and the seventh generation of the Caodong school).
Yiqing resided at Touzi. In the fourth month of the sixth year of the Yuanfeng era, he manifested slight illness.

He then sent a letter of farewell to the local magistrate and various officials, as well as to his lay patrons (*dānapati*). On the fifteenth day of the fifth month, after ascending the hall to bid farewell to the assembly, he wrote this verse: "Two..."
"Abiding in this position, there is nothing that can assist the Way. Take care, all of you; there is no need for further seeking. Thereupon, he set down his brush and passed away.

His remains were cremated, and his relics and sacred bones were collected and enshrined in a stupa at Sanfeng Hermitage. At first, he followed Yue, serving as the head of the assembly under Daowu. He led several disciples and went to visit Shouzhi.
Before Shouzhi had spoken more than a few sentences, [Daoyuan] fully understood the depth of his realization. Shouzhi then smiled and said, "I observe the Head..."

Yuanzhao’s bearing was extraordinary; yet how could his speech and breath be like those of a drunkard? Yuanzhao blushed with heat and sweat broke out as he said, "I pray that the Master will show me compassion.
Zhi then spoke further to him, piercing him with sharp words. Yuanzhao was left utterly bewildered and subsequently requested to enter the room for instruction.

[Dongshan] replied, "You should simply investigate where that smell of urine arises. Yuan Yue then went to visit Fayan Wenyi and profoundly grasped his profound meaning.
