Guang’en replied, “There is nothing to be doubted. Gaō said, “As for the ancients, they knew whether one was sincere or insincere before a word was even spoken;
or upon hearing their words, they immediately recognized their depth or shallowness. How is this principle to be understood? Guang’en was struck with awe. Gaō then instructed him:
Jiuyouju Wujun once asked Dayang Hengzhao, "When I arrive at this point, I cannot attain thorough penetration. Where does my illness lie?
He replied, "Your illness is most peculiar; why do the physicians of the world fold their hands in helplessness? Others may die, but they cannot bring you back to life."
"Though alive now, one has never truly died. To reach the ground of great peace and bliss, one must die once; only then can it be attained.
Because of this, Guang became even more doubtful. Later, he entered the room. Daokao asked, "The porridge is finished, the bowl is washed, and the medicinal taboos have been removed.
Bring me a phrase! Guang said, "Torn asunder. Daokao let out a thunderous shout and said, "You are talking about Zen again! Guang—

He immediately attained great enlightenment. Daogao struck the drum and addressed the assembly, saying: "To grasp the hair of a tortoise, one laughs heartily; with a single blow, ten thousand layers of locks are opened.
What joy and fulfillment in my life is found this very day! Who would say that a thousand li have deceived me here? Guang presented a verse, saying:
"A single pressure brings forth the roar of a thunderbolt at the opportune moment; It startles the Mount Sumeru and causes the Northern Dipper to hide within it. The vast waves roll on boundlessly—"
[The waves] surged to the heavens. [Zhaozhou] held his nostrils but lost his mouth. ○ Zonggao, Guanyin, and Lin Shike, the Magistrate, established a hermitage on Haishang.
Yangyu welcomed Zonggao, who subsequently moved his residence there. Tanyi and Zunpu had once studied together under Keqin; they claimed to have reached a state of non-doubt.
Tanyi took up the position at Xiangyun, with Zunpu assisting him; the Dharma assembly was quite flourishing. Zonggao took note of this.

His realization was not yet stable; fearing he might mislead the assembly, Yuanwu sent a letter ordering him to come. Xuyi hesitated. Dahui Gaofeng, during a *xiaocan* (informal discourse), severely rebuked his errors and issued a public proclamation to the fourfold assembly.
Only then did Xuyi break his summer retreat to come and see Gaofeng. Gaofeng interrogated him regarding his realization, saying:

"With such a view as yours, do you dare claim to be a successor of the Elder Yuanwu? Xuyi returned home and subsequently withdrew from his monastery, whereupon he went together with Daopu to rely upon Gaofeng.

At a Dharma assembly, one day Xiangguo asked Xingpu, "Regarding the dialogue concerning whether San-sheng and Xing-hua 'came forth' or 'did not come forth,' and whether they were acting as men or not acting as men:
tell me, do these two old fellows have a place to manifest themselves, or not? Xingpu gave Xiangguo a punch on his knee.
Xiangguo said, "This punch of yours—was it to vent your anger for Xing-hua, or was it to vent your anger for San-sheng? Speak quickly!"
"Quick! said Baizhang. As Yantou Puxiu hesitated, Baizhang struck him across the back with a staff and said, "First of all, you must not forget this one blow.
On another day, while listening to another monk enter the room for private instruction, Baizhang asked the monk, "When Deshan saw a monk enter the gate, he immediately struck him with his staff."
When Linji saw a monk enter the gate, he would immediately shout. When Xuefeng saw a monk enter the gate, he would immediately say, "What is this?
When Muzhou saw a monk enter the gate, he would immediately say, "This is a ready-made case; I grant you thirty blows. Do these four old fellows have any way of benefiting others?
[The Master] said: "They do. [The Master] said: "Zha! A monk hesitated, and Baoguo immediately shouted and sent him out. Puxiu.
Upon hearing this, Yi suddenly attained realization. One day, when Yi entered the inner quarters, Xuedou Gao asked him, "I want someone who does not understand Chan to serve as National Teacher.
Yi replied, "I shall go and serve as National Teacher. Gao shouted and drove him out. After a long time, Gao said, "Xiangyan’s place of awakening was not at the point where the bamboo was struck;
Jushi’s place of awakening was not on the tip of his finger. At these words, Yi also attained realization. Later...
Yi. He resided at Yuquan. Dingxu was the son of the Lin family of Fuzhou; his style name was Lan’an. As a youth, he sat for the jinshi examinations and achieved renown.

At the age of twenty-five, while reading the *Śāriputra-prakaraṇa* (The Sutra of the Bequeathed Teaching), he suddenly exclaimed, "How nearly have I been misled by the scholar’s cap! Desiring to leave the household life, he sought ordination.
His mother, concerned that he was of marriageable age, urged him to take a wife. He replied, "The peach and the apricot shall be entrusted at once;

as for the spring breeze, the green bamboo, and the yellow flowers, from now on they shall be my companions forever. In the end, he followed Baoshou to become a monk and traveled with his single staff through Huxiang.
He traveled extensively to consult renowned masters. Upon returning to his hometown, he built a hermitage on the summit of Qiang Peak and did not descend the mountain for three years.
Focin (Fuxin) later enticed him out to lead the assembly. Once, when he was asked by a student about the karmic conditions regarding "the mind itself is Buddha," Zonggao was then residing at Yangyu.
Mingguang and Xu were close friends; Mingguang sent a letter saying, "The master’s methods are distinct from those of other quarters; you should come."

Fayan Xiu was somewhat reserved and did not respond to [Zhaozhou’s] questions. Guoqing invited him to attend a gathering by means of a stratagem. While Wumen Guang was leading the assembly into the room for private instruction, Xiu followed the crowd and took his place in the ranks.

Guang asked him about the koan "The mind itself is Buddha; how do you understand this? Xiu offered a response, whereupon Guang rebuked him, saying, "With such a level of understanding, how dare you presume to act as a teacher to others?
He then beat the drum for a public sermon and exposed Xiu’s lifelong shortcomings. [Guang concluded with: "Take care! (Zhenzhong).
Regarding the points where he had gained strength, he dismissed them all as erroneous interpretations. He reflected upon his own delusions and perversities until tears flowed down his cheeks.
He thought to himself in silence: "If what I have attained is not the truth, then what indeed is the meaning of that which was not transmitted from the West?
Thereupon, he returned his heart to the ranks of the disciples. One day, Dayuan asked: "When there is no letting out within and no letting in without—at such a time..."
"How is it? Xu needed to open his mouth to respond. Daogao raised his bamboo staff and struck him three times across the spine.
Xu suddenly attained great enlightenment and, without realizing it, cried out, "The Master has already given me too much! Daogao struck him once more. Xu prostrated himself.
Daogao laughed and said, "Today you finally know that I have not deceived you. He then sealed this with a verse: "The top of the head stands erect like a *māṇavaka*."
*Xi*. A talisman for snatching life, slung diagonally from the elbow behind the eye; it blinds the eyes—remove the talisman. Zhaozhou hangs a gourd on the eastern wall.
○ Zuyuan was the son of the Lin family of Fujian. He studied under Zonggao at Yangyu. Yuan’s physical bearing was lean and austere, and he would sit upright all day long.
Zonggao called Yuan "the withered tree. He once said: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is [something]."
[The Master] spoke. After three or four days of rigorous questioning, one day while sitting in meditation, he saw a monk trim a lamp.

Suddenly, he attained a sudden, expansive realization. He presented a verse, saying: "Trimming up the lamp, it is fire; It shatters the ignorance of kalpas. Returning to the hall, I bump into the Holy Monk;
I nearly let him slip past my face. What is it that does not slip past? For fifteen years, it has been extraordinary; As before, it remains just so."
"This is it. Hongzhao Zonggao certified this with a verse, saying: "Leaping off a precipice ten thousand fathoms high, Rising up, one is as ever clearly awake.
Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, there is nothing at all; What need is there to discuss whether one is the person of old or not? Zonggao resided at Yangyu.
Among those who attended him, there were only fifty-three people, yet within less than fifty days, thirteen attained the Dharma. At that time...
The followers of the school set aside sublime awakening, leaving students mired in silent stagnation. Daogao composed a treatise to forcefully refute their errors.
A scholar from Min named Zheng Ang, style name Shangming, was brilliant and well-versed in all fields; having had some contact with venerable masters, he spoke of Chan with ease wherever he went.
One day, carrying incense, he entered the master’s room, his voice and expression both stern, saying: "I, Ang, wish to settle this matter with you, Master."
"This matter is simply like remaining silent and without words; it is the foremost place of rest within the Dharma-gate.
Why do you, Master, so recklessly revile it? [The Master] asked, "Have you read *Zhuangzi*? [The Disciple] replied, "I have. [The Master] said, "'*Zhuangzi* says:

If words are sufficient, one may speak all day long and exhaustively express the Dao. If words are insufficient, one may speak all day long and exhaustively describe phenomena. As for the Dao and phenomena...'"
Ultimate. Words and silence are insufficient to carry it; yet neither words nor silence—its meaning reaches its ultimate point.
Confucius said, "Zhan, my Way is one that runs through everything. Zengzi replied, "Yes. This very principle is what makes Zengzi’s words sufficient and Confucius’s words sufficient.
His disciples did not understand and asked, "What do you mean? Zengzi, however, turned back toward the first...
Second, responding to another’s words: it is said that the Way of the Master cannot be without words;
thus he said, "The Way of the Master is simply loyalty and reciprocity. Yet, as for the ultimate point of the Way and all things, it lies neither in speech nor in silence.
Speech cannot convey it, and silence cannot convey it either. What you have said is still not [it].
If one can accord with the intent of Zhuangzi, how much more so must one accord with the intent of Śākyamuni and Bodhidharma?
Consider Master Zhao for a moment; he brought forth that state beyond words and spoke it out for others, saying: "Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha;
Vimalakīrti remained silent in Vaiśālī; Subhūti proclaimed 'no teaching' to manifest the Way, such that even Śakra and Brahmā ceased their listening and rained down [flowers]."
Flowers. All of these are instances where principle is governed by the Divine; thus, the mouth remains silent because of them. How could one say there is no discernment?
It is simply that there is that which discernment cannot speak of. This is Principle meeting the Divine in a sudden collision, such that one unconsciously arrives at a point beyond words.
Although there is no speech, its resonance is like thunder. Within this world, all cleverness and eloquence are of no use here.
It cannot be attained. Only when one reaches such a state is it truly the place where one lets go of the body and relinquishes life.
Such a realm must be personally realized and awakened to by oneself before it can be achieved. Therefore, a sutra says: "The palaces of the Tathāgata are boundless;
those who are spontaneously awakened dwell within them. This is the dharma-gate of great liberation of all the sages of antiquity, intended solely for the sake of sentient beings.
Their faculties and natures are narrow and inferior; they fail to reach the realm of the sages of the Three Teachings, and thus they divide and discriminate between this and that.
Little do they realize that the realm is so vast and great, yet they sit in silence within a ghost cave beneath Black Mountain.
Therefore, the ancient sages condemned it as a deep pit of liberation; it is a place of terror.
To observe it with the divine eye of the Way, it is a mountain of knives and trees of swords, amidst boiling cauldrons and furnace ashes—yet those who sit there are all masters of the same school.
He was still not lingering in the state of silence, let alone being a guest under the gate of the Patriarchs. Yangun (Aṅ) unconsciously prostrated himself.
Daogao (Gǎo) then asked, "How old are you this year? He replied, "Sixty-four. Daogao said, "Where did you come from sixty-four years ago?"
Yang was speechless. Gao struck him across the back with his bamboo staff. The next day, Yuan entered the room again. Gao said, "Sixty-four years ago, it was not so.
Yuan replied, "I was at Zheng’s house in Fuzhou. Gao said, "Listen now as I speak a segment of the Dharma.
It is vividly and clearly manifest. Before you were born, where exactly did you reside? Yuan said, "I do not know. Gao said, "If you..."

If you do not know, this is precisely the arising of the great [self]. Now, in this life, one is limited to a hundred years. After those hundred years, the four elements and five aggregates will all at once disperse.
There will be eyes that cannot see objects, ears that cannot hear sounds, and a lump of flesh that is a heart, yet its discernment no longer functions.
There will be a body that feels no pain even when burned by fire or hacked with a blade. At this point, there remains only this vivid, solitary luminosity.
He then went toward such a state. [The Master] said, "I do not know. [The Master] said, "Since you do not know, you are already dead and great.

Therefore it is said: "Impermanence is swift; the matter of birth and death is great. I shall ask you further: throughout your life you have produced so much of this "zhi-hu-ze-re" (scholastic pedantry);
on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, with which single phrase will you confront that birth and death? You must surely know it. From the moment of birth...
"Only when one dies can the matter be clearly resolved. If you do not know this, you are a fool. Ang was thus moved to submit his heart.
Morning and evening he sought instruction. Fodeng Shouxun first appeared in the world at Heshan and later moved to Tianning.
He addressed the assembly: "My late master lived only to the age of fifty-nine; I am now fifty-six. There are not many days remaining. On the day of Jia-yin, the retreat will be concluded."
Tui Tianning said to Zhang Ji: "The eighth day of the tenth month is the anniversary of the passing of Fojian;
that is when my time has come. I beg to return to the south of Zhang. On the fourth day of the tenth month, Ji sent his younger brother, the monk Daoru, to inquire after him.
Xun said, "Your coming is exactly at the right time. If you had not arrived a day early, you would have missed it by a day late. Although I am one with the Buddha..."
Jian said, "We were born of the same root, but we shall not die of the same root. Tomorrow morning, find a small boat for me.
When his disciple came as instructed, Jian asked, "Do you want a long one or a tall one? [The disciple replied,] "About five feet tall. On the third day at cockcrow, he sat upright as usual.
His attendant requested a final verse, to which he replied, "I have never composed one. Having finished speaking, he passed away.
(Yimao) Master Jusŭng resided at Dongam Jusŭng.
He was the son of the Yang family of Chengdu. Having left the household life, he relied upon Master Wŏnjang.

When Wŏnjang raised the koan of Xiangyan’s “The Dragon Roars Within the Withered Tree,” Jusŭng engaged in a back-and-forth exchange of inquiry and response until he attained great enlightenment beneath the master's words. One day, Wŏnjang said: "Do not remain guarding the cold crag."
Sitting amidst the green of different grasses, the Baiyun school is set aside as not being ultimate. “How about you? Yuan asked. Yunju replied, “One must surely brandish the sword;
if one does not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in his hut. Yuan was startled and said, “This little fellow! Yunju said, “Take care,” and then departed.
He went out to reside at Dongyan, where he addressed the assembly: “The most essential point for studying the Way is nothing other than what the former Nantang spoke of: ‘the first phrase.’”
If you can penetrate the final phrase, your life’s work will be complete. Should this not yet be the case, I shall further divide it for you into ten gates, each to be verified against your own mind;
will you then attain a sense of stability? First, you must believe in the separate transmission outside the teachings.
Second, you must know that there is a separate transmission outside the teachings. Third, you must understand that insentient beings preach the Dharma, just as sentient beings do.

1. Preach the Dharma with a mind free from duality. 2. One must see one's nature as clearly as observing an object in the palm of one's hand, understanding it with perfect clarity, such that every stage of realization is stable and secure.
3. One must possess the eye of discernment regarding the Dharma. 4. One must traverse the mysterious path of the birds. 5. One must be proficient in both civil and martial arts. 6.
One must suppress the heterodox and manifest the orthodox. 7. One must possess great capacity and great function. 8. One must engage with those of different species.
The Middle Practice. Those who wish to perpetuate and glorify the Buddhas and Patriarchs must exhaustively fulfill these essential principles;
only then can they sit upon this curved wooden seat and receive the prostrations of all people under heaven, daring to act as teachers to the Buddhas and Patriarchs themselves.
If you do not reach such a state, you will remain nothing but empty-headed; at that time, on that day, Old Yama will not let you go, and you will still be among those with something left to learn.
[The following] are presented as verses for each section. The introductory verse says: "The essential outline of the ten gates is placed within the palm;
when the opportunity arises, action follows naturally. The author need not arrange a formal sequence; for the most part, the beginning and end constitute the foundation. Qing Su studied under Fa Yan.
One day, upon hearing the raising of the dialogue concerning the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, he suddenly attained realization. He then composed [the following]:
The verse says: "Inversion, inversion, inverted inversion. The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it.
When it was said, "How very groundless! he turned his head; unaware, his cloth shirt had been torn. Yan then asked about Baizhang’s story of the wild fox: "What about this?
[Baizhang] replied, "Those who come to speak of right and wrong are themselves people of right and wrong. Yan was greatly delighted. On the day of the fourth month in the year of Yi-mao.
He suffered a slight illness and wrote a verse, saying: "A wooden man prepares a boat; an iron man prepares a horse. The child of the Bing and Ding stems mounts steadily.
With a shout, he scatters the white clouds and returns home. He then passed away. Yuanjing resided at Daisui. An old master there gave this instruction:
"At the crossroads of the street, erect a single thatched hut; it simply does not permit anyone to defecate therein."
The monk reported this to Jìng. Jìng said, "You have already defecated; what more do you expect anyone else to do? The old master gazed afar at Dàsuí, burned incense, and paid his respects.
In the seventh month of the autumn of the Yǐmǎo year, there was heavy rain and snow upon the mountain, accompanied by extraordinary portents.
Jing said, "My time has come. He then took his leave of the Prefectural Governor. Three days later, he manifested a slight illness.

At night in Tianpeng, he asked an attendant monk, "When it is dawn and there is no moon, what then? The monk had no reply. Jing said, "You have taught me back; only then shall I perform the cremation for you.
The following day, he returned to the Xiangkou Monastery, left behind his final instructions, and passed away peacefully. His younger brother...
The son carried his entire body back home. Smoke and mist gathered from all four directions; monkeys and birds cried out in sorrow. During the cremation, an extraordinary fragrance filled the wilds.
The root of the tongue remained as it was before. The five-colored *śarīra* relics were beyond counting. Shitou returned of his own accord; he had been a stonecutter in the world.

Although he was illiterate, his mind aspired toward the school of Emptiness (*śūnyatā*). He received oral instruction on the *Lotus Sūtra* from others and was able to recite it. Abandoning his home, he retired to a place of stillness.

When someone brought him river stones to sweep and clean, he would not let go of his hammer and chisel; he recited the sūtra without ceasing. A man named Jing saw him and said, "Today there is clattering;
tomorrow there will be clattering. When birth and death arrive, how will you settle the account? [Hui]hui was struck with sudden realization.

He prepared offerings and sought the ultimate Dharma. He instructed him to temporarily cease his recitation of the sutras and instead contemplate the karmic conditions of Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman.

As he returned to this thought, it would not leave his mind. After some time, while he was chipping at a stone, the stone became somewhat hard; as he struck it with all his might, he suddenly caught sight of a flash of fire.
In that instant, he attained sudden and thorough enlightenment. He rushed to the abbot’s quarters, prostrated, and presented a verse, saying: "Exhausting every effort, it was all..."
"No chin. Sparks flew and scattered. "It has been here all along. Jing Xian said, "You have attained thorough penetration.
He then offered this verse on Zhaozhou’s interrogation of the old woman: "The three armies do not move, yet the banners flash; The old woman is precisely the footstep of the Demon King."

Zhaozhou’s handleless iron broom sweeps away the dust and smoke until all is empty and desolate. Jingke bestowed upon him the monastic robes. Liangshan Shi Yuan was a successor of Jingke; his style name was Kuoran.
He was the son of the Zeng family of Hechuan. His "Ten Oxherding Pictures" along with their verses circulate in the world.
Shangshu Mo Jiang, whose courtesy name was Shaohu, was a native of Fenning. While serving as an official in Western Shu, he visited [the master].

Jing consulted him regarding the essentials for resolving the mind. Jing instructed him to maintain mindfulness toward that which is wholesome. While using the toilet, he happened to smell a foul odor;

he immediately covered his nose with his hand and suddenly attained realization. He presented this verse: "From of old, my natural grace has always favored elegance; I have often laughed at those who seek it outwardly.
Though there be ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences, The place where it is found is originally right here on the tip of the nose. Jing said:
When a single dharma is just penetrated, all dharmas are fully encompassed; what further need is there to seek its wondrous function in either vertical or horizontal directions?

A green serpent emerges from its scabbard and the demonic armies submit; the blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head. —Written by Scholar Wang Xiao, style name Guanfu, during his stay at Zhaojue Temple.

Upon hearing the sound of the board signaling the opening of the meditation period, he had an awakening. He asked Master Jing, "I have a certain point of view, yet as soon as someone questions me, I cannot open my mouth.
I do not know where the fault lies. Jing replied, "The fault lies in having a certain point of view. Jing then questioned him further.
"When did your morning banners arrive at your post? He replied, "The fourth day of the eighth month last year. "Since leaving the yamen as an Inspector, how much time has passed?
He replied, "The twentieth day of last month. "Why do you say that one cannot open one's mouth? At these words, Xiao attained sudden enlightenment.
○ Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin Passes Away (The Dharma heir of Wuzu Yan; the eleventh generation of Linji).
Keqin returned to Sichuan and once again resided at Zhaojue Temple in Chengdu. On the [blank] day of the eighth month in the fifth year of the Shaoxing era, he manifested a slight ailment.

Sitting upright in meditation, he wrote a verse to leave for the assembly, then cast down his brush and passed away. During the cremation, his tongue and teeth remained unburnt, and five-colored *śarīra* were produced.
The stupa is located beside Zhaojue Temple. He was posthumously titled Great Master Zhijue. Huiyuan was the son of the Peng family of Meishan.
Having studied under Keqin, he heard the karmic conditions concerning Layman Pang’s "not being a companion to the myriad dharmas. At that moment, Yüan attained sudden enlightenment.

Huiyuan prostrated himself among the assembly. The assembly helped him up. Huiyuan said, "I have awakened from my dream. Later that night, during a small *śamaya* (informal teaching), Huiyuan came forward and asked:
"It is pure and naked, empty with not a single thing; it is bare-boned and poor, with not a single coin. My house is broken and my family is lost; I beg the Master for relief.
[The Master] replied, "The seven treasures and eight jewels are all seized at once. He said, "Calamity does not enter the door of a prudent household. He said, "The pivot..."
Yuanli fell into a sea of poison. Qinquan followed this sound from afar and shouted; he then diligently struck the meditation seat with his staff, saying, "Have you finished eating the staff yet?
Yuanli shouted again. Qinquan shouted twice in succession. Yuanli then prostrated. From that time on, his spiritual acumen became sharp and piercing.
After Qinquan passed away, Yuanli entered the world of teaching and resided at several famous monasteries.
(Bingchen year) Chan Master Kong of Gutan Xiufeng visited Zonggao.
Gao asked about the story of Xiangyan climbing the tree. Kong replied, "Singing the *zhègū* [partridge] song in the spring breeze.
Gao asked, "Is that a statement made from atop the tree, or one made from beneath it? Kong was left at a loss. He subsequently went to Shushan, where he studied the case further.

Having attained realization through his previous discourse, he claimed to have suddenly seen the functioning of Wondrous Joy (Miaoxi). He subsequently returned to Min and stayed at Xiufeng in Gutian. Shao Long resided at Huqiu;

former fellow practitioners from his past training all gathered there at once. Whenever Long ascended the seat, he would invariably reveal the Dharma with composure, teaching with a single flavor of equality.
According to the capacities of those present, there was no one whose mind was not satisfied. He remained there for one term.
In the third year, on a day in the fifth month of the Bingchen year, he was afflicted by a slight illness. He sought out his brush and wrote a gāthā in large characters, saying:

"There is no dharma that can be taught; this is called teaching the Dharma. Thus, in the Buddha-dharma, there are no superfluous words. "Take care," he said, and casting aside his brush, he passed away while sitting.
(Dingsi year) When Chan Master Zonggao was inaugurating the Dharma at Mount Jing, Zhang Jun was in Sichuan;
at that time, Kechin personally entrusted Zonggao to him, declaring that he had truly attained the marrow of the Dharma.

When Zhang Jun went to court, he subsequently invited Zonggao to Mount Jing. Although Zonggao declined three times, he could not but finally consented and set out for the mountain. Upon his arrival...

In Sanqu, he met Zhao Lingjin at the government post station. Lingjin and Daogao had previously sat together on the same Dharma seat, and they had always cautioned one another against pursuing worldly office over the transcendence of the world.
By this time, Lingjin had been appointed to the Southern Bureau of Imperial Clan Affairs, while Daogao was heading for Mount Jing.
Daogao composed a verse, saying: "Transcendent and wondrous, we both have practiced together; Meeting suddenly by chance, each feels ashamed. I am departing to dwell in the mountains."

The Master leaped upon his horse; "three times three before and three times three after. Upon arriving at Lin’an, he ascended the Dharma hall and cited the story of Attendant Wang, who one day visited Linji.
They went together into the monks' hall, and the Attendant asked, "Do the monks in this hall study the sutras?"
Linji said, "I do not read the sutras. The Attendant asked, "Do you practice Chan? Linji said, "I do not practice Chan.
The Attendant said, "If you neither read the sutras nor practice Chan, what exactly are you doing? Linji said, "I am simply teaching everyone to become Buddhas and Patriarchs.
The Attendant said, "Though gold dust is precious, when it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract. What then?"
Linji said, "I took you for a mere worldly fellow. Huangbo then said, "Old man Linji, wielding a Vajra King’s precious sword that pierces the universe, you roamed freely across the world.
Yet, with a mere slight pressure from this official, you were instantly seen to melt away like ice and crumble like tiles. Tell me, what excellence does this official possess? Listen."
I shall cite a verse: "Rare events, both mundane and supramundane, require a person of transcendent capacity to manifest them.
With the very hands that mend robes and season soup, one turns the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata. Upon entering the monastery and ascending the hall, I tell you:
even before I left Quanzhou, I had already met you all; in Lin’an Prefecture as well, I had already met you all.
And so it was. When he arrived at the mountain, he struck the Dharma drum; sitting and standing with solemn dignity, they gazed into one another’s eyes. Why, then, did they not recognize each other?

It is simply because clarity reaches its ultimate limit that what is attained is instead delayed. Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "In the past, the ancient patriarch Yangqi plowed and hauled the oxen, displaying his spiritual powers.

His descendants, however, carry water and drag mud—how much more so!"* *Note: The final character "熨" (yùn) appears to be a scribal error or a specific term from the source text; in this context, it likely functions as a concluding particle or a phonetic marker within the specific lineage's oral tradition.*
The tea cauldrons for brewing are not the same. Entering the hall, he said: "The mud ox at the bottom of the water chews raw iron;
Gopāla bites his own tongue. The Sea God, enraged, seizes his coral whip; Sumeru, King of Mountains, suffers pain that penetrates to the marrow. He struck the meditation seat and descended.
Entering the hall, he took up his staff, struck it once, and called to the assembly: "Do you hear? He then raised it again and said:
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva has arrived. At Mount Jing, he stands with staff in hand, murmuring incessantly:
"All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; they are laws of arising and ceasing. When arising and ceasing are extinguished, quiescent extinction manifests.

Hearing a sound from within his incense casket, he opened it immediately and obtained [relics] as before, though they were slightly redder and more lustrous.
Lady Fan of Chengdu had lived as a widow for many years; she often sat but never lay down. Having heard that Fakuqin resided at Zhaojue Temple, she went there.
He prostrated and requested instruction on the causes and conditions for entering the Way. Qín instructed him to diligently contemplate:

"Neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing—what is this? After a long time, he had no realization. The County Lady wept and said, "Master, what skillful means do you have to enable me to understand this easily?
Qín replied, "There is indeed a skillful means: neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing. The County Lady...

Layman Zeng Kai visited Chan Master Huiyuan during the Xinwei year of the Shaoxing era.
Zeng Kai asked: "What is a good spiritual friend? [Huiyuan] replied: "The lantern reveals itself."

Zhaozhou said, "A pillar; a cat; a dog. Daowei asked, "Why is it that praise brings joy and disparagement brings affliction? Daowei asked, "Have you ever met a true teacher (a *kalyāṇamitra*), Minister?
Daowei replied, "I have been seeking instruction for thirty years; why do you say I have not seen one? Daowei said, "See him in the place of joy;
see him in the place of affliction. As Daowei began to deliberate, Yuanzhen let out a shout. As Daowei was about to respond, Yuanzhen said, "Open your mouth!"
“Di is not the Master. Kaigwan was bewildered. Yuan summoned him, saying, “Where have you been, Minister? Kaigwan suddenly attained realization and nodded his head.
He spoke a verse, saying: “Alas, that blind donkey! A calamity to the monastic community. With one roar that shakes the earth, the celestial mechanism has been leaked.
If anyone asks further what this meaning is, I will raise my whisk and strike them across the mouth! Yuan said, “Even so, he only managed to—”
One Stake. Prefect Ge Tan, courtesy name Qianwen, style name Xinzhai. Having attained the highest honors in the civil service examinations in his youth, he devoted his heart to the joy of Chan.

He first visited Wuan Quan to investigate the koan “This very mind is Buddha,” but after a long time, he had not yet attained entry. He requested, saying, “Master, what skillful means can you provide so that I may gain entry?
[Wuan] replied, “The Layman is simply too insatiable. At that time, Huiyuan arrived and took up residence at Jian...
Daci raised the entire passage and requested that [Hui]yuan preach it for the assembly at large. Yuan said: "To say 'the mind is Buddha' is for the eyebrows to trail upon the ground;

to say 'neither mind nor Buddha' is for the two eyes to stare askance. Amidst the dream of a butterfly, home is ten thousand li away; on the branch of the *subing* tree, the moon is already in its third watch."
He stayed for ten days and then returned. One day, when the Master fully raised the phrase, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing," Tan attained a sudden awakening.
He spoke a verse, saying: "Not mind, not Buddha, nor yet a thing; Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, the mountain looms abrupt."
"Amidst the shadows of the brilliant sun, he turns his body upside down; the wild fox leaps into the den of the golden-haired lion.
Fully approving of this, [Zhaozhou] immediately sent a letter to Changqing Huiyuan. Huiyuan replied: "This matter cannot be fully exhausted by paper or ink.

If you, Layman, can come to me, you shall surely hear it. Thereupon, he visited Huiyuan again. Huiyuan welcomed him, saying: "The scope of your insight, Layman, can only enter the realm of the Buddha."

"Entering the realm of Māra—this has not yet been attained. When Tan bowed, Yuan assumed a solemn expression and said, "Why do you not say that the golden-haired lion leaps into the den of the wild fox?
At this, Tan attained sudden realization. He once asked various Chan masters, "When a husband and wife are fighting..."
He summoned his son and heir to bear witness. Now tell me: does this witness testify for the father, or does it testify for the mother?
In the eighth year of the Chunxi era, he fell ill. One night, he suddenly asked for a brush and wrote a verse: "Beating the drum within the vast ocean, Hearing the bell atop Mount Sumeru.
The karmic mirror suddenly shatters; Turning over, I emerge into the void. He then summoned his officials and subordinates and showed them [the verse], saying: "Life..."
"Life and death are like day and night; there is nothing strange about this. If one speaks from the perspective of the Way (dharma), how could there be birth and death?
If one interprets them as birth and death, one is far removed from the Way. Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away.
(Ren-shen) Chan Master Jingshen entered nirvana (the successor of Baofeng Zhao in the tenth generation of the Cao-Dong lineage).
Jingshen resided at Zhitong. At the beginning of the Xiangshi era, he returned to Baozangyan and lived as a commoner, wearing lay clothing.

On the second month of the Ren-shen year, he manifested a slight ailment and said, "My worldly ties have come to an end. On the thirteenth day of the third month, he gave a small-scale sermon for the assembly, further saying:
The verse says: "There is no need to shave the head; why bother with bathing? A single mass of red flames—ten thousand feet, ten thousand times satisfied.
Although it is thus, tell me: is there still something further above this, or not? Thereupon, he closed his eyes and passed away.
(Guiyou) Chan Master Yin Su Resides at Cihua, Shaoxing, Guiyou Year.
Yin Su, while residing at Cihua, once said: "When one leaves home to become a monk, for what purpose should one do so?

When one donning the black robes and shaving the head, by what cause is this fundamentally undertaken? If one does not repay the state and support the family, one vainly bears the imperial grace. If one does not guide [others]..."
Huating Danana was falsely ordained as a son of the Śākya clan. For twelve years, he wore coarse paper robes and ate simple food, his side never touching the mat.
One day, while reciting the *Huayan lun* (Treatise on the Avataṃsaka), he reached the passage: "When the fundamental is realized, emotions vanish; when the mind is known, it merges with the essence.

At that moment, he attained a sudden and great awakening, and sweat poured from his entire body. He exclaimed, "I have now personally realized the realm of the Huayan! He then addressed the assembly, saying: "The Elder Master Li..."

At the very beginning of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, a heavy blow was struck, shattering the trichiliocosm as if pouring hot water upon snow, leaving not even a hair’s breadth remaining. For those who come later, this might serve as an obstacle;
yet when the Old Man Pú-ān saw it, he could not help but swallow the five thousand and forty-eight fascicles whole, transforming them into a single breath that fills all of space.
Only then will you truly believe the saying that Śākyamuni could not help but let out his breath;

thereafter, he shattered a single mote of dust to bring forth this *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, which pervades the entire Dharma-realm, encompassing all principles without exception and penetrating every dharma without fail.
Then you will see that Lady Māyā is your own body, the terraces of Maitreya are your own essence, and as for Sudhana, what is he but a mere eggplant? (Text)
He was no different from Samantabhadra; he had practiced alongside me. Without leaving his place of practice, he pervaded the entire Dharma-realm.

Weeping with compassion yet filled with joy, he leaped for boundless delight, as if returning to life from death or suddenly waking from a dream. After a long while, he said: "Inexpressible, inexpressible, and again inexpressible.
Only then did I believe the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* when it says: "When the mind of faith is pure, one immediately gives birth to the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*)."

Once the true mark (*dharmatā*) has arisen, the marks of deluded thought (*vikalpa*) are extinguished; the entire body of reality (*dharmakāya*) pervades all places, and only then does the great function manifest before one.
Thus, he spoke this verse: "It cannot be squeezed into a ball, nor can it be pushed apart; What need is there for Nanyue or Tiantai?"
"At the gateways of the six sense organs, no one employs them; this provokes a barbarian monk to come here on purpose. One day, he presented this to his two disciples, Xinzhai and Yuantong, saying:
"When the fundamental is realized, emotions vanish; when the mind is known, the essence is unified. How do you understand this?

The two looked at each other and smiled, saying, "We have not yet reached it. The next day, each presented a verse. Xu (Xinzhai) inscribed the title: "Judging by the Eye of the School, these are mere phrases."

The mind has reached it, yet it has not yet arrived; its substance has not yet merged, yet its emotional attachments have not yet perished. Taking advantage of this opportunity, he forcibly cites two verses from the *Jiepeiling* (Unfastening the Girdle), saying:
"When a person with clear eyes looks upon it, thirty blows of the staff will not be spared.
Why is it so? It is improper to add frost to snow. The first verse says: "Before heaven and before earth, what name and what form does it have? Amanta, there is none."

When things are compared and illustrated, awakening (bodhi) is encountered at every turn; yet people are unwilling to accept this and instead wander in saṃsāra, lingering in attachment to names and forms.
Within the perfectly interfused Dharma-realm, there is no thought and no conceptualization. The rice of Luling requires no deliberation; as soon as the life-vein is opened, it flows freely.
Then one knows: striking wood produces no sound; yet striking empty space results entirely in golden resonance. The second verse says:

Standing in the cypress courtyard amidst the snow was a total failure. To realize non-action is to rest in the present moment. Surrounded by hundreds and thousands of layers, there is only this solitary, perfect moon of the mind.
Unpolished, it remains eternally bright and pure. Without excess and without deficiency, there is neither hearing nor speaking. —Shaoyang.
Old Qi obtained but a single peg. When the Ten Sages and Three Worthies heard it raised, their souls dissolved and their gallbladders shattered;

only Puan remained transcendent and quiescent. Feng Jie’s Chan studies were profound and refined; in his later years, he devoted himself exclusively to the practice of Pure Land. He led both monastics and laypeople in assemblies for mindfulness recitation.
Later, he served as the Prefect of Qiongzhou, remaining serene and withdrawn in all his stations without weariness. He composed a verse which says: "Beyond the completion of public affairs..."

He delighted in sitting in meditation. Rarely did he allow his side to touch the bedding when sleeping. Although he manifested the appearance of a high-ranking official, his reputation as an Elder was renowned throughout the four seas.
In the autumn of the Guiyou year of the Xiangshu era, he informed his relatives and acquaintances in advance, setting the date for his passing on the third day of the tenth month.
On that day, he had a high seat prepared in the rear hall and received visitors as usual. Between the hours of Chén and Sì, he descended the steps and gazed toward—

He performed a solemn prostration and requested that the Transport Commissioner take charge of the affairs of Qiong. Donning his monastic robes and sandals, he sat upon the high seat and exhorted the officials, clergy, and laity alike:
"Each of you should turn toward the Way, support the gates of the Teaching, and establish the banner of the Dharma.

The Transport Commissioner requested, saying, "Since you have such freedom regarding your coming and going, why not leave behind a verse to record this rare occasion? Zhe opened his eyes wide, sought out a brush, and wrote:
He said: "The first three, the eleventh; the middle nine, the lower seven. The old man’s words are exhausted; the tortoise’s eyes turn red.
Having finished writing, he took up his staff, rested it upon his knee, and passed away. After the Jianyan era, many of the Tripitaka collections at famous monasteries had been destroyed by fire.
Zhiyi donated his stipend to print and distribute one hundred twenty-eight sets. There is a verse that says: "I am afflicted by a chronic obsession with folly; I regard wealth as [equal to]..."
All is empty and void. He makes no plans for descendants, nor does he seek the pleasures of sound and form. Whatever monthly stipend he receives, he uses solely to redeem Buddhist scriptures.
He hopes that all who read them may enter the realm of Nirvana without remainder. Even the Buddhas of antiquity abandoned their entire bodies for the sake of half a verse;
therefore, he does not begrudge his wealth to reveal the path to those lost in delusion. I ask those who begrudge their wealth: how can they spend their days calculating?
A mere grain or two. When the day of impermanence suddenly arrives, how can one avoid birth and death?
(Jiaxu) Chan Master Zonggao sent a verse to Tanhua. Initially, Tanhua studied under Keqin.
When Keqin entered Shu, he directed him to see Shaolong. Within less than half a year, he attained thorough penetration of the Great [Dharma].
Fahua Chushi was a world-transcending, wondrously adorned master who traveled through renowned monasteries before finally settling at Nianzong.

When Zonggao was at Meiyan, he saw Hua’s *Chuishishu* (Words of Instruction) and praised it with the utmost fervor, sending him a verse that said: "Severing the path atop the First Peak of the Golden Wheel, A thousand demons and a hundred monsters all hide their traces.
In recent years, I have received a true message: It is reported that the authentic pulse of Yangqi has been restored."
Xiaoying, whose courtesy name was Zhongwen, received the Dharma from Zonggao. He retired to Luohu, where he closed his door and declined visitors.

There, he recollected what he had previously heard and seen within the monastic community—some obtained from the formal expositions of venerable masters, and some from fragmentary inscriptions on broken steles.
As the years passed, fearing that [these records] might be lost or neglected, I have compiled them into a single volume and entitled it *Luohu Yalu* (The Wild Records of Lake Luo).
(Bingzi year) Chan Master Zonggao resided at Ayuwang Temple.
While he was in Hengyang, several scholar-officials sent letters to inquire about the Way; this increasingly displeased those in high office. Shao...

In the year of Xing-gengwu (1190), he moved to Mei and Yang. Over the course of six years, he gathered and transformed disciples both far and near. In the winter of the year of Yi-hai (1195), he received imperial favor and was permitted to reside at his own convenience.

In the spring of the year of Bingzi (1196), he departed from Mei and Yang and arrived at Gan Prefecture. At that time, Zhang Jiu-cheng had been released from banishment in Nan’an and was serving as the Magistrate of Yongjia.
Fengmao moored his boat to wait for him. Once they met, they engaged in an intense discussion on the essential tenets [of the Dharma], never uttering a single word regarding their past history.
At that time, Cheng had a nephew named Yu Xian who was accompanying his uncle back to Xin Gan; Cheng ordered Xian to pay his respects to Fengmao. Xian said, "I have never bowed to monks."
He said, "Try knocking on it. Xian then took up the *Zhongyong* passage, "That which Heaven mandates is called nature; following nature is called the Way;

cultivating the Way is called instruction," and used it to question him. Baogao said, "Ordinary people already do not know where their own primal destiny resides, yet they further drag good people into the fire pit.
How can they fail to penetrate the very first step of the sages and worthies?"
[Cheng] broke [the seal]. Cheng asked, "Can you, Master, break it open for me? Cheng replied, "'That which Heaven mandates is called nature'—this is the pure *dharmakāya*.
'To follow one's nature is called the Way'—this is the perfect *saṃbhogakāya*. 'The cultivation of the Way is called instruction'—this is the billions of *nirmāṇakāyas*.
He then looked at Cheng Xian and said, "What words can you use to decline my prostrations? Prime Minister Zhang Jun was residing in Changsha; his mother...
Lady Ji of the Qin state, whose name was Fazhen, was lying ill and her condition was critical. She said, "I shall no longer see Master Miaoxi.
Although she had a private debt of gratitude to repay, she sent messengers three times to Qiu Jun in Yichun to urge him to come.
By the time Jun arrived, [Miaoxi] had already passed away. Jun said, "To my late mother, I wish to provide for the Venerable Monk for one year as an offering to repay her virtue."
He then took up residence in the East Hall of Guangxiao Temple. Initially, Fazhen had lived as a widow since her youth;

she had cast aside all worldly distractions and subsisted on vegetarian fare while devoted to ritual recitation. Daogao dispatched Daoqian to visit Jun, and Fazhen asked him, "How does the Abbot of Mount Jing usually guide people?
Daoqian thereupon recounted Daogao’s instructions for people to contemplate the kōans of the "dog has no Buddha-nature" and the "bamboo stick. Furthermore—

He was instructed to temporarily suspend his ritual recitations and concentrate solely on contemplating the *huatou*. Once he had penetrated the *huatou*, he realized that even ritual recitations were its wondrous function.

Having attained true conviction, one day he suddenly experienced a state of total clarity. He then described the circumstances of his awakening and presented several verses to Wumen Kō. One of them says:
"Reading the sutras day after day is like meeting an old acquaintance; do not say that there are frequent obstacles, for with each recitation it becomes new.
Gao saw this and approved of it. Daoyan, whose style name was Wan’an, had studied under Keqin for a long time and attained a slight degree of awakening.

When Keqin returned to Shu, he instructed Daoyan to rely upon Gao, sending him a letter of instruction that said: "The painting on the walls of Yan River is already complete; only the final touch remains."
He bestowed the "eye-opening" transmission upon Yan. It cannot be measured how great his future legacy will be. While Daogao resided at Yunmen and Yangyu, Yan was always present;

morning and evening they investigated their doubts together until Daogao attained great enlightenment. In the year Bingzi, when Daogao passed through Jiujiang, the local governor invited him to reside at Yuan Tong Monastery.
Although he declined three times, he could not avoid the request, so he appointed Yan to fill his position. Subsequently, an imperial edict summoned Daogao to reside at Ayuwang Mountain. 11.
In the month of Yúe, Xiǎogǎo arrived in Míngzhōu and ascended the hall to preach the Dharma. Those who traveled there with provisions to seek the Way numbered twelve thousand.
He restored all that had fallen into ruin, surpassing both the present and the past. Zhāng Lì, courtesy name Jìngfū, was the son of Zhùnjùn. He once sought instruction from Yán Hóngdào, saying:
"When you see, you simply see; when you contemplate, you immediately miss it. Yan asked, "What about this? Yan said, "It is like asking whether one knows or does not know.
Chishi asked, "What is it like when one knows? Yan said, "Hearing sounds and seeing forms is just as it always has been. At these words, Chishi had a sudden realization.
He then left behind this verse: "Hearing sounds and seeing forms are just as they always have been; examine them thoroughly, coarse or subtle, and the principle will manifest of itself.

It is like the void containing the azure expanse—there has never been so much as a single hair’s breadth of excess. Yan Ken approved of it. Later, when Lü Xi was on the verge of death, [the verse was presented].
Ding Sǒu requested instruction. Xié said, "Casting off the private desires of human nature like a cicada shedding its shell; the subtle wonder of the heavenly principle is as warm as spring.
Having finished speaking, he passed away. His disciples honored him as Master Nánxuān.
(Dingchou year) Chan Master Zhengjue of Tiantong entered nirvana (the tenth generation of the Caodong lineage, successor of Danxia Chun).
Zhengjue resided at Tiantong for thirty years, during which the Caodong school flourished greatly. In the ninth month of the Dingchou year...
He paid his respects to the local officials and the *dānapati*. Next, he visited Zhao Lingcong, the Military Governor of Yue, and took his leave.
On the seventh day of the tenth month, he returned to the mountain. On the following day, between the hours of Chén and Sì, he bathed, changed his robes, and sat upright to address the assembly.

Looking toward his attendant monk, he asked for a brush and wrote a letter to Yuwang Zonggao, requesting him to preside over his funeral affairs. He then inscribed this verse: "Dreams, illusions, and empty flowers."
In the sixty-seventh year, the white birds vanished into the mist; the autumn waters joined the heavens. He cast down his brush and passed away.
His shrine remained for seven days, his countenance appearing as if alive. By imperial decree, he was posthumously titled Hongzhi, and his stupa was named Miaoguang.

Jingci Huihui first called upon Zhenxie and attained a slight realization. Later, he visited Zhengjue. Zhengjue raised the phrase: "Within light there is darkness; do not take it as the aspect of darkness."
They met. It was as if there were light within the darkness, yet they did not perceive one another through the appearance of light. When asked about it, their words did not accord.

At the end of the first watch of the night, Huì returned from his meditative concentration and went before the sacred image of the Buddha to burn incense; Jué arrived just then. Upon seeing him, Huì suddenly understood the previous conversation.

The next day, when entering the room for instruction, Jué remarked, "Alas, the complexion of your face on the day you departed was like jade, yet now I sigh that your hair at your return is like hoarfrost. He questioned Huì about this. Huì—
It was said: "His entry is detached and his exit is subtle; from that point on, there was no obstruction. Zonggao was recognized as a true son within the hall.
(Wuyin) In the Wuyin year of the Shaoxing era, Chan Master Zonggao began his dharma teaching at Mount Jing.
